# DreamTeam — internal module specification

This is the contract between modules. Every public name below must exist with exactly this
signature/behaviour. Implementation details not covered here are up to the implementer, but
must not leak into other modules. Language of code, comments and docstrings: English.
User-visible texts for agents live in `prompts.py` (ru/en). Python >= 3.11, asyncio.

## 0. Conventions

* Time: `time.time()` floats everywhere (DB, events, messages).
* Actors: a member name (`"John Smith"`), or the reserved `USER = "user"` (the human).
  `"all"` is a pseudo-recipient for messages. Names are unique, case-insensitive, stored canonically.
* Errors meant for the caller (agent, user, MCP client) are raised as `models.ToolError(msg)`.
  Messages are short, in English, and tell the caller how to fix the call.
* JSON in DB: `db.dumps` / `db.loads` (ensure_ascii=False; a value holding a lone surrogate, e.g. from LLM
  tool arguments, is written with ASCII escapes instead, so it is storable and loads back identical).
  Plain TEXT columns cannot hold lone surrogates: `db.utf8_safe(text)` replaces them with U+FFFD; a tool
  whose arguments hit one returns an "invalid Unicode" error instead of an internal error.
* Every state change emits exactly one event via `swarm.bus.emit(type, actor, **data)` (see §9).
* No module prints to stdout (stdio MCP mode uses it). Use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`.
* Event loop: everything runs in one asyncio loop; the DB is used synchronously from it.
  Blocking work (git, big file IO) goes through `asyncio.to_thread`. Shell commands never use the loop's default
  executor (git does, and `asyncio.run` waits for its threads at exit): their spawn, output reader and waiter are
  daemon threads of their own (§7). Every loop is started by `cli.run_loop(main)` (§18.3), never a bare
  `asyncio.run` (tests/test_loop_start.py checks src).

## 1. Layout

```
src/dreamteam/
  __init__.py  __main__.py
  config.py      Config / ModelProfile / templates                  (exists)
  db.py          Database (sqlite); FORUM_SCHEMA, the thread mode's tables (§22.1)  (exists)
  models.py      USER, ALL, ToolError, Status, Task, AgentKind...    (exists)
  events.py      EventBus; read_page: a page of the journal by id (§21.6)  (exists)
  names.py       generate_name                                       (exists)
  prompts.py     system_prompt(mode), t(), mode_key(), PLANNING_TASK, DEFAULT_ROLE (exists; texts by mode, §22.6)
  roles.py       role catalog: presets, [[roles]] overlay, resolution, starting team, saved teams (§17.3); imports
                 nothing from the package
  goal_text.py   split_goal, shorten_title: a goal typed as one text -> title + description (§3)
  board.py       Board          — tasks, goal field, discussion, independent review (§4)
  forum.py       Forum          — the thread mode: posts, comments, votes, subscriptions, the goal vote (§22)
  mailbox.py     Mailbox        — direct messages
  workspace.py   Workspace      — shared files, git, locks
  hubgit.py      DreamTeam's own git in the members' folders: environment, fixed options, the repository's
                 commands disarmed (§7 "DreamTeam's own git")
  hubauth.py     the hub token: what a hub with one asks of every peer, where `dreamteam sandbox` keeps it,
                 what DreamTeam's clients send (§14.2); standard library only
  shell.py       run_shell, start_command, RunningCommand, Capture, scrubbed_env, secret_free_env (§7)
  netoff.py      sessions without network: isolation, wrap, environment, sandbox_entry (§7.2);
                 netns_helper.py makes the offline commands' network namespace and joins a command to it
  procs.py       ProcessTree    — a command's contained process tree: Windows Job Object, POSIX process group with a
                 lifeline watchdog (§7); standard library only
  jobs.py        JobManager, ShellOutcome — background jobs of the members' shell commands (§7.1)
  triggers.py    TriggerEngine + condition DSL
  llm/__init__.py  create_llm(profile)
  llm/base.py      ToolCall, Usage, LLMResponse, LLMError, LLMClient, estimate_tokens
  llm/anthropic_llm.py  AnthropicLLM
  llm/openai_llm.py     OpenAILLM
  llm/scripted.py       ScriptedLLM (tests / demos)
  mcp_forge.py   MCPForge, MCPConnection — agent-built MCP servers + library
  skills.py      skill folders (SKILL.md), their sources (folder, zip, Git, Claude Code) and the shared library (§19)
  swarm_skills.py SessionSkills — the skills attached to one session, the agents' mirror, the wake-up index,
                 members' proposals and the user's library decision, the roles' skills (§19)
  skill_deps.py  skills' script dependencies: manifest detection, EnvManager — environments shared by all sessions
                 under ~/.dreamteam/skill-envs, builds, OS locks, Node views, cleanup (§19)
  tools/__init__.py  registry: ToolSpec, ToolContext, tool(), tools_for(), schemas_for(), call_tool(); the session
                 modes (`MODES`, `ToolSpec.modes` and `variants`, `parameters_for`, §22.5)
  tools/board_tools.py comm_tools.py file_tools.py job_tools.py swarm_tools.py trigger_tools.py mcp_tools.py
  tools/skill_tools.py the skills tools: the user's `skills`, `skill_attach`, `skill_detach`, `skill_approve`,
                 `skill_reinstall`, and the members' `skill_propose` (§19)
  tools/forum_tools.py the thread mode's tools: `feed`, `post_read`, `post_create`, `post_update`, `comment`,
                 `vote`, `subscriptions`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, and their id parsers (§22.5)
  tools/frozen.py    frozen LLM tool sets: revisions in one numbering for both modes (board 5, thread 6:
                     TOOLSET_REVISIONS), the kv record of each agent, `python -m dreamteam.tools.frozen` (§6.1,
                     §22.5)
  tools/snapshots/   llm_r<N>.json (board) and llm_thread_r<N>.json (thread): the shipped LLM tool sets, revision
                     OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION..NEWEST_REVISION (now 5 and 6; en and ru), never edited
  agent.py       AgentRuntime   — ReAct loop of one LLM agent
  swarm.py       Swarm          — composition root
  hub_mcp.py     the swarm as an MCP server (stdio / streamable HTTP / stdio->HTTP proxy)
  web.py         Starlette app of one swarm: REST + WebSocket + /mcp + static board UI
  httpjson.py    JSONResponse / json_text for HTTP and WebSocket (lone surrogates escaped, never a 500)
  tracing.py     Tracer / Trace — agent traces (§16)
  trace_api.py   REST routes of the traces, mounted by web.create_app (§16.3)
  tools/trace_tools.py  the `agent_traces` tool (§16.2)
  settings.py    global settings of a home: read/write/validate, public view, updates, endpoint checks (§17.1)
  sessions.py    SessionManager — the sessions of a home (§17.2)
  copyfrom.py    a folder or a zip copied into a new session before its first start, and the uploaded zips
                 (§17.2 "Copying files into a new session"); v1's uploads, name and path rules (§21.3, §21.8);
                 never imports sessions.py
  transfer.py    `dreamteam export` / `dreamteam import` of a home: the export folder, the secret check, the import

  treecopy.py    copy or measure a folder tree byte for byte, with a digest that is the same on every OS (§20)
  mcp_library.py the shared MCP library on disk, usable without a Swarm: list, read, add atomically, remove (§20)
  launcher.py    launcher web app: sessions page, settings, /s/{sid}/ routing (§18.1)
  launcher_mcp.py  the launcher as one MCP server (§18.2)
  api_v1.py      the external HTTP API under /api/v1: ApiV1(manager, host), its Starlette app, routes and aclose()
                 (§21)
  autoreply.py   the requests to the user (requests_of, read_requests, blocking_requests), the hub's automatic
                 answers for a session created with answers "auto" (SessionAutoReply), and a session's journal

  eventtext.py   one plain line per event for people, outside the tui package (§21.6)
  uitext.py      the feed's texts (ru/en), moved out of tui/i18n.py, which stays as a shim (§21.6)
  symbols.py     the feed's symbols, moved out of tui/theme.py, which re-exports them (§21.6)
  result.py      the result object of a run, shared by `dreamteam -p` and the API (§21.7)
  instruct.py    what `dreamteam -p -r` and the API's continue do with a prompt: coordinator (board sessions),
                 continue_step, post_parts (a post by the user in a thread session, §22.9); the sessions `-c`
                 picks from: without_api_sessions (§21.2, §21.4)
  sessionopts.py team, model and limits of a request -> session overrides, shared with the launcher MCP (§21.4)
  apifolders.py  [api] folders: the roots, their checks, a request's folder (§21.10)
  nofollow.py    open, list and walk inside a root without following links (§21.8)
  static/        index.html app.js traces.js style.css traces.css (board), home.html home.js home.css (launcher),
                 markdown.js and icons.css (both); no build step
  console.py     terminal chat client (talks to the REST API)
  tui/           terminal UI client (docs/TUI.md)
  docker.py      sandbox: build & run DreamTeam in Docker (for a home also its [api] folders roots, §21.10)
  cli.py         `dreamteam` command
tests/  conftest.py (FakeSwarm fixture) + test_*.py
```

A **home** (launcher, §17–18; `~/DreamTeam` by default) on disk:
```
<home>/dreamteam.toml               global settings (§17.1); dreamteam.toml.bak = the previous version
<home>/sessions/<id>/session.json   {"title", "uid", "created_at", "overrides", "autostart", "pending_goal"?,
                                     "workspace"?: {"path", "adopted", "in_home"?}, "workspace_notice"?,
                                     "origin_uid"?} (§17.2; "uid": the session's identity across homes, 32
                                     lowercase hex; a session.json without it gets one derived from
                                     "created_at" on read, `sessions.session_uid`; "origin_uid": §20.4)
<home>/sessions/<id>/workspace/     the session's shared files (unless "workspace" names another folder)
<home>/sessions/<id>/.dreamteam/workspace-move.json  only while a workspace move runs, or after one whose
                                    undo failed (§17.2 "Workspace folder")
<home>/sessions/<id>/.dreamteam/    the session's swarm.db and logs/ (a project directory as below)
<home>/sessions/.deleted-<id>-<ns>/ a session being deleted (renamed away first, then removed)
<home>/sessions/.importing-<id>-<pid>-<hex8>/  a session an import stages before renaming it in (§20.4)
<home>/sessions/.replaced-<id>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-N]/  the last copy of a session an import rewrote: session/
                                    (the old session folder), workspace/ (its in_home folder, if any), swap.json
                                    only while the swap runs or after it died halfway (§20.4)
<home>/.dreamteam/hub.json          the running launcher (same format as below; "project" = the home)
<home>/.dreamteam/logs/dreamteam.log
<home>/.dreamteam/swarm.db          only in a home that was a single-swarm project before: session `main`
```

Project (one swarm of `dreamteam run`; a session directory has the same layout without `dreamteam.toml` and
`hub.json`) on disk:
```
<project>/dreamteam.toml
<project>/workspace/            shared files (git repo), workspace/mcp/<name>/server.py
<project>/workspace/.scratch/<slug>/  each member's temporary files, never committed (§7 "Scratch folder")
<project>/workspace/.scratch/<slug>/jobs/  j<N>.log (and j<N>.prev.log): the output of the member's background
                                jobs (§7.1)
<project>/.dreamteam/swarm.db   sqlite
<project>/.dreamteam/jobs/      job logs when `.scratch` is not a plain folder of the workspace (§7.1)
<project>/.dreamteam/hub.json   {"base_url": "...", "mcp_url": "...", "pid": 123, "project": "<abs path>",
                                "machine": "<platform.node()>" | null}
                                written once the server listens; other commands trust it only if GET /api/hub
                                confirms the same pid and project; "machine" is null in a container (§18.3)
<project>/.dreamteam/logs/      dreamteam.log, mcp-<name>.log
```

## 2. Data model (db.py SCHEMA is authoritative)

* `tasks`: id, title, **goal** (why the task exists / success criterion), description, status,
  assignee, reviewer, created_by, parent_id, depends_on (json int list), priority (0 low,1 normal,
  2 high,3 critical), tags (json str list), result, created_at, updated_at, crew (0, or 2..8: a crew task, §4.2;
  `INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `db.ADDED_COLUMNS` adds it to an older file). A task in `review` keeps its
  executor as `assignee` (NULL only when the executor left the swarm, §4.1); there is no separate executor column.
* `comments`: the per-task **discussion**: id, task_id, author, text, reply_to (comment id | null), ts.
* `agents`: name, kind (`llm`|`external`), role (a catalog role by its canonical name in the member's language,
  §17.3), instructions (the hirer's own; a catalog role's instructions are only in the system prompt), model
  (profile name, set at hire; it follows a profile rename saved through the settings, §17.2 `update_settings`;
  NULL for an external member), language, status (`idle`|`working`|`paused`|`error`|`retired`), hired_by,
  created_at, last_active, cost_usd, tokens_in, tokens_out, notes, system_prompt (frozen at creation),
  context_tokens.
* `history`: agent, seq, msg (json neutral message, §6.1) — append-only per agent except compaction.
* `messages` + `inbox(message_id, recipient, read_at)`.
* `notifications`: id, ts, recipient, kind (prompt key), text (rendered), data (json), delivered_at. Data flags
  (§3 `notify`): `_quiet` (sent with `wake=False`); in a thread session also `_digest` (a digest item) and `_settle`
  (a waking `f_file` waiting for its run of changes to settle), §22.3.
* `triggers` (§8): id, owner, condition, note, actions (json), once, active, created_at, last_value, last_fired,
  fire_count, last_error, and the wake limit's told_at (when the trigger last told its owner), held (fires since then
  whose notice waits), held_last (the latest of them), held_files (json `{path: {count, by, first, last, settled}}`:
  their file_changed() changes); the last four are in `ADDED_COLUMNS` too, so an older file gets them at its next
  open. `mcp_servers`, `kv`, `events`.
* `file_locks`: path (primary key, workspace-relative), owner, acquired_at, expires_at, wanted_at (when its holder
  was told that members wait for it, `n_lock_wanted`; NULL for a new lock, kept by a refresh; an older file gets the
  column at its next open, `ADDED_COLUMNS`). `lock_waiters` (§7 "Lock waiters"): agent, path (what it was refused,
  as it asked for it), since; primary key (agent, path).
* `jobs` (background jobs, §7.1; index `jobs_owner(owner, status)`): id (AUTOINCREMENT: `j<id>`, unique for the
  session's life), owner, command, shell (display name), origin (`timeout`|`background`|`detached`), status
  (`running`|`ended`|`stopped`|`lost`), reason (stopped: `owner`|`user`|`lifetime`|`retired`|`session`; lost:
  `crash`), stopped_by (the owner's name or `user` for reason owner/user), exit_code (the shell's own code once it
  ended by itself, also while processes it started run on; NULL when the shell was killed), log (workspace-relative
  posix path, or absolute for the data_dir fallback), pid, pgid (POSIX), token (the random
  `DREAMTEAM_PROCESS_TOKEN`), hub_pid (the process that ran it), processes (json list of names), tail (the last
  2000 characters of the output, at the end), started_at, background_at, ended_at. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`:
  an older database gets it at its next open.
* `traces`, `spans`, `history_archive(agent, epoch, seq, msg, archived_at)`: tracing.py SCHEMA (§16).
* `posts`, `post_comments`, `votes`, `subscriptions`: the thread mode, `db.FORUM_SCHEMA` (§22.1), only in a thread
  session's database (never in `SCHEMA`: a board session's file stays importable into 0.4.x).
* kv keys: `goal` → `{"title","description","status":"active"|"done","summary","set_by","updated_at"}`, plus
  `completed_by` (set by `complete_goal`: the actor; null when a retire, rule change or start met a thread
  session's vote) and, in a thread session while done, `decision` (§22.1, §22.4; no `artifacts`),
  `limits` → `{"max_cost_usd": float, "max_agents": int}` (overrides config), `paused` → `{"paused": bool,
  "reason": str}` (a member's question, §3.1: `{"paused": true, "reason": "question", "asker": str, "message_id":
  int, "since": float}`), `budget_notice` → `{"limit": float, "at": float, "spent": float, "ts": float}` (the money
  notice sent for that limit and fraction, §3 `record_usage`; a new limit or fraction re-arms it),
  `tools:<agent name>` → `{"rev": int, "language": "en"|"ru", "tools": [{"name","description","parameters"}],
  "mode"?: "board"|"thread"}` (the agent's frozen tool set, §6.1; no "mode" = board, §22.1, §22.5; kept for retired
  agents, traces read it), `wait_progress:<actor>` → the last events id whose board progress (in a thread session:
  the feed's progress, §22.5) `wait_for_events(progress=true)` returned to that actor (§12), `swarm_mode` →
  `"board"` | `"thread"`: the session's mode, fixed when it is created (§22.1).

## 3. Swarm (swarm.py) — what other modules may use

```python
class Swarm:
    config: Config; db: Database; bus: EventBus
    board: Board; mail: Mailbox; workspace: Workspace; triggers: TriggerEngine; forge: MCPForge
    forum: Forum | None                      # the thread mode's posts, votes, subscriptions; None on a board
                                             # (§22.2)
    mode: str; is_thread: bool               # "board" | "thread", from kv swarm_mode, fixed at creation (§22.1)
    goal_rule: str                           # config.swarm.goal_rule; only thread sessions read it (§22.4)
    runtimes: dict[str, AgentRuntime]        # running LLM agents
    language: str                            # config.swarm.language
    llm_semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore
    tracer: Tracer                           # §16
    jobs: JobManager                         # background jobs of the members' shell commands (§7.1)
    skills: SessionSkills                    # the skills attached to this session and their mirror (§19)
    session_id: str | None; session_title: str | None   # set by SessionManager (§17.2)
    hub_url: str | None                      # MCP URL of this swarm while a web server runs (snapshot mcp_url)
    stopping: bool                           # set by stop()/close(): long polls (wait_for_events) end at once

    def __init__(self, project_dir, config: Config | None = None,
                 llm_factory: Callable[[ModelProfile, str], LLMClient] | None = None): ...
        # a failure after the database was opened (a corrupt swarm.db...) closes it before re-raising
    async def start(self, run_agents: bool = True) -> None
        # tracer.recover(), then jobs.recover() (rows a previous process left running become `lost`, §7.1 "Crash
        # recovery"), and the trace prune first (§16.1); the very first start creates the starting team through
        # `_create_member` (not `hire`: no limit check and no n_hired; in a thread session its thread prompt, thread
        # role texts and automatic subscriptions come from `_create_member`, §22.3):
        # roles.starting_team(swarm.starting_roles, swarm.start_agents), member i gets starting_roles[i], the rest
        # (and blank entries) are generalists (§17.3); LLM agents with open tasks, reviews waiting for them or
        # pending events (goal active), or whose last activation was cut short (the stored history ends
        # mid-activation), get `n_restart`; hire() respects run_agents. After forge.start(): skills.start() (the
        # session's skills read again, their script dependencies planned in a daemon thread and held in use, the
        # agents' mirror rebuilt from the session copies with its node_modules links, the owners of decisions made
        # while stopped told, §19), then skills.ensure_deps() as a `_background` task (builds never waited for);
        # after the starting team is created: skills.ensure_role_skills(announce=False)
        # (the skills the members' roles list; nobody is told: every first wake-up after a start shows the index).
        # A thread session (§22.4, §22.7): `_digest_floor` = now and `_thread_quiet` / `_thread_quiet_woken` empty;
        # `forum.rewrite_goal_rule()` and `forum.recheck_goal(None)` once after the starting team exists, before the
        # restart notices; a goal set before the very first start gets `_kickoff_thread(USER, goal, True)`, never
        # `_kickoff` (no planning task)
        # The scheduler calls skills.check() (the mirror, at most once a minute) and skills.touch_envs() (hourly)
    async def stop(self) -> None
        # wakes every wait_signal() waiter (stopping=True), closes external trace sessions (a failure is logged:
        # tracing never keeps a session from stopping), stops the runtimes (an LLM agent's foreground command dies
        # with its cancellation), then jobs.stop_all() (every job and every foreground command, e.g. an external
        # member's call, is killed; every finish and call in flight has returned and every job log and handle is
        # closed, §7.1), then commits every member's held new files (workspace.commit_held(None, "when the session
        # stopped"), after a settle() when there are any; §7 "Held new files"), then forge.stop(), then waits for
        # git commands still running in threads
        # (workspace.settle(), §7): nothing touches git or the database afterwards. stop_all, forge.stop and
        # settle run in `finally`: also when an earlier step failed or the stop was cancelled (the caller closes
        # and drops the session after a failed stop, so no process may outlive it); then skills.stop_deps() (no
        # more build news, the view tasks cancelled, the session's in-use set released; builds go on in the
        # process); in an adopted folder (§17.2) skills.remove_mirror() last: no copy of a skill stays in the user's
        # project
    def close(self) -> None                              # closes the database
    def reconfigure(self, config: Config) -> None        # hot-apply new settings (§16.1)
        # when the roles' skills changed (swarm_skills.role_skill_pairs) under a running swarm (started, not
        # stopping): skills.ensure_role_skills() in a background task (`_role_skills_task`, in `_background`: stop()
        # cancels it; a newer change while it runs makes it run once more, never cancels it: its copy thread
        # would go on past the lock); a save that does not touch them starts nothing

    # members
    def member(self, name: str) -> dict | None          # agents row as dict (any status), exact canonical name
    def members(self, include_retired: bool = False) -> list[dict]
    def is_member(self, name: str) -> bool              # exists and not retired (llm or external)
    def agent_count(self) -> int                        # active LLM members: what max_agents limits (external
                                                        # members, MCP clients that joined, neither count nor are
                                                        # limited)
    def kind_of(self, name: str) -> str | None          # "user" | "llm" | "external" | None
    def resolve_member(self, name: str, allow_user: bool = True, allow_retired: bool = False) -> str
        # case-insensitive / whitespace-tolerant, a leading "@" ignored, a unique first name alone accepted;
        # USER_ALIASES ("user", "пользователь", "the user", "human", "человек") -> USER when allowed, else
        # ToolError("The user cannot be used here..."); "" -> ToolError("Empty member name.");
        # raises ToolError("Unknown member 'x'. Members: ...") with close-match suggestions.
        # The rules live in module-level `resolve_member_in(pool, name, allow_user)`, shared with FakeSwarm.
    def language_of(self, name: str) -> str             # member language, else swarm language

    # notifications / waking
    def notify(self, recipient: str, key: str, *, wake: bool = True, batch: bool = False, defer: bool = False,
               **kw) -> None
        # text = prompts.t(language_of(recipient), key, **kw); insert notifications row (kind=key,
        # data=kw); emit "notification" {recipient, kind, text}; if wake: signal(recipient).
        # wake=False for a member: data also gets "_quiet": true; such a row is news for the member's
        # next wake-up (render_wake delivers it) but does not count in has_pending
        # batch (thread sessions, only with wake=False, never for USER): data also gets "_digest": true (DIGEST_KEY),
        # a digest item of the forum's delivery (§22.3; `digest` stays an ordinary data key: u_mcp_pending passes
        # `digest=` for its `{digest}` placeholder); defer (only with wake=True, never for USER): the row is
        # waking but not signalled, then defer_wake(recipient) (§22.3 "Quiet new posts"). A quiet row becomes news
        # that wakes only when the thread scheduler drops its "_quiet" (a due digest, a settled file item, §22.7):
        # a bare signal never activates a member with nothing pending (§6.2)
    def signal(self, name: str) -> None                 # wakes LLM runtime / releases wait_signal waiters
    async def wait_signal(self, name: str, timeout: float) -> bool
    def has_pending(self, name: str) -> bool            # unread inbox or undelivered non-quiet notifications
    def waits_for_job(self, name: str) -> bool
        # an AI agent asleep (runtime state idle) while a command of its own runs on as a job it waits for
        # (JobManager.busy) and whose end will wake it (JobManager.awaited): a member's broadcast reaches it without a
        # wake (§5 "Quiet broadcasts")
    def defer_wake(self, name: str) -> None              # such news reached `name` unwoken (_wake_deferred, below)
    def digest_deadline(self, name: str) -> float | None
        # thread sessions: when the oldest undelivered digest item of `name` other than a vote falls due
        # (max(ts, _digest_floor) + [agents] digest_seconds); None while the goal is not active or there is none.
        # The scheduler's digest batching and `wait_for_events` use it (§22.3 "Digest items")
    def team_asleep(self, caller: str | None = None) -> bool
        # nobody in the team can act or be woken by something already set (scheduler item 9 below, `wait`'s result,
        # §12). `caller`, when given, is the member calling `wait` (still working): it counts as idle with nothing
        # pending. True when all of these hold: every LLM member with a runtime is idle as `_idle_llm_members` counts
        # it (status idle, nothing pending, not `jobs.busy`) or in error with no recovery scheduled
        # (`runtime._recovery` None: one with a recovery timer will be retried, so it counts as awake), and at least
        # one is idle (or is `caller`); none of them waits for something of its own: a job whose end wakes it
        # (`jobs.awaited`) or a file it was refused (`workspace.waits_for_lock`), counted however long either lasts
        # (the job's end or `n_lock_free` will come: a forgotten `background` server keeps it false until `[shell]
        # job_max_minutes`); no delayed notification is pending (`_timers` empty: staggered kickoffs not delivered
        # yet); `triggers.unattended(now)` is false (§8 "Unattended triggers"; `now` from the engine's `clock`, which
        # stamps the triggers' times); no external member made a hub call in the last `EXTERNAL_IDLE_SECONDS` (15
        # min, tracing.py): `_external_seen` {member: time.time()}, in memory, stamped by `hub_call` (§13) for every
        # call but `wait_for_events`, whether tracing is on or not (a client that only listens is asleep like the
        # others); in a thread session (§22.7) also false while the goal is active and an idle LLM member other than
        # `caller` has an undelivered `_digest` row other than an `f_vote` one, or any member a `_settle` row
    def stall_ids(self, name: str) -> frozenset[int]
        # the public form of `_stall_ids` (scheduler items 2-3, `wait`'s result): the in_progress task ids of `name`
        # that count as stalled, not a clarify planning card whose holder waits for the user's answers (`asks_user`,
        # §3.1) nor a crew task with a direction that can still move (`Board.has_live_directions`); a `waiting` task
        # never counts (answers wake its holder, system prompt rule 7); always empty in a thread session (§22.7)
    def render_wake(self, name: str, incoming: bool = False, stamps: bool = False,
                    since: float | None = None) -> str | None
        # drains (marks read/delivered) and renders the wake-up text (§6.3); None if nothing pending
        # and incoming=True; stamps/since: only wait_for_events (§12), never an agent's wake-up
    def notes_shown(self, name: str, notes: str) -> None   # the agent's context now holds these notes
    def skills_shown(self, name: str, value: bool | None) -> None
        # what the agent's context holds of the Skills index (§6.3): True the full index, False "none attached",
        # None nothing known (the next wake-up shows the full index); in memory, like notes_shown

    # goal
    def goal(self) -> dict | None
    def set_goal(self, actor: str, title: str, description: str = "") -> dict
        # every goal comes through here (the set_goal tool, a session's pending goal, swarm.goal of
        # dreamteam.toml, `run --goal`): title/description pass through goal_text.split_goal (the first
        # non-empty line is the title, at most 200 chars; the other lines open the description, followed by
        # `description`; an empty title takes the text from the description), and the goal dict stores the split
        # values, so the goal line of every wake-up is one line; empty title -> ToolError("The goal title is
        # empty."); an empty board gets a planning task (`prompts.planning_task(language, clarifying)`: PLANNING_TASK
        # with the tag planning, or in clarify mode its clarify variant with the tags planning and clarify, §3.1;
        # body = its text + title + description);
        # agents are kicked off staggered: `n_kickoff` {by, title, description, team, task_id, task_title}, with
        # team = "Name — Role; ..." of all members, or `n_goal_updated` when the board was not empty.
        # PLANNING_TASK's steps: 1 look around (only as much as splitting the work needs: research, experiments,
        # reproducing a problem and environment checks are separate tasks for the others, the team waits for the
        # planner's tasks meanwhile; `hint_planner` reminds a planner that has created none); 2 independent work at once (work that needs no contracts:
        # literature and theory, the environment and tools, data, exploratory experiments, becomes tasks before
        # CONTRACTS.md, so the members waiting for the plan start now; only the planner creates the plan's tasks);
        # 3 then the contracts; 4 then the rest of the tasks (created without parent_id: they are not parts of
        # the card, which an open subtask would keep from completing, §4.2 "Finishing"); 5 no false dependencies (a final task: report,
        # summary, documentation, release, depends only on the tasks it cannot be written without; exploratory and
        # optional tasks do not block it); 6 tests by someone else; 7 reviews; 8 team; 9 finish quickly. n_kickoff
        # tells the others that the first tasks come before the plan is complete. A clarify card wakes only the first
        # LLM member; the others get the same n_kickoff quietly (§3.1 "Kickoff"). A thread session (§22.4) never
        # gets a planning task: `forum.ensure_system_posts(goal)` writes or rewrites #1 and #2 whether or not the
        # swarm is started, then, when started, `_kickoff_thread` sends `n_kickoff_thread` (first goal) or
        # `n_goal_updated_thread`; with a clarify #2 (a first or a new goal) only one asker is woken, by the clarify
        # variant
    def complete_goal(self, actor: str | None, summary: str, *, decision: dict | None = None) -> dict
        # ToolError when there is no goal, it is already done, or the summary is empty; notifies USER u_goal_done;
        # background jobs keep running (a dev server may be for the user): when some run, USER also gets the quiet
        # u_jobs_running {jobs: "j3 (Anna Smith: npm run dev, 25 min); ..."}, and their later ends wake nobody
        # `decision` (a thread session, §22.4) goes into kv `goal` in the same write; actor None when no voter met
        # the rule; with a decision USER gets u_goal_decided in place of u_goal_done (none at all for rule `user`)
        # and every LLM member the quiet n_goal_decided
    def complete_goal_by_user(self, summary: str = "") -> dict
        # thread sessions only (a board session: ToolError): complete_goal(USER, summary or goal_completed_by_user,
        # decision={rule: "user", ...}); swarm_control complete_goal (§12, §22.4)
    def reopen_goal(self, actor: str, comment: str = "") -> dict
        # only a done goal (else ToolError); notifies ONE LLM member n_goal_reopened: the one who completed
        # the goal, else the most recently active (the others are offered new tasks by the scheduler). A thread
        # session (§22.4): `decision` popped, summary "", the votes on #1 cleared, the comment posted on #1 unless empty
        # or "-", n_goal_reopened_thread waking to every LLM member (staggered, as the kickoff).
        # set_goal and reopen_goal both end wrap-up mode (end_wrap_up, below)

    # team
    async def hire(self, by: str, role: str, instructions: str = "", model: str | None = None,
                   name: str | None = None, language: str | None = None, kind: str = "llm") -> str
        # the role is resolved in the role catalog (roles.find_role, §17.3) in the member's language: a catalog
        # role is stored by its canonical name ("tester" -> "Tester" / «Тестировщик») and brings its description,
        # instructions and model profile; any other name is a new role that only `instructions` describe.
        # Model profile: explicit `model` (unknown -> ToolError) > the role's `model` (a profile missing from
        # the settings logs a warning and falls back) > agents.default_model. The frozen system prompt
        # (LLM members only) is prompts.system_prompt(language, name, swarm, role, role_description,
        # instructions, shell, scratch, max_agents, foreground_max): role_description = the catalog description,
        # instructions = the catalog's then the hirer's (blank line between), scratch = workspace.scratch_rel(name)
        # (§7), foreground_max = [shell] foreground_max (§7.1). The agents row keeps only the hirer's instructions.
        # u_member_joined (quiet, when `by` is not USER) and n_hired carry the canonical role. The tool's guard (a
        # new role needs instructions) is in `hire_agent` (§12), not here: the starting team and programmatic hires
        # need none. An LLM hire beyond max_agents (agent_count()) is a ToolError: "The swarm already has the
        # maximum of N AI agents (members who joined through MCP do not count). Retire someone or ask the user to
        # raise max_agents."; external members are not limited. After the member is created and before n_hired:
        # skills.ensure_role_skills([name]) (its role's skills, §19; the other members are told, not the new one,
        # whose first wake-up lists them), the report kept for `hire_agent` (skills.note_hire / hire_report)
        # In a thread session (§22.3, §22.4, §22.6): `_create_member` (shared with the first start()'s starting team, §3
        # start) uses roles.find_role(..., mode="thread") and system_prompt(..., mode="thread") and calls
        # forum.auto_subscribe(name) (feed, reactions, posts 1 and 2, all digest, for every kind of member); hire then
        # sends n_hired_thread (no recheck_goal: a hire never meets the rule, §22.4)
    async def retire(self, by: str, name: str, reason: str = "") -> list[int]   # returns released task ids
        # before the first await: the ids of its running jobs, and jobs.forbid(name) (none of its commands may
        # become a job while it leaves); then tasks and locks released (workspace.release_all: its own lock waits are
        # dropped, the members waiting for its locks woken, §7 "Lock waiters"), triggers deactivated, status retired,
        # `agent.retired` {name, reason, released, jobs}, its pending question dropped (`_drop_question(by, "left")`,
        # §3.1), n_member_retired; in a thread session also forum.drop_subscriptions(name) with the triggers'
        # deactivation (every row, the feed one too, §22.3) and forum.recheck_goal(None) after n_member_retired_thread
        # (§22.4); then its runtime stops; last
        # jobs.stop_owner(name, "retired"): its jobs and its foreground commands (an external member's call in
        # flight) are killed and awaited, committed under its name, with no notice to it; then its held new files
        # (workspace.commit_held(name, "when <name> left the team", leaving=True): it is no suspect any more, §7
        # "Held new files")

    # budget / control
    def limits(self) -> dict                             # {"max_cost_usd", "max_agents"}
    def set_limits(self, actor: str, max_cost_usd: float | None = None, max_agents: int | None = None) -> dict
    def spent_usd(self) -> float
    def record_usage(self, agent: str, usage: Usage, profile: ModelProfile, model: str | None = None) -> float
        # adds cost_of(...) to the agent; a call that counted tokens as $0 (uncounted_fields, §10) gives USER the quiet
        # u_cost_unknown {profile, model, fields} once per start() for each (profile, provider, base_url, model,
        # fields), plus a log warning (the set `_cost_warned` lives in memory and start() clears it).
        # Then the money notice: limit = limits()["max_cost_usd"], at = `float(config.swarm.budget_notice_at or 0)`
        # (read at each call, §17.1), spent = `spent_usd()`; when limit > 0, 0 < at < 1, spent >= at × limit − 1e-9,
        # spent < limit and kv `budget_notice` does not hold this {limit, at} (only those two fields are compared):
        # kv `budget_notice` {limit, at, spent, ts} is written, then every LLM member (not retired, not external)
        # gets `n_budget_low` {spent, limit, pct}, waking (`wake=True`) for a member that works or has open tasks,
        # reviews waiting for it or news pending, quiet for an idle one with none of those, and USER gets the quiet
        # `u_budget_low` {spent, limit, pct}; pct = min(round(100 × spent / limit), 99) (no format spec in the texts,
        # §17.1). At or past the limit nothing is recorded: `u_budget` covers it, so a call that jumps past the limit
        # gives no low notice, and a raised limit gives it at the next call that finds spent past the new threshold.
        # A new limit (set_limits, a settings change, reconfigure) or a new fraction differs from the kv record and
        # so re-arms the notice, with no hook; the same limit set again does not
        # In a thread session (§22.7) the notice is `n_budget_low_thread`; the task and review terms are empty there
    def budget_exceeded(self) -> bool
    paused: bool; pause_reason: str
    def pause(self, actor: str, reason: str, **details) -> bool
        # False (a no-op) when already paused; `details` go into kv `paused` and the `swarm.paused` data (reason
        # "question": asker, message_id, since; §3.1)
    def _set_pause(self, actor: str, reason: str, *, outcome: dict | None = None, **details) -> None
        # writes the pause slot even while paused (a question pause turned into a budget pause: `outcome` is then the
        # event's `question` data); USER gets the quiet u_budget (reason "budget") or u_question (reason "question");
        # a fresh pause (not paused before) with the user's reason, "paused by the user" (a swarm.py constant beside
        # QUESTION, which `swarm_control` passes, §12), while jobs run (`jobs.running_of()`) gives USER the quiet
        # u_paused_jobs {jobs: "j3 (Anna Smith: npm run dev, 25 min); ...", built like u_jobs_running}: "Background
        # jobs of the agents are not paused with the swarm: {jobs}. A pause stops only the agents' model calls; the
        # jobs run until you stop them or the session stops: use the Jobs tab on the board or /jobs stop <id> in the
        # terminal." (ru alike: «Процессы», no identifier in backticks, test_background_job_texts). None for a
        # budget or question pause (u_budget / u_question cover them, and a `stop_when_done` session stops its jobs
        # right after a budget pause, §21.4), nor for a question pause turned into a budget pause
    def resume(self, actor: str, *, question: dict | None = None) -> None
        # n_resumed to LLM agents with open tasks, reviews waiting for them, pending events or an activation the
        # pause cut short (runtime.interrupted); a reply owed to the user by that activation is still forwarded.
        # No-op when not paused; ToolError while the budget is exhausted. `question`: the `swarm.resumed` data of the
        # question this resume ends (§3.1); a resume without it while a question is pending drops that question
        # (outcome "dropped", why "resumed"): its asker gets a waking n_question_unanswered instead of n_resumed.
        # A pause is no planning or decision time: the pause's length (`_paused_at`, in memory, so a pause that began
        # before a restart is not counted) moves on the planning hint's clock (scheduler item 4), every
        # `_considering` start (`_nudge_idle`'s decision window; an offer made during the pause counts from the resume)
        # and every free-place clock (`_crew_gaps`, scheduler item 8: a crew task's state does not age while paused);
        # it drops the team-asleep clock (`_team_asleep` = None, scheduler item 9: its `n_resumed` wakes the holders)
        # In a thread session (§22.3, §22.7) it also sets `_digest_floor` to now and drops `_thread_quiet` and
        # `_thread_quiet_woken`; a member whose only news is digest items gets no n_resumed: the digest batch wakes it
    def pending_question(self) -> dict | None            # {asker, message_id, since} of the question holding the
                                                         # pause (kv `paused` with reason "question"), else None
    def last_message_id(self, sender: str, recipient: str, since: float = 0.0) -> int | None
        # the newest message of `sender` that reached `recipient` (its inbox row: named or through "all"), sent at
        # `since` (a timestamp) or later; None when none did (the public form of the `_LAST_TO` query, §21.5)
    def pause_text(self) -> str                          # "waiting for the user's answer to X's question #N" for a
                                                         # question, else the reason (swarm_status, traces)
    def ask_user(self, asker: str, message: dict) -> tuple[str, dict]
        # send_message(pause_swarm=true) after `message` was stored: the outcome (asked, user, no_user, off, auto,
        # pending, own, paused, budget; §3.1) and the details of its result note; synchronous
    def question_answered(self, message: dict, question: dict) -> None
        # Mailbox.send's hook (§5): the user's `message` answers `question`; tells the others, then resumes (or turns
        # the pause into a budget pause); never raises
    def asks_user(self, name: str, task: Task | None = None) -> bool  # the clarify planner waits for the user's
                                                         # answers (§3.1); in a thread session the kickoff asker
                                                         # of a clarify #2, task None (§22.4 "Clarify")
    clarifying: bool                                     # [swarm] clarify and no auto-reply lease (§3.1)
    def hold_auto_reply(self) -> None                    # the lease for this object's whole life (§3.1, §21.5)
    wrapping_up: bool                                    # the user's wrap-up mode (kv "wrap_up" {"on", "by", "since"})
    def wrap_up(self, actor: str) -> bool
        # wrap-up mode on (False when it was on already): the team finishes with what it has. Emits `swarm.wrap_up`
        # {on: true} and notifies every LLM member once, waking it: `n_wrap_up` (start no new computations or
        # background jobs, not even one more quick pass; task_complete with the result so far and what is left; do
        # the reviews waiting for you; stop the jobs nobody needs; when every task is finished the goal is completed
        # with what was achieved and what is left, without new tasks). While on: every wake-up carries
        # `wrap_up_line` (§6.3), no command of a member becomes a new job (§7.1 "Wrap-up mode"), `_check_all_done`
        # sends `n_all_done_wrap_up` (goal_complete, no new tasks) instead of `n_all_done`. Nothing is paused; the
        # user's own actions are not restricted. A thread session (§22.4, §22.7): `n_wrap_up_thread` and
        # `wrap_up_line_thread`; a like on #1 then means "finish with what we have"; no `_check_all_done`
    def end_wrap_up(self, actor: str, clear_votes: bool = True) -> bool
        # off (False when it was not on): `swarm.wrap_up` {on: false} and a quiet `n_wrap_up_end` to every LLM member
        # (shown at its next wake-up); called by the user (swarm_control wrap_up=false), set_goal and reopen_goal
        # (these two pass clear_votes=False: they reset the votes on #1 themselves); a thread session: §22.4
    def make_llm(self, profile_name: str | None, agent: str) -> LLMClient
        # a member's profile (agents.model) that no longer exists in the settings (deleted, or renamed by a hand edit
        # of dreamteam.toml) falls back to the default profile with a warning, instead of crashing that agent at every
        # activation
    def rename_profiles(self, renames: dict[str, str]) -> None
        # {old: new} profile names (settings.profile_renames): agents.model of every member (retired ones too) and
        # the runtimes' profile_name follow, in one statement (db.remap_sql: a swap or a chain of names stays
        # correct); no client is reset here (the reconfigure that update_settings runs next rebuilds them);
        # u_cost_unknown already sent for the old name is not repeated (under either name)
    def snapshot(self) -> dict                           # §14.1
    def workspace_info(self) -> dict                     # {"path", "default", "adopted", "exists"} (§14.1, §17.2)
```

Tests use `tests/conftest.py::FakeSwarm`, which implements the subset: `config, db, bus, language,
member, members, is_member, kind_of, resolve_member, language_of, notify, signal, has_pending,
board, mail, workspace, triggers, goal, set_goal, complete_goal` (attributes may be None until a test
wires them), and records notifications in `fake.notified: list[tuple[recipient, key, kw]]`. Its
resolve_member is the real `resolve_member_in`; set_goal / complete_goal validate, split the goal and notify
like the real ones (complete_goal takes `decision=` and an actor of None too; the planning task is created when a
real Board is wired: `prompts.planning_task(language,
config.swarm.clarify)` with its tags, §3.1). It has no `pending_question`, `ask_user`, `asks_user` or `pause_text`:
their callers (Mailbox.send, send_message, the in-activation nudge, `_stop_reason`) look them up with getattr, so
with FakeSwarm a message never answers or pauses anything. Nor has it `team_asleep` or `stall_ids` (and its
`triggers` is None): `wait` (§12) looks them up with getattr and gives the plain result.

Scheduler (every 3 s): expires file locks, then settles the lock waiters (`workspace.settle_waiters()`, §7 "Lock
waiters": a member refused a path that is free now is woken, a long holder told; also while paused, the
notifications then wait for the resume), compares the skills mirror with its manifest (`skills.check()`, at most
every `SKILLS_CHECK_SECONDS` = 60 s, §19), prunes old traces (every 6 h) and closes idle external trace
sessions (§16); unless paused, `_wake_deferred` first (an agent a broadcast reached without a wake, §5, that no longer
`waits_for_job` while the news is still unread is woken once: e.g. the busy window of its server ended), then in this
order. "Idle" (`_idle_llm_members`) is an LLM agent with status idle, a
runtime, nothing pending and not busy with a job (`JobManager.busy`, §7.1 "Liveness"):
1. `_nudge_idle`: offers ready unassigned tasks to idle LLM agents (`n_ready`), never more agents considering
   offers than there are ready tasks, and the kickoff counts as everyone's offer of the planning task; with
   independent review on, a member with reviews waiting for it is not offered more work (it is reminded of them
   instead); the free directions of crew tasks are ready tasks like any other (§4.2), except that a member is never
   offered the directions of a crew task it works on a direction of (`Board.busy_crews`); a ready task is offered to
   each member once while it stays ready with the same finish state (`_nudged` is keyed by the pair (task id,
   finish state), §4.2 "Offers"), so a parent without an assignee whose subtasks have all just finished is offered
   again to every idle member, those that took its subtasks included;
2. `_wake_stalled`: wakes once (`n_stalled`) an idle agent whose activation ended with plain text while holding
   in_progress tasks even after the nudge (§6.2);
3. `_wake_idle_holders`: an idle agent holding in_progress tasks (e.g. after `wait` with nothing that will wake
   it) is woken once per such set of tasks with `n_stalled`, once it has been idle with that set for
   `agents.idle_nudge_seconds` (the clock starts when it was first seen idle with that set, or at its
   `last_active` when that is later: an activation in between restarts it); the woken sets are shared with
   `_wake_stalled`, so a set is never woken about twice. Neither 2 nor 3 wakes an agent while the end of one of
   its running jobs will wake it (`JobManager.awaited`, what its `wait` result promised): it waits for that job
   (a `detached` one, or a `background` one past its busy window), it has not stalled; nor while it waits for a
   file it was refused (`Workspace.waits_for_lock`: a `lock_waiters` row, what the refusal promised; `n_lock_free`
   wakes it, and every lock ends by unlock, expiry or retire). Nor do they count a clarify
   planning task whose holder waits for the user's answers (`asks_user`, §3.1), nor a crew task with a direction
   that can still move (§4.2; `Board.has_live_directions`: one in review; one `in_progress` or `waiting` that does
   not wait for a held-back direction, through its `depends_on` that are not done or its open subtasks,
   transitively (held back: a `todo` direction whose assignee, a member, may not take it now, since it works on
   another direction of the crew task or the working set is full without it; it moves only when a working
   direction is handed in, so a crew task whose working directions all wait for one never moves); or a `todo`
   one, not held back, none of whose blockers is stuck while the crew task itself is not blocked by a stuck task;
   stuck: `failed` or `cancelled`, or `todo` while blocked by a stuck task in turn (a direction also while its
   crew task is), or while its blockers lead back to it or to the crew task, or a working direction that waits
   for a held-back one, or a held-back one once every working direction waits for one; the check is iterative, so a chain of any length is fine) among their ids: while each of
   them has an assignee it
   waits for them, so its owner has nothing to continue there (its own direction counts on its own; the
   in-activation nudge of §6.2 skips such a crew task too), and a free one is the "free directions" mark below. A
   crew task whose open directions all wait, directly or through other todo tasks, for a failed or cancelled task,
   or that is blocked by such a chain itself, is among the ids: nothing else would move it, and its completion
   refusal names the blockers (§4.2 "Finishing"). Both items also count
   three marks, compared apart from the task ids (§4.2 "Finishing", Liveness): a task `todo` (not blocked),
   `in_progress` or `waiting` that has at least one subtask, all of them terminal (its holder has to complete it, or, for a crew task
   with a failed direction or only cancelled ones, decide what to do), a `todo` direction assigned to the member
   that its claim would take now, and a crew task with a free direction that its owner, working on none of its
   directions, could take (§4.2 "Offers"). Items 2 and 3 compute the same key, so a set is
   woken about once; item 3's idle clock is keyed by the same pair, so a mark that appears on an unchanged set of
   ids waits the full `idle_nudge_seconds` again;
4. `hint_planner()` (planning hint; run 008-013: a planner researched for 40 minutes before creating any task while
   the team idled): an LLM member holding a task tagged `planning` in `in_progress` that has created no task (no
   task with `created_by` = it and an id above the planning task's) gets `n_planning_hint` {id, steps, elapsed} once
   it has made `agents.planning_hint_steps` (default 8) LLM steps (`AgentRuntime.llm_steps`) or
   `agents.planning_hint_minutes` (default 10) have passed since the swarm first saw it holding the task (a claim,
   another holder, or a restart starts the count again; a pause stops the clock: `resume` moves its start on by the
   pause's length); once more at twice either value, and only after at least one step since the first hint; never a
   third time for that member and task (the hints it already had, `n_planning_hint` and `n_clarify_hint` below, are
   counted from the notifications table when the count starts, so neither a re-claim nor a restart brings more),
   never with fewer than two members, never while the goal is not active, the swarm is paused or in wrap-up mode
   (`wrapping_up`), never while the holder of a clarify card waits for the user's answers (`asks_user`, §3.1: the
   watch is dropped on every pass, the scheduler's and the planner's own `hint_planner(name)`, so its clock starts
   again after the answer); 0 turns a trigger off. While `[swarm] clarify` is on, the holder of a clarify card that
   has not messaged the user since the card was created (it is still finding the forks) gets `n_clarify_hint` {id,
   steps, elapsed} in its place, with the same watch and triggers: if the goal has forks, send the user all the
   questions in one message now, then the task `waiting` and `wait`, no task before the answer; with nothing to
   ask, plan now with `task_create`. So the clarify planner is never told to create tasks before its questions. The
   two kinds share the count (two hints at most in all), and once the planner has asked, its later hint is
   `n_planning_hint`. The agent
   also calls `swarm.hint_planner(name)` after the tools of each step (§6.2), so the step trigger lands in that
   activation's `incoming`; the scheduler pass catches the time trigger
   and a holder that went idle (the notification wakes it). No hard limit: the planner may go on researching;
   `_planning_watch` (in memory) holds the counts and forgets tasks nobody holds;
5. `_remind_reviewers` (independent review only): review reminder and hand-over (§4.1 "Liveness");
6. `_check_all_done`: sends `n_all_done` to one idle agent when every task is finished but the goal is open
   (`review` is an open status, so it waits for every review); not while any LLM member works or is busy with a
   job (with no open task only a `timeout` job can make it busy: its command may still change the result); once
   per board state, the key `(task count, MAX(tasks.updated_at))` kept in `_all_done_key` (item 9 reads it);
7. `_remind_user_reviews` (both modes): `u_reviews_waiting` when only the user's reviews keep the swarm going
   (§4.1 "Liveness");
8. `_tell_crew_gaps` (§4.2 "A free place"; run of 2026-11-13: for hours one member worked on the last direction of
   a crew task while a place was free and three members idled, its owner among them, and nothing told the owner):
   the owner of a crew task that has a free place, a direction in `in_progress` or `waiting` and none a member may
   take now (`Board.crew_gaps()`), while other members are idle with no task of their own to go on with, gets
   `n_crew_gap` once the crew task has been in that state with the same open and named directions for
   `CREW_GAP_FACTOR` (10) × `agents.idle_nudge_seconds`, and only while the owner is idle itself; once per such
   state, at most `CREW_GAP_MAX` (2) times per owner and crew task (counted from the notifications table, so a
   restart does not reset the count); never while the goal is not active or in wrap-up mode (`wrapping_up`; the
   clocks start again afterwards; a pause stops them: `resume` moves them on by its length). It runs after items
   1-7, in the code too: it reads the offers item 1 made in the same pass (`_nudged`), and a member that items 1-7
   woke has news pending, so it is not idle. It wakes nobody but that owner;
9. `_wake_team_asleep` (§4.2 "Notifications": `n_team_asleep`, `u_team_asleep`, `u_team_waits`): the whole team
   sleeps while work is open and nothing set will wake the team: a member waits, after item 3's one wake, for a
   process the hub does not track (`jobs` does not list it: on macOS one that left its command's process group, on
   Linux one that also cleared its environment, §7 "Process layer"), members wait for each other, or a member
   waits for the user's answer to a plain message. It runs last, after item 8, in the code too: a member that
   items 1-8 or `_wake_deferred` woke in the same pass has news pending, so it is not idle.
   - *When* (in item 9 an open task is one in `todo`, `in_progress` or `waiting`, not `Status.OPEN`: `review` is
     apart, the review condition below handles it; *Whom* and `u_team_waits` read "open" the same way): in a pass,
     all of these hold: the goal is active (wrap-up mode included); the board has an open task, or no open task,
     every task terminal, and item 6 has already spoken for this board state (`_all_done_key` equals the key
     below); an empty board gives nothing; no task is in review whose review item 5 still works on (independent
     review on and the reviewer an LLM member: item 5 reminds it and hands it over); a review held by USER or an
     external member, or any review while independent review is off, does not count, but item 7's state stands
     item 9 down (USER's reviews wait, `not self._has_task_in_progress() and not self._has_actionable_todo()`: item
     7 tells the user, nothing else is left); no clarify planner waits for the user's answers (`asks_user` on an
     open planning card of an LLM member, §3.1); and `team_asleep()` (above: every LLM member idle or in error with
     no recovery, nothing of theirs awaited, no delayed notice, no unattended trigger, no recent external call).
   - *Clock*: the key is item 6's, `(task count, MAX(tasks.updated_at))` (a claim or a status change makes a new
     one, a comment does not). `_team_asleep` (key, since), in memory: `since` is when a pass first saw the
     conditions hold with that key, raised to the latest `last_active` of the idle LLM members (not of those in
     error: a failing retry does not restart it); a pass where the conditions fail, or the goal is not active,
     drops it; a changed key starts a new clock; `resume()` drops it (§3 `resume`).
   - *Due* when `now - since >= TEAM_ASLEEP_FACTOR * 2 ** min(sent, TEAM_ASLEEP_DOUBLINGS) * idle_nudge_seconds`
     (`agents.idle_nudge_seconds`) and `per_key < TEAM_ASLEEP_MAX`. `sent` = the `n_team_asleep` notifications under
     the current goal (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notifications WHERE kind = 'n_team_asleep' AND ts >=
     goal.updated_at`: a restart keeps it, a new or reopened goal starts again); `per_key` = those sent since the
     key was first seen (`_team_asleep_woken` (key, count), in memory). Module constants, monkeypatchable:
     `TEAM_ASLEEP_FACTOR` = 5, `TEAM_ASLEEP_DOUBLINGS` = 5, `TEAM_ASLEEP_MAX` = 2; with the default 60 s the wakes
     come after 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 160… minutes, at most 2 per board state, so a member that changes a task's
     status at every wake still waits twice as long each time. With `idle_nudge_seconds` = 0 the delay is 0 and
     the doubling does nothing (as items 2-3 and 8 have no delay then): item 9 is due at the first pass that finds
     the team asleep, still at most 2 per board state, so a member that changes a task's status at every wake is
     woken again at almost every pass (3 s) for as long as it does so, or until the budget pauses the swarm.
   - *Whom*: among the idle LLM members (not those in error), the one active last (`last_active`) of the first
     group that has one: 1. holding an `in_progress` or `waiting` task; 2. holding a `todo` task; 3. any idle
     member, when an open task has no assignee, or no open task is left (item 6's state). It gets the waking
     `n_team_asleep` {elapsed, jobs}; `per_key` is recorded right after that notify succeeds. Then, in its own
     try/except with a log line, USER gets `u_team_asleep` {elapsed, name} with the first wake of each key, waking
     (`wake=True`, as `u_reviews_waiting`: a user MCP client in `wait_for_events` is told). When no LLM member
     holds an open task and every open task has an assignee (USER or an external member), no member is woken: USER
     gets the waking `u_team_waits` {elapsed, tasks: "#3, #5"} once for that board state (`per_key` is set to the
     cap at once; `sent` is not touched). `elapsed` = `fmt_duration(now - since)` in the recipient's language;
     `jobs` = "" or `team_asleep_jobs` {jobs} naming the member's running jobs whose end is quiet
     (`jobs.running_of(name)` minus `jobs.awaited(name)`, labels `j3, j5`).
   - *Texts* (en; ru alike, the same placeholders and backticked identifiers; in ru such an untracked process is
     «процесс, запущенный через & или nohup, которого нет в списке `jobs`», never «фоновый процесс», which is a
     job; no text puts & or nohup in backticks, which the identifier tests would refuse): `n_team_asleep`
     ``Nobody in the team has worked for {elapsed}, and nothing is set to wake the team: no running background job
     whose end wakes its owner, no trigger that can still fire on a time or a file, no locked file someone was
     refused.{jobs} A process started with & or nohup that `jobs` does not list is not tracked: its end wakes
     nobody. If you are waiting for one, check it now; if it still runs, set a trigger with a deadline before you
     `wait` (`trigger_create`, e.g. file_exists("out/result.json") or elapsed(1800)), and start the next such run
     with background=true, without & and nohup. If you are waiting for the user's answer, don't ask again: the
     user was told. If you are waiting for another member, ask in the task's discussion: a post wakes them.
     Otherwise go on with your tasks, or finish them, or set them back to `todo` (or `failed`) with a comment; when
     every task is finished, verify the result and call `goal_complete`; if you hold none, look at the `board` for
     open tasks nobody moves.``; `team_asleep_jobs` ` Your background jobs {jobs} still run, but their end will not
     wake you while you hold no task in progress.` (ru «фоновые процессы»); `u_team_asleep` `Nobody in the team
     has worked for {elapsed}, and nothing is set to wake the team: no background job whose end wakes its owner, no
     trigger that fires on a time or a file. {name} was woken to check their work. If the team waits for you (an
     answer, a review, a decision, access), write to the member who asked; to end the run, stop the session.`;
     `u_team_waits` `Nobody in the team has worked for {elapsed}: the open tasks {tasks} are held by you or by
     members who joined through MCP, and nothing is set to wake the team. Do them or hand them to the team; to end
     the run, stop the session.` The member's texts name only tools every open revision has (§12 R0′).
   - *Limits accepted*: a job whose end wakes its owner (`JobManager.awaited`: a `background` server past its busy
     window counts until `[shell] job_max_minutes`, 480 min by default; 0: as long as it runs) and a wait for a
     refused file (until the lock ends: unlock, expiry after `[workspace] lock_ttl_minutes`, at most 24 h, or
     retire) keep item 9 silent however long they last; a trigger that reads only files counts for
     `UNATTENDED_FILE_SECONDS` (§8). Open tasks held only by LLM members in error with no recovery scheduled, none
     without an assignee, wake nobody and send no `u_team_waits`: USER was told of the error (`u_agent_error`). No
     external member is ever woken (no scheduler item wakes one), and a `dreamteam -p` run still waits, until its
     `--timeout` when one is given, with the user's notice on stderr (docs/TUI.md §2).

In a thread-mode session (§22) items 1-9 do not run: §22.7 replaces them with digest batching (`_deliver_digests`)
and the quiet check (`_check_quiet`); the steps before item 1, `_wake_deferred` included, run in both modes.

`reconfigure()` applies new settings to a running swarm, lifts a budget pause the new budget allows and retries
agents in ERROR; a changed role catalog (§17.3), `[swarm] independent_review` and `crew_review` apply at once (new
hires use the new catalog; existing members keep their frozen prompts); `[swarm] clarify` switched off lifts a
question pause and tells a clarify planner that waits for the user (§3.1). The money notice needs no hook: a new
`max_cost_usd` or `[swarm] budget_notice_at` no longer matches kv `budget_notice`, so the next `record_usage` past the
new threshold sends it again (§3 `record_usage`); `agents.idle_nudge_seconds` reaches item 9's delay (in a thread
session the quiet check's, and `agents.digest_seconds` digest batching, §22.7) at the next pass. In a thread session
a changed `[swarm] goal_rule` (frozen per session, §22.4) runs `_goal_rule_changed()`: #1's text names the new rule
and `forum.recheck_goal(None)` may complete the goal.

### 3.1 Clarify mode and questions that pause the swarm

One session option, `[swarm] clarify` (bool, default false, §17.1), read live (`config.swarm.clarify`: a session
override or a PATCH reaches it through `reconfigure`), turns on two things: the planner asks the user first, and a
member's critical question pauses the whole swarm until the user answers. **Effective clarify** is
`Swarm.clarifying` = `config.swarm.clarify and not auto_reply_active` (the lease below: `dreamteam -p` with automatic
replies works as before); `set_goal`, `ask_user` (its own outcome `auto`) and the `swarm_status` CLARIFY line use it.
A thread session has no clarify card: the decision is a flag on system post #2, its kickoff wakes one asker, and
every guard below that names the card's holder means that asker (§22.4 "Clarify").

- **The clarify planning card.** `set_goal` on an empty board with `clarifying` creates
  `prompts.planning_task(language, True)` (`PLANNING_CLARIFY`, tags `["planning", "clarify"]`: `prompts.CLARIFY_TAG`)
  instead of PLANNING_TASK (tags `["planning"]`; `planning_task(language, False)` is PLANNING_TASK itself). It is
  board data like PLANNING_TASK, never the system prompt or a tool schema, so no frozen prefix depends on the option.
  Title «Уточнить цель у пользователя, затем спланировать: …» / "Clarify the goal with the user, then plan: …"; the
  goal starts with a clarify prefix (the user was asked in one message about the forks of the goal, and the task's
  result says what was asked); a head replaces the first line of the classic description, then steps 1-9 follow
  verbatim. The head: find the forks (readings of the goal that change the result or the plan); none → write
  nothing to the user and plan at once; else ONE `send_message` to ["user"] with numbered questions (at most seven),
  each with its options and the default, then the task `waiting` and `wait`; on the answer back to `in_progress`;
  the default where the user leaves a point open or says "decide yourself" («прими решение сам»); the decisions and
  the defaults (as assumptions) into CONTRACTS.md and the task descriptions; the result says what was asked; until
  the answer no task, no CONTRACTS.md, no research (this overrides the system prompt's rule to go on with the work
  that does not depend on the answer). The card is never rewritten: the option switched later changes only the
  next card (a new goal on an empty board).
- **Kickoff.** With a clarify card (its tag decides, not the live option) only the first LLM member gets a waking
  `n_kickoff`; the others get the same notice quietly, so they spend nothing until the first tasks reach them
  (`n_ready`). Only the planner is in `_nudged[(card, None)]` (§3 item 1), and it is put into `_considering` with
  the card: if it never claims, `_nudge_idle` offers the card to the next idle member once the planner is idle
  without it or
  `NUDGE_DECISION_SECONDS` passed. A pause stops that clock (`resume`, §3), so neither a kickoff made during a pause
  (`set_goal` on an empty board while paused) nor a long pause before the claim offers the card (`n_ready`) to the
  quiet members while the planner's first call is in flight (a pause that began before a restart is not counted).
- **Before the questions.** A clarify planner that explores longer than `agents.planning_hint_steps` /
  `planning_hint_minutes` before it has messaged the user gets `n_clarify_hint` (ask now, or plan if there is nothing
  to ask), never the classic `n_planning_hint` that says to create tasks (§3 scheduler item 4).
- **The nag guard** `asks_user(name, task)`: clarify is on, `task` has the tags planning and clarify, `name` has
  created no task since it (an id above the card's), and `name`'s last message to the user since the card was
  created is newer than the user's last message to it (named or through "all"), and that message is no question the
  user went on without (below). Then `_wake_stalled`, `_wake_idle_holders`, `hint_planner` (§3 scheduler) and the
  in-activation nudge (§6.2) leave the planner alone. Both bounds keep an old message (an earlier goal) or a note to
  the user after planning started from silencing the nags for ever; a comment on the task is no message and does
  not count. A question the user went on without is one that a `swarm.resumed` event, or the `swarm.paused` event of
  the budget pause it turned into, carries as `question` with outcome "dropped" (a manual resume, clarify switched
  off; the `autoreply.QUESTION_DROPPED` query, on the events type index, runs only when the guard would hold
  otherwise): its asker was told `n_question_unanswered` (take your defaults), so it waits for nothing, and the
  board's quiet `clarify_wait` banner (§14.1) hides; its next message to the user turns the guard on again. The rule
  past the tags is `autoreply.planner_question(scalar, name, task_id, since)` (the id of the question the planner
  waits on, else None), which the requests to the user read from a session's file too (§21.5), so the guard, the
  banner and the requests cannot drift apart.
- **A question that pauses the swarm.** `send_message` has the optional boolean `pause_swarm`. The message is always
  stored first; then `ask_user(asker, message)` pauses only after these checks, in this
  order, each giving its outcome and result note (§12): `user` (the sender is the user), `no_user` ("user" is not a
  recipient), `off` (`[swarm] clarify` is off), `auto` (the auto-reply lease), `own` / `pending` (a question is
  pending already: one at a time), `paused` (paused for another reason, which stays), `budget` (spent), else
  `asked`: `pause(asker, "question", asker=, message_id=, since=)`. Every outcome but `asked` leaves an ordinary
  message. AI agents and external MCP members can pause. There is no cap per member.
  - State: the question lives only in kv `paused` (`{"paused": true, "reason": "question", "asker", "message_id",
    "since"}`); `pending_question()` reads it. Every exit rewrites that one slot, so a stale question never captures
    a later message. `swarm.paused` {reason: "question", asker, message_id, since}, actor the asker; USER gets the
    quiet `u_question` {name, id}.
  - It pauses like any pause (§6.2): an LLM call in flight and all tool calls of its response finish, the next step
    breaks, a woken agent goes to `paused`, the scheduler skips its passes; jobs, triggers and external members go
    on (unlike the user's own pause, it sends USER no `u_paused_jobs`: `u_question` covers it, §3 `_set_pause`). The
    asker reads its result only after the resume, together with the answer.
- **The answer rule.** While `pending_question()` is {asker A, message_id Q}, the **first** message from USER (any
  surface: the board's chat, the TUI, the console, MCP) whose resolved recipients include A (named, or through
  "all") is the answer; `reply_to` alone does not count. `Mailbox.send` (§5) fills `reply_to = Q` when it has none (A
  sees "(reply to #Q)"), stores and signals, then calls `question_answered`: every other active member gets
  `n_user_answer` {asker, id, question, answer} (both texts cut to `QUESTION_CHARS` = 4000), or
  `n_user_answer_seen` {asker, id, question, answer_id} when the answer reached it as a message too; quiet for AI
  agents, waking for external members. Then `resume(USER, question={asker, message_id, outcome: "answered",
  answer_id})`: its usual `n_resumed` wakes the members with work (A among them: the answer is unread). No answer: a
  user message only to other members (they read it after the resume), task comments, `task_review`, `set_goal`,
  anything after the pause ended, and a message of a user-owned trigger (`Mailbox.send(..., automatic=True)`). The
  user's `send_message` result then ends with the A-ok or A-budget note (§12).
- **Lifecycle** (A the asker, Q the question):

  | situation | what happens |
  |---|---|
  | the answer arrives with the budget spent (steps in flight crossed it) | the notices as above, then `_set_pause(USER, "budget", outcome=…)`: a budget pause, `swarm.paused` {reason: "budget", question: {asker, message_id, outcome: "answered", answer_id}} and `u_budget`; raising the limit resumes it as any budget pause |
  | a manual resume (the board's «Продолжить», `/pause` in the TUI, `/resume` in the console, `swarm_control` action=resume) | the question is dropped: `swarm.resumed` {question: {asker, message_id, outcome: "dropped", why: "resumed"}}; A gets a waking `n_question_unanswered` {id} (take your defaults, write them down) instead of `n_resumed`; a later user message to A is ordinary; when A holds a clarify card, the nag guard no longer waits for Q (`asks_user` false, no `clarify_wait` banner) until A messages the user again |
  | `swarm_control` action=pause meanwhile | nothing changes: `Done: already paused (waiting for the user's answer to A's question #Q).` |
  | `[swarm] clarify` switched off (PATCH, ⚙, `/clarify off`, the global settings) | `reconfigure` → `_clarify_switched_off()`: the holder of a clarify card that has created no task since it (`_plans`, the bound the nag guard uses) and whose card is `waiting` (also after a reply that answered nothing) or `asks_user` gets a waking `n_clarify_off` {task_id} (plan now with your defaults); a holder that created a task plans already, so its `waiting` card waits for something else (research, a follow-up question): it gets none, and its tasks' events or the user's answer wake it; then `_drop_question(USER, "clarify_off")` resumes (why `clarify_off`) or, with the budget spent, turns it into a budget pause; A gets `n_question_unanswered` either way |
  | clarify off while the session was stopped | the end of `start()` runs `_clarify_switched_off(once=True)`: the same, with at most one `n_clarify_off` per card |
  | clarify switched on later | nothing is rewritten: `pause_swarm` works from its next call, the next card is the clarify one |
  | A retires or leaves | `retire` → `_drop_question(by, "left")` (why `left`, no notice to A); USER gets `u_question_left` {name, id} unless USER retired it |
  | a session restart | kv persists: still paused for the question, and `start()` sends no kickoff and no `n_restart`, as for any pause (the resume's `n_resumed` covers them); the answer and a manual resume work as before; the lease is lost |
  | `set_goal` / `reopen_goal` meanwhile | the pause stays until it is answered or resumed |
  | wrap-up mode | independent: both can be on |
  | an external member asks (`hub_call` with `as_agent`) | as an agent; its result says to call `wait_for_events`, where the answer comes; it is not paused itself |
  | the user acts through MCP | `send_message` as USER answers through the same choke point, `swarm_control` resume drops, `wait_for_events` returns `u_question`, `sessions_list` shows the question (§18.2) |

- **The auto-reply lease.** The print client (`dreamteam -p`, docs/TUI.md §2) sends the header
  `X-DreamTeam-Auto-Reply: 1` (`models.AUTO_REPLY_HEADER`, while `HubClient.auto_reply`) on every request and on
  the WebSocket handshake, only with automatic replies on. The Swarm keeps an in-memory lease:
  `auto_reply_stream()` (a context manager around an event WebSocket whose handshake carried the header),
  `auto_reply_seen()` (the launcher's `POST /api/sessions` and `/start` before `swarm.start()` and again right
  before the pending `set_goal`; `POST /api/act/{tool}`), `hold_auto_reply()` (the hub answers for the user itself:
  a session of the HTTP API v1 with `answers: "auto"`, §21.5; `_start_locked` takes it before `swarm.start()` on
  every start path, and it holds until the Swarm is unloaded) and `auto_reply_active`: held, a stream is open, or
  less than `AUTO_REPLY_GRACE` (90 s, longer than print mode's 60 s without the hub) passed since the last sign (the
  clock is the module's `_monotonic`). Nothing is persisted: a hub or session restart forgets it, a dead client's
  lease ends 90 s after its socket closed. Under the lease `clarifying` is false (the classic card) and `ask_user`
  gives `auto`
  ("the user is not available"). A gap in the lease (a hub restart, a session reload) can still give a short
  question pause, which print mode answers at once (an answer that failed is sent again after a state read that
  still shows the pause, never twice for one question: docs/TUI.md §2).
- **No stuck states.** A question pause ends with an answer (every surface can send one), a manual resume, the asker
  leaving, or clarify switched off (live or at start); after a conversion the budget auto-resume takes over.
  `resume` is idempotent, and the hook acts only while `pending_question()` still equals the question it read.
  `question_answered` checks the budget before it resumes and logs every failure: the user's message, stored
  already, never fails. The nag guard counts only messages since the card, ends once the holder created a task, and
  ignores a question the user went on without; `n_clarify_off` goes only to a holder that has created no task.
