    owner form prefix `All its directions were cancelled: `);
  - otherwise (at least one is `done`), the **all finished** ending: `check that they fit together, write #N's
    result from theirs (what each one delivered and where, and what was left out) and complete it
    (task_complete).` (creator form: `take #N (task_claim), check that they fit together, …`; owner form prefix
    `All its directions are finished: `).
  The plain ending's owner form has the prefix `All its subtasks are finished: `.
  The **draft** of #N's result follows the all finished ending, in the holder's form and in its owner form, in
  every text that asks the owner, or whoever takes #N, to write #N's result: `n_subtasks_done` to the holder, the
  result of the owner's own call that finished the last direction, the result of the call that makes the actor the
  holder (a claim of an ownerless crew task, or a `task_update` that does it, "The owner"; the owner sentence),
  `n_crew_owner` (whose `directions` is then "": the draft lists them) and the "subtasks done" mark (Liveness,
  below). The owner still writes the result itself; the draft is what it assembles it from. The draft is a line
  break and `crew_draft` {id, items}: `Draft for #{id}'s result: its directions in the order they were created,
  with the results of the done ones:` then a line break and `{items}`. The board renders it
  (`Board._crew_draft(task, lang)`) in the recipient's language as a part of `ending` or `instructions`, like
  `counts`, so the keys keep their placeholders and no notification key is added; the ru twins of `crew_draft`,
  `crew_draft_cut`, `crew_draft_more` and `crew_draft_no_result` live in prompts.py like the other crew texts.
  The creator form has no draft (the creator is asked to take #N, and its claim's result gives the draft).
  `n_review_rejected` has none either: the owner wrote #N's result itself, and the reviewer's comment is in #N's
  discussion. After a return or the creator's reopening, the texts above that ask for #N's result again
  (`n_subtasks_done` when the new directions finish, the owner sentence of whoever takes #N, `n_crew_owner` to the
  holder the reopening keeps or makes) carry the draft of all its directions, the earlier ones included, in
  creation order.
  - Items: every direction of #N (`subtasks_of`, id ascending: the order they were created in), one line each,
    `- #15 [done] "pkce" @Anna Smith` (the title cut like `fmt.trim(title, 80)` and quoted in the recipient's
    language, ru `«pkce»`, as in the owner sentence's list and the "free directions" mark; ` @holder`, the
    direction's assignee, left out when it has none). The line of a `done` direction is followed by its result, its
    line
    breaks kept and every line indented by four spaces; an empty one (USER set the direction `done`) reads
    `crew_draft_no_result` `(no result)`. A `cancelled` or `failed` direction has its line and no result (in
    practice only `cancelled` ones: a `failed` direction gives the `failed` finish state, whose ending asks for no
    result).
  - Cuts: one budget B = `min(CREW_DRAFT_CHARS, agents.tool_output_chars // 2)` (board.py `CREW_DRAFT_CHARS` =
    8000; the setting read at each render) bounds everything the draft adds: its leading line break, the
    `crew_draft` header, the item lines, the result pieces and `crew_draft_more`, each with its line breaks. So a
    draft appended to a tool result leaves room for the rest of it and is not cut in the middle by the runtime,
    which cuts every tool result for the model to `tool_output_chars` (12000 by default) with
    `shell.truncate_middle` (`AgentRuntime._run_tools`, §6.2). A done direction's **piece** is its result with
    every line indented by four spaces (indented first, then cut) and, when cut, the indented `crew_draft_cut`
    {id} after it: `(cut: task_get #{id} shows more of it)`. Its **least piece** is the whole indented result when
    that is no longer than the indented `crew_draft_cut` (the indented `crew_draft_no_result` for an empty one),
    else the indented `crew_draft_cut` alone. The board builds the draft in two passes:
    1. Which items: the directions are taken in creation order while the header, their lines, the least pieces of
       the done ones among them and, when not all of them fit, `crew_draft_more` (counted with k = all its
       directions) fit in B. The items stop before the first one that would pass it, and `crew_draft_more` {k, id}
       ends the draft: `… more directions not shown: {k}; task_get #{id} lists them, and task_get on a direction
       shows its result.` (the count after a colon, so neither twin needs plural forms; ru «… ещё не показано
       направлений: {k}; …»). When B holds no item, the draft is the header and `crew_draft_more` (k = all its
       directions); when it cannot hold even those, `crew_draft_more` alone; when not even that, there is no draft
       (the ending still names #N).
    2. The results of the items: what is left of B after the header, the lines and `crew_draft_more` is shared
       among the done ones, the shortest first, each getting the share S = min(`NOTIFY_TEXT_LIMIT`, what is still
       left ÷ the results not yet served, what is still left minus the least pieces of the results served after
       it; the last term matters only when task ids differ in length, which makes the pointers differ by a
       character). A piece that fits in S is the whole result; a longer one is cut with
       `shell.truncate_middle`, as a tool result is (it keeps the start and the end, where a result says what was
       done and what is left; the marker line it adds is not indented), to S minus the indented `crew_draft_cut`
       and minus the marker (`\n... [{skipped} characters skipped] ...\n`, counted with the result's whole length
       as {skipped}), so the piece, marker and pointer included, is at most S. When that would keep less than
       `CREW_DRAFT_MIN` (300) characters of the result, or would still pass S, the piece is its least piece. No piece
       passes 1500 characters (`NOTIFY_TEXT_LIMIT`, the cut of a result in `n_task_closed`, §4). Served shortest
       first, each share is at least the least piece of its result (pass 1 kept room for all of them), so the
       draft never passes B.
  - Reading in full: `task_get` (every member has it: audience LEU, §12) shows a direction's result in its card
    (`fmt.task_detail`: Goal, Description, Result, then Subtasks and the crew line, Required by and the last 5
    posts), and for #N its `Subtasks:` lines. The whole result shows while that card fits in `tool_output_chars`;
    past that, the
    card is cut in the middle like any tool result, and no member tool reads that part of the result. The draft
    shows the directions as they are when the text is built.
  The owner completes the crew task (`task_complete`, its `result` the one it wrote). What follows depends on
  `[swarm] crew_review` (read at each completion and each review request; session overrides apply):
  - **On** (the default): the owner's completion goes to `review` by the ordinary rules (§4.1: with independent
    review on, always: to the crew task's own valid reviewer if it has one, else to `pick_reviewer`; with it off,
    only to a reviewer other than the actor). The **check of the whole** is a review of a crew task with at least
    one `done` direction while `crew_review` is on: the pick uses the contributor key ("Reviews"), and every review
    request of it (the completion, a hand-over, a re-pick in `release_all`, a reviewer changed by `update`, the
    board's re-pick when USER makes the reviewer the assignee) is `n_crew_review_requested` (wakes) in place of
    `n_review_requested` (`Board._whole(task)`). The request reads `n_crew_review_requested` {by, id, title, n},
    `n` the number of its done directions, `by` as for any review request (§4.1): `#{id} "{title}" (sent by {by})
    is a crew task whose {n} directions are done: check it as a whole — do the directions fit together, and does
    the result meet its goal? Approve it, or return it with what does not fit (task_review).`; USER gets
    `u_review_requested`, `u_review_fallback` or `u_review_handed_over` as for any task (§4.1), with the same `by`.
    A crew task none of whose directions is done (it has none, or all were cancelled and the owner did the work
    itself) is reviewed as any task (`n_review_requested`, the pick without the contributor key).
  - **Off**: no second review, since each direction was reviewed already. An agent's completion of a crew task
    (its owner's, its `result` the one the owner wrote) makes it `done` at once, always: whatever
    `independent_review` says and whatever reviewer the crew task holds (named in `task_create` or `task_update`
    `reviewer`, set by USER, or picked by the board for an earlier review and kept after a return). The board picks
    no reviewer and nobody is asked for a review; the reviewer field is cleared, so the reviewer spread (§4.1,
    reviews so far) counts no review its holder never gave. The same holds for a crew
    task none of whose directions is done. Whoever wants a crew task reviewed turns `crew_review` on.
  - A toggle of `crew_review` while a crew task is in review changes nothing for that review: it stays in review
    with its reviewer, whose verdict (or the user's) settles it as usual; only a later completion follows the new
    setting. Nothing stores whether a review is a check of the whole, so a request made while it waits (a
    hand-over or a re-pick in `release_all`, which keep a review going, §4.1 "Liveness", or a reviewer changed by
    `update`) follows the setting at that request: `n_crew_review_requested` and the contributor key only while
    `crew_review` is on. After a return from that review, the owner's next completion with `crew_review` off is
    `done` at once (above), the reviewer of the returned review notwithstanding.
  USER completes a crew task as any task (§4.1 `complete` by USER: to review only with a reviewer of its own), open
  or failed directions notwithstanding.
  A crew task returned from review goes back to its owner (`in_progress`; `todo` without one, and its next owner
  reads the owner form of the crew ending that applies; the reviewer's comment is in #N's discussion), which fixes
  it itself or with new directions and completes it again; the new directions are reviewed one by one, and when
  they are finished the owner is told as above. `n_review_rejected` gains `{ending}`, rendered by the board in the
  recipient's language: the plain one, the current ``Fix it, then call `task_complete` again.`` (ru «Исправь и
  снова вызови `task_complete`.»), or for a crew task ``#N is a crew task: fix it yourself, or with new directions
  (task_update directions) and, once they are finished, update #N's result; then call `task_complete` again.``
  (ru «#N — групповая задача: исправь её сам(а) или новыми направлениями (task_update directions) и, когда они
  завершатся, обнови результат #N; затем снова вызови `task_complete`.»).
  A direction that fails while another one is still open, and its crew task is open and not in review, tells the
  crew task's owner at once (unless the owner is
  the actor; for the last one `n_subtasks_done` above says it; an owner that created the direction gets it in
  place of `n_task_closed`, never both): `n_direction_failed` {by, id, title, parent} (wakes): `#{id} "{title}", a
  direction of your crew task #{parent}, failed ({by}): reopen it to be done again (task_update #{id} status=todo),
  or cancel it if #{parent} does without it (status=cancelled).` A direction cancelled, by anyone, while another one
  is still open tells the owner the same way, under the same condition, if it has one (unless the owner is the
  actor, or its assignee, which gets `n_subtask_cancelled`; an owner that created it gets this in place of
  `n_task_closed`):
  `n_direction_cancelled` {by, id, title, parent} (wakes): `#{id} "{title}", a direction of your crew task
  #{parent}, was cancelled ({by}): if #{parent} still needs that part, add it again (task_update directions).`
  Liveness (§3 items 2 and 3): `_wake_stalled` and `_wake_idle_holders` compare and record (`_stall_woken`) one
  key, the pair (task ids, marks): the ids as before (in_progress, without the exempt ones; item 2 only those of
  its stalled set still held), and the marks, a frozenset of `(id, kind)` read from the board now by one helper
  both items call, so the two never sort or compare ids with tuples and never differ for the same state:
  - `(N, "subtasks done")` for each task `todo`, `in_progress` or `waiting` of the member that has at least one
    subtask, all of them terminal (what `n_subtasks_done` was sent about; a task without subtasks, a crew task with
    no directions yet included, gets no mark; `todo` too, because an owner often holds its crew task `todo` for its
    whole life: `task_create` with `assignee` leaves it so, and the owner texts tell it to take a direction, never
    to claim #N; but not a `todo` task that is blocked: it is not to be completed yet, and `n_unblocked` wakes its
    holder when its dependencies are done);
  - `(M, "direction to take")` for each `todo` direction M assigned to the member that its claim would take now
    (`Board.directions_to_take(name)`: M not blocked, #N `todo`, `in_progress` or `waiting` and not blocked, a
    place for the member or the member in the working set already, and no other direction of #N it works on): a
    direction assigned while #N was full or blocked (its claim was refused with "#M is free again when one of them
    hands its direction in" / "take #M when #N is no longer blocked"), or the owner's own part created `todo` under
    a blocked crew task, is pointed at once it can be taken, since nothing else offers an assigned task;
  - `(N, "free directions")` for each crew task the member owns that has a free direction (`todo`, no assignee, no
    blocker of its own, #N `todo`, `in_progress` or `waiting` and not blocked: the owner's claim needs no free
    place) while the owner holds none of its directions in `in_progress` or `waiting`, nor one to take (the
    "direction to take" mark names that one instead; it is never among the ids while it has a direction that can
    still move, §3 items 2-3).
  A holder woken about ({N}, {}) before N's subtasks finished differs from ({N}, {(N, "subtasks done")}) and is
  woken once more, so a holder that missed `n_subtasks_done`, or the owner of a crew task open again with all its
  directions finished (returned, or taken by a new owner), is told; one
  that keeps stalling afterwards gives both items the same pair and is not woken again. Item 3 wakes also when the
  ids are empty and the marks are not (a `waiting` or `todo` parent, a direction to take). The wake is `n_stalled`
  naming the ids that carry no
  mark (when there are any), followed by one sentence per mark, in the member's language: for "subtasks done"
  ` #N "title": ` and the owner form of the ending `n_subtasks_done` would give it now (`All its subtasks are
  finished: assemble their results and complete it.` or a crew ending above, the all finished one with the draft
  of #N's result: the mark is sent once per key, so the draft is bounded like the others; a compaction may have
  replaced the history that held the first one, §6.1; when one wake carries the drafts of several crew tasks,
  they share one budget B, each built with B ÷ their number); for
  "free directions" ` #N is a crew task with free directions nobody has taken: #17 "oidc". Take one yourself
  (task_claim), or cancel the ones it does without (task_update status=cancelled).` (at most 20 named, then `…`;
  the in-activation nudge of §6.2 adds the same sentence for such a crew task); for "direction to take" ` #M "title",
  your direction of crew task #N, can be taken now: claim it (task_claim) and do it, or unassign yourself if you
  will not (task_update assignee='').` (`mark_direction_to_take` {sub, title, id}, ru « #M «title», твоё
  направление групповой задачи #N, теперь можно взять: …»; the title cut like `fmt.trim(title, 80)`). The sentences
  (`Board.mark_text(name, marks)`, sorted by id and kind, each starting with a space; a sentence after one that
  spans lines, a draft, starts on a line of its own, its leading space removed, so it never reads as a part of the
  draft's last result) end `n_stalled` as its `{marks}` (the last placeholder of both texts, "" without marks).
  With no unmarked ids the wake is those sentences alone (`n_marks_stalled` {text}: their leading space removed).
  A mark that no longer applies when the text is built gives no sentence; when nothing is left to send, nothing is
  sent and the key is not recorded, so the next pass reads the marks again. `_stall_woken` is set only
  after the text is built: a render that raises is logged, nothing is recorded, and the scheduler pass goes on to
  its next items (the next pass tries again). Tests: a parent holder whose subtasks are all terminal stalls three
  times in a row and gets one wake for that key; a `waiting` task without subtasks is never woken by items 2-3
  (item 9, §3, may still wake its holder when the whole team sleeps). A trigger `all_done(parent=N)` (§8) needs
  every subtask `done`, so for a crew task it fires when all its directions are done, before its owner has written
  #N's result (and never once a direction is cancelled): wait on `done(N)` or `finished(N)` for the crew task
  itself instead.
- **Reviews.** A direction is reviewed by the ordinary rules (§4.1), independently of the others: its own reviewer
  if one was set and is valid, else `pick_reviewer` at its completion (any member but its executor; the owner too,
  though for the directions it added it is their creator and comes after the others, like any creator); with
  independent review off, a direction without a reviewer of its own is done when it is handed in. Reviews spread
  evenly (§4.1 "Reviewer selection"), so the directions of one crew task usually go to different members. The check
  of the whole (`crew_review` on, "Finishing"; with it off the board picks no reviewer for a crew task's
  completion): for a crew task the key of `pick_reviewer` gains `is a contributor` right after `cannot act now`
  (`Board.contributors_of(task)`: the assignees of its subtasks, finished ones included; the owner is the crew
  task's assignee and never reviews it), so a member outside the crew checks it when there is one; otherwise a
  contributor does, before USER: "independent" means "not the owner" here, and such a contributor checks how all
  the directions fit together, its own included (it executed a direction, not the crew task).
- **Leaving and closing.** When the owner releases a crew task (`status todo`) or leaves (`release_all`), its
  directions go on: the crew task goes back to `todo`, unassigned, ready, and its next claim makes a new owner. An
  owner that releases only the crew task keeps its own direction (as that direction's assignee it stays in the
  working set). The direction of a member that leaves goes back to `todo`, unassigned (§4.1): a free direction
  again, and the crew task's assignee after the release, if it has one, gets the quiet `n_direction_freed` {id,
  title, by} (nobody does when the owner itself leaves: the next owner reads the directions in the owner sentence;
  nor when that assignee is USER). Every direction of the leaving member that went back to `todo` counts: one
  `in_progress` or `waiting`, one assigned to it and still `todo`, and, with independent review off, one in review;
  with independent review on, a direction in review stays there and is not freed.
  When a task with open subtasks goes from an open status to a terminal one (`done` set by USER or by the approval
  of USER's completion, `failed`, `cancelled`), its `todo` subtasks
  without an assignee are cancelled in the same mutation (one `task.updated` each, after the parent's, and no other
  notice: their creators get no `n_task_closed`, the parent's closing is the news; one level only: their own
  subtasks are left as they are, except that a crew task cancelled this way takes its open directions along by the
  same rule, its `todo` directions without an assignee cancelled after it and the holders of the others told with
  `n_parent_closed` naming the crew task, since nobody may take a direction of a terminal crew task) and the
  assignees of its other
  open subtasks get `n_parent_closed` {id, title, status, sub} (wakes): `#{id} "{title}", of which your #{sub} is a
  part, is {status}: finish #{sub} only if it is still needed on its own; otherwise cancel it (task_update
  status=cancelled).` A move from one terminal status to another cancels nothing (`n_task_closed` still goes out).
  The actor's own open subtask (the owner's direction, when the owner closes the crew task) gets
  no notification: the result of its call adds the same sentence as ` Your #{sub} is still open: finish it only if
  it is still needed on its own; otherwise cancel it (task_update status=cancelled).` (USER's call too: the REST
  result carries the board's notes).
  The same rule holds after the closing: an open direction that a later change would leave `todo` without an
  assignee while its crew task is terminal (its holder releases it or leaves, `release_all`; the parent's creator or
  assignee unassigns it; its review is returned after its executor left) is cancelled in the same mutation instead,
  since nobody may take it and it would keep the goal open: one `task.updated`, no `n_direction_freed`,
  `n_task_closed` or `n_subtask_cancelled`, not among the ids `release_all` returns; the result of the actor's call
  adds `note_direction_closed` {id, parent, status} ` #{parent} is {status}, so #{id} is cancelled instead of going
  back to the board: nobody takes a direction of a closed crew task.` A reopening by USER is not such a change.
  Such a direction has the cascade above too, `release_all` included: its `todo` subtasks without an assignee
  (the leaver's own ones it just returned included, which are then not among the returned ids either) are
  cancelled, one `task.updated` each after the direction's, and the holders of its other open subtasks but the
  leaver get `n_parent_closed`.
  Any task that becomes `failed` or `cancelled` while open tasks list it in `depends_on` (they stay blocked: only a
  done dependency clears), the subtasks the cascade cancels with it included, adds `note_dependents_blocked` {deps,
  id, status} to the result of the actor's call: ` #5, #7 depend on #{id}, which is {status} now: they stay blocked
  until that dependency is removed (task_update depends_on) or they are cancelled.`, for a single one
  `note_dependent_blocked` {deps, id, status}: ` #5 depends on #{id}, which is {status} now: it stays blocked until
  that dependency is removed (task_update depends_on) or it is cancelled.` (`release_all` has no result to add them
  to).
- **Offers.** A free direction is a ready unassigned task: `ready_unassigned` (§4) returns a subtask of a crew task
  only while that crew task is `todo`, `in_progress` or `waiting`, not blocked, and has a free place. So `_nudge_idle`
  (`n_ready`), the wake-up's `ready` list and wrap-up mode treat directions like any ready task: `_nudge_idle`
  offers it to each member once while it stays ready. Neither `n_ready` nor the wake-up's `ready` list names to a
  member the directions of a crew task in which it works on a direction (`in_progress` or `waiting`;
  `Board.busy_crews(name)`): its claim would be refused. Its fallback is the owner: an idle owner working on none
  of the directions is woken once about a free one ("free directions" mark, "Finishing", Liveness). With nothing
  left to take while a place stays free and other members are idle with no task of their own to go on with, the
  owner is told once ("A free place").
  A parent without an assignee is ready the whole time its subtasks are worked on, so most members were offered it
  already when they finish. `_nudged` is therefore keyed by the pair (task id, finish state), the finish states of
  the ready tasks read at each pass (`Board.finish_states`, "Finishing"; the kickoff's entry is (card id, None)),
  and a key no longer among the ready ones is dropped as before: when a parent's subtasks have all finished (and
  again when its finish state changes, e.g. its last failed direction is cancelled), it is offered afresh to every
  idle member, those that took its subtasks included, and the result of the claim that takes it adds the owner
  form of the ending that applies (for a crew task, in the owner sentence; the all finished one with the draft of
  #N's result, "Finishing"). `_considering` is unchanged.
- **Texts for agents.** `Task.short()` adds `crew 2/3` to a crew task (working set / `crew`; `Board` fills
  `Task.crew_working`, like `blocked_by`); a subtask keeps its `parent #N`. `board` lists a subtask indented (`  ↳ `)
  right under its parent when the parent is listed (two more spaces per level below it, the board's order kept
  within a level; the 100-task cut applies after this order), otherwise at the top level. `task_get` of a task
  with subtasks adds
  `Subtasks:` and one line each, `#15 [done] "title" @Anna Smith — <the result's first line, cut to 120 characters>`
  (the title cut to 80, the first non-empty line of the result),
  and for a crew task, after them (also with no directions yet, then without `Subtasks:`), `Crew task: up to 3
  members at once, the owner included; 2 working now (owner X #16; Anna
  Smith #15). Free directions: #17 "oidc".` (`Task.crew_working` in its order, each member followed by its
  directions in `in_progress` or `waiting`, comma-joined; free directions as in "Taking a direction", without the
  place, at most 20 then `…`, or `none`). The results of `task_create` and of a `task_update` that adds directions
  name them after the task line: `Directions: #15 "parser", #16 "cli".` (only the new ones; such an update's
  summary adds `N direction(s) added`, so passing only `directions` is not "No changes"), and `task_update`'s
  summary shows a change of `crew` like the other fields (`crew 0 → 3`). The board's notes (§4 `notes`) follow on
  a line of their own. `n_direction_taken`: `{by} took #{id} "{title}", a direction of your crew task #{parent}.`
  `n_direction_freed`: `#{id} "{title}", a direction of your crew task, is free again: {by} left the swarm.`
  `n_crew_owner`: the owner sentence above; `n_crew_review_requested`, the crew endings of `n_subtasks_done` and
  `n_review_rejected`, the draft of #N's result (`crew_draft`, `crew_draft_cut`, `crew_draft_more`,
  `crew_draft_no_result`), `n_direction_failed`, `n_direction_cancelled`, `n_marks_stalled`: "Finishing";
  `n_crew_gap`, `crew_gap_held`, `crew_gap_held_you`, `crew_gap_held_wait` and `crew_gap_blocked`: "A free place".
  `Task` gains `crew: int` (stored) and `crew_working:
  list[str]` (filled by `Board`, not stored); both are in `to_dict()`, so in the state API and the events (an
  export copies the column `tasks.crew`). The web and the TUI show a crew task's chip from its `crew_working` in the
  board's snapshot and fetch the snapshot again after changes (the web on every bus event, the TUI for `/board` and
  `/task`), so a direction's `task.updated` is enough and the board emits no event for the parent.
  `n_crew_changed`: `{by} set the crew of #{id} "{title}" to {crew}
  (0 = an ordinary task).` `n_subtask_cancelled`: `{by} cancelled #{id} "{title}", your part of #{parent}: stop the
  work on it; if what you have done is still needed, say so in #{parent}'s discussion.`
- **Notifications** of subtasks and crew tasks, and the liveness wakes of §3 items 2, 3 and 9 (texts in prompts.py,
  ru/en; never to the actor, who reads the same text in its call's result where this section says so, through the
  board's `notes`, §4; one per member and change, "Finishing"; "quiet" = `wake=False`):

  | when | to | key {placeholders} | wakes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | a parent open and not in review gets another finish state that is not None ("Finishing") | its assignee (a crew task's owner), else its creator when an active member | `n_subtasks_done` {id, title, total, counts, ending} (in place of `n_task_closed` to the creator of the subtask that changed; to the holder of a crew task with all directions finished, `ending` is the all finished one followed by the draft of #N's result) | yes |
  | a direction fails while another one is open and its crew task is open and not in review | the owner, unless it is the actor | `n_direction_failed` {by, id, title, parent} (in place of `n_task_closed` when the owner also created the direction) | yes |
  | a direction is cancelled while another one is open and its crew task is open and not in review | the owner, unless it is the actor or its assignee (`n_subtask_cancelled`) | `n_direction_cancelled` {by, id, title, parent} (in place of `n_task_closed` when the owner also created the direction) | yes |
  | an open subtask is cancelled by someone other than its assignee | its assignee (for one in review, its executor) | `n_subtask_cancelled` {by, id, title, parent} (in place of `n_task_closed` when it also created it) | yes |
  | someone else's call would send `n_assigned` for a direction it leaves held back for its assignee ("A held direction") | that assignee, an LLM member | `n_direction_held_busy` {by, id, title, parent, m} or `n_direction_held_full` {by, id, title, parent, working, crew, names} (in place of `n_assigned`) | no |
  | a direction is taken (a claim, an `update`, a `parent_id` move) | the owner, unless it is the actor or the taker | `n_direction_taken` {by, id, title, parent} | no |
  | a direction's holder left the swarm | the crew task's assignee after the release | `n_direction_freed` {id, title, by} | no |
  | someone else makes or tells a member the holder of a crew task (an assignment, the creator's reopening, `crew` set) | that holder | `n_crew_owner` {id, title, crew, directions, instructions} (in place of `n_assigned`; with all directions finished, `instructions` is the all finished owner form with the draft, and `directions` "") | yes |
  | a crew task has had a free place, a working direction and none a member may take now for 10 × `agents.idle_nudge_seconds`, while other members are idle with no task of their own to go on with ("A free place", §3 item 8) | its owner, an idle LLM member | `n_crew_gap` {id, title, working, crew, names, idle, directions, held} | yes |
  | the assignee changes the `crew` of a task it did not create | the creator | `n_crew_changed` {by, id, title, crew} | no |
  | the creator or USER changes the `crew` of a task someone else holds, not making it a crew task | the holder | `n_crew_changed` {by, id, title, crew} | no |
  | a parent with open subtasks becomes terminal ("Leaving and closing") | the assignees of its other open subtasks | `n_parent_closed` {id, title, status, sub} | yes |
  | a check of the whole is requested | the reviewer | `n_crew_review_requested` {by, id, title, n} (§4.1 table) | yes |
  | a crew task is returned | its owner | `n_review_rejected` with the crew `ending` (§4.1 table) | yes |
  | a holder stalls with marks and no unmarked ids (Liveness) | the holder | `n_marks_stalled` {text} (a "subtasks done" mark of a crew task with all directions finished carries the draft of #N's result, in `n_stalled` too) | yes |
  | a holder stalls with unmarked ids (Liveness, §3 items 2 and 3) | the holder | `n_stalled` {tasks, marks} (`marks`: the mark sentences, "" without marks) | yes |
  | the whole team asleep (§3 item 9) | one idle LLM member | `n_team_asleep` {elapsed, jobs} | yes |
  | same, the first wake of a board state (§3 item 9) | USER | `u_team_asleep` {elapsed, name} | yes |
  | same, every open task held by USER or external members | USER, no member | `u_team_waits` {elapsed, tasks} | yes |

- **System prompt** (en and ru; frozen per agent, so for members created from then on). Rule 3 (which says to hold
  one task in progress at a time) adds at its end `A crew task ("crew 2/3" on the board) is split into directions:
  take a free one like any task, then write its card (task_update: title, goal, description) before the work. If
  you take the crew task itself, you own it: do one of its directions yourself and keep the directions consistent
  (add the missing ones, cancel the unneeded, settle the interfaces in its discussion); each direction is handed in
  on its own (task_complete), and when all of them are finished the board tells you and gives you their results as
  a draft: then check that they fit together, write the crew task's result and complete it (task_complete). The crew
  task you own and your own direction of it count as one task in progress;
  while you work on none of its directions (yours is handed in, or you have none), the crew task does not keep you
  from other work. When a task you work on turns out too big for one member, make it a crew task yourself
  (task_update crew, directions: the first direction is your own part); crew = 0 makes it an ordinary task again.
  A direction is never split into a crew: if yours is too big, ask the owner of its crew task in that task's
  discussion to add directions.`; rule 8 adds, right after its sentence that prefers a few meaningful deliverables
  over many tiny tasks, `When a deliverable is too big
  for one member and its detailed split is unclear before the work starts, create one crew task: crew = how many
  members may work on it at once, its owner included; directions = its areas, one per item; the members who take
  them write the details.` The planning card (board data, §3) says the same in one sentence, and its "only one task"
  counts a crew task the planner owns and its own direction of it as one (and the crew task alone as none while the
  planner works on none of its directions). Every member of a board session this version opens has board revision 5
  or later (§17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version"; a thread session's members have the thread revision 6, which has
  no tasks, §22.5), so these texts and every board text for agents (`prompts.BOARD_KEYS`, §22.6) may name crew tasks,
  `crew` and `directions` (§12 R0′, per mode §22.5); shared and thread texts never do. External members have no
  system prompt (their briefing, join_swarm's text, is
  unchanged): they see the live `task_create` / `task_update` descriptions and learn the rest from the claim
  results and `n_crew_owner`.
- **Surfaces.** The web board shows subtasks in their parent's stack (§18.4 "Subtasks"). The TUI (docs/TUI.md,
  updated with the code) does the same in text: a parent's line ends with one `●` per direct subtask in its status
  colour (the TUI's status colours, ASCII `o`; at most 12 dots, then `+N`, as the web's toggle), `done/total`,
  `crew 2/3` for a crew task (ru «групповая 2/3»; for any task whose `crew` is an integer ≥ 2, with or without

## 5. Mailbox (mailbox.py)

```python
class Mailbox:
    def __init__(self, swarm): ...
    def send(self, sender: str, to: str | list[str], text: str, reply_to: int | None = None, *,
             automatic: bool = False) -> dict
        # to: name, list of names, "all" (all active members except sender; USER not included) or USER.
        # Resolves via swarm.resolve_member; duplicates removed; sender cannot be the only recipient.
        # text non-empty, <= 50000 chars. Inserts message + inbox rows; emits "message.sent" {message};
        # swarm.signal(each recipient), except quiet broadcasts (below). Inside `sent_as_seen_by(members, sender)` (a context manager over a
        # ContextVar, set by hub_mcp.hub_call with the caller as `sender`, §13) a message from that sender reaches
        # those recipients with their inbox row already read and no signal: the MCP client that sends acts as them
        # too, so the message is in their history but is no news to them. Only that sender's: a task started inside
        # the block inherits the context (an agent runtime starts in a context of its own anyway, §6.2), and the
        # messages of every other sender reach those members as news. `seen_as(sender)` returns the block's
        # members for that sender, else frozenset() (§22.3).
        # The answer to a question pause (§3.1): a message from USER, not `automatic` (a user-owned trigger's message
        # action passes it, §8), whose resolved recipients include the asker of `swarm.pending_question()` (looked up
        # with getattr: FakeSwarm has none) gets `reply_to` = the question's id when it has none; after the store and
        # the signals `swarm.question_answered(message, question)` runs (it never raises). The emitted message dict
        # is never changed after the emit.
    def get(self, message_id: int) -> dict
    def unread(self, name: str, mark_read: bool = True, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]
    def mark_read(self, name: str, message_ids: list[int]) -> int   # returns how many were unread
        # read_messages marks every message it shows (with=..., include_read) read for its caller
    def unread_count(self, name: str) -> int
    def history(self, name: str, with_name: str | None = None, limit: int = 50, before_id: int | None = None) -> list[dict]
    def conversation(self, a: str, b: str, limit: int = 200, since_id: int = 0) -> list[dict]
        # messages where (sender a and b in recipients) or (sender b and a in recipients), ascending
    def recent(self, limit: int = 100, since_id: int = 0) -> list[dict]
    def user_conversation(self, after: int = 0, limit: int = 200) -> list[dict]
        # the user's conversation with the members (HTTP API v1, §21.5 "Messages"): messages the user sent or that
        # reached the user, id > after, ascending; after 0 is the OLDEST page (conversation/recent give the latest).
        # Dicts {"id","ts","sender","recipients","text","reply_to"} (no to_all: the columns every version has)
def read_user_conversation(db_path, after: int = 0, limit: int = 200) -> list[dict]
    # the same from a session's database file (db.reading_file, nothing written next to it); [] without one
# message dict: {"id","ts","sender","recipients":[...],"text","reply_to","to_all"}
# to_all: sent to "all" (column messages.to_all; Database adds it to a file of an older version: db.ADDED_COLUMNS)
```

Quiet broadcasts: when a member (not the user) sends to "all", a recipient reached only through "all" (not also
named) that `swarm.waits_for_job` (an AI agent asleep while it waits for the end of its own job, §3) is not signalled:
its inbox row stays unread (`has_pending` is true; it is not idle for the scheduler, being busy anyway), and the
job's end wakes it and shows the message in the same wake-up instead of a wake-up of its own (which would re-read its
whole context to read "all" news). `swarm.defer_wake` records it; should its wait end without a wake (the busy window
of a server ended, its end became quiet), the scheduler's `_wake_deferred` wakes it. Personal messages (also to several
named members, or "all" plus its name), every message of the user (its "all" included), reviews, assignments and
notifications wake as always. The sender's result is unchanged. In a thread session a member's new post that
reaches a member only through its `feed` subscriptions in `wake` follows the same rule (`notify(..., defer=True)`,
§22.3 "Quiet new posts").

## 6. Agent runtime (agent.py)

### 6.1 Neutral message format (history rows, LLM input)
```python
{"role": "user", "content": str}
{"role": "assistant", "content": str, "tool_calls": [{"id": str, "name": str, "arguments": dict}],
 "raw": {"provider": "anthropic", "model": str, "content": [block dicts]} | None}
{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": str, "name": str, "content": str, "is_error": bool}
```
History is **append-only** (Anthropic binds thinking blocks to the exact prefix). The only rewrite is
*simple compaction*: when the context is too large, the agent asks its LLM (same system prompt and
tools, `compaction_request` appended as a user message) for a summary and replaces the whole
history with one user message `compacted` (+ the agent's `notes`, if any) + `continue`, followed by the
newest trailing user-side texts kept verbatim (the wake-up that started the activation, new events;
at most 40000 chars, never an earlier summary). The old history is archived for traces in the same
transaction. Without a usable LLM summary (a context-overflow error or another non-retryable 400 for
the compaction request, or an overflow of the main call) the agent compacts without the LLM: notes +
a digest of its latest steps + the kept texts. The system prompt is frozen in `agents.system_prompt` at
creation, and the tools array is frozen per agent (below; agent-built MCP tools go through `mcp_call`). New rules
reach existing members through tool results and notifications, and new tools at their next compaction.
In a thread session `compaction_request` and `compacted` are replaced by `compaction_request_thread` and
`compacted_thread`, and while the goal is active the summary message also gets the `my_goal_vote` line, after the
notes (§22.6).

**Frozen tool sets** (tools/frozen.py). The tools array is part of the prompt prefix that thinking blocks are bound
to, so every LLM agent sends exactly the array it was given, and the array changes only where nothing is bound to
it:
- Every released LLM tool set is a numbered **revision** (`{"revision": N, "en": [...], "ru": [...]}`, a thread
  set also `"mode": "thread"`), never edited, and a number is never reused: one numbering for both session modes,
  each number belonging to one mode (§22.5). The revisions a session this version opens can hold, from
  `OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION` to `NEWEST_REVISION`, are shipped as `tools/snapshots/llm_r<N>.json` (board) and
  `llm_thread_r<N>.json` (thread). `TOOLSET_REVISIONS[mode]` (now board 5: `task_create` and `task_update` gain
  `crew` and `directions`, §4.2; thread 6, §22.5) is what `schemas_for("llm", language, mode)` builds.
- Record: kv `tools:<name>` = `{"rev", "language", "tools", "mode"}` (§2; no `mode` = board), stored through
  `db.set` (`db.dumps`: key and tool order round-trip exactly). `AgentRuntime.__init__` (`_load_tools`) reads it
  with the session's mode; an agent without a usable one (`frozen.valid`, below; a record of the other mode is
  unusable too, §22.5) gets `frozen.current_record(language, swarm.mode)`, written at once: a session this version
  opens
  has no agent with a history and no usable record (§17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version"), so a missing record
  means the agent never ran; `member_tool_names` follows the same rule. View-only loads (no runtime) write nothing.
- `AgentRuntime`: `tools_rev`, `tools` (the record's list, passed unchanged to `llm.complete`), `tool_names`
  (frozenset), `tool_parameters(name) -> dict | None` (None: the agent lacks that tool).
- **Upgrade at compaction only**: `_replace_with_summary` moves an agent whose `tools_rev !=
  TOOLSET_REVISIONS[swarm.mode]` to `frozen.current_record(language, swarm.mode)`, never across modes (`!=`: after
  a code downgrade it realigns too); the record is written in the same
  `db.transaction()` as the history rewrite (`_replace_history(messages, tools=)`), and the new history holds no
  assistant turn bound to the old array. The compaction request itself still sends the old array. Downgrading the
  code below a session's newest revision is unsupported. When the upgrade adds tools, the summary message gets
  `tools_added` {tools: the added names, each in backticks, joined by ", "} before `continue`; an upgrade that adds
  no tool (only properties or descriptions) gets no such line. `agent.compacted` data and the compaction span meta
  carry `tools_revision`.
- **Oldest revision opened**: `OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION = 5`, a fixed constant (the revision of crew tasks, 0.2.0; never
  derived from `TOOLSET_REVISIONS`, so a later revision still opens sessions of revision 5; one literal for both
  modes: the thread set, revision 6, is not below it). A session with a member
  recorded below it, or with an agent that has a history and no record (it ran before tool sets were frozen), was
  made by an earlier version and is not opened (§17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version"): no session this version
  opens builds a runtime below revision 5 (`AgentRuntime` itself does not check: the check is the session's), and
  the upgrade at compaction moves only revisions 5 and later. Only the revisions from `OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION` on are
  shipped (tests/test_frozen_tools.py checks that exactly these are, and that each stays served, §12 R0′).
  `frozen.for_span` reads them for trace spans recorded before an agent's last upgrade. `--check` compares only the
  current revisions' files (one per mode).
- `frozen` API: `kv_key(name)`, `normalize(tools)`, `revisions(mode=None)`, `mode_of(rev)`, `snapshot(rev,
  language)` (a fresh copy, found by its number whatever the mode; unknown language → en), `current(language,
  mode="board")`, `record(rev, language, tools, mode="board")`, `current_record(language, mode="board")`,
  `valid(rec) -> bool` (a dict with an integer, non-bool `rev`, `tools` a list of dicts with a str `name` and a
  dict `parameters`, and `mode` absent or in `MODES`; shared by `read` and `db.made_by_earlier_version`),
  `read(db, name, mode=None) -> dict | None` (a record that is not `valid`, or one of another mode than `mode`, is
  logged and ignored), `write(db, name, rec)`, `names(tools)`, `for_span(db, name, language, revision)` (§16),
  `member_tool_names(swarm, member) -> frozenset` (a runtime's names, else the record or the set its first start
  will freeze in the session's mode, nothing written; the live registry of the session's mode for external
  members and the user); `TOOLSET_REVISIONS`, `NEWEST_REVISION`, `OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION`, `MODES` (§22.5).
  `python -m dreamteam.tools.frozen --write [--force] [--mode board|thread]` writes the current file of every mode,
  or of one (`llm_r5.json`, `llm_thread_r6.json`; exit 2 when a different file exists: a released revision is
  never edited), `--check` exits 1 when the code differs from one of them.

### 6.2 Loop
```python
class AgentRuntime:
    def __init__(self, swarm, name: str): ...
    name: str; state: str
    def start(self) -> None            # creates the asyncio task, in a fresh contextvars context: it never inherits
                                       # the request context of its starter (hub_call's sent_as_seen_by, §5)
    async def stop(self) -> None
    def wake(self) -> None
    def end_turn(self) -> None         # called by the `wait` tool
    def note_sent_to_user(self) -> None  # called by send_message when USER is a recipient
```
* Waits for `wake()`. Skips if swarm paused (for any reason, a member's question too: §3.1) or nothing pending
  (unless the last activation was cut short: `interrupted`). Activation: `render_wake(name)` →
  user message; loop up to `max_steps_per_turn`: budget check (exceeded → `swarm.pause`), compaction
  check: last prompt tokens + its output tokens (or, without reported usage, an estimate of the history
  + system prompt + tool schemas) + estimate of appended messages > budget, where budget = context
  limit (`profile.context_tokens` or `agents.context_tokens`) − min(max_tokens, limit/4) − the
  compaction request, so the summary call still fits when the limit is the model's real window; when a
  fresh compaction already fills more than 3/4 of the budget, the next one waits until the history grew
  by half a budget (no thrashing), but, while a fresh compaction still gets under the limit − min(max_tokens,
  limit/4), never past that (the window may be real: a larger prompt would fail every request; a summary call
  that no longer fits there falls back to the compaction without the LLM; a compaction above it means the limit
  is not the real window). Then `async with
  swarm.llm_semaphore: llm.complete(system, history, tools)`, record usage, append assistant message,
  emit `agent.activity` events (thinking summary / text / tool call / tool result, truncated 2000
  chars), count the reply in `llm_steps`, execute tool calls sequentially via `tools.call_tool`, append results
  (`_run_tools` cuts each one for the model to `agents.tool_output_chars` with `shell.truncate_middle`; the trace
  keeps the whole text, §16.1), call `swarm.hint_planner(name)` (§3 scheduler item 4; in a thread session only its
  clarify branch, §22.4; never raises); after tools, if
  `render_wake(name, incoming=True)` returns text, append it as a user message. Stops when: `wait` was
  called, no tool calls (a `nudge` once per in_progress task the agent holds (never in a thread session, §22.7),
  except a clarify planning task it
  waits for the user's answers about, `swarm.asks_user` looked up with getattr, §3.1, and a crew task with open
  directions, §3 item 3, unless one is free and its owner, working on none of them, could take it: then the nudge
  is the "free directions" sentence of §4.2 "Finishing" (Liveness; `Swarm.crew_nudge(name, tasks)`, looked up with
  getattr), after the usual `nudge` when another in_progress task is new to it, once per activation, and `stalled`
  holds only the other ids; none while it is busy with a
  job, §7.1 "Liveness": the job's end wakes it, nor while it waits for a file it was refused,
  `workspace.waits_for_lock`, §7 "Lock waiters": `n_lock_free` wakes it; after plain text even then, `stalled`
  records those tasks and
  the scheduler wakes it once with `n_stalled`, also once the busy window ended), refusal, or
  step limit (then `notify(name, "n_step_limit")`). A reply cut off by max_tokens gets `cut_off` and
  the loop continues. At the end of an activation that is not stopping (any outcome), the new files its commands
  left are committed unless a command still running may write them (`workspace.commit_held(name, "at the end of
  <name>'s turn")`, §7 "Held new files"; never raises). After an activation, the agent re-wakes itself if events are still pending.
* Output limit after a cut-off reply (`_output_limit`): a reply cut off by max_tokens **without tool calls**
  (typically all thinking) makes the next step ask for twice the limit of the cut-off call, and it keeps doubling
  while replies keep being cut off, up to the profile's ceiling `max_tokens_ceiling` (None = 2 × max_tokens; at
  or below max_tokens = never raised; `ModelProfile.output_ceiling`) and never beyond the context room
  (`_context_limit() − _prompt_estimate()`: when context_tokens is the model's real window, prompt + max_tokens
  must fit; less room than the profile's own limit = the profile's limit). Any other reply (tool calls, a normal
  end) returns to the profile's max_tokens; so does a new activation, and so do compaction calls. The limit goes
  to the client as `complete(..., max_tokens=n)` only when raised (a client whose `complete` has no such keyword,
  `accepts_max_tokens`, is never raised). If a raised request fails with a non-retryable `bad_request` about the
  output limit (`is_output_limit_error`: "max_tokens", "max_completion_tokens", "max_output_tokens",
  "max_new_tokens", "maximum output", "output tokens", "completion tokens"), the same step is retried once with
  the profile's limit (not a counted attempt) and the runtime remembers for this client (`_limit_refused_by`,
  cleared when `reset_llm` / a stop drops the client) not to raise again; a context overflow of a raised request
  (`is_context_overflow`, checked first: vLLM's "maximum context length ... (32000 > 32768 − 1000)" and Anthropic's
  "input length and `max_tokens` exceed context limit" name max_tokens too) is retried the same way but not
  remembered. A raised limit also replaces a limit key in the profile's `extra` (the SDKs merge `extra_body` over
  the body, so the old value would silently win). Both are an `output_limit_fallback` event in the trace and an
  `error` activity; any other error of a raised request behaves as before. The `cut_off` text is unchanged.
* If the activation was caused by a USER message and the agent finished with plain text without
  messaging USER, the text (all parts, truncated to the mailbox limit) is forwarded to USER as a
  message from the agent; an activation cut short owes that reply to its continuation.
* LLM errors: retryable → backoff 2,4,8,16,32 s (5 tries, stopped by pause/stop); a context overflow →
  compaction without the LLM and one retry; otherwise state `error`, notify USER (kind `u_agent_error`,
  once per streak of the same error), end the activation. Retryable failures and crashes are retried
  automatically after `RECOVERY_DELAYS` (30, 60, 120, 300, 600 s); non-retryable ones wait for the next
  event (or `reconfigure()`). A crash (any exception, or a CancelledError the task was not asked for)
  repairs dangling tool calls, sets `error` and schedules a recovery. History is repaired on start
  (dangling tool calls get `"interrupted"` tool results; only results after the last assistant message
  count). A history row is inserted before the in-memory history is updated.
* `stop()` cancels the task without swallowing the caller's cancellation, resets WORKING to IDLE and
  closes the LLM client (`aclose`). `reset_llm()` drops the cached client after a settings change.
* State changes emit `agent.status` {name, status}; persisted in `agents.status`.

### 6.3 Wake-up text (render_wake)
In a thread session the wake-up is §22.6's (no task lines, a `digest` group, the vote line); below is the board's.

`wake_header` (or `incoming_header`), then (not for incoming, only while the user's wrap-up mode is on, §3) the one-line
`wrap_up_line` ("Wrap-up mode (the user): start no new computations or background jobs; finish your tasks with what
you have."), `reasons:` then one bullet per undelivered notification text and
per unread message (`msg` template, recipients list with the agent shown as `you`), then, only when one of those
messages was sent to "all" (`to_all`, from the user or a member; incoming too), the one-line `all_hint` ("Before
creating a task for a message to all, check the board: one member creates it, the others take it or comment."), then
(not for incoming) goal line (one line: the goal is stored split, §3 `set_goal`; `goal_none` without a goal), for an
LLM member while the budget has a limit (`limits()["max_cost_usd"]` > 0) the line `money` {spent, limit, pct}
(spent = `spent_usd()`; "Money: spent $1.20 of $5.00 (24%)." / «Деньги: потрачено $1.20 из $5.00 (24%).»; pct as
in `n_budget_low`, §3 `record_usage`, so it shows 99 at most), `my_tasks`, one `my_blocked` {id,
blockers: "#3, #4"} per open task of the agent with unfinished dependencies, except one in review whose result is
already produced (it may remove those it can do without, §4), `my_reviews` (only when
tasks wait for its review: `#id title (assignee or -)`), `my_jobs` (only while it has running background jobs,
§7.1: `my_job` items `j3 npm run dev (running 25 min)` joined with "; ", the command cut to 60 characters, the
duration in the member's language; a silent job, §7.1, is `my_job_silent` `j3 npm run dev (running 50 min, no output
for 40 min)`), `ready` (up to 8; free directions of crew tasks included, §4.2), for an LLM member the Skills index
(below), notes: in full only when they
changed
since they were last put into the agent's context (a wake-up or a compaction; once more after a restart),
otherwise the one-line `notes_unchanged`, since the history is append-only. The `money` line is never in an
incoming render nor for an external member, and never between the header and `wrap_up_line` or before the news.

**System prompt** (en and ru; frozen per member at hire, so for members hired from then on; no new placeholder and
no new numbered rule, every pinned substring kept): rule 1's list of what a wake-up shows names `the money spent
(while the budget has a limit)` next to the global goal (ru «потраченные деньги (пока у бюджета есть лимит)»);
rule 9 ends with `When a notice says that most of the money budget is spent, don't wait for the user to ask for a
wrap-up: finish what is nearly done and start nothing large.` (it echoes `n_budget_low`; ru «Если уведомление
говорит, что большая часть денежного бюджета потрачена, не жди, пока пользователь попросит закругляться: доводи до
конца то, что почти готово, и не начинай ничего большого.»); rule 10 ends with ``A process you start with & or
nohup that `jobs` does not list is not tracked: its end wakes nobody.`` (ru «Процесс, запущенный через & или
nohup, которого нет в списке `jobs`, не отслеживается: его завершение никого не разбудит.»; `jobs` in both, so the
backticked identifiers still match). A thread session's members get `SYSTEM_THREAD_EN` / `SYSTEM_THREAD_RU` instead
(§22.6), which keep these sentences (the budget one in its thread wording).

The **Skills index** (§19 "Delivery to agents"; never for external members, never in an incoming render): with skills
attached, the full `skills_index` (or `skills_index_own` when the member's role lists one of them) once per agent
memory: when `Swarm._skills_shown[name]` is not True (never shown, after a restart, or after a compaction whose text
had none); every later wake-up shows the one-line `skills_names` (the names with their marks) instead. With none
attached, nothing, except one `skills_none` line for a member that had seen an index (`_skills_shown` False then; a
later attach shows the full index again).

For a member (never the user), before the undelivered notifications are read, `triggers.release_held(name)` turns
the fires its repeating triggers held back (§8 "Wake limit") into one quiet `n_trigger_held` per trigger, so they come
with this render (a wake-up, the news between two steps, a `wait_for_events` result) and need no wake-up of their own.
An in-memory set of the owners with held fires keeps this free of queries for the others.

`stamps=True` (only `wait_for_events`, whose one result may hold hours of news; an agent's wake-up stays as above so
its history does not grow): when the oldest undelivered notification or unread message, or `since` (the oldest
progress line shown with it), is more than `fmt.STAMP_SPAN` (60 s) older than now, each notification and message
bullet starts with its time (`fmt.item_time`: `HH:MM`, with the date when not today's) and the header shows the range
(`fmt.stamp_range`: `2026-10-11 10:50–12:50`) instead of one stamp.

## 7. Workspace (workspace.py) and shell (shell.py)

```python
class Workspace:
    root: Path                                   # config.workspace_dir
    def __init__(self, swarm): ...
    async def init(self) -> None                 # mkdir; ensure_scratch() (with or without git); if git
                                                 # enabled+available: init repo, .gitignore, initial commit
                                                 # (Swarm.start decides git_isolated before: _prepare_offline);
                                                 # with record_head, then (still under the git lock) HEAD into
                                                 # head_at_init: `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^{commit}` of
                                                 # the folder's own .git, else None (§21.4 `base_commit`)
    record_head: bool                            # set by SessionManager._start_locked for a v1 session's first
    head_at_init: str | None                     # start; None with git off, without git, no commit or no .git
    git_isolated: bool                           # DreamTeam's git here may run isolated ("Defense in depth")
    def hold_git(self) -> None                   # the network went off: _git() waits (counted holds) until
    def release_git(self) -> None                # Swarm._network_changed's _prepare_offline has decided
    def ensure_scratch(self, actor: str | None = None) -> None
        # `.scratch/` with its marker `.scratch/.gitignore` (rewritten when missing or changed) and, for `actor`,
        # the member's folder scratch_rel(actor); synchronous, best effort (an OSError is logged); a `.scratch`
        # that is a file or a link/junction resolving elsewhere is left alone, and a marker that is a link is
        # never written through
    def resolve(self, path: str) -> Path         # inside root (no escape, no .git); ToolError otherwise
    def rel(self, p: Path) -> str                # posix relative path
    def read(self, path: str, offset: int = 1, limit: int = 400) -> str   # lines offset..offset+limit-1, header "[path: lines a-b of N]"; binary -> ToolError
    async def write(self, actor: str, path: str, content: str) -> str
    async def edit(self, actor: str, path: str, old: str, new: str, replace_all: bool = False) -> str
        # both refuse a path under SKILLS_MIRROR (`.scratch/_skills`, a lexical check on the resolved relative path,
        # case-folded on Windows): ToolError "'.scratch/_skills/' holds the swarm's skills and is rebuilt by
        # DreamTeam. To change a skill, copy its folder (without node_modules) into your scratch folder and edit it
        # there, then call skill_propose." (§19)
        # a read-only file elsewhere (a copy of a mirror folder keeps its read-only files) is made writable first
        # (owner write bit), unless it has other hard links; the write is the member's explicit edit
        # old must occur exactly once unless replace_all; ToolError with hints otherwise
        # write and edit write in one checked step: refused when the file's folder now resolves outside the
        # workspace, the file became a link, or it has another hard link (st_nlink > 1, checked on the opened file
        # before it is truncated; resolve() cannot see a hard link); reading such a file is allowed
    def list(self, path: str = ".", depth: int = 2) -> str   # tree text, dirs end with "/", skips .git, sizes;
        # folders named `.scratch` are shown collapsed like the NO_EXPAND ones (".scratch/ (2 entries)"), so the
        # agents' temporary files do not inflate every listing; list(".scratch/<slug>") lists them; tree() (the
        # web file tree) shows them
    def tree(self, path: str = ".", depth: int = 4) -> list[dict]   # for the web UI: [{"path","type","size","mtime"}]
    def read_raw(self, path: str, max_bytes: int = 2_000_000) -> tuple[str, bool]  # (text, truncated) for UI
    def lock(self, actor: str, path: str, minutes: float | None = None) -> str
    def unlock(self, actor: str, path: str, force: bool = False) -> str   # force for USER (file_unlock)
    def locks(self) -> list[dict]                # [{"path","owner","acquired_at","expires_at"}]
    def check_writable(self, actor: str, path: str) -> None
    def release_all(self, actor: str) -> int     # retire: also drops the actor's own lock waits, then settles
    def expire_locks(self) -> int                # never settles (below)
    def settle_waiters(self) -> int              # the waiters woken; never raises ("Lock waiters" below)
    def waits_for_lock(self, name: str) -> bool  # a lock_waiters row of `name` (one indexed query)
    def lock_waits(self, name: str) -> list[str]  # the paths `name` waits for, the oldest first
    def awaited_locks(self, name: str) -> list[str]  # lock_waits whose release wakes it ([] once the goal is done)
    def write_mark(self) -> tuple[int, frozenset[str]]   # write_file/edit_file writes: sequence, paths in flight
    # (a write whose call is cancelled stays in flight until its thread ends, then emits its file.changed)
    def written_since(self, mark, key: str) -> bool   # ... of path key `key` in flight at `mark` or since (§8)
    def held_locks_note(self, actor: str) -> str  # the task_complete reminder ("" when it holds no lock)
    async def autocommit(self, actor: str, message: str = "", *, kind: str = "", detail: str = "",
                         skipped: list[str] | None = None, hold: bool = False) -> str | None
        # commits everything except `.scratch/` and nested repositories as `actor`, one commit per call; commit hash
        # or None (nothing outside .scratch changed). The message is `message` as given or, with `kind` ("shell",
        # "job j3", "jobs j3, j5"), commit_message(kind, the paths staged after `git add`, detail): the subject names
        # the changed files, the body holds `detail` (the command that changed them). `skipped` receives the paths
        # of the nested repositories left out. `hold` (the `shell` tool and the jobs pass it): new untracked files
        # wait one more command ("Held new files" below; `ended`: the serial of the command whose end the commit
        # follows, None when none has ended); without it everything is committed now, held files of anyone
        # included, and nothing stays held. Returns the last commit made (a commit of held files included)
    async def commit_held(self, actor: str | None, when: str, *, leaving: bool = False) -> str | None
        # a flush: the actor's task completion or turn end counts as its next command for the held files once none
        # of its commands running when they were first seen is left (`leaving`: it is no suspect any more); the
        # files no longer waiting for anyone are committed, each under its owner (None: every held file); `when`
        # ends the note of the commit ("at the end of Anna Smith's turn"); never raises; no git call when nothing
        # becomes committable
    def held(self) -> dict[str, HeldFile]
        # path -> HeldFile(owner, kind, detail, stamp, others, waiting, running, after)
    def nested_repos_note(self, actor: str, paths: list[str]) -> str
        # the line for the actor's tool result about them ("" when none is new to this actor in this session)
    def mtime(self, path: str) -> float | None
    def exists(self, path: str) -> bool
```
Writes/edits check locks, create parent dirs, write UTF-8, emit `file.changed` {path, op} (the actor is
the event's top-level `actor`), then commit that path; a path under `.scratch/` is written and emits
`file.changed` but is never committed, and the result says so (`Created .scratch/anna.smith/c.py (1 line, 9 B)
(in .scratch/: not committed).`). In a thread session (`Workspace.commit_events`) a whole-tree autocommit and each
per-owner commit of held new files also emit `files.committed` (§22.2), which `file` subscriptions follow (§22.3);
`file.changed` itself is unchanged. Lock events: `file.locked` {path, owner, expires_at, refreshed},
`file.unlocked` {path, owner, forced} or {path, owner, expired: true}. Unless the folder is adopted (below),
`init()` also writes repo-local settings (`_configure_repo`: core.autocrlf=false, commit.gpgsign=false, on
Windows core.longpaths=true, and a default identity), so that git commands run from the shell behave like the
autocommits (line endings, long paths, no signing); an agent's own commits carry its identity from the shell
environment (`agent_git_env`, below).

**Lock waiters.** A lock is advisory: only `write_file`, `edit_file` and `lock_file` check it (`shell` does not).
A lock blocks another owner's lock on the same path, a folder above it or a path under it, and another owner's
write or edit of a path it covers. These refusals, and a member's `lock_file` unlock=true of someone else's lock,
are English ToolErrors that keep `'{rel}' is locked by X until HH:MM (N min left)[ (lock on '{path}')]` (the unlock:
`…, not by you: only they can unlock it.`) and end with ``You will be notified when it is free; there is no need to
message them. Meanwhile do other work, or call `wait` if nothing else is left.`` (`wait_for_events` for a member
whose tools have no `wait`, an external one: `frozen.member_tool_names`). Only a member is recorded (`is_member`;
the user's own unlock without force says `Pass force=true to unlock it anyway.`, a name outside the swarm `Try again
once it is unlocked.`): one `lock_waiters` row per member and path (compared through `_norm`; a repeat keeps its
first `since`). A successful own lock clears the actor's rows that it covers, a passing write or edit the row of
that path, so no stale note follows. `settle_waiters()` (after `unlock`, after `release_all` that released
something, and at every scheduler tick, §3): every row whose path no live lock of another owner overlaps any more
is collected (an expired row counts as free, deleted or not; a row of a member that left is deleted silently); each
such member gets ONE waking `n_lock_free` {paths} (at most `WAITERS_SHOWN` = 10 named, then ` (+N)`) and its rows
are deleted; once the goal is done the notice is quiet (like a job's end, §7.1), so a finished session, also one
reopened later, wakes nobody about a lock. Every waiter of a freed path is woken (no queue): the first to lock it
wins, the others are refused and recorded again.
`expire_locks()` never settles: it also runs lazily inside a waiter's own retry, which would
otherwise get a "free" note for what it has just taken; the tick settles within 3 s (also an expiry found by
`locks()` in a snapshot, or the rows left before a restart: the table persists). After the free rows,
`settle_waiters` tells the holders (`_tell_holders`; also at each refusal, for the lock that refused): a live lock
with `wanted_at` NULL that rows of other members overlap, held (`now - acquired_at`) for at least `[workspace]
lock_wanted_minutes` (default 5; 0: at once), gets ONE waking `n_lock_wanted` {path, held (`jobs.fmt_duration` in
the holder's language), waiters} to its owner, then `wanted_at = now`; `waiters` lists each waiting member in
`since` order, with its in_progress and waiting tasks as `lock_waiter_task` ("Anna Smith (task #7 Parser)"; a
crew task with open directions left out, a direction named `#15 pkce (direction of #7)`, §4.2). A holder of
nested locks of its own (a folder and a file in it) gets one notice: its locks that overlap a told one are marked
told with it (also one taken later). Nothing is told while the goal is done (the lock stays untold). A refresh keeps
`wanted_at` (the same lock), a new lock starts untold. The user's `file_unlock` {path} (§12) calls `unlock(USER,
path, force=True)`: `Unlocked docs (it was locked by Anna Smith).`, `file.unlocked` {path, owner, forced: true}, the
waiters woken, the holder told nothing; a path that is not itself locked is a ToolError naming the folder lock that
covers it (`'docs/a.md' is not locked itself: it is under the lock on 'docs' (Anna Smith); unlock 'docs'
instead.`), or the locks there are (`Locked now: a.md (Boris King).`, up to 10), or `no file is locked now`. The
user reaches it through the web Files tab's Unlock link (§18.4), `/unlock path` in the terminal UI (docs/TUI.md) and
in the line console (`dreamteam console`), and an MCP user client.

The whole-tree autocommit (after every `shell` call): `ensure_scratch()` (an agent may have deleted the marker),
`git status --porcelain -z` (`porcelain_entries`), `git reset -q -- .scratch` when something under `.scratch/` is
staged (a manual `git add -f`; it only resets index entries to HEAD), nothing more when nothing outside `.scratch/`
changed, else `git add -A --ignore-errors -- . ":(exclude)[.]scratch" ":(exclude)[.]scratch/*"`
(`SCRATCH_EXCLUDES`, with pathspec magic, `literal=False`; plus the nested repositories; with `hold`, `git add -u`
instead, "Held new files" below) and a commit of the index without a pathspec (a merge an
agent left in progress concludes as before). With `kind`, its message is built from `git diff --cached --name-only
--no-renames -z` (`_index_message`; a rename shows as its old and its new path, deleted files are named; a failed
diff quotes the detail instead). The excludes are spelled with `[.]`: git add takes a literal
`:(exclude).scratch` as naming the folder and, when the root `.gitignore` ignores `.scratch/` (`DEFAULT_GITIGNORE`
does), reports it as an ignored path and exits 1 on every autocommit, burying real add errors in the log. Path
commits of `write`/`edit` keep literal pathspecs (`-- rel`).

**Nested repositories** (`_nested_repos`): an agent that runs `git init` in a generated project (e.g.
`examples/lab_project/a`, or a folder literally named `--help`) leaves an untracked folder with its own `.git`;
`git add -A` would commit it as a gitlink (mode 160000) without a `.gitmodules` entry, an empty reference nobody
can check out. Before `git add`, the untracked folders of the status (`git status --porcelain -z
--untracked-files=normal`, whatever the user's `status.showUntrackedFiles`, which `git add -A` ignores; `??`
entries that are directories, outside `.scratch/`; up to `NESTED_PATHSPECS_MAX` = 100 of them by name, else all) go to `git ls-files --others
--exclude-standard -z -- <folder>/...` (literal pathspecs after `--`): it stops at a nested repository and names it
with a trailing `/`, also one deep inside an untracked folder, which `git status` shows only as that folder. Those
with a `.git` (folder or file) are excluded with `:(exclude,literal)<path>` and passed to the caller (`skipped`).
Ignored folders are never listed, and tracked submodules (an adopted project's own, with `.gitmodules`) are
tracked, so they are left as they are. The `shell` tool appends one line to its result, each path named once per
session to that member (`Workspace._nested_reported`, in memory), at most `NESTED_SHOWN` = 5 paths + "and N more":
`Not committed: examples/lab_project/a, --help — folders with their own .git (nested repositories). Delete their
.git or move them into your scratch folder .scratch/<slug>/ if they are temporary.` Job commits leave them out the
same way without a note (the owner's next `shell` call names them); `write_file` / `edit_file` commit one path
and cannot create one. The initial "Initialize workspace" commit (`init_repo`, also for an adopted folder that was
not a repository yet) leaves them out as well (`nested_repo_paths` of `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
-z`); the first `shell` autocommit afterwards names them to the agent.

#### Held new files
A test run often leaves files that the next run deletes (cookiecutter's test hooks: `…/test-hooks/hooks/
post_gen_project.bat (+2 more)` added by one `shell` commit, deleted by the next). So the `shell` and job autocommits
(`hold=True`) commit changes to tracked files (edits, deletions, renames) at once as before, but a **new untracked
file** only once it has outlived one more command; a held file that vanished meanwhile never enters the history, and
history is never rewritten.
- The untracked files are those `git add -A` would add: the `??` files of the status and, for its `??` folders,
  `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` (the listing that finds nested repositories; `_untracked` maps each
  file to its `??` entry). Not `.scratch/`, not inside a nested repository, not ignored.
- Commands are told apart by `RunningCommand.serial` (one counter per process, `shell.last_serial()` the last one
  started): `jobs.running_commands()` = (serial -> member of every foreground `shell` call and running job, the last
  serial). The `shell` tool passes `ended` = its command's serial when the command has ended (None when it goes on as
  a job), a job's end commit its command's serial, a job commit while processes of it still run None.
- `Workspace._held` (in memory; path -> `HeldFile(owner, kind, detail, stamp, others, waiting, running, after)`): a
  file not held yet is held with the autocommit's actor as `owner` (the member whose commit first saw it), that
  commit's `kind` and `detail` (the command) and its (size, mtime) `stamp`. Git cannot tell who wrote a file, so the
  suspects are the owner and, as `others`, every member with a command running then or an autocommit of its own
  waiting for the git lock (`_queued`: the end of a command queues its commit at once, with no await in between),
  taken right after the file listing. `running`: the commands running then (the owner's own job too, e.g. its test
  run that went on as a job while it reads the log). `waiting`: the suspects whose next command the file has not
  outlived yet. A suspect's next command is one that ended (`ended`) with a serial above `after[member]`: the last
  serial at first sight, or, for a member with commands in `running`, the last serial when the last of them had
  ended and its commit was made (`_settle_held`, at every hold commit and flush) — so neither a command running when
  the file appeared, nor its own end commit, nor a quick command started while it still ran counts. Every
  whole-tree autocommit first forgets held paths no longer untracked (deleted, ignored now, committed by
  `write_file` / `edit_file` or by hand: those commit their file at once as before).
- At each `hold` autocommit of a member: a held file with another stamp (deleted and written again by the next run)
  is held anew, as a new file of this commit; one with its stamp counts the command for that member. Files no longer
  waiting for anyone have outlived the next command of every member that may have written them and are committed
  first, in a commit of their own per command that left them, under their owner: `git add -A --ignore-errors --
  <paths>` and `git commit -- <paths>` (only those paths), subject `commit_message(f"{kind} (new files)", paths)` ("shell (new files): src/new.py"), body the original
  command and `HELD_NOTE`: "New files first seen after this command of Anna Smith, committed after the next command
  of Anna Smith left them in place: a new file waits until it outlives one more command, so leftovers that the next
  command deletes (of a test run, say) never enter the history." With `others` it adds " (Boris King also had a
  command running then; git cannot tell who wrote a file)" after the owner and reads "after the next commands of
  Anna Smith and Boris King". Then the call's own commit: `git add -u --ignore-errors -- . <SCRATCH_EXCLUDES>`
  (tracked files only) and, for a tracked file moved with plain `mv` (`_moved`: a new file whose blob id, `git
  hash-object --stdin-paths`, equals that of a file the call deleted in HEAD, `git cat-file --batch-check` of
  `HEAD:<path>` lines through stdin, any number of them; exact content, at most `MOVED_CANDIDATES_MAX` = 500 new
  files), `git add -- <new paths>`, so the rename stays one commit; then the index commit as before. When every
  change outside `.scratch/` is a new file (all `??`), nothing was moved and no git operation is halfway
  (`_operation_in_progress`: GIT_OPERATIONS in the workspace's own `.git` folder; without one the commit is tried),
  there is nothing to stage: no `git add -u`, no index commit tried.
- Another member's commit never sweeps them up: with `hold` no untracked file but a moved one is staged, so every
  held file stays out, and a file a command still running creates between the status and the add waits for the next
  autocommit. The hold belongs to the tree, not to an actor: a tester's test run that leaves files while a
  developer's quick command ends is first seen by the developer's commit, and waits for the tester's next run too
  (which deletes them: nothing enters the history). The commit of held files is attributed to their owner, and its
  body names the other suspects (HELD_OTHERS). Paths of a commit of held files are collapsed: an untracked
  folder all of whose files go into it is named once (`_collapse`; never one holding a nested repository).
- Flush points (`commit_held(actor, when)`): the actor's boundary counts as its next command for every held file it
