  -- python -m dreamteam ARGS`: the hub never keeps NET_ADMIN, and it runs as root with the offline group, so what it
  creates (files of `write_file`, `.git`) is the commands' to write without a set-group-id bit on any folder. A
  failure (an old image, no owner match) prints a warning, and the sessions without network get "env".
  `Swarm._prepare_offline` (at start, before `Workspace.init()`, and when the setting turns "off") runs
  `netoff.prepare_workspace(root)` for
  "docker": an entry root owns (or the image's `dreamteam-agent`, of an earlier run) gets the group GID with the
  owner's bits copied to the group (a read-only entry, e.g. the skills mirror, stays read-only); what UID owns already
  and what anyone else owns is left as it is. It walks by file descriptors (`os.fwalk`, each entry opened with
  `O_NOFOLLOW`, then `fchown`/`fchmod`): the members' commands may run meanwhile, and a file swapped for a symlink
  must not get root's chmod on its target. A session switched off later in a container started without the firewall
  gets "env" (shown "container") until the sandbox restarts. `DREAMTEAM_OFFLINE_USER` and
  `DREAMTEAM_OFFLINE_FIREWALL` never reach the agents' environment (`shell._INTERNAL_ENV`).
- **MCP servers.** Their command and environment go through `netoff.command`. A command that names a URL of another
  machine (`netoff.remote_url`: http(s)/ws(s), not localhost, 127.x, ::1 or *.localhost; a stdio bridge such as
  `npx mcp-remote https://...`) is refused with a ToolError before it starts. A change of the setting closes the
  running connections (`MCPForge.close_connections`): each starts again with the new setting at its next use. Each
  connection records the setting it was started with (`MCPConnection.offline`): `_open` never hands out one of the
  other setting, and `_connect` starts a server again when the setting changed while it was starting (once; a second
  change is a ToolError to call again).
- **Skills.** `EnvManager.plan(..., network=False)` gives a skill of the agent trust class (`trust_class(frm)`, §19:
  a member's proposal, a `claude-project` skill) no install: state
  `off`, reason `network` (`deps_reason_network`, UI `sk_reason_network`), unless its environment is ready on disk
  already; the plan key includes the setting, and a change replans (`SessionSkills.replan`). The user's own skills
  install as before: DreamTeam installs them, not an agent.
- **Git.** DreamTeam's own git never runs hooks, an fsmonitor command or what else the members may have named in the
  repository's config (filter, textconv, diff and merge drivers, ssh and credential helpers, included files,
  config-based hooks, a submodule's own), with or without network, and its environment is filtered of secrets like
  the agents', whatever `shell.pass_env` lets through to them (§7 "DreamTeam's own git"). Under "docker" and "netns"
  every git DreamTeam runs for the session also runs like the members' commands (the workspace's from before `init()`
  on, held while the setting turns "off" until `_prepare_offline` is done; sessions.py's checks and commits:
  `Workspace.git_isolated`, `_Plan.network_off`, `hubgit.run(offline=True)`: the offline user's ids or the session's
  namespace; §7 "Defense in depth"): a key added at the very moment of DreamTeam's call, or one in the "global" config
  the members can write under "netns", runs with their rights and without network (the offline user's global config in
  the Docker sandbox is disarmed like the repository's).
- **Telling the members.** `render_wake` (the wake-up and the incoming news) first calls `Swarm._tell_network(name)`:
  the member's last `n_network_off` / `n_network_on` notification is the state it knows; when that differs from the
  setting, a quiet one (wake=False) is added. Each member is told once, also across restarts, and again when the user
  switches it back; no system prompt changes. `swarm_status` adds `; NO NETWORK for the members' commands, jobs and
  MCP servers (<isolation>)` to the state.
- **A change while running** (`Swarm.reconfigure` → `_network_changed`): new commands get the new setting at once;
  running jobs keep the one they started with.
- The snapshot's `swarm.network` is `netoff.describe(config)` = {"mode": "on"|"off", "isolation": kind or null (not
  detected yet)}; the session summary has `network` ("on"/"off"); the launcher's `GET /api/settings` has
  `network_isolation`.

## 8. Triggers (triggers.py)

Condition DSL: a Python *expression* parsed with `ast` and evaluated by a whitelist interpreter
(never `eval`). Allowed: `and or not`, comparisons `== != < <= > >= in not in`, literals (str, int,
float, bool, None, tuple/list/set of literals), bare status names (`todo in_progress waiting review
done failed cancelled`) evaluate to strings, function calls below (positional + keyword). Max 500
chars / 200 AST nodes.

| function | value |
|---|---|
| `status(id)` | status string, `"missing"` if no task |
| `done(*ids)` | all done |
| `any_done(*ids)` | at least one done |
| `finished(*ids)` | all terminal (done/failed/cancelled) |
| `failed(*ids)` | at least one failed |
| `assignee(id)` | assignee or None |
| `count(status=None, tag=None, assignee=None, parent=None)` | number of matching tasks (status may be a tuple) |
| `all_done(tag=None, parent=None)` | ≥1 matching task and all done |
| `message(sender=None, contains=None)` | a message to the owner arrived after creation/last fire |
| `comment(task=None, sender=None, contains=None)` | a discussion post (not by the owner) after creation/last fire |
| `file_exists(path)` / `file_changed(path)` | workspace file exists / the file changed since creation/last fire and that run of changes has settled, not counting the owner's own edits (below); a path outside the workspace (a UNC or device path included, never resolved) is false |
| `after("2026-10-09 18:00")` | local time reached (ISO) |
| `elapsed(seconds)` | seconds since creation |
| `every(seconds)` | ≥ seconds since last fire (min 10); makes the trigger periodic |
| `agent_status(name)` | member status |
| `goal_done()` | global goal status is done |

In a thread session (§22.5) the engine refuses at creation, on every surface, a condition that calls a task function
(`status`, `done`, `any_done`, `finished`, `failed`, `assignee`, `count`, `all_done`, `comment`) or uses a bare
task-status name, and the `set_status` and `create_task` actions; its errors end with `GRAMMAR_THREAD` /
`ACTIONS_HELP_THREAD`. No function reads the forum in v1: posts and comments are followed with subscriptions.

```python
class TriggerEngine:
    tick_seconds: float = 2.0
    def __init__(self, swarm): ...
    def validate(self, condition: str) -> None              # ToolError with its mode's grammar summary on error
    def create(self, owner: str, condition: str, *, note: str = "", actions: list[dict] | None = None,
               once: bool = True) -> dict
    def delete(self, actor: str, trigger_id: int) -> None    # owner or USER
    def list(self, owner: str | None = None, include_inactive: bool = False) -> list[dict]
    def mark_dirty(self) -> None
    def evaluate_all(self) -> int                            # returns number fired; then the held notices due
    async def run(self) -> None                              # loop: wait dirty-or-tick, evaluate_all; the files
                                                             # the active triggers watch are stat'd (and their
                                                             # file_changed() paths resolved) in a thread first
    def release_held(self, owner: str) -> None               # the held fires of owner's triggers, quietly; never
                                                             # raises (Swarm.render_wake, §6.3)
    def pending(self, trigger_id: int) -> list[tuple[str, int, float | None]]   # file_changed() changes not fired
                                                             # yet: (path, changes, seconds since the latest)
    def create_notes(self, trigger: dict) -> list[str]       # the trigger_create result's notes (§12)
    def unattended(self, now: float) -> bool                 # an active trigger may still fire while nobody acts
                                                             # and its fire reaches an LLM member ("Unattended
                                                             # triggers" below; Swarm.team_asleep, §3)
```
`create` resolves member names in the condition (`sender=` of message/comment, `assignee=` of count,
`agent_status(name)`) with `swarm.resolve_member(allow_retired=True)` (a unique first name, `@Name`, any
case; agent_status does not accept the user) and stores the condition rewritten (`ast.unparse`) with the
canonical names; an unknown member is a ToolError at creation. Evaluation compares names exactly
(case/whitespace-insensitive).
Fires on false→true edge (and on every evaluation where it is true if it uses `every`); a trigger
true at creation fires on the first evaluation. `once` → deactivated after firing. Actions
(default `[{"type": "wake"}]`): `wake` → `notify(owner, "n_trigger", id, condition, note)`, or
`n_trigger_files` {id, condition, changes, note} when file_changed() files changed since the last fire, or
`n_trigger_held` while fires are held (both below);
`message` {to, text} → `mail.send(owner, to, text, automatic=True)` (a user-owned trigger's message never answers
a question pause, §3.1); `set_status` {task_id, status} →
`board.update(owner, ...)`; `create_task` {title, goal?, description?, assignee?, tags?, priority?} (both board
sessions only: refused in a thread session, §22.5).
Action errors are stored in `last_error` and reported to the owner via `n_trigger` note. Evaluation
errors are stored in `last_error`, not fired. After a fire, `message()`/`comment()`/`file_changed()`/`every()`
are measured from that fire. A repeating trigger with message/set_status/create_task actions that fires 20
times within 10 s is deactivated and its owner is told why (flood guard). The engine listens to the bus: `task.*`, `message.*`,
`file.*`, `goal.*`, `agent.*` mark it dirty. Events: `trigger.created`, `trigger.fired`, `trigger.deleted`.
Trigger dict: {"id","owner","condition","note","actions","once","active","created_at","last_fired","fire_count",
"last_error","held","told_at","wake_at"} (`wake_at` = told_at + `trigger_wake_seconds` while fires are held by an
active trigger and the limit is on, else None).

**file_changed(): one fire per settled run of changes.** `file_changed(path)` is true when the file changed since
the reference point (its signature (mtime_ns, size) differs from the one at creation or the last fire, or its run
counted a change, also one that left the signature as it was; after a restart its mtime is newer) *and* that run of
changes has settled. Once and repeating triggers use the same rule; the edge, `once`, `every()` and and/or/not apply
to its value as to any function. The engine keeps a run per trigger and path in memory:
- Count = the `file.changed` events of the path from other actors (write_file/edit_file, with the editor's name) +
  the changes no event explains (commands, jobs). The owner's own write_file/edit_file edits do not count, so own
  edits alone do not fire it; its commands and jobs are unattributed and count. A pass takes
  `Workspace.write_mark()` before it probes: for a path that a write_file/edit_file write was writing then, or
  started writing since (`written_since`), the probe may show the file before the write or in the middle of it
  (opened, truncated, then written), so the pass is unsure of the path: its probe is not used (the run's signature
  does not move) and it does not settle the run by the editors' turns. A sure pass's probe shows every write whose
  event came since the previous sure pass, finished (a path stays in flight until its write's event): a new
  signature is explained when at least one event of the path came in between, and is one change no event explains
  when none did. So two writes of commands between two sure passes count as one, and a command's change between
  them together with an edit is not counted apart from it; together with only the owner's own edits it is not
  counted at all, so it is not told (the probe cannot tell it from those writes, which do not count; the command
  has to land after the last sure pass, at most one tick before the edit). A fire in an unsure pass takes the new
  run's baseline from the next sure probe, without counting it (the edits the new run counted by then are in it; a
  command's change before it is not counted); an edit of another actor that the new run has counted by then (that
  write's event came after the fire) is told as any run's count. A trigger created while a write of its file is in
  flight takes its baseline the same way; one created while a pass waits for its stat takes nothing from that pass's
  probe, which is older than its baseline (if another part of its condition fires it in that pass, the new run takes
  its baseline from the next sure probe, as above). The count of a run never goes down, and its cap counts from its
  first counted change; the times of a run followed in memory are at most now (a wall clock set back does not hold
  it).
  Events and probed paths are compared by `workspace.path_key` of the workspace-relative path (case-insensitive on
  Windows), the condition's path resolved like the probe.
- Settled when the count is > 0 and: no change (anyone's, the owner's included) for `[agents] file_settle_seconds`
  (60; 0: at the first pass that sees a change), or every change is explained by an event and every other editor is
  an AI agent whose runtime is not WORKING (one without a runtime, e.g. retired, counts as done; an external member
  or the user as an editor leaves it to the quiet window), or `file_max_wait_seconds` (300; 0: no cap) passed since
  the first counted change. The end of the editors' turns emits `agent.status`, so the fire comes at the next pass;
  while the swarm is paused no runtime is WORKING, so a pending run settles then. During an unsettled run
  file_changed() is false, so `not file_changed(p)` stays true until it settles. While the file is missing
  file_changed() is false and its run stays pending, past the quiet window and the cap alike (the file's return is
  itself a change: the run is then told by the same rule, at once if the cap has passed); a deletion alone is not a
  change.
- When another part of the condition fires first (`file_changed('a') or message()`, `every()`), the unsettled run is
  absorbed: the fire starts new runs, as everything is measured from the fire, and its notice lists the file as still
  changing.
- The notice: `n_trigger_files` {id, condition, changes, note}, `changes` = one fragment per file with changes
  (`trigger_file_settled` {path, count, by, quiet}: "File docs/AUDIT.md was changed (changes: 7, by Anna Smith); the
  last change was 2 min ago."; `trigger_file_changing` {path, count, by, duration} for a run fired by the cap or
  absorbed: "File x is still changing (changes: 11, by Anna Smith in 5 min)."; `by` = `trigger_file_by` naming at
  most 5 editors, then "(+N)"). Without changes the plain `n_trigger`. `trigger.fired` carries `files`
  [{path, changes, by, settled}] then.
- After a restart (or for a trigger another engine followed) the runs are seeded from the journal: the
  `file.changed` events since the reference point (their times, at most now; the cap counts from the first event of
  another actor); a newer mtime with no such event counts as one change no event explains, whose quiet window and
  cap start now, so each restart postpones both for that change (a write in flight at that pass is no such change:
  its event counts it, and the next sure probe is the baseline). The events of any actor, the owner's included, stand
  for the file's changes: with one in the journal, a command's change next to it is not counted, also one the run
  had counted in memory before the restart, so it is not told. A reseeded trigger still needs an mtime newer than its
  reference: a counted edit older than that (a write stored before the fire, a clock set back) stays pending and is
  told with the next change, and a command's change before a clock set back can count as a change after a trigger
  created since. No schema change.

**Wake limit.** A member's (an AI agent's or an external member's) repeating trigger wakes its owner at most once per
`[agents] trigger_wake_seconds` (180; 0: at every fire), counted from the last time it told the owner anything
(`told_at`). A fire within the interval runs in full (fire_count, last_fired, the reference point, the actions);
only its notice is held: `held` + 1, `held_last`, and its file_changed() changes merged into
`held_files` (counts summed, editors joined). The user's triggers, once triggers and the flood guard's notice are
never held; `every()` triggers are limited like the others. The held fires reach the owner in ONE `n_trigger_held`
{id, condition, count, since, last, interval, changes, note} ("Trigger #4 fired again since it last told you at
18:40 (fires: 3, the last at 18:46): file_changed('docs/AUDIT.md'). File … A repeating trigger wakes you at most
once every 3 min."), whichever comes first: the owner's next render_wake for any reason (§6.3: quiet, no wake of
its own), a fire after the interval (that fire's notice, with count = held + 1), or the end of the interval
(evaluate_all after each pass: waking; a clock gone back, told_at in the future, releases too). A release's note
carries the last action error (`Trigger action errors: …`, not an evaluation error). Fires held when the limit was
switched off (`trigger_wake_seconds` = 0) come as `n_trigger_held_off` (the same text without the interval
sentence) at the next pass or fire. Notices are never told twice:
whichever releases first sets `told_at` and clears `held`. The set of owners with held fires is rebuilt from the
table when the engine starts; held fires survive a restart. A trigger made inactive (its owner left) keeps them
untold (`wake_at` None). No new event type: every fire still emits `trigger.fired`, whose trigger dict carries
`held` / `wake_at`; a release emits only its `notification`. The limit is per trigger and only for triggers:
lock (`n_lock_free`) and job wake-ups are not limited, and a trigger's message action still wakes its recipients at
every fire (the flood guard limits those).

**Unattended triggers.** `unattended(now)` (for `Swarm.team_asleep`, §3 scheduler item 9) is true when an active
trigger both reaches an LLM member and may still fire while nobody acts:
- *Reaches an LLM member*: its owner is an LLM member and its actions include `wake` (the default when there are
  none), or its actions include `message` to "all" or to a name that resolves to an LLM member (not to "user" or
  only to external members), `set_status` or `create_task`. A trigger of USER or of an external member that only
  wakes its owner does not count (an hourly `every(3600)` reminder of the user's keeps no LLM member awake).
- *May fire unattended*: it holds fires (`held` > 0: the end of the wake limit's interval releases them with a wake,
  "Wake limit"); or its condition uses a time function and the next moment it can come true has not passed by more
  than `UNATTENDED_GRACE` (10 s): `elapsed(s)` → created_at + s, `after(t)` → t, `every(p)` → (last_fired or
  created_at) + p, with several of them the latest (read from their literal arguments). A moment that passed
  without a fire means another part of the condition holds it back (`elapsed(60) and done(3)`): it waits for someone
  to act. Or its functions are only `file_exists` / `file_changed` (no time function): it counts for
  `UNATTENDED_FILE_SECONDS` (30 min) from its creation or last fire, then no longer (a process that died never
  writes the file); a condition that mixes files with board state counts like board state. So
  `file_exists("out/result.json") or elapsed(1800)`, which the team-asleep texts suggest, counts until its deadline.
- It does not count either when it is a repeating trigger that is not periodic and whose condition is true now
  (`last_value` = 1: it fires again only after the condition turns false), or when its condition reads board,
  message or agent state only (`status`, `done`, `count`, `message`, `comment`, `agent_status`, `goal_done`, …): it
  waits for someone to act.
One query over the active triggers (owner, condition, actions, once, created_at, last_fired, last_value, held), the
conditions compiled through the engine's cache (`CompiledCondition.elapsed` and `.after` keep the literal seconds and
moments, as `.every` keeps the periods); `UNATTENDED_GRACE` and `UNATTENDED_FILE_SECONDS` are module constants
of triggers.py. The check never fires, evaluates or changes a trigger.

## 9. Event types (bus)

`task.created task.updated task.comment message.sent notification goal.set goal.completed
goal.reopened agent.hired agent.retired agent.status agent.activity agent.compacted agent.usage
file.changed file.locked file.unlocked trigger.created trigger.fired trigger.deleted
mcp.created mcp.status swarm.paused swarm.resumed swarm.wrap_up swarm.limits job.started job.ended
skill.attached skill.detached skill.proposed skill.library skill.deps session.started session.stopped
post.created post.updated post.comment post.vote subscription.changed files.committed` (the last six: the thread
mode, §22.2)

`session.started` {} and `session.stopped` {reason: `user` | `done` | `budget` | `shutdown` | `restart` | `failed`,
error?}, actor None: the session manager journals them into the session's own journal when a run starts (right before
the swarm starts, so the run's own start events follow it) and when it ends (after its agents stopped and before its
database closes; a start that failed carries `error`, its absolute paths named by their last component). A start
refused by the checks before the swarm starts journals nothing. Neither changes the session's `last_activity`
(§17.2) or an import's comparison of histories (§20.4). The reasons and the rules are in §21.6; the web feed and the
TUI's verbose feed show them as a line of their own.

`skill.attached` {name, from, files, replaced: bool, via, attached_via} and `skill.detached` {name, via}, actor = the
user (§19); `via` is the surface (`act`, `mcp`, `launcher-mcp`; `role` for the skills a role brings), `attached_via`
`user`, `role:<Role>` or `create`. `skill.proposed` {name, owner, files, replaced: bool}, actor = the member who
proposed it; `skill.library` {name, owner, status: saved or rejected, comment, via}, actor = the user (a decision
on a stopped session's files emits none). The feeds (web, TUI) name the owner of a decided proposal ("saved Ann
Lee's skill x to the library") and the surface of a skill change an MCP client made ("(via MCP)", "(via the launcher
MCP)"; the user's own surfaces `act`, `home`, `cli`, `role`, `create` are not named): a save no UI click made shows
as such. `skill.deps` {name, ecosystem: python | node, status: installing | ready |
failed, files, env, key, installer?, reused: bool, seconds?, error?}, actor None: a skill's script dependencies,
emitted by every session that has the skill when a build really starts and when it ends (§19 "Script
dependencies").

`trigger.fired` {trigger, errors, files?}, actor = the trigger's owner, at every fire (also one whose notice is held
by the wake limit, §8): `trigger` is the trigger dict, with `held` and `wake_at`; `files` [{path, changes, by,
settled}] only when file_changed() files changed since the last fire. The web feed and the TUI's verbose feed add
"(wake-up held until 18:48)" / «(пробуждение отложено до 18:48)» to a fire with `held` > 0.

`swarm.wrap_up` {on: bool}, actor = who switched it (the user, or the actor of the set_goal / reopen_goal that ended
it).

`swarm.paused` {reason, asker?, message_id?, since?, question?}, actor = who paused it: reason `question` (a
member's question, §3.1) carries asker, message_id and since, actor the asker; a budget pause that ends a question
pause carries `question` {asker, message_id, outcome, answer_id?, why?} of that question. `swarm.resumed`
{question?: {asker, message_id, outcome: answered | dropped, answer_id?, why?: resumed | clarify_off | left}}, actor
= who resumed (the user for an answer); `question` only when the resume ends a question pause. There are no event
types of their own for questions: the question and the answer are `message.sent` events, and the notices are
`notification` events (kinds in §3.1).

`job.started` {job} and `job.ended` {job: … + `duration` (seconds)} carry the public job dict (§7.1), actor = the
job's owner; a job's output is never sent as events. `agent.retired` also carries `jobs` (the ids of the jobs it
stopped), `agent.compacted` `tools_revision` (§6.1).

Live-only events (sent with the EventBus method `publish(type, actor, **data)` instead of `emit`: delivered to
listeners and WebSocket subscribers with id None, not journaled): `trace.started`, `trace.span`,
`trace.finished` (§16), `job.silent` {job} (a job turned silent or printed again, §7.1).

## 10. LLM (llm/)

```python
@dataclass class ToolCall: id: str; name: str; arguments: dict; parse_error: str | None = None
@dataclass class Usage: input_tokens: int = 0; output_tokens: int = 0; cache_read_tokens: int = 0;
                        cache_write_tokens: int = 0; cost_usd: float | None = None   # provider-reported
@dataclass class LLMResponse: text: str; tool_calls: list[ToolCall]; usage: Usage; stop_reason: str;
                              model: str; raw: dict | None = None; thinking: str = ""
class LLMError(Exception): message: str; retryable: bool; kind: str  # rate_limit auth bad_request server connection refusal other
class LLMClient(Protocol):
    profile: ModelProfile
    async def complete(self, system: str, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict], *,
                       max_tokens: int | None = None) -> LLMResponse
        # tools: [{"name","description","parameters"}]; stop_reason normalised to
        # "end_turn" | "tool_use" | "max_tokens" | "refusal" | "other"; max_tokens: this request's output limit
        # (None = profile.max_tokens; the agent passes it only to raise the limit after a cut-off reply, §6.2, and
        # only to a client whose complete() takes it, `accepts_max_tokens`). A raised limit also gets a request
        # timeout of its own (the client's timeout is derived from profile.max_tokens)
def estimate_tokens(obj) -> int    # ~ len(json)/3.5
def create_llm(profile: ModelProfile) -> LLMClient   # llm/__init__.py
# clients may also expose `async aclose()` to release their HTTP pool (called when an agent stops)
# stop_reason "other" covers pause_turn / stop_sequence and unknown values
def cost_of(profile: ModelProfile, usage: Usage, model: str | None = None) -> float
    # usage.cost_usd (the provider's cost) when set, else the tokens at profile.prices(model)
def uncounted_fields(profile: ModelProfile, usage: Usage, model: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]
    # the price fields whose tokens cost_of counted as $0: profile.missing_prices(model); () when usage.cost_usd is
    # set and for the scripted provider (tests and demos have no bill)
```
* **Prices** (config.py `ModelProfile`, USD per 1M tokens): `input_price`, `output_price`, `cache_read_price`,
  `cache_write_price`; None = not set, 0 = free. `prices(model)` takes the profile's price, else the built-in
  `KNOWN_PRICES` entry of the response's model or the profile's model (`_table(model)`, exact ids), else 0 (the
  cache prices: input × 0.1 / × 1.25). `PRICE_FIELDS = ("input_price", "output_price")`.
  `missing_prices(model)` → the PRICE_FIELDS that are None while `_table(model)` has no entry (their tokens count
  as $0); `price_source(model)` → `"none"` (both missing), `"partial"` (one), `"table"` (the built-in prices fill
  what is not set), `"free"` (both set to 0), `"profile"` (both set); `has_prices` = no missing prices. A call
  whose `uncounted_fields` is not empty is reported to the user once per start (`Swarm.record_usage`, §3:
  `u_cost_unknown`); a provider that reports the cost (`usage.cost_usd`) never is.
* **AnthropicLLM** (`anthropic.AsyncAnthropic`, SDK 1.x): converts neutral → Messages API (consecutive
  user-side items merged into one user message, tool_result blocks first; assistant uses `raw.content`
  verbatim when `raw.provider == "anthropic"`), top-level `cache_control={"type":"ephemeral"}`,
  `thinking={"type":"adaptive","display":...}` unless profile.thinking == "off", `output_config.effort`,
  `max_tokens`. Beta features (`fallbacks`, `thinking_mismatch` → `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior`)
  switch to `client.beta.messages.create(..., betas=[...])`; if the API rejects a beta parameter, the
  client disables betas for itself and retries once. On a 400 about an invalid thinking `signature`,
  retries once with all thinking blocks stripped. `raw.content` = `[b.to_dict(mode="json", exclude_none=True)]`.
  stop_reason `refusal` → LLMResponse with stop_reason "refusal" and text describing the category.
* **OpenAILLM** (`openai.AsyncOpenAI`, chat.completions, any compatible base_url): tool calls
  `function.arguments` JSON-parsed (failure → `parse_error`), `reasoning_effort` from profile.effort,
  max tokens param name from profile (default `max_completion_tokens` for api.openai.com, else
  `max_tokens`), `usage.cost` used when the provider reports it (OpenRouter).
* **ScriptedLLM(handler)**: `handler(system, messages, tools) -> LLMResponse | dict | str` (sync or
  async); dict shorthand `{"text": ..., "tool_calls": [{"name","arguments"}]}`; str = text only.

## 11. MCP forge (mcp_forge.py)

```python
class MCPConnection:      # one running stdio MCP server, owned by a dedicated asyncio task
    def __init__(self, name: str, command: list[str], cwd: Path, env: dict, log_path: Path): ...
    async def start(self, timeout: float) -> list[dict]      # tool list [{"name","description","input_schema"}]
    async def call(self, tool: str, arguments: dict, timeout: float) -> tuple[str, bool]
    async def close(self) -> None
    alive: bool

class MCPForge:
    def __init__(self, swarm): ...
    async def start(self) -> None     # register config.mcp.external servers (origin "config"); no processes yet;
                                      # refresh the stored cwd of forged/imported servers (server_dir: the
                                      # workspace may have moved, §17.2)
    async def stop(self) -> None
    async def create(self, actor: str, name: str, description: str, code: str, *, scope: str = "swarm",
                     task_id: int | None = None, requirements: list[str] | None = None,
                     save_to_library: bool = True) -> str
    def list(self, actor: str, query: str = "") -> list[dict]
    async def tools(self, actor: str, name: str) -> list[dict]
    async def call(self, actor: str, server: str, tool: str, arguments: dict | None = None,
                   timeout: float | None = None, max_chars: int | None = None) -> tuple[str, bool]
        # result cut to max_chars (default agents.tool_output_chars); mcp_call passes ToolContext.output_cap
    async def approve(self, actor: str, name: str, approve: bool, comment: str = "", digest: str = "") -> str
    async def remove(self, actor: str, name: str) -> str
    def get(self, name: str) -> dict | None
```
* Server code uses the mcp 2.x high-level API: `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer`,
  `mcp = MCPServer("name")`, `@mcp.tool()`, `mcp.run()` (stdio). Files: `workspace/mcp/<name>/server.py`,
  `meta.json` (the members' working copy, `server_dir`) and the snapshot `.dreamteam/mcp/<name>/server.py`
  (`snapshot_dir`: outside the workspace, where write_file and edit_file do not reach), the code that runs. Name:
  `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,39}$`.
* Command: `[sys.executable, "<snapshot_dir>/server.py"]`, or with requirements and `uv` on PATH:
  `["uv", "run", "--no-project", "--with", "mcp>=2.3,<3", "--with", req..., "python", "<snapshot_dir>/server.py"]`;
  cwd: the working copy's folder (files a server keeps next to itself stay there and are opened by relative paths:
  `__file__` is the snapshot's; other modules there are not imported: sys.path[0] is the snapshot's folder, which
  holds server.py only). A smoke test that failed with FileNotFoundError or ModuleNotFoundError adds this note
  (`SNAPSHOT_HINT`) to the create report.
  Env = `shell.scrubbed_env` (plus `COLUMNS=200` unless set: MCPServer logs through rich, whose 80-column boxes
  would wrap the error lines). stderr → `.dreamteam/logs/mcp-<name>.log`; the log tails shown to agents drop
  the padding and right borders of rich's boxed tracebacks. In a session without network the command and the
  environment go through `netoff.command`, and a command naming a remote URL is refused (§7.2).
* Client: `mcp.Client(mcp.stdio_client(StdioServerParameters(...), errlog=file))`; enter/exit inside the
  connection's own task (anyio requirement); `list_tools().tools[i].input_schema`; `call_tool(name, args)`
  → `CallToolResult(content, structured_content, is_error)`; text from TextContent, placeholders for
  other content, structured_content JSON when there is no text; truncated by MCPForge.call.
* `create`: write files, smoke test (start + list tools, startup_timeout), on failure status `failed`
  and return the error plus the log tail so the agent can fix and call create again (same name
  overwrites, only by owner or USER). Success → status `active` (or `pending` if
  `config.mcp.require_approval`, actor != USER and the snapshot's digest is not the record's `approved_digest` →
  notify USER kind `u_mcp_pending`). Statuses:
  `active`, `pending`, `failed`, `rejected`, `removed`, and `available` for library entries not yet
  imported. Origins: `workspace` (built here), `library`, `config`. Importing from the library also honours
  `require_approval`. Swarm-scoped servers
  are copied to the library (`config.library_dir/<name>/` server.py + meta.json) when save_to_library.
* Snapshots: `snapshot_digest(code, requirements)` = sha256 over `{"command":["python","server.py"],
  "requirements":[...]}` (compact ASCII JSON), a NUL byte and the bytes of server.py (the interpreter's path is the
  machine's, so it is left out). Columns `digest` (the snapshot's) and `approved_digest` (the last snapshot the user
  approved, or created: a USER `create` that becomes active). `create` writes the code to the working copy and the
  snapshot, smoke-tests the snapshot and records its digest; `remove` deletes the snapshot too. Before a forged or
  imported server starts (no live connection) and before `approve`, `_sync_snapshot` checks that the snapshot still
  hashes to `digest` and that the working copy is the same bytes (a missing working copy is written back from the
  snapshot). Otherwise the working copy is taken as a `create` of that code by the server's owner (`_rebuild`): a
  new snapshot, smoke-tested, then `failed`, `pending` (with `require_approval`, unless its digest is
  `approved_digest`; `u_mcp_pending` to USER) or `active`, announced as `mcp.created`; the library is not written
  then; an interrupted `_rebuild` (its caller cancelled) leaves the stored record as it was: its digest is not the
  new snapshot's, so the next start or `approve` tests the working copy again. A smoke-test process that started
  under the other network setting is closed instead of pooled (§7.2), in `create` too. So with `require_approval` an
  edit of the working copy never runs before the user approves it, and without it the edit is tested and used at
  the next start with no question. `approve` of a pending server whose working copy changed raises (the user is
  asked about the new snapshot); otherwise it approves the current snapshot (`approved_digest = digest`; a running
  connection stays, it runs that snapshot). Its `digest` (mcp_approve's optional argument: the record's
  `snapshot_digest`, in full or its first 8 or more hex digits, as `mcp_list`, the MCP card, the TUI dialog and
  `u_mcp_pending` show it; the dialog and the web card send the one they show, `/approve <name> <sha256>` in the
  console and the TUI takes it, and the TUI's `/approve <name>` alone sends the one of the last dialog shown for
  that server) refuses the approval when the record's digest does not start with it (the message shows the
  current one): the owner created the server again meanwhile. A rejection given with a `digest` (the HTTP API v1
  sends one, §21.5) is refused the same way; one without (the dialog, the card) rejects whatever waits. The TUI
  closes an open dialog whose server is created again with another digest and asks about the new code. A record of
  an older version has no digest: its first start tests the working
  copy again (with `require_approval` it waits for approval once); an `approve` of such a pending record tests it,
  raises with a plain message (recorded by an older version, without a snapshot) and leaves it pending with its new
  digest.
* Library and snapshots: `_copy_to_library` writes the snapshot's bytes, not the working copy, and meta.json gets
  `digest`, `approved_digest` (equal to `digest` when the user approved or created that code, else null) and
  `project`. An entry that another project saved is replaced only by the user's own `create` (an agent's save is
  skipped with a note), and an agent cannot replace an imported server whose entry another project keeps, whatever
  its owner's name. An import hashes the library's server.py: when that equals the entry's `approved_digest`, the
  server is `active` without a question even with `require_approval`; any other import as before. Approving a
  pending import records `approved_digest` in the entry while its server.py is still that code.
* Scopes: `private` (owner only), `task` (owner + creator/assignee/reviewer of task_id), `swarm` (all).
  USER sees all. `list` merges project servers and library entries not in the project (`origin: "library"`);
  using a library server imports it into the project first.
* Events: `mcp.created` {server}, `mcp.status` {name, status}. Server dict: {"name","owner","scope",
  "task_id","description","status","origin","tools":[names],"error","requirements","command","created_at",
  "digest"} (`command`: a configured server's argv; `[]` for a forged one, which runs its snapshot's `server.py`;
  `digest`: the snapshot's, null for a configured server).

## 12. Tools (tools/)

```python
@dataclass
class ToolSpec:
    name: str; description: dict[str, str]  # {"en","ru"}
    parameters: dict                        # JSON schema {"type":"object","properties":...,"required":[...]}
    handler: Callable[[ToolContext, dict], Awaitable[str]]
    audience: frozenset[str]                # subset of {"llm","external","user"}
    allow_empty: frozenset[str]             # required string args that may be "" (write_file content...)
    order: tuple[int, int]                  # (module rank, definition order): registry order
    modes: frozenset[str]                   # the session modes that have it (default both, §22.5)
    variants: dict[str, ToolVariant]        # per-mode texts and schema ("thread"): describe/parameters_for(mode)
@dataclass
class ToolContext:
    swarm: Swarm; actor: str; runtime: AgentRuntime | None = None
    via: str = "act"                         # the surface: "act" (web /api/act: web UI, TUI, console), "mcp"
                                             # (hub_call), "launcher-mcp"; recorded where the user's changes are
                                             # audited (skills, §19)
    @property kind -> str                    # swarm.kind_of(actor), "unknown" for a non-member
    @property output_cap -> int              # max chars of big outputs (shell, MCP results): with a runtime
                                             # (it cuts results for the model and traces them in full)
                                             # max(tool_output_chars, tracing.max_payload_chars), else
                                             # agents.tool_output_chars
    def has_tool(self, name: str) -> bool    # the caller has that tool: an LLM agent's own frozen set
                                             # (runtime.tool_names, §6.1), else the live registry for ctx.kind;
                                             # results that point at a tool are tailored with it
    @property mode -> str                    # the session's mode (getattr(swarm, "mode", "board"), §22.5); for
                                             # callers without a frozen set has_tool also needs ctx.mode in modes
REGISTRY: dict[str, ToolSpec]               # sorted by `order` once all modules are loaded (import-order free)
def tool(name, en, ru, properties, required=(), audience=("llm","external","user"), allow_empty=(),
         modes=("board","thread"), thread=None): decorator   # thread: the thread variant (§22.5)
def tools_for(kind: str, mode: str | None = None) -> list[ToolSpec]   # mode None: both modes
def schemas_for(kind: str, language: str, mode: str = "board") -> list[dict]   # [{"name","description",
                                                                     # "parameters"}], deterministic copies
async def call_tool(ctx: ToolContext, name: str, args: dict) -> tuple[str, bool]
    # rejects actors that are neither USER nor an active member; an LLM agent (a runtime with
    # tool_parameters) calls only the tools of its frozen set, with their frozen parameters: a tool it lacks is
    # "Unknown tool" with close matches and the list from its own set only (never a newer tool), and arguments
    # its schema lacks are dropped with the note "[Ignored unknown argument(s): .... Usage: <its frozen
    # signature>]"; validation still uses the registry spec (hence R0′ below); unknown tool -> close matches + the
    # available tools; audience errors say how to fix the call (join_swarm/as_agent); checks required args
    # (whitespace-only = missing unless allow_empty) and types with coercion ("5"/"#5" -> 5, JSON strings for
    # arrays/objects, 0/1 -> bool, numbers -> str, case-insensitive enums, finite numbers); validates enums;
    # unknown args are ignored but reported in the result; ToolError -> ("Error: msg", True);
    # UnicodeEncodeError (lone surrogate) -> an "invalid Unicode" error; other exception ->
    # ("Internal error in <tool>: ...", True) + log
    # a tool outside the session's mode (ToolSpec.modes) is refused before the audience check with the mode
    # fix-it text; validation uses spec.parameters_for(ctx.mode), the unknown-argument drop
    # frozen_params or spec.parameters_for(ctx.mode) (§22.5)
```

In a thread session (§22.5) the board-only tools (`board`, the eight `task_*` tools, `goal_complete`) exist for no
audience; the forum tools are added (`feed`, `post_read`, `post_create`, `post_update`, `comment`, `vote`: LEU;
`subscriptions`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`: LE); `send_message`, `wait`, `agents`, `retire_agent`, `mcp_create`,
`trigger_create`, `wait_for_events`, `swarm_status`, `swarm_control` and `agent_traces` have thread variants; the
LLM set is revision 6. `swarm_control` also takes `complete_goal?` (boolean) and `goal_summary?` (string), thread
sessions only: the user completes the goal (§22.4).

Tool results are plain text (compact, line-oriented), language = English for data, ToolError texts in
English. The `wait` tool calls `ctx.runtime.end_turn()`. `send_message` calls
`ctx.runtime.note_sent_to_user()` when USER is a recipient.

`send_message` and `pause_swarm` (§3.1). The description (en and ru) keeps "wakes its recipients" and
adds that `pause_swarm=true` is only for a question to ["user"] whose answer decides how the team goes on, so that
work under way would otherwise be redone: the session *may* then pause the whole swarm until the user answers, and
every member gets the question with the answer; never for what the agent can decide itself, a question about its
own task, or a report; ask everything in that one message and make it the only tool call of the response; the
result says whether the swarm was paused, and if not, go on with the work that doesn't depend on the answer. The
property is last, after `reply_to`, not required, without `default`, its description English in both arrays; the
usage line is `send_message(to, text, reply_to?, pause_swarm?)`. The result starts as always, `Sent message #N to
….` (a call without `pause_swarm` is byte for byte as before); one note follows, starting with a space:
- `asked`, an AI agent: ` The swarm is paused until the user answers this question; the user's answer then reaches
  every member with your question, and the swarm goes on.`; an external member (no runtime): ` The swarm is paused
  until the user answers this question; every member then gets the answer with your question. Call wait_for_events:
  the answer comes there.`
- otherwise ` pause_swarm was ignored: …`: `off` (this session does not pause for questions, the user's setting, so
  the others keep working; go on with the work that doesn't depend on the answer), `auto` (the user is not
  available: questions get an automatic reply), `pending` (the swarm already waits for the user's answer to
  {asker}'s question #{id}; yours was sent as an ordinary message, which the user sees too; don't send it again),
  `own` (… to your question #{id}), `paused` (the swarm is already paused ({reason})), `budget` (the budget is
  exhausted), `no_user` (it pauses the swarm only for a question to "user"), `user` (only a member's question to the
  user pauses the swarm).
- The user's message that answers a question: ` This answers {asker}'s question #{id}: every member got the question
  and your answer, and the swarm goes on.` (A-ok), or with the budget spent `…, but the budget is exhausted, so the
  swarm stays paused until you raise max_cost_usd.` (A-budget).

**R0′: LLM tool schemas are released as revisions.** Every LLM agent sends its own frozen tools array (§6.1), and
Anthropic thinking blocks bind to the exact prefix, so a changed name, description, parameter, `required` list, enum
or order of a tool with the `llm` audience is released as a new revision, in one change:
1. change the code;
2. set the mode's entry of `frozen.TOOLSET_REVISIONS` to `frozen.NEWEST_REVISION + 1` (one numbering for both modes;
   a change to a tool both arrays share is released in each mode whose array changes, §22.5);
3. run `python -m dreamteam.tools.frozen --write` (it writes `tools/snapshots/llm_r<N>.json`, or
   `llm_thread_r<N>.json` for the thread mode);
4. pin its exact-order digests (`sha256(db.dumps(tools))` per language) in tests/test_frozen_tools.py (`RELEASED`).

Existing agents keep their revision until their next compaction; new agents get the current one. Arguments are
still validated against the current registry (its schema for the session's mode, `parameters_for`, §22.5), so for
each mode the registry must keep serving every shipped revision of that mode
(tests/test_frozen_tools.py checks it): no tool leaves the `llm` audience, no property is removed or retyped
(`items.type` included), the current `required` is a subset of every shipped one, enums only grow, a free property
never gains an enum. Revisions 1-4 were the tool sets of 0.1.x (their sessions are not opened, §17.2); 5 = crew
tasks (§4.2): `task_create` and `task_update` gain `crew` and then
`directions` (last, after `tags` / `comment`; their descriptions English in both arrays, like the other board
properties: `task_create` `crew` `Crew task: how many members may work on it at once, its owner included (2..8);
0 = an ordinary task`, `directions` `With crew: its areas, one title per item; each becomes a draft subtask whose
taker writes its card`; `task_update` `crew` `Creator or assignee: 2..8 makes it a crew task (members at once, its
owner included); 0 makes it an ordinary task again`, `directions` `Directions to add to a crew task (titles); the
first is your own part while you have none`; neither has min or max limits), and `task_create`'s description
gains a last sentence (en): `A deliverable
too big for one member whose detailed split is unclear: pass crew (how many members may work on it at once, its
owner included) and directions (its areas; the members who take them write the details).` (ru « Если результат
слишком велик для одного участника и его подробное деление заранее неясно, передай crew (сколько участников могут
работать над задачей одновременно, включая её владельца) и directions (её направления; подробности напишут те, кто
их возьмёт).»), and `task_update`'s
description a last sentence (en): `A task you work on that turns out too big for one member: pass crew
and directions; you then own it and the first direction is your own part; each direction is handed in on its own,
and when all of them are finished you write the task's result and complete it (crew 0 makes it an ordinary task
again).` (ru « Если задача, над которой ты работаешь, оказалась слишком велика для одного участника, передай crew и
directions: ты станешь её владельцем, а первое направление — твоя часть; каждое направление сдаётся отдельно, а
когда все они завершены, ты пишешь итог задачи и завершаешь её (crew 0 снова делает её обычной задачей).»; no
other tool changed, `task_claim` included); 6 = the thread mode's first set (§22.5). A session with a member below
`frozen.OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION` (5) is not opened (§6.1, §17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version"), so board
notifications and wake-up texts name only tools and parameters of every shipped board revision from 5 on
(tests/test_prompts.py), crew tasks, `crew` and `directions` included; tool results that point at a newer tool check
`ToolContext.has_tool`, and a notification the recipient's frozen record (`frozen.member_tool_names`). `allow_empty`
is validation only, not part of the schema. Tools of the `user`/`external` audiences only (e.g. `set_goal`) are not
in the LLM tools array, and external members and the user always see the live registry. The texts rule holds per
mode (§22.6 "Keys by mode"; tests/test_prompts.py): board texts against the board revisions, thread texts against
the thread revisions, shared texts against both (so no shared text names crew tasks, `crew` or `directions`).

`trigger_create` and `trigger_list` say what the frozen description cannot (§8), with the settings in force:
- `trigger_create`: `Trigger #N created: CONDITION (NOTES)` then `; actions: …` when they are not just a wake.
  NOTES, joined with "; ": `repeating`; for a condition with file_changed() `file_changed() becomes true once the file
  has stopped changing: after 1 min without a change or once the agents who changed it have ended their turns, at
  the latest 5 min after the first change, and your own write_file/edit_file edits do not count` (no cap: without
  the "at the latest" part; `file_settle_seconds` 0: `file_changed() does not count your own write_file/edit_file
  edits`); for a member's repeating trigger with a wake action while `trigger_wake_seconds` > 0 `it wakes you at most
  once every 3 min, with the fires in between in one notice`. Without notes no parenthesis (`Trigger #1 created:
  done(1).`).
- `trigger_list`: each line `#N [state, repeating] owner=… when … — note actions=… (fired Nx, last …; 2 fires held,
  wake-up at 18:48) pending: docs/AUDIT.md changed 3x, last 40 s ago error: …`: the held part while fires are held
  (without the wake-up time for an inactive trigger), `pending` for the file_changed() changes not fired yet (as far as
  the last pass saw).

Results and checks of the review and role-catalog flows:
- `task_claim` by the task's designated reviewer (independent review, §4.1) adds "You were its reviewer; since
  you execute it now, another member will review it."
- `task_complete` says where the task went: `Task #N is done.`; `Task #N was sent to X for review.` (the task's
  own reviewer); `... was sent to the user for review: nobody else in the team can review it. You will be told the
  verdict; meanwhile take the next task or call wait.`; or `... was sent to X for review: a member other than you
  checks it, and you will be told the verdict.` (picked by the board). Once the board accepted the call (a refused
  one commits nothing) it commits the caller's held new files (`workspace.commit_held`, §7 "Held new files"). A
  member that still holds file locks gets ``You still hold locks on: docs/AUDIT.md (until 14:05). Unlock those you
  no longer need (`lock_file` with unlock=true).`` appended (`held_locks_note`, at most 10 named); locks are not
  tied to tasks, so none is released.
- Dependencies (§4 `update`): `task_get` of an open task (not in review) the caller holds while it is blocked adds `You hold it while
  it is blocked: if its result can be produced without some of #3, #4, remove those with task_update (depends_on =
  the ones still needed) and say why in its discussion.`; `task_update` in which an assignee that did not create the
  task removed dependencies adds `Its creator (X) was told that you removed #3, and the discussion records it.` (or
  `The discussion records that you removed #3.` when the creator is the user or has left) and, without a `comment`,
  ` Say there why the task can do without them (task_comment).`
- Likely duplicates (run 006: three agents created three alike tasks for one message to all): `task_create` of an
  agent or an external member (not the user) still creates the task, and when open tasks look like it its result
  adds, in the caller's language (`similar_tasks`), `Similar open tasks: #33 "Fix the parser" [in_progress, Anna
  Smith], #34 "..." [todo]. If yours duplicates one of them, cancel it (`task_update` status=cancelled) and take or
  comment on that one.` `Board.similar_open(task)`: the open tasks of other creators (a planner splits work into
  alike tasks on purpose; run 006's duplicates came from different members) except the task's parent and the tasks it
  depends on, ranked by `board.similarity` (pure). The titles decide: their words lower-cased, without punctuation,
  numbers, words under 3 letters and an en+ru stop list (generic verbs such as fix/implement/исправить, function
  words), each cut to its first 5 letters; two words match when equal or one (≥ 4 letters) is a prefix of the other;
  the score is the share of the shorter title's words found in the other (overlap coefficient), with ≥ 2 shared
  words. From 0.75 the titles alone decide; from 0.5 the goals must confirm (title + goal still ≥ 0.5 with a shared
  word more); goals never make a match alone (siblings repeat the swarm goal's words in theirs). Tasks told apart by
  a parameter (the tokens with a digit differ: N=100 / N=200, C5, 1e-3), a kind of work (fix / build / verify /
  optimize / measure / research / document / remove / deploy words, en+ru) or a side (lower / upper, staging /
  production, нижн / верхн, ...) score 0. At most 3, best first, then the older. "Fix crash in parser on empty input"
  ~ "Parser crashes on empty input" (1.0); "Benchmark solver on N=100" / "N=200", "Optimize the step function" /
  "Verify the step function", "Compute lower bound for C5" / "upper bound", "Write unit tests for the parser" /
  "for the lexer" (0.67, no goal confirms) and "Implement login page UI" / "Implement login API endpoint" (one shared
  word) are not. `board.similar_items(title, goal, candidates, limit=SIMILAR_MAX)` is the same ranking over any
  items with `.id`, `.title` and `.goal` (`similar_tasks` is its wrapper); `post_create` uses it for posts (§22.2).
- `goal_complete` (switch on) is refused while tasks are in review: ``Tasks are still waiting for review: #N
  (reviewer), .... The goal can be completed only after every task is reviewed: call `wait` ...``. The "already
  achieved" check comes first.
- `agents` appends, in the caller's language, `Role catalog (hire_agent role=<name>; a catalog role brings its
  description and model profile, and instructions may then be empty; any other name is a new role you describe
  in instructions):` and one line per visible role, `- <name>[ (model <profile>)]: <roles.summary(description)>`.
- `hire_agent` resolves `role` in the catalog (swarm language). `instructions` stays required in the schema
  (R0′), so a missing one is still "Missing required argument(s)"; `""` is accepted (`allow_empty`). An unknown
  role with empty instructions: ``'X' is not in the role catalog: describe the new role's responsibilities in
  instructions, or pick a catalog role (`agents` lists them).`` plus up to three similar catalog roles
  (`roles.close_roles`). Results start with `Hired <name> as "<canonical role>".`, then either `They got the
  catalog description of the role; model profile P.` or `"X" is a new role (not in the role catalog): your
  instructions are all they know about it.`, then `They are woken now: ...`. The user (the board's hire form, the
  TUI, the console: `ctx.is_user`) gets texts about the user's own tools instead: the error says to describe the
  new role in the instructions (`/hire X | instructions` in the terminal) or pick a catalog role (the hire form's
  list, `/roles`), and the result is `Hired <name> as "<role>" (catalog role, model profile P).` or `Hired <name>
  as "<role>": a new role, not in the role catalog; your instructions are all they know about it.`
- `join_swarm` shows the canonical role and, for a catalog role, appends `\nYour role (<role>): <description>`
  (an external member has no system prompt); its description and result say that members who join this way do not
  count toward max_agents.

Results of the team, wait and job flows:
- In a thread session `agents`, `hire_agent`, `retire_agent`, `join_swarm`, `set_goal`, `swarm_status`,
  `swarm_control`, `shell`'s wrap-up refusal and `wait_for_events(progress=true)` give the thread texts of §22.5
  (no task, board or planning card).
- `agents` starts with `AI agents: 2 of max 6, plus 1 external member (not counted).` and the budget line (the
  same team line in `swarm_status`); a member line ends with `, background jobs: j3, j5` while it has running jobs.
- `swarm_status`: its first line `Swarm "<name>" — running` (or `PAUSED: <Swarm.pause_text()>`: `PAUSED: waiting
  for the user's answer to Anna Smith's question #12` for a question, §3.1; for the user it adds ` (your next
  send_message to {asker} or to all is the answer: every member gets it with the question; swarm_control
  action=resume goes on without it)`) ends with `; WRAP-UP MODE: the agents finish their tasks with what they have, no
  new computations or background jobs` while the user's wrap-up mode is on, and with `; CLARIFY MODE: the planning
  task first asks the user, and a member's question to the user with pause_swarm=true pauses the swarm until the user
  answers` while `clarifying`.
- `swarm_control`: in a thread session the refusals of `complete_goal` first (with `reopen_goal_comment`;
  `goal_summary` without it; nothing applied, §22.4), then the limits, then `reopen_goal_comment` (which ends wrap-up
  mode) or `complete_goal` (`goal marked reached`), then `action`, then `wrap_up`;
  `pause` while paused changes nothing and is listed as `already paused (<pause_text>)`, so `Done: already paused
  (waiting for the user's answer to Anna Smith's question #12).` during a question pause; `Done: ...` lists what was
  done: `wrap-up mode on: every agent was told to finish its tasks with what it has, and no
  new background jobs start` / `wrap-up mode was already on` / `wrap-up mode off` / `wrap-up mode was not on`. Nothing
  to do: `Nothing to do: pass action (pause/resume), wrap_up, a limit or reopen_goal_comment.` A `pause` that paused
  (reason "paused by the user", §3 `_set_pause`) while jobs run (`jobs.running_of()`) adds, after the joined parts,
  a sentence of its own with the ids only (USER's `u_paused_jobs` has the details): `Done: paused; wrap-up mode off.
  Background jobs keep running (j3, j5): a pause stops only the agents' model calls; job_stop stops a job.`; without
  jobs the result is unchanged (`Done: paused.`), and a pause while already paused never adds the sentence
  (`Done: already paused (…).`).
- `swarm_status` adds `Background jobs: 2 running (j3 Anna Smith: npm run dev, 25 min; j5 ...).` while jobs run (a
  silent one, §7.1: `j5 Bob: pytest, 50 min, no output for 40 min`),
  and for a member caller `Your background jobs: j3, j5.` after its open tasks. `brief=true` shows the goal as one
  line, `Global goal [active]: <title>` (no description, no summary); the rest is the same.
- `wait` (description: the end of one of its background jobs wakes it too; "End every turn with it" stays): `OK,
  waiting. You will be woken up by new events.`, plus `, also when your background job j3 ends.` / `…jobs j3, j5 end.`
  for the caller's jobs whose end will wake it (`JobManager.awaited`: never one a done goal makes quiet), and/or
  `, also when docs/AUDIT.md, which you were refused, is free.` (`… are free` for several, at most 10 named;
  `Workspace.awaited_locks`: none once the goal is done, when n_lock_free is quiet; §7 "Lock waiters"); both:
  `…, also when your background job j3 ends and when docs/AUDIT.md, which you were refused, is free.` With neither,
  the plain text gets one more clause when all of these hold: the goal is active; `swarm.stall_ids(caller)` is not
  empty (an `in_progress` task, not a clarify card waiting for the user's answers, not a crew task with live
  directions; a `waiting` task alone does not count: answers wake it, system prompt rule 7); the caller has no
  active trigger of its own (any trigger: it set it on purpose); and `swarm.team_asleep(caller)` (nobody else can
  act or be woken by something set, §3). Then: ``OK, waiting. You will be woken up by new events, but nothing of
  yours is set to wake you and nobody else in the team is at work. A process started with & or nohup that `jobs`
  does not list is not tracked: its end will not wake you. If you are waiting for one, the next time set a trigger
  with a deadline before you wait (trigger_create, e.g. file_exists("out/result.json") or elapsed(1800)), and start
  such runs with background=true, without & and nohup.`` (English like every result; `wait` ends the activation,
  so the agent reads it only after its next wake-up, hence "the next time"; scheduler item 9 wakes such a team
  later). `team_asleep`, `stall_ids` and `triggers` are looked up with getattr (FakeSwarm, §3: the plain text).
  In a thread session the `stall_ids` condition is dropped and `team_asleep` has its digest clause (§22.7).
- `goal_complete` appends, while jobs run, `Note: background jobs are still running: j3 (Anna Smith: npm run dev, 25
  min). Stop the ones nobody needs with job_stop; the rest stop with the session.`
- `shell`, `jobs`, `job_stop`: §7.1.
- `wait_for_events(progress=true)` also returns when others make board progress: `task.created`, `task.updated` with
  a status change, `goal.set`, `goal.completed`, `goal.reopened`, `agent.hired` (an external member: "joined"),
  `agent.retired`, `swarm.wrap_up` (`wrap-up mode on (user): finish your tasks with what you have, no new computations
  or background jobs` / `wrap-up mode off (user)`) (the caller's own changes and events about itself are skipped). They are read from the events
  journal after a per-actor cursor (kv `wait_progress:<actor>`; the first such call starts at the journal's end;
  calls without progress neither use nor move it) and appended as `Board progress:` / `Прогресс на доске:` with `• `
  lines (at most 20, then ``… and N more: see `board` ``), after the incoming header when nothing else is pending.
  Each progress line starts with the time of its journal event (`• 10:50 #2 Parser: todo → in_progress (Ann Lee)`).
  In a thread session the progress is the feed's (`Feed:` / «Лента:»: new posts, comments, goal and member events,
  with the tally of #1 when it changed; votes never end the wait, §22.5).
- In a thread session `wait_for_events` also returns once the caller's `Swarm.digest_deadline` has passed (each
  sleep is capped at it): an external member that keeps the feed in `digest` gets its digest about every
  `[agents] digest_seconds` while it waits; on a timeout the digest items gathered so far still come with the
  result (§22.3 "Digest items").
- `wait_for_events` renders with `render_wake(actor, incoming=True, stamps=True, since=<oldest progress line>)`
  (§6.3): one result may hold hours of news (progress collected since the last progress call, notifications queued
  while the client was away), so when it spans more than a minute the header shows the range and every notification
  and message has its time; within a minute: one stamp, no times but the progress lines'. Example:
  ```
  === New events while you were working (2026-10-11 10:50–12:50) ===
  What happened:
  • 12:20 Task #3 "API" was assigned to you by Ann Lee. Claim it with `task_claim` when you start working on it.
  • 12:50 Message #7 from Ann Lee to you:
  status?
  Board progress:
  • 10:50 #2 Parser: created by user
  • 11:40 #2 Parser: todo → in_progress (Bob Stone)
  ```

## 13. Hub MCP (hub_mcp.py)

```python
def build_hub_server(swarm) -> mcp.server.lowlevel.Server
    # on_list_tools: tools for audiences E∪U, each schema extended with optional "as_agent"
    # (string: name returned by join_swarm; omit to act as the user). on_call_tool: actor =
    # as_agent (must be an active external member) or USER; returns
    # CallToolResult(content=[TextContent], is_error). `instructions=` explains the swarm.
async def hub_call(swarm, name: str, args: dict, client: str | None = None, *, via: str = "mcp") -> tuple[str, bool]
    # one MCP tool call with the actor rules above (also used by the launcher MCP, §18.2); calls of external
    # members are traced (tracer.external_call), except UNTRACED_TOOLS = {"wait_for_events"} and except while the
    # swarm stops (a call that returns then, e.g. a shell command killed by the session stop, must not write into
    # the database that Swarm.stop's caller closes next). A call of an external member (actor not USER and
    # swarm.is_member(actor)), except UNTRACED_TOOLS, stamps `swarm._external_seen[actor] = time.time()` before and
    # after it, whether tracing is on or not (Swarm.team_asleep, §3: a long shell call counts from its start to its
    # end: with `[shell] background_on_timeout`, the default, an external member's call waits at most
    # `EXTERNAL_WAIT_MAX`, 600 s, below `EXTERNAL_IDLE_SECONDS`, so the stamp before it covers the whole call; with
    # it off, a call longer than `EXTERNAL_IDLE_SECONDS` counts for that long from its start; a client that only
    # waits in wait_for_events does not count). `client` (default: serving_client's) names the MCP
    # client: a message it sends (as the call's actor) reaches the external members it acts as already read
    # (mailbox.sent_as_seen_by(members, actor)), so it never comes back to it as news; messages others send, e.g.
    # an agent this call hires, reach them as news. `via` becomes ToolContext.via (the launcher MCP: "launcher-mcp").
    # No self-approval: `skill_approve` with approve=true, as the user, of a proposal whose owner is an external
    # member this client acts as (HubClients.members_of(client)) returns "Error: skill 'x' was proposed by Ann Lee,
    # the member this MCP client acts as; the user decides it in the web UI, the TUI or the console." without
    # running the tool (also for the launcher MCP's forwarded calls, inside serving_client); rejecting is allowed.
    # A client nothing names (client None) cannot be told from any external member: approve=true of an external
    # member's proposal returns "Error: skill 'x' was proposed by Ann Lee, an MCP member, and this MCP client cannot
    # be told apart from it (it sends no X-DreamTeam-Client header and has no MCP session); the user decides it in
    # the web UI, the TUI or the console."
CLIENT_HEADER = "X-DreamTeam-Client"
def client_key(ctx, local: str) -> str | None
    # the client of a request: `local` without HTTP (stdio, in-process: one client per server), else
    # "client:<CLIENT_HEADER>", else "session:<mcp-session-id>", else None (the 2026-07-28 protocol without the
    # header: such a client cannot be told from another one and may get its own message back once)
def serving_client(client) -> ContextManager       # hub_call inside it (and in tasks it starts) comes from `client`
def hub_clients(swarm) -> HubClients               # external member -> the client that last acted as it (as_agent,
                                                   # or join_swarm: a new member or a welcome-back)
def proxy_http_client(url: str)                    # the stdio proxy's httpx client, with a random CLIENT_HEADER
                                                   # and hubauth.httpx_auth() (a sandbox hub's token, per request:
                                                   # §14.2); a loopback `url` never through the environment's proxy
async def serve_stdio(swarm) -> None
async def serve_stdio_proxy(url: str, instructions: str | None = None) -> None
    # stdio server forwarding to a running hub's /mcp (a swarm's or the launcher's); the client gets the
    # upstream server's instructions unless `instructions` is given
class MCPHttpEndpoint:   # ASGI app for /mcp backed by StreamableHTTPSessionManager
    def __init__(self, swarm, host: str, extra_hosts=()): ...   # extra_hosts: DREAMTEAM_ALLOWED_HOSTS
    manager: StreamableHTTPSessionManager
```
In mcp 2.x the request context is passed to handlers (`ctx.session` is per request), so identity
is explicit via `as_agent`. Stdio servers read stdin with `_StdinLines` (a daemon reader thread), so a stop
signal ends them even while the client keeps stdin open. The launcher MCP (§18.2) names its clients the same way:
each launcher server has its own `local:<uuid>` key, and it forwards every call inside
`serving_client(client_key(ctx, local))`, so `hub_call` in the session gets the client (also in the task that
`_call_in_session` starts).

`INSTRUCTIONS` (also in the launcher's, through `HUB_INSTRUCTIONS`) tell the user's side that `wait_for_events` with
`progress=true` also returns when the board moves on and that `jobs` and `job_stop` list and stop every member's
background jobs; and the members' side that members who join do not count toward max_agents, that a `shell` command
still running at its timeout (at most 600 seconds over MCP) continues as a background job, that `background=true`
starts one at once, that processes a command leaves running become a job too, and that a job's end arrives through
`wait_for_events` (no polling); `swarm_control` also switches wrap-up mode (§3), in which no new background job
starts. After the pause/resume sentence they say: "When `swarm_status` says the swarm is paused waiting for your
answer to a member's question, your next `send_message` to that member (or to all) is the answer: every member gets
it with the question and the swarm goes on; `swarm_control` action=resume goes on without it." (§3.1; the tool list
is live, so external members see `pause_swarm` at once). The user's side also learns `skills`, `skill_attach`,
`skill_detach` and `skill_approve` (not for a member the client acts as); the members' side that skills (SKILL.md
folders under `.scratch/_skills/`) are listed by `join_swarm` and `swarm_status`, and that `skill_propose` proposes
one.

In a thread session (§22.9) `on_list_tools` lists the E∪U tools of that mode only (`hub_specs(mode)`, the schema of
`spec.parameters_for(mode)`, `_description(spec, language, mode)`), and `instructions=` is `INSTRUCTIONS_THREAD`: the
feed, posts, comments, votes and subscriptions, the vote on #1 and the user's direct completion instead of the task
board. `INSTRUCTIONS` stays as it is. A tool of the other mode is refused by `call_tool` (§22.5), for every surface.

## 14. Web (web.py) — REST for the UI and the console

`create_app(swarm, host, *, on_library_change=None) -> Starlette` is the app of ONE swarm: the whole server of `dreamteam run`, and the
per-session app the launcher serves under `/s/{sid}/` (§18.1). All JSON (`httpjson.JSONResponse`; the
WebSocket sends `httpjson.json_text`). POST /api/* bodies require `Content-Type: application/json` (the
exceptions are the launcher's uploads, `raw_posts`: §18.1 and §21.3). Guard
(`GuardMiddleware`, every bind, also 0.0.0.0 in Docker): Host must be localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]; for
non-loopback binds also the bind address, or an IP literal that is the address the connection reached (ASGI
`server`; any IP literal only on a request with the hub token: a port mapping that rewrites the address); plus names
in `DREAMTEAM_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (comma-separated). Origin must be the host and port the request was made to, the origin
of `DREAMTEAM_PUBLIC_URL` (`env_public_origin`, its path aside: a same-host proxy that rewrites the Host) or an
allowed name, WebSockets and `/mcp` too: never another port of a loopback name, which is another program on the
computer (for a request the hub token's cookie authorizes, same-origin also by scheme). Then the hub token
(§14.2): with one, every peer needs it, the hub's own loopback too (401 / WebSocket closed 1008 before accept);
without one, nothing is asked, and `serve` refuses a non-loopback bind.

**The external API's branch** (`/api/v1`, §21.1). The launcher's guard is `GuardMiddleware(..., api=True)`, and its
`raw_posts` maps a path to a set of content types (a plain string is one type). A request whose path `web.is_api_path`
takes (`/api/v1` itself, or a path under `/api/v1/`; the launcher's dispatcher uses the same predicate) goes through a
branch of its own: the Host check (a valid Bearer counts as the token there), the Origin check (`origin_allowed`,
never the cookie's rule), then 403 `api_disabled` when the hub has neither an API token nor a hub token, 401
`token_required` (with `WWW-Authenticate`) without a valid `Authorization: Bearer`, and the 415 rule, where a path
`raw_posts` lists takes its own types alone, JSON refused too (`/api/v1/uploads` stores any body it takes, §21.3). Then
`scope["dreamteam.api_caller"]` (`web.API_CALLER`) is `"owner"` for the hub token or `own_token()`, `"api"` for the
API token (`hubauth.api_digest()`), and the request goes on. The cookie and `?token=` count for nothing on that branch
(no 303). Its refusals are JSON `{"error", "code"}` (`forbidden_host`, `forbidden_origin`, `token_required`,
`api_disabled`, `unsupported_media_type`); every other path keeps the plain texts above and never takes the API token.
`web.create_app` (`dreamteam run`) has no such branch.

`DREAMTEAM_PUBLIC_URL` is the base URL users reach the hub at (shown as the MCP URL and written to
hub.json; `dreamteam sandbox` sets it). `serve(swarm, host, port, ..., on_started=)` sets
`swarm.hub_url = public_base(host, port) + "/mcp"`, calls back once listening and shuts down gracefully when
cancelled. Pages (`/`, launcher `/`) are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`; `/static` is `UIStaticFiles`
(`Cache-Control: no-cache`: browsers revalidate, so an upgraded server never runs a stale app.js).

| method path | response |
|---|---|
| GET `/` | static/index.html |
| GET `/static/{file}` | static files |
| GET `/api/state` | snapshot (§14.1 below) |
| GET `/api/roles` | `{"language": swarm language, "roles": [{key, name, description, instructions, model, builtin, names, skills}], "hidden": [same]}`: the visible roles of the catalog in the swarm's language (§17.3; the board's hire dialog, the TUI's `/roles`), and the hidden ones, which a hire by name still resolves; `names`: every spelling `roles.find_role` resolves to the role (its name and id, a built-in role's name in either language); also for a stopped session; not in the snapshot (several KB) |
| GET `/api/hub` | {pid, project, name, version, sandbox}: identity of this hub process (checked against hub.json); `sandbox`: inside the Docker sandbox (the host library is a read-only source, folder paths are the container's) |
| GET `/api/tasks/{id}` | {task, discussion: [...], events: [...]} |
| GET `/api/posts/{id}?since_id=` | {post, comments, votes, goal_vote?}: a thread session's post (§22.8); else 404 |
| GET `/api/messages?with=Name&limit=&since=` | conversation USER↔Name; without `with`: all recent messages |
| GET `/api/inbox?since_message=&since_notification=` | `{"messages","notifications"}` to USER: with since_* > 0 the ones with a larger id (oldest first, ≤ 500); without, the newest 500 (ascending). `since` = alias of since_message. Messages carry `read` |
| POST `/api/read` | body `{"with"?: name}`: marks USER's messages (from that member) read → {"ok", "unread"} |
| GET `/api/events?since=&limit=&types=` | events |
| GET `/api/agents/{name}/activity?limit=` | `agent.activity` events of that agent |
| GET `/api/files?path=` | dir → {"type":"dir","entries":[...]}; file → {"type":"file","content","truncated"} |
| POST `/api/act/{tool}` | run tool as USER: body = args → {"ok": bool, "result": str}; the user's `jobs` and `job_stop` (§7.1) go through it too: background jobs have no endpoint of their own; with `X-DreamTeam-Auto-Reply: 1` it first calls `swarm.auto_reply_seen()` (below) |
| GET `/api/skills` | `{library_dir, library: [entry], claude: [item], host: [entry], sandbox, container, limits: {max_mb, max_files, max_attached, max_archive_mb}, install, attached: [snapshot item + source_digest]}` (§19): the Skills tab; `source_digest` is the attached skill's own source now (`SessionSkills.source_digest`: "Update" compares with it only) |
| POST `/api/skills` | an import body (§19 "Requests": exactly one of `path`, `zip`, `git`, `claude`, `host`; `pick`, `replace`) plus `attach?: bool` → the import report + `install`; with `attach` every imported skill is attached as `library:<name>` (`attached: [{name, status, files}]`, `failed: [{name, error, status}]`, as `attach_source`); `attach` on a stopped session is 409 `STOPPED_SKILLS_TEXT` (importing works) |
| GET `/api/skills/{name}?from=library\|claude-user\|claude-project\|host-library\|session` | the entry + `files_list`, `skill_md`, `deps` (`show_folder`) + `install`; `session`: the session copy with its metadata and shown path |
| DELETE `/api/skills/{name}?confirm={name}` | `{"removed": name}` (`Library.remove`; the sessions keep their copies); 400 without a matching confirm |
| GET `/api/skills/{name}/deps-log?ecosystem=python\|node` | `{name, ecosystem, status, path, log}`: the install log of the attached skill's environment (the failed one first; `EnvManager.log_tail` / `log_path`); 404 when DreamTeam installs nothing for it |
| `/api/traces...`, `/api/spans/...`, `/api/agents/{name}/traces.jsonl` | traces (§16.3) |
| WS `/ws` | pushes every bus event as JSON (also the live-only `trace.*` events); a handshake with `X-DreamTeam-Auto-Reply: 1` runs the whole connection, `accept()` included, inside `swarm.auto_reply_stream()` (below) |
| `/mcp` | hub MCP over streamable HTTP |

**The auto-reply header** `X-DreamTeam-Auto-Reply: 1` (`models.AUTO_REPLY_HEADER`) is sent only by the print client
of `dreamteam -p` while its automatic replies are on (`HubClient.auto_reply`, docs/TUI.md §2), on every request and on
the WebSocket handshake; the interactive TUI, the web UI, the console and MCP clients never send it. It holds the
session's auto-reply lease (§3.1): no planning card asks the user first (in a thread session no clarify #2 is
