written, §22.8) and no question pauses the swarm. The
launcher forwards it to the session apps unchanged (`SessionRouter` passes the scope's headers), and reads it itself
on `POST /api/sessions` and `/start` (§18.1). Only these refresh the lease: those two launcher routes, `POST
/api/act/{tool}` and the `/ws` event stream (held while open, then `AUTO_REPLY_GRACE`); the GET routes and `/mcp`
never do, so a `-p` client keeps it through its stream and its acts. Nothing about it is persisted.

The skills routes are `skill_routes(config_of, workspace_of, *, via, swarm=None, changed=None) -> [Route]`, shared
with the launcher (§18.1): `config_of()` the settings (here the swarm's), `workspace_of(request)` the folder whose
`.claude/skills` is `claude-project` (here the workspace), `via` recorded in the library (`act` here), `swarm` the
session (its attached list, `attach`, `from=session`, `deps-log`; the launcher passes none), `changed()` after a
library change (here `on_library_change`, which the launcher's `SessionRouter` sets so the home page reloads its
Skills tab). `on_library_change` is also called after a successful `/api/act` call and a successful call of the
app's `/mcp` (`build_hub_server(swarm, on_library_change)`) of a `hub_mcp.LIBRARY_TOOLS` tool (`skill_attach`,
`skill_approve`); the launcher MCP's forwarded calls of those tools send the `skills` change themselves. Every `{name}` goes through `check_name` before any path is built (400). Errors are
`skill_error_response(exc)`: `{"error", **extra}` (e.g. `exists`) with the SkillError's / ToolError's status. The
stopped check uses `Swarm.started`.

### 14.1 snapshot
```json
{"swarm": {"name","language","paused","pause_reason","wrap_up": bool,   // the user's wrap-up mode (§3)
           "question": {"asker","message_id","since","text"}|null,   // the question holding the pause (§3.1),
                                       // text: the question message cut to QUESTION_PREVIEW_CHARS (600)
           "clarify": bool,                // [swarm] clarify, the setting (§3.1)
           "auto_reply": bool,             // the auto-reply lease of `dreamteam -p` is active (clarify does not apply)
           "clarify_wait": {"name","task_id"}|null,   // the first open clarify planning card whose holder waits for
                                       // the user's answers (asks_user, §3.1; null again once the user went on
                                       // without its question): the board's quiet banner
           "limits":{"max_cost_usd","max_agents"},
           "agent_count": n,               // what limits.max_agents counts (Swarm.agent_count: external members do not)
           "spent_usd","goal": {...}|null, "counts": {status: n}, "mcp_url", "models": [profile names],
           "mcp_token": bool,              // the hub has a token (§14.2): the board's MCP command shows the header
                                           // with a `<token>` placeholder; never the token itself
           "session": {"id","title","status": "running"|"stopped",
                       "pending_goal": {"title","description"}|null}|null,   // null outside a SessionManager;
                                       // pending_goal: the goal a never-started session gets at its first start
           "tracing": bool,
           "independent_review": bool,   // Board.independent_review, read live (§4.1)
           "mode": "board"|"thread",     // the session's work mode (§22.8; not /api/hub's "mode", not network.mode)
           "goal_rule": "democracy"|"veto",   // the thread mode's rule (§22.4); in a thread session tasks [],
                                       // counts all 0, independent_review inert, clarify_wait {"name","post_id": 2}
           "workspace": {"path","default","adopted","exists"},    // Swarm.workspace_info(): the folder the
                                       // members work in (same shape as a session summary's "workspace", §17.2)
           "network": {"mode": "on"|"off", "isolation": "docker"|"netns"|"env"|"container"|null}},   // netoff.describe, §7.2
 "tasks": [Task.to_dict() + {"blocked_by","comments"}],
 "agents": [{"name","kind","role","status","model","language","cost_usd","tokens_in","tokens_out","hired_by",
             "created_at","last_active","instructions","context_tokens","open_tasks":[ids],"unread",
             "jobs": n,                    // its running background jobs
             "subscriptions": [{"id","kind","target","by","mode","auto"}]}],   // §22.3; [] in a board session
 "triggers": [...],
 "jobs": [job...],                         // JobManager.snapshot(): the running jobs (from memory), then those that
                                           // ended in the last hour (one query, at most 50); the public job dict of
                                           // §7.1 ({"id","label","owner","command","origin","status","reason",
                                           // "stopped_by","exit_code","started_at","background_at","ended_at","log",
                                           // "processes"}); no "busy" (it needs the board)
 "mcp": [...],
 "skills": [{"name","description","from","owner","library","comment","attached_by","attached_at","updated_at",
             "attached_via","files","size","digest","manual",
             "path",                       // SessionSkills.shown_path: ".scratch/_skills/<name>/SKILL.md", or the
                                           // session copy's absolute path when .scratch is not local
             "roles": [names],             // the catalog roles that list it (§19); from memory, no query
             "deps": [EnvState]}],         // its script dependencies, one per ecosystem (§19), [] without manifests:
                                           // {"ecosystem","status","files","packages","env","key","python"?,"bin"?,
                                           // "commands"?,"node_modules"?,"linked"?,"view"?,"log"?,"error"?,
                                           // "installer"?,"reason"?,"queued"?,"other_process"?,"seconds"?,...}
 "locks": [...],
 "posts": [...], "goal_vote": {...}|null,   // the thread mode (§22.8): every post without its text, the vote
                                           // on #1; [] and null in a board session
 "user": {"unread": n}}
```

### 14.2 Hub token (hubauth.py)
Inside the Docker sandbox the hub listens on 0.0.0.0: a published port reaches the container's interface, never its
loopback (a hub bound to 127.0.0.1 there answers no one outside), so every container on the same Docker network
reaches it as well. The token closes that.

- **The hub.** Its guard keeps only the token's SHA-256: `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN_SHA256` (`DIGEST_ENV`, 64 hex; what
  `dreamteam sandbox` and docker-compose.yml pass, so the token itself is never in the container's environment) or
  else the digest of `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN` (`TOKEN_ENV`, the token itself: a hub started with it on the host, the
  host's clients). `cli.main` moves both out
  of os.environ first (`take_env_token`, after
  `netoff.sandbox_entry`, whose re-exec still carries them): no process DreamTeam starts inherits them, and
  `shell._INTERNAL_ENV` drops both from the agents' environment and DreamTeam's git (`secret_free_env`) whatever
  `shell.pass_env` says. `hub_digest()` is the hub's digest (a `DIGEST_ENV` that is no SHA-256 becomes the digest of a
  random token: never "no token"); `env_token()` is the token for clients. `GuardMiddleware(token=FROM_ENV)` of
  both apps (and of every session app; `token="..."` is a raw token, hashed) keeps `digest` and asks every HTTP and
  WebSocket request, whatever its peer (the hub's own loopback too: the agents' commands in the sandbox's container
  come from there), for one of: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the cookie
  `dreamteam_hub_<sha256(token)[:12]>` (`cookie_name(digest)`; one name per hub: browsers send cookies to every port
  of a host), or, on a GET/HEAD, `?token=<token>`, which is answered with 303 to the same path and query without it,
  `Set-Cookie: <name>=<the token the URL brought>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The
  `Location` is always a path on the hub: the raw path is percent-encoded except plain path characters (`\`, tab and
  newline included: a browser reads `/\host` as `//host`) and its leading slashes become one. Without a token: 401
  `TOKEN_TEXT` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="DreamTeam"`, or `websocket.close` 1008 before accept
  (WebSockets: header or cookie, never the query). A request the cookie authorizes takes an `Origin` only if it is
  its own (`same_origin`: scheme, host and port), the public URL's or an allowed name (`cookie_origin_allowed`):
  SameSite counts every port of 127.0.0.1 as the same site. Comparisons are `hmac.compare_digest` of `sha256(given)`
  with the digest
  (`matches`). The header may also carry `own_token()`, the token of the clients in the hub's own process
  (`serving`, below): made in memory at first use, never stored, logged or put in a URL, and taken by every guard of
  that process that has a digest (`own_digest()`), never as the cookie or `?token=`; a hub started with `DIGEST_ENV`
  alone has no other token for its own console. A same-host reverse proxy or port forwarder gets nothing for its
  clients either: they need the token like everyone else's. `hub_server_config` gives uvicorn `proxy_headers=False`,
  so `X-Forwarded-For` / `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` never change the peer. No token on a loopback bind (127.0.0.1,
  localhost, ::1, or another loopback IP literal exactly as written, `web._loopback_bind`: 127.0.0.2 too, whose own
  address the guard takes as the Host; a string with brackets or a `%` scope is no IP literal and needs a token):
  nothing is asked of anyone, as before there were tokens (the default `dreamteam serve`); a loopback bind with a
  token (`DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN` set on the host) asks every peer like any other. The token is never logged, never in the
  snapshot (`mcp_token` says only that there
  is one), the settings or `/api/hub`. `web.check_hub_token(host)` raises `NoTokenError` for a non-loopback bind
  without a token (fail closed: the image's default CMD, a plain `docker run`, compose without
  `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN_SHA256`, which compose passes by name, so that `docker compose ps`, `logs` and `down` work
  without it, and the container's log shows the reason); `DREAMTEAM_HUB_NO_TOKEN=1` (`NO_TOKEN_ENV`) lets it start with a warning. It runs before
  anything is created or started, after `running_hub` (a hub of the home that runs already is reported whether this
  process has a token or not, and `serve` opens it in the browser unless `--no-browser`; one that asks for a token no
  client here may send stops the command with `TokenRequired`'s text): `cli._token_missing` (`warn=False`) in
  `cmd_serve` (before `--goal`
  creates and starts a session and imports its `--skill`) and in `cmd_run` (before the swarm starts and the goal is
  set) prints `The web server cannot start on <host>:<port>: <its text>` and exits 1; the TUI's
  `_start_launcher` checks a free configured port before its launcher marker (`HubError(0, ...)`, which `dreamteam`
  and `dreamteam -p` print; a busy port keeps the fallback to an ephemeral port on 127.0.0.1); `dreamteam mcp`, whose
  web part is optional, logs serve()'s refusal and goes on over stdio. `serve` and `serve_launcher` check once more.
- **The API token** (§21.1): a second token, `DREAMTEAM_API_TOKEN` or its SHA-256 in `DREAMTEAM_API_TOKEN_SHA256`
  (`hubauth.api_digest()`), for `/api/v1` only. `take_env_token` moves both out of os.environ with the hub token's
  names (`_api_taken`, `_api_taken_digest`; `api_env_token()` is the token), `shell._INTERNAL_ENV` drops both,
  `docker.env_passthrough` never passes the host's, and `dreamteam sandbox` of a home passes the digest by name, as
  `DIGEST_ENV`. A digest variable that is no SHA-256 asks for a token nobody has, with one warning per value (never
  its value; `_api_digest_warned` counts a value only once the log has a handler, so a command's early check before
  `setup_logging` does not keep it out of the log file). It is never one of `client_tokens()`, never a cookie or
  `?token=`, and it opens no other path. A hub whose API token equals its hub token does not start
  (`check_hub_token` raises `NoTokenError`, `dreamteam run` included; the TUI's `_start_launcher` tries no other
  port after it, and `dreamteam mcp` logs it and goes on over stdio as above); a launcher with an API token and no
  hub token logs `api_token_warning()` outside the image (§21.1).
- **`dreamteam sandbox`** (`docker.run_sandbox`): refuses when a container `dreamteam-<port>` exists
  (`container_exists`); makes `new_token()` (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`) per container; `store_token(port, token,
  mounted, also_mounted=[sandbox_host_library(config), <each mounted [api] folders root>])` (§21.10 "Sandbox") writes
  `<tokens_dir>/<port>.json` `{"port","token","home"}`
  (mode 0600, folder 0700 on POSIX) unless the folder is inside any mounted directory (`_inside`: `os.path.normcase`,
  and `os.path.samefile` per ancestor for a case-insensitive file system Python does not know about; then None:
  nothing stored, the printed lines name `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN` instead); `tokens_dir()` is `DREAMTEAM_TOKENS_DIR` or
  `~/.dreamteam/hub-tokens`. `sandbox_command` passes `-e DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN_SHA256` by name and
  `subprocess.call(cmd, env={...without docker.TOKEN_NAMES, DIGEST_ENV: digest(token)})` gives the value (never on
  a command line, never the token itself; `env_passthrough` never passes the host's own); for a home with an API
  token it also passes `-e DREAMTEAM_API_TOKEN_SHA256`, whose value `API_DIGEST_ENV: hubauth.api_digest()` joins
  that env (§21.1). `access_lines` prints the board URL with
  `?token=`, the MCP URL and `claude mcp add --transport http dreamteam <base>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer
  <token>"`, and the stdio registration `claude mcp add dreamteam -- dreamteam mcp ...` that survives restarts; with
  `api=True` (a home with an API token) also `API: <base>/api/v1  (header Authorization: Bearer <your
  DREAMTEAM_API_TOKEN>)`, which names the variable, never the token or its digest.
  `forget_token(port, token)` removes the file when the container ends (only if it still holds this token).
- **Clients.** `client_tokens(url, user_url=None)` is the one rule of where a token may go, in the order a client
  tries them: the token stored for the URL's port only to a loopback URL (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]); `env_token()`
  to a loopback URL or to the hub address the user typed (`user_url`, `dreamteam console --url`: the same scheme, host
  and port), whatever its host; nothing to any other URL (a hub.json sits in the mounted folder, and the agents must
  not be able to send a client's token anywhere else). The clients of a hub in their own process pass its own address
  as `user_url`: `cli._start_console` (the console of `serve`/`run`: `public_base`, the bind address or
  `DREAMTEAM_PUBLIC_URL`), the board `serve` and `run --open` open in the browser once they listen
  (`browser_url(<board>, user_url=public_base)`) and the TUI's `_start_launcher` (`HubClient(base, user_url=base)`,
  also for its stream and its `/web`), so that `serve --host <a LAN address>` with `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN` lets its own
  console, browser and TUI in. The console and the TUI's launcher also call `serving(base)` for a hub with a token:
  `client_tokens` then offers `own_token()` to that scheme, host and port, after the others (`own=False`, which
  `browser_url` and `client_token` pass, leaves it out: a browser is no client in this process), so that a hub
  started with `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN_SHA256` alone lets its own console and TUI in.
  Duplicates go; the token a hub took last (`token_taken`, per
  scheme, host and port; ws counts as http) goes first while it is still a candidate, so a stale stored token (a
  sandbox killed before its `forget_token`) costs one refused request before `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN`. Clients look the
  tokens up for every request, since `dreamteam sandbox` makes a new one at every start on the same port while they
  stay attached: `open_hub(request, timeout, user_url=)` (urllib: `cli.hub_identity`, so `running_hub`, `_hub_json`,
  `cmd_status`, `_hub_delete_session`, `console.Hub`) and `httpx_auth(user_url=None)` (an `httpx2.Auth`, imported
  lazily: the TUI's `HubClient` per request, `hub_mcp.proxy_http_client(url)`, which Claude Code keeps running) send
  the first candidate
  and retry with the next one on `refused(status, headers)` (401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="DreamTeam"`;
  another server's 401 is no refusal); the TUI's stream computes the header at every (re)connect
  (`HubClient._ws_open`) and tries the next candidate on a refused handshake (401/403: the guard closes before accept).
  A redirect never takes the token along: `open_hub` sends it as an unredirected header (urllib copies the others to
  the redirect's target), httpx2 and websockets drop it on a cross-origin redirect. A loopback URL (`is_loopback_url`)
  never goes through the environment's proxy (`HTTP_PROXY` without `NO_PROXY` for loopback would get the request and
  its token): `open_hub` opens it with an opener without proxies (`_urlopen`), `proxy_http_client(url)` and the
  TUI's `HubClient` set `trust_env=False` for it, the stream `proxy=None`. When the hub refuses every candidate (or
  none may go there), `open_hub` raises `TokenRequired(url, user_url=)`, whose text names what was tried (the stored
  file, `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN`) and what to set, or, for a URL no token may go to, that a token goes only to loopback
  or to an address typed with `dreamteam console --url`, and that an address read from a hub.json gets none (never a
  ready-made `--url <that address>`: whoever wrote the hub.json would get the user's token from it); `HubClient`
  raises `HubError(401, <that text>)`, the console prints it once per outage (at its first read of the inbox too: a
  console that ended there would end `serve` or `run` with it), the TUI when its stream is refused (it asks the hub
  over REST, for a single swarm's stream too), `main()` for the other commands; `running_hub` never takes such a hub
  for a dead one. `browser_url(url, user_url=None)` adds `?token=` (the first candidate) for `webbrowser.open` (the
  TUI's `/web`, `serve` finding a running hub, `serve` and `run --open` opening their own board); what is shown on
  screen is the URL without it.

## 15. CLI (cli.py)

Commands of a single-swarm **project** (a directory with `dreamteam.toml`, made by `init`); the launcher
commands of a **home** are in §18.3.
```
dreamteam init [DIR] [--lang ru|en] [--provider anthropic|openai|openrouter|ollama|vllm] [--name N] [--goal G] [--force]
dreamteam run [DIR] [--goal G] [--host H] [--port P] [--no-console] [--open] [--network on|off]
    [--mode board|thread] [--goal-rule democracy|veto]   # the mode is fixed when swarm.db is first made (§22.8)
    # one swarm, its board at / (web.serve); refuses when a hub already runs for DIR; --goal sets the goal
    # unless the stored one is active with the same title (compared with split_goal(G)[0], so a multi-line
    # --goal does not reset the goal at every restart); after the banner, settings.unpriced_line (§17.1) on stderr
```
`console`, `mcp`, `status` and `sandbox` work with a project as well as with a home (§18.3). A project whose
`.dreamteam/swarm.db` was made by an earlier version (§17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version") is refused by `run`,
`mcp`, `status` and `traces` before anything is written: the project message on stderr, exit 1. The check is the
first step of `Swarm.__init__` once its `config` is resolved (before its `logs` mkdir and `Database(...)`); `run`
(right after `Config.load`) and project-mode `mcp` call `db.made_by_earlier_version` themselves
(`cli._earlier_project`) before `setup_logging(project)`, so a refused project gets no log file either, and
`traces`, which builds no `Swarm`, checks before `Database(...)` (§18.3). In the CLI's own checks a database that
cannot be read (a sqlite or OS error) counts as not earlier: `Swarm` or `Database` then fails on it the usual way.

## 16. Traces (tracing.py)

Each activation (wake-up) of an LLM agent is one **trace** (`kind = "llm"`). An external member (hub MCP
`as_agent`) gets **session traces** (`kind = "external"`) that group its tool calls. A trace holds **spans**:

| kind | name | input | output | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| input | `wake` / `incoming` / `nudge` / `continue` | – | text added to the context | `record()` |
| llm | `step` / `compaction` (the purpose) while running; the model id when finished | `{"epoch","upto","messages","extra","tools_rev"}` (`tools_rev`: the revision of the frozen tool set the call sent, §6.1) | `{"stop_reason","thinking","text","tool_calls":[{id,name,arguments,parse_error?}]}` | usage, cost; meta `{purpose, attempt}` (+ `max_tokens` when the request's output limit was raised, §6.2) + `{stop_reason}`; a refusal ends the span with status `error`; every failed attempt is its own span with status `error`, `error` text and meta `{error_kind, retry_in?}`, named after the configured model; a call cut off by a stop is `interrupted` (error_kind `cancelled`, not counted as an error) |
| tool | tool name | arguments (dict) | full result text (before truncation for the model) | meta `{call_id, chars, shown_chars?}`; status `error` if is_error; task ids in `task_id` / `parent_id` / `depends_on` are added to the trace's `tasks` |
| compaction | `compaction` | `{"messages","prompt_tokens"}` | summary text | parent of its llm span; meta `{epoch_archived, fallback?, tools_revision}` (the tool set from then on, §6.1); status `error` when the summary call failed |
| event | `reply_to_user` / `refusal` / `budget_pause` / `step_limit` / `stopped` / `crash` | – | text | `refusal` and `crash` have status `error` |

- Span statuses: `running`, `ok`, `error`, `interrupted` (cut off: a stop, or a finished/recovered trace).
- Trace statuses (`TRACE_STATUSES`): `running`, `done`, `error`, `step_limit`, `refusal`, `paused`, `stopped`,
  `interrupted`. The list filter `status=failed` matches error, step_limit, refusal and interrupted.
- Trace row: `{id, agent, kind, started_at, ended_at, status, outcome, trigger, from_user, steps, llm_calls,
  tool_calls, errors, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, tasks: [ids],
  model, duration_ms}` (a running trace's duration counts to now). Summaries (lists, events) cut `trigger` to
  300 chars. Span row: `{id, trace_id, agent, parent_id, step, kind, name, started_at, ended_at, duration_ms,
  status, input, output, meta, usage, cost_usd, error}`.
- `trace.outcome` is a short human sentence.
- Payload strings are capped at `tracing.max_payload_chars` (middle cut `…[N chars cut]…`); NaN / Infinity in
  payloads are stored as strings (the HTTP JSON encoder rejects them); plain TEXT columns go through
  `db.utf8_safe`, so model output with lone surrogates never breaks the writer.
- Live events are published with `bus.publish` (§9): `trace.started {trace}`, `trace.span {trace, span}` and
  `trace.finished {trace}`. Here `trace` is a trace summary and `span` is
  `{id, kind, name, step, status, duration_ms, cost_usd, usage, parent_id}`.
- Compaction archive: `AgentRuntime._replace_history` calls `swarm.tracer.archive_history(db.conn, name)` inside
  its `db.transaction()`, before deleting the history. The epoch number comes from the `history_archive` table (a
  rolled-back transaction leaves no gap); every archived epoch has a marker row (`seq = -1`, msg NULL), and with
  tracing off only the marker is written (plus the messages when the agent's newest LLM trace may still need
  them). `Tracer.span_context(span_id)` then rebuilds `{span_id, agent, epoch, model, system, tools, messages,
  complete, note}` for any LLM span, reading the live epoch from the table (a second reader such as the CLI
  gets it right too); its `tools` (unless given) are the tools that call sent: `frozen.for_span(db, agent, language,
  input.tools_rev)` = the agent's record when its revision matches, else that revision's shipped snapshot, else the
  record's tools (the current set when the agent has no record). `export()` passes `tools=[]`.
- External members: `tracer.external_call(agent, tool, args_without_as_agent, result_text, is_error, started_at)`
  for every hub tool call by an external member except `wait_for_events`. A session trace closes (`done`) at
  its last call after `EXTERNAL_IDLE_SECONDS` (15 min) without calls (scheduler: `close_external(idle_seconds)`),
  when the swarm stops (`close_external()`), or at the next start (`recover()`).
- API (all on `Tracer(db, bus=None, *, enabled=True, max_payload_chars=200_000)`):
  `begin(agent, trigger="", *, kind="llm", from_user=False, started_at=None) -> Trace`,
  `finish(trace_id, status="done", outcome="", *, ended_at=None)`, `recover() -> int` (open traces of a previous
  process: llm → `interrupted`, external → `done`), `external_call`, `close_external(idle_seconds=None)`,
  `current_epoch(agent)`, `archive_history(conn, agent) -> epoch`,
  `list_traces(agent=None, *, limit=50 (max 500), before=None, status=None, task=None, kind=None)` (newest
  first), `trace_summary(id)`, `get_trace(id, *, payload_chars=0)` (with `spans`), `get_span(id, *,
  payload_chars=0)`, `span_context(id, tools=None)`, `stats(agent=None, since=None)`, `export(id, *,
  contexts=False)` and `prune(older_than_days) -> int`.
  - `stats()` → `{agent, traces, llm_calls, tool_calls, errors, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens,
    cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, statuses: {status: n}, tools: [{name, calls, errors, avg_ms, max_ms}],
    models: [{name, calls, errors, avg_ms, cost_usd, output_tokens}]}` (a covering index keeps it fast).
  - `export()` → the trace with spans plus `member {name, role, model, language, system_prompt}`; with
    contexts=True every LLM span carries `context {messages, complete}` (each history epoch read once).
  - `prune(days)` deletes finished traces (with spans) older than that and history archived before then,
    keeping the newest epoch marker of every agent.
- `Trace` (the writer of one trace; every method is a no-op when tracing is off, and `llm_start` then runs no
  SQL at all): `start`, `end`, `record`, `note_tasks`, `llm_start(messages, *, purpose, extra, attempt,
  parent, tools_rev=None)`, `llm_end(span, response, cost)`, `llm_error(span, error, *, kind, retry_in=None,
  model=None, status="error")`, `tool_start(call_id, name, arguments)`, `tool_end(span, result, is_error,
  shown_chars=None)`, `finish(status, outcome)`.
- Text renderers (CLI, console, the tool; UTF-8-safe): `trace_line(t)`, `render_trace(trace, detail_chars=300)`,
  `render_span(span, limit=20000)`, `render_context(ctx, offset=0, limit=30, chars=4000)`.

### 16.1 Runtime integration (swarm.py, agent.py)
- `Swarm.__init__`: `self.tracer = Tracer(self.db, self.bus, enabled=cfg.tracing.enabled,
  max_payload_chars=cfg.tracing.max_payload_chars)`; `session_id` and `session_title` are None until a
  SessionManager sets them.
- `Swarm.start`: first `self.tracer.recover()` (then `self.jobs.recover()`, §7.1), then
  `self.tracer.prune(retention_days)` if it is > 0. The scheduler prunes again every 6 h.
- `Swarm.stop`: wakes the long polls, `self.tracer.close_external()`, then stops the runtimes (each closes its
  LLM client with `aclose()`), then the jobs (§3).
- `Swarm.reconfigure(config: Config)`: hot-apply new settings to a loaded swarm.
  - Keep `project_dir` (data_dir and workspace stay), `self.language` and the agents' frozen system prompts.
  - Replace `self.config`; update the tracer `enabled` / `max_payload_chars`.
  - Replace `llm_semaphore` with a new one if `max_parallel_llm_calls` changed.
  - For each runtime, `runtime.reset_llm()` (the next call builds a client from the new profile); an agent in
    ERROR whose activation was cut short is woken to retry it.
  - Lift a budget pause the new budget allows.
  - Called for the global settings (`update_settings`) and for one session (`SessionManager.update`: its
    `overrides`, or the partial `settings` of the board's settings dialog, §17.2, §18.4). The rest is read at each
    use: `[shell]` limits at the next command or job check, `agents.max_steps_per_turn` at the agent's next
    wake-up, `context_tokens` (when the model profile has none of its own) and `tool_output_chars` at the next
    call, `idle_nudge_seconds` at the next scheduler pass, `planning_hint_steps` / `planning_hint_minutes` at the
    planner's next step or scheduler pass, `[swarm] budget_notice_at` at the next `record_usage` (a new fraction or
    limit re-arms the money notice through kv `budget_notice`, §3).
- `AgentRuntime`:
  - `self.trace` is the current `Trace`, or None (`_tr` is a disabled writer outside an activation).
  - `_activate` finishes a trace left open (`interrupted`), begins the trace after a non-empty wake text and
    records `input/wake`. It sets `trace.step = step` at each loop iteration. It records `input/incoming`,
    `input/nudge`, `input/continue`, `event/reply_to_user` (auto-forward), `event/refusal` and
    `event/step_limit`; `event/budget_pause` finishes with `paused`.
  - Finish statuses: `stopped` (the agent stopped or left, or the swarm was paused), `paused` (budget),
    `step_limit`, `refusal`, `error` (the LLM failed after retries), `done` otherwise.
  - Outcome: `"Turn ended (wait)"`, `"Answered without tool calls"`, `"Step limit reached (N steps)."`,
    `"The model declined the request."`, the stop or pause reason (`_stop_reason`: `The swarm was paused
    (<Swarm.pause_text()>).`, looked up with getattr, §3.1), or `"{kind}: {message}"` of the LLM error.
  - A crash inside `_activate` is caught by `_run`: it records `event/crash` and finishes the trace with `error`;
    a stop records `event/stopped` and finishes with `stopped`.
  - `_call_llm(messages, *, purpose="step", extra=None, parent=None)` opens one llm span per attempt:
    success → `llm_end(span, response, cost)` (cost = `swarm.record_usage(...)`); retryable error →
    `llm_error(..., retry_in=delay)`; final error → `llm_error(...)`; cancelled → `llm_error(...,
    kind="cancelled", status="interrupted")`. Failed attempts are named after `_model_id()` (the configured
    model of the cached client; never builds one).
  - `_run_tools` uses `tool_start` / `tool_end` with the full text and `shown_chars` when truncated. A parse
    error becomes a tool span with status `error`.
  - `_compact` opens a `compaction` span, calls `_call_llm(..., purpose="compaction", extra=[request],
    parent=span)` and ends the span with the summary (`_compact_without_llm` ends it with meta `fallback`).
  - `reset_llm()` closes (`aclose`, scheduled as a task when a loop runs) and drops the cached client.
  - `agent.activity` events stay as they are.

### 16.2 Tool `agent_traces` (tools/trace_tools.py, audience user + external)
Arguments: `agent` (member name, retired ones too; optional = all members), `trace_id`, `span_id`, `context`
(bool, with span_id), `status` (a trace status or `"failed"`), `task` (int; board sessions only), `limit` (traces:
default 10, max 50; context messages: default 20, max 100), `offset` (first context message, default 0).
In a thread session `agent_traces` has no `task` (its thread variant, §22.5), and a `task` filter of the REST trace
list is a 400 `a thread session has no tasks`: no thread tool takes a task id, so `traces.tasks` stays empty there
(§22.1).

Behaviour:
- No ids: a header and one `trace_line` per trace of `list_traces` (newest first).
- `trace_id`: `render_trace(get_trace(id, payload_chars=600))`.
- `span_id`: `render_span(get_span(id))`.
- `span_id` + `context=true`: `render_context(span_context(id), offset, limit)`.
- Unknown ids (or a context of a non-LLM span) → ToolError.

The descriptions (en, ru) say that it shows what agents did: LLM calls (thinking, text, tool calls, tokens,
cost, latency) and tool executions with full arguments and results.

### 16.3 REST (trace_api.py; per swarm, so `/s/{sid}/api/...` in the launcher)
| method path | response |
|---|---|
| GET `/api/traces?agent=&status=&task=&kind=&limit=50&before=` | `{"traces": [summary...]}` (limit 1..500; `before` = trace id for paging) |
| GET `/api/traces/stats?agent=` | `Tracer.stats()` |
| GET `/api/traces/{id}?payload=20000` | trace with spans; strings clipped to `payload` chars (0 = full); 404 `{"error"}` if missing |
| GET `/api/traces/{id}/export?contexts=0\|1` | JSON attachment `trace-{id}-{agent}.json` (`Tracer.export`) |
| GET `/api/spans/{id}` | full span; 404 if missing |
| GET `/api/spans/{id}/context` | `span_context`; 404 for a missing or non-llm span |
| GET `/api/agents/{name}/traces.jsonl` | `application/x-ndjson` attachment `traces-{name}.jsonl`, streamed: the agent's newest 500 traces (oldest first), one export (no contexts) per line |

Attachment names with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9-_.]` (e.g. Cyrillic member names) are sent as an RFC 5987
`filename*=UTF-8''...` with an ASCII `filename` fallback (`trace-{id}.json`, `traces.jsonl`); downloads are
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

## 17. Sessions and settings

### 17.1 Settings (settings.py, config.py)
- The **home** is `$DREAMTEAM_HOME`, else `~/DreamTeam` (`default_home()`); the CLI flags `--home` / DIR
  override both. Its settings file is `<home>/dreamteam.toml` (`settings_path(home)`) with the sections
  `SECTIONS = swarm, agents, server, shell, workspace, mcp, skills, tracing, api, teams, roles, models` (same format
  as a project's `dreamteam.toml`; `teams` and `roles` are arrays of tables, `[[teams]]`, the saved teams, and
  `[[roles]]`, the role catalog, both of §17.3; `api` is edited by hand only, below).
- `ensure_home(home, language="ru", provider="anthropic")` creates the directory, `sessions/` and the settings
  file from the template; `read_raw(home)`; `validate(home, raw) -> Config` (ValueError with a readable text);
  `dump_toml(data)` (a top-level non-empty list of tables is written as `[[name]]` blocks after every table,
  None values skipped; a leaf `env` or `extra` table is written inline, except a root of that name under
  `[api.folders]`); `deep_merge(base, override)`.
- `[swarm] budget_notice_at` (a number from 0 to 1, default 0.8; a field of `SwarmSettings` right after
  `max_cost_usd`; out of range is a ValueError through `config._MAX["budget_notice_at"] = 1`, `[swarm]
  budget_notice_at must be between 0 and 1, got 1.5`; a whole number in the file stays one, so it is read as
  `float(config.swarm.budget_notice_at or 0)`): the share of the session's money limit at which every AI agent gets
  one `n_budget_low` and USER one `u_budget_low` (§3 `record_usage`: once per limit and fraction, kv
  `budget_notice`); 0 or 1: no such notice (`u_budget` at the limit covers it). Read at each `record_usage`; session
  overrides and `reconfigure` apply, and a new fraction or limit re-arms the notice. Texts ({pct} without a format
  spec): `n_budget_low` ``Money: spent ${spent:.2f} of the ${limit:.2f} budget ({pct}%). When it is used up, the
  swarm pauses: every agent stops between two steps, even in the middle of a task. Don't wait for the user to ask
  for a wrap-up: from now on finish what is nearly done and hand it in (`task_complete`), do the reviews waiting
  for you, keep the results consistent with what they say, and start nothing large.`` (ru «Деньги: потрачено
  ${spent:.2f} из ${limit:.2f} денежного бюджета ({pct}%). …»); `u_budget_low` `The team has spent ${spent:.2f} of
  the ${limit:.2f} budget ({pct}%); the agents were told to finish what is nearly done and start nothing large.
  When the budget is used up, the swarm pauses; to let it work longer, raise the limit.` The warning colour of the
  budget bar stays at 80 % of the limit whatever the fraction (the board's `#budget-bar`, the TUI's status line).
  The template has the line `budget_notice_at = 0.8` after `max_cost_usd`, with a Russian comment; the settings
  page's «Новые сессии по умолчанию» section has its field (§18.4), and only there, like `crew_review`: not the ⚙
  dialog, the new-session modal, the API's create fields or a CLI flag.
- `[swarm] independent_review` (bool, default true; a non-bool is a ValueError naming `[swarm]
  independent_review`): an agent's finished task is approved by another member, or by the user when nobody else
  can (§4.1); false: a task without a reviewer is done at once. The template has the line `independent_review =
  true` with a comment, after the `starting_roles` comment (which names the starting team rule, §17.3), and a
  commented `[[roles]]` example before the model profiles, with a commented `[[teams]]` example before the role
  catalog's.
- `[swarm] crew_review` (bool, default true; a non-bool is a ValueError, "true or false"): the review of a crew task
  its owner completed with at least one direction done is the check of the whole (§4.2 "Finishing"): its reviewer
  is picked preferably outside the crew and asked to check how the directions fit together; whether it is reviewed
  at all follows `independent_review` (off: only by a reviewer of its own). false: no second review, since each
  direction was reviewed already: the owner's completion makes the crew task `done` at once, whatever
  `independent_review` says and whatever reviewer it holds; the board picks no reviewer for it. A toggle leaves a crew task already in review alone. Read at each completion and review request;
  session overrides apply. The template has the line `crew_review = true  # завершённую групповую задачу проверяет
  целиком, по возможности, агент вне её направлений; false — без второго ревью (направления уже проверены): готова,
  как только владелец её завершит, даже с назначенным ревьюером` after
  `independent_review` (one line in the file, its `#` in the column of the lines around it).
- `[swarm] network` ("on" | "off", default "on"; anything else is a ValueError naming `swarm.network`): "off"
  cuts the members' commands, their jobs and the stdio MCP servers off the network (§7.2). Read at each use;
  session overrides apply (a running session: from its next command). The template has the line after
  `crew_review`, with a Russian comment that says it is strict only in Docker and on Linux.
- `[swarm] clarify` (bool, default false; a non-bool is a ValueError, "true or false"): clarify mode (§3.1): a new
  planning task first asks the user about the goal's forks while the others wait, and a member's `send_message` with
  `pause_swarm` pauses the swarm until the user answers. Read live; session overrides and the partial `settings`
  update apply (`clean_overrides` keeps `false`, so a session can switch off a global `true`); switching it off on a
  running swarm lifts a question pause (`reconfigure`). Under the auto-reply lease of `dreamteam -p` it does not
  apply. The template has the line `clarify = false` after `network`, with a Russian comment that covers both modes;
  in a thread session clarify means §22.4 "Clarify".
- `[swarm] mode` ("board" | "thread", default "board"; anything else is a ValueError `swarm.mode must be 'board' or
  'thread', got ...`): the mode of new sessions (§22). An existing session's mode is its database's (kv `swarm_mode`,
  §22.1): a change here, in a project's dreamteam.toml or in session.json never changes it (`main` and `dreamteam
  run` projects included; a value that differs logs a warning and is ignored). The template has `mode = "board"`
  after `clarify`; the settings page's «Новые сессии по умолчанию» section has «Режим работы», the new-session
  modal `#ns-mode`, and a session's ⚙ dialog shows its mode read-only (§22.8).
- `[swarm] goal_rule` ("democracy" | "veto", default "democracy"; anything else is a ValueError `swarm.goal_rule
  must be 'democracy' or 'veto', got ...`): the default rule of new thread sessions, frozen into each at create
  (§22.4); board sessions ignore it. The template has `goal_rule = "democracy"` after `mode`; the settings page's
  «Новые сессии по умолчанию» section has «Решение о цели», the new-session modal `#ns-rule`, and the ⚙ dialog of
  a thread session its group «Тред» (§22.8).
- `[agents] idle_nudge_seconds = 60` (number ≥ 0): how long the scheduler lets an idle member be before it steps in
  (§3): the spacing of item 1's offers to one member, the stall wakes and liveness marks of items 2-3 (§4.2
  "Finishing"), the review reminders (item 5, §4.1 "Liveness"), ten times over (`CREW_GAP_FACTOR`) the free-place
  notice of item 8 (§4.2 "A free place"), whose free members must also have been idle this long, and five times
  over (`TEAM_ASLEEP_FACTOR`), doubled with each such wake under the goal, the team-asleep wake of item 9 (0
  removes every such delay: item 9 then still wakes at most twice per board state, but a member that changes a
  task's status at every wake is woken again at almost every pass, §3 item 9 *Due*). Read at each scheduler pass;
  session overrides apply. The template has no line for it; the settings page's «Агенты»
  section and the session dialog's «Агенты» group have its field («Напоминание простаивающим, с»).
- `[agents] planning_hint_steps = 8` (whole number ≥ 0) and `planning_hint_minutes = 10` (number ≥ 0): the planning
  hint of §3 (scheduler item 4; in clarify mode, before the planner has asked, its `n_clarify_hint`), after this
  many LLM steps or minutes of holding the planning task without creating a task, once more at twice the value; 0
  turns that trigger off. Read at each use; session overrides apply. The
  template has both lines with Russian comments after `stagger_seconds`.
- `[agents] file_settle_seconds = 60`, `file_max_wait_seconds = 300` and `trigger_wake_seconds = 180` (numbers ≥ 0;
  §8): file_changed() is true once the file has had no change for `file_settle_seconds` or the agents who changed
  it have ended their turns, at the latest `file_max_wait_seconds` after the first counted change (0: at every
  change / no cap); a member's repeating trigger wakes it at most once per `trigger_wake_seconds`, the fires in between come in
  one notice (0: at every fire). The worst delay of a file_changed() notice is about settle + interval, or max_wait +
  interval for a file that keeps changing. Read at each pass and use; session overrides apply. The template has the
  three lines with Russian comments after `planning_hint_minutes`; the settings page's «Агенты» section and the
  session dialog's «Агенты» group have a field for each.
- `[agents] digest_seconds = 60` (a number ≥ 10, through `config._MIN`: `[agents] digest_seconds must be >= 10, got
  5`; §22.3): in a thread session, while the goal is active, an idle AI agent whose oldest undelivered digest item
  (votes aside) is this old is woken once with what has gathered, and an external member's `wait_for_events` returns
  then (with no goal or a done goal nothing is batched: digest items wait for the next wake-up). Read at each use;
  session overrides apply; board sessions ignore it. The template has the line with a Russian comment after
  `trigger_wake_seconds`; the settings page's «Агенты» section has «Сводка подписок, с», the ⚙ dialog of a thread
  session its group «Тред» (§22.8).
- `[shell]` (`ShellSettings`, read at each use, so `reconfigure` and session overrides apply at once; §7, §7.1):
  `program = "auto"` (auto | bash | sh | powershell | pwsh | cmd), `timeout = 120` (seconds a call waits; a command
  still running then continues in the background), `max_timeout = 1800` (the largest `timeout`, and the lifetime of a
  command that went on at its timeout; the wait itself is capped by `foreground_max`, over MCP by 600 s),
  `background_on_timeout = true` (false: such a command is killed, as before), `foreground_max = 180` (an AI agent's
  call waits at most this, whatever its `timeout`, while its command could become a job), `max_jobs_per_member = 4`
  and `max_jobs = 16` (running background jobs per member and per session; 0 = no background jobs),
  `job_max_minutes = 480` (lifetime of jobs started in the background or left running by their command; 0 = no
  limit), `job_log_mb = 2` (output kept per job in two files; at most 64 is used), `cpu_threads = "auto"` (the
  thread pools of numeric libraries per command: "auto" shares the cores among the AI agents, N, 0 = no cap; "auto"
  in any case or a whole number, also written as a string; anything else is a ValueError `[shell] cpu_threads must
  be "auto" or a whole number ...`), `pass_env = []`. `timeout`, `max_timeout`, `foreground_max` and `job_log_mb`
  are at least 1. The template lists every key with a Russian comment.
- `[workspace]` copy limits (`WorkspaceSettings`, next to `git` and `lock_ttl_minutes`): `copy_max_mb = 1024` and
  `copy_max_files = 100000`, the largest copy into a new session (§17.2 "Copying files into a new session"): the
  MB and the files of a folder copy or an unpacked zip (the left-out names `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`
  and `__pycache__` do not count); `copy_max_mb` also caps a zip file's own size and an upload of `POST
  /api/uploads` (§18.1). Both are at least 1 (`_MIN`: 0 would refuse every copy). Read from the global
  settings at each create and each upload (`copyfrom.CopyLimits.from_config`; a hand edit of the file applies at
  once). A session override of them passes validation but has no effect: the copy is made
  before the session exists, and an upload has no session. The template's `[workspace]` block has both lines with
  Russian comments.
- `[mcp] library_dir = "~/.dreamteam/library"` (the shared MCP library, §11; `Config.library_dir`, where
  `DREAMTEAM_MCP_LIBRARY_DIR` wins, as `DREAMTEAM_SKILLS_DIR` does for the skills library: the tests set it). The
  variable is one of shell's `_INTERNAL_ENV` (never in the members' commands, §7) and of `docker.SKILLS_ENV` (never
  passed into the sandbox by name).
- `[workspace]` (`WorkspaceSettings`): `git = true` (the shared workspace under git with autocommits),
  `lock_ttl_minutes = 30` (whole number ≥ 1: the time of a `lock_file` call without `minutes`; 0 would refuse every
  such call), `lock_wanted_minutes = 5` (number ≥ 0: a lock members were refused is named to its holder once it has
  held it this long, `n_lock_wanted`, §7 "Lock waiters"; 0: at the first refusal). The lock keys are read at each
  use; session overrides apply. The template has them with Russian comments; the settings page's «Workspace»
  section has a field for each.
- `[api]` (`ApiSettings`, global only: not one of the session `OVERRIDE_SECTIONS`; §21.9, §21.10): `max_running = 3`
  (0 = no limit), `uploads_pending = 32`, `archive_max_mb = 1024`, `folders = {}` (`[api.folders.<name>]` tables with
  `path` and `in_place`, only their shape checked at load). `Config.api` holds it; `config.parse_api_folders(raw)`
  turns the folders into `{name: ApiFolder(name, path, in_place=False)}`. It is edited by hand only: `public_view`
  leaves it out (the settings page has no section for it), and `apply_update` drops an `[api]` key that is None or
  equal to its default, and an empty section (`settings.api_values`), so a save never writes it. The template has
  only a commented `# [api]` block, with the defaults and one example root. `api.folders` is one of `LOCAL_KEYS`
  (§20.4).
- `[skills]` (`SkillsSettings`, global only: not one of the session `OVERRIDE_SECTIONS`; §19): `library_dir =
  "~/.dreamteam/skills"` (the shared skills library; `Config.skills_library_dir`, where `DREAMTEAM_SKILLS_DIR` wins:
  the Docker sandbox and the tests set it), `claude = true` (offer Claude Code's skills), `max_mb = 10` and
  `max_files = 200` (one skill), `max_archive_mb = 50` (one zip or Git checkout before a skill is picked from it),
  `max_attached = 40` (skills of one session), `max_proposals = 10` (skills the members of one session may
  propose; 0 turns proposals off). Script dependencies (§19): `install = true` (install a skill's
  requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / package.json), `install_proposals = true` (also for the agent trust
  class, §19: members' proposals and `claude-project` skills; never in a session without network, §7.2),
  `envs_dir = "~/.dreamteam/skill-envs"` (`Config.skill_envs_dir`, where `DREAMTEAM_SKILL_ENVS_DIR` wins: the
  sandbox's volume and the tests), `python = ""` (the environments' interpreter: "" = the base interpreter DreamTeam
  runs on; a path, a command, or with uv a version such as "3.12"), `install_scripts = false` (npm lifecycle
  scripts of the dependencies), `install_timeout = 900` (seconds per install command), `env_retention_days = 30`
  (unused environments are removed after this; 0 = never automatically), `install_env = []` (variables the
  installers of the user's own skills get, e.g. a private index's password; each must be a variable name, else
  ValueError `skills.install_env: 'x y' is not an environment variable name`). Changes apply at the next attach or
  session start (a plan is keyed by `skill_deps.settings_hash`). All but `max_proposals` and `env_retention_days`
  are at least 1. `Config.skills_host_library_dir` is `DREAMTEAM_HOST_SKILLS_DIR` (set only inside the sandbox),
  else None. The template has the block after `[mcp]` with Russian comments.
- `[[roles]]` → `Config.roles: list[RoleSettings]` (`RoleSettings(name, description="", instructions="",
  model=None, hidden=False, skills=[])`), checked by `config.parse_roles(raw, profiles)` after the model profiles (§17.3).
- `[[teams]]` → `Config.teams: list[TeamSettings]` (`TeamSettings(name, roles)`), checked by
  `config.parse_teams(raw, entries)` after the roles (§17.3 "Saved teams").
- `config.Config.from_dict` checks every field against its type (bool / int / float / str / list[str] /
  tables; integral floats become ints, bools are not numbers, no NaN/inf, counts and sizes >= 1, port <= 65535;
  None = the default) with messages like `[agents] max_steps_per_turn must be ...`; API keys are never echoed.
  `make_profile(name, spec)` builds a `ModelProfile`; `env_var_name(value)` normalizes `api_key_env`
  (`$NAME`, `${NAME}`, `%NAME%` → `NAME`), and a value that cannot be a variable name is treated as a pasted
  key (`api_key`). `toml_string()` writes TOML basic strings (used by `render_template` for name and goal).
- `write_raw(home, raw)`: validates, refuses data that would not read back identically, keeps the previous
  file as `dreamteam.toml.bak`, writes atomically (temp file + replace, never left behind) and makes the
  settings and the backup owner-only on POSIX (they hold API keys).
- `public_view(raw)`:
  - every section with defaults filled in, but no `api` (§21.9: edited by hand only); no `swarm.goal` /
    `swarm.goal_description`;
  - in model profiles, `api_key` is null and comes with `api_key_set`, `api_key_hint` (`…abcd`) and
    `api_key_env_set` (true/false, or null when there is no env name); `api_key_env` is a variable name or
    null (a key pasted there is never shown); `price_source` is `ModelProfile.price_source()` (§10). These computed
    fields (`_PUBLIC_KEY_FIELDS`) are dropped by `apply_update` and `profile_from_view`;
  - values of `mcp.external.<server>.env` are masked as `SECRET_MASK + hint` (`••••…abcd`);
  - `roles`: the stored `[[roles]]` entries `[{name, description, instructions, model, hidden, skills}]`, normalized
    (a built-in role by its id, e.g. «Тестировщик» → `tester`); `[]` when there are none;
  - `teams`: the stored `[[teams]]` entries `[{name, roles}]`, normalized (§17.3 "Saved teams"); `[]` when there are
    none.
- `apply_update(raw, update)` (a dict of sections; ValueError for bad input):
  - `roles` is the complete list of entries: not a list → "Section roles must be a list of roles", an item that
    is not an object → "Role N must be an object"; names get their whitespace collapsed; fields that are null,
    `""`, `[]` (no skills) or `hidden: false` are not stored (an untouched field of a built-in role keeps the built-in value);
    `[]` removes every customization; a role's `model` follows a profile rename; the rules themselves are
    checked by `validate` (`[roles.N] ...`);
  - `teams` is the complete list of entries: not a list → "Section teams must be a list of teams", an item that is
    not an object → "Team N must be an object"; only null values are dropped, so the file keeps what was sent, and
    `Config.teams` and the view normalize it at each load; `[]` removes the key; the rules themselves are checked by
    `validate` (`[teams.N] ...`);
  - each section present replaces the stored one (null values dropped); a stored `swarm.goal` stays; `api` (never
    sent by the settings page) is stored without the keys equal to their default (`api_values`), and an empty one
    removes the section;
  - masked `mcp.external.*.env` values get their stored value back (same server first, then a renamed one);
    an unknown mask is a ValueError;
  - `models` is the complete set of profiles (missing ones are deleted; names `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`; at least one);
    per profile, an `api_key` that is null or absent keeps the stored key (of the same profile, or of
    `renamed_from`), `""` removes it, and any other string sets it (whitespace stripped); a key pasted into
    `api_key_env` becomes the `api_key`;
  - renaming the default profile (`renamed_from`) moves `agents.default_model` along (`profile_renames(update)`
    gives `{old: new}` of every card whose `renamed_from` differs from its name, a swap or a chain in one save
    included, applied in one step; an old name that a card not renamed from anything still has is left out). A
    stored value carries an old name and follows; an `agents.default_model` or role `model` sent with the update
    that names one of its profiles is a new name and is kept (the web UI sends the names after the save: in a swap
    a new name is also an old one).
- `profile_from_view(raw, data, name=None) -> ModelProfile` (an unsaved UI profile; a missing key falls back to
  the stored key of profile `name`, only when `data` has the provider and base_url that profile is saved with
  (a trailing `/` aside), else a ValueError. A key from the hub's environment (`api_key_env`, or with no key the
  SDK's own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the official OpenAI endpoint) goes only to the
  provider's default endpoint (no base_url), or to the endpoint of a `PROVIDER_CHOICES` preset or of a saved
  profile without a stored key that names the same variable, else a ValueError (save first); a key in `data`
  goes anywhere. ValueError for unknown fields or wrong types).
  The official URL spelled out (`https://api.openai.com` with or without `/v1` for the OpenAI client,
  `https://api.anthropic.com` for anthropic; parsed host and path compared exactly, never as a substring) counts
  as the default endpoint. `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` (provider anthropic) and `OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS` (the
  OpenAI client's providers) from the hub's environment (the SDKs add them to every request; `_headers_env`)
  go, whatever the key, only to the default endpoint or to that of a saved profile, else a ValueError (save
  first); `scrub_keys()` masks their values too.
- `async list_models(profile, timeout=20)` (GET /models, free; ValueError with a readable message).
- `async check_profile(profile, *, live=False, timeout=30)` → `{ok, models, models_error, model_found, error,
  reply, latency_ms, cost_usd, cost_source}`. `live=True` sends one tiny request (max_tokens <= 512; effort `low`
  only when the profile uses effort); `cost_source` is then `"provider"` when the response reported its cost, else
  the probe's `price_source(response model)` (`"none"` / `"partial"`: those tokens counted as $0), null without a
  live request. Errors and replies pass through `scrub_keys()`: an endpoint echoing a rejected key never sends it
  to the browser.
- `PROVIDER_CHOICES`: presets for the UI (`anthropic`, `openai`, `openrouter`, `ollama`, `vllm`, `lmstudio`,
  `custom`), each `{id, label, provider, base_url, api_key_env | api_key, model, models, ...}`. The `openai` preset
  sets `input_price = 1.25` and `output_price = 10.0` (as the init template), the local ones 0 / 0.
- `unpriced_line(config) -> str | None`: the note the `serve` and `run` banners print (§18.3), English and ASCII:
  `Note: model profiles without prices: remote (some-model-v1), half (kimi: no output_price). Their unpriced tokens
  count as $0 and the budget does not see them, unless the provider reports the cost. Set input_price and
  output_price ($ per 1M tokens, 0 for a free model) in Settings > Models and endpoints or in dreamteam.toml.`; the
  profiles with `missing_prices()`, the scripted provider aside; None when there are none.

### 17.2 Sessions (sessions.py)
`SessionManager(home, *, llm_factory=None, language="ru", provider="anthropic")` (`ensure_home` + the
settings; ValueError when they are invalid):
- Attributes: `home`, `raw` / `config` (the global settings), `swarms` (loaded Swarm objects by sid),
  `running` (the set of started ones), `hub_url` (set by `launcher.serve_launcher`; a session swarm's `hub_url`
  is `f"{hub_url}/s/{sid}/mcp"`), `sessions_dir`, `uploads` (`copyfrom.Uploads(<home>/.dreamteam/uploads)`, the
  zips of `POST /api/uploads`: "Copying files into a new session" below), `api_uploads`
  (`copyfrom.Uploads(<home>/.dreamteam/uploads/api)`, the files of `POST /api/v1/uploads`, §21.3;
  `clean_copy_leftovers` sweeps both).
- Methods: `listen(fn)` / `unlisten(fn)`, `settings_view()`, `async update_settings(update)`, `ids()`,
  `exists(sid)`, `dir_of(sid)`, `meta(sid)`, `config_for(sid)`, `config_view(sid)`, `summary(sid, *, workspace=True,
  requests=False)` (`workspace` False: `"workspace": None`, the folder not looked at; `requests` True: its
  `requests` count, which only v1's summary asks for), `list()`,
  `default_session()`, `async create(title, goal="", description="", *, overrides=None, start=True,
  workspace=None, skills=None, via="home", auto_reply=False, copy_from=None, copy_from_upload=None, api=None,
  sources=None, mark=None)`, `validated_overrides(overrides)`,
  `async load(sid)`, `async start(sid, *, skills=None,
  via="home", auto_reply=False, marked=None, then=None)`, `mark_starting(sid, mark=None)`, `unmark_starting(sid, mark)`,
  `async stop(sid, *, remember=False, reason="user", uid=None)`, `async unload_idle(sid)`, `async control(sid, *,
  max_cost_usd=None, max_agents=None, wrap_up=None, uid=None)`, `update(sid, *, title=None,
  overrides=None, settings=None)`, `async delete(sid, *, skills=None, via="home", uid=None)`, `async resume()`,
  `plan_resume()`, `cancel_resume()`, `watch(sid)`, `is_final(sid)`, `journal(sid, after, limit, types=None, *,
  recipient=None)`, `sid_of_uid(uid)` (`uid=` of `stop`, `control` and `delete`: the uid the caller resolved,
  checked again once the session's lock is taken, 404 when the folder name holds another session by then),
  `api_sids()`, `sid_of_client_ref(ref)`, `global_config()`, `reading(sid)` (the Swarm a reader in a thread uses:
  `journal` below),
  `session_skills(sid, show=None)`, `async decide_skill(sid, name, approve, *, comment="", replace=False,
  via="home")` ("Skills" below),
  `finished(sid)`, `async shutdown()`, `copy_overrides(sid)`, `default_workspace(sid)`, `workspace_of(sid)`,
  `async set_workspace(sid, path, *, expect=None)`; for an import (§20.4) `staging_path(sid)`, `clean_staging()`,
  `backups(sid)`, `import_overrides(overrides, models)`, `async import_add(staged, meta, workspace, *, sid,
  before_swap=None)`, `async import_rewrite(sid, staged, meta, workspace, *, expect=None, before_swap=None)`,
  `async import_settings(sid, meta, *, expect=None)`, `recover_swaps()` and `interrupted_swaps()`; module functions
  `read_stats(db_path, conn=None, *, clarify=False, running=True, requests=False, mode="board",
  goal_rule="democracy")` (§22.8), `read_lists(db_path, conn=None)`, `read_posts(db_path, conn=None)` (§22.9),
  `slugify(title)`, `external_workspaces(home)`,
  `new_uid()`, `session_uid(meta)`, `api_meta(meta, *, create=False)` and `api_answers(api)`.
- `listen` callbacks receive `{"type": "sessions.changed", "session": sid | None, "change", "ts"}`. The change is
  one of `created`, `started`, `stopped`, `updated`, `deleted` or `settings` (session None).
- **A run's start and end, waiting for a change** (§21.6, §21.7).
  - `_start_locked` journals `session.started` right before `swarm.start()` and, when that raises,
    `session.stopped` {reason: `failed`, error} before its unload (`error` through `_public_text`: an absolute path
    named by its last component, the session's folders whole, see "Sessions of the HTTP API v1" below; the log has
    the whole text); when it is cancelled (the hub stops),
    `session.stopped` {reason: `shutdown`}. `_unload(sid, reason=None)` of a running session journals
    `session.stopped` {reason} after `Swarm.stop` and before the database closes (errors logged, never raised). The
    reasons: `stop()` passes its `reason` (`STOP_REQUEST_REASONS`: `user` by default; `done`, `budget` for
    `stop_when_done`; another is a ValueError); `shutdown()` passes `shutdown`, a workspace move `restart`, a delete
    `user` (the journal goes away with the session when the delete succeeds; when the folder cannot be renamed away,
    409, the session stays stopped, without its resume mark).
  - `watch(sid)` (a context manager) gives an `asyncio.Event` set by every journaled event of the session (one bus
    listener per Swarm, added by `_load_locked`; live-only events do not count), by `_changed(sid, …)`, by resume()
    handling the session, and by the release of the session's lock (the locks are `_SessionLock`, which pokes the
    waiters on release: the end of a start, a stop, a move). It is keyed by session, never by a bus, so it outlives
    an unload. Waiters clear it before each read.
  - `is_final(sid)`: not running, not in `starting` (creates and v1 `continue`s in flight), not in `resume_pending`,
    and the session's lock is not held.
  - `journal(sid, after, limit, types=None, *, recipient=None)` → (events, last, more): one page of the session's
    journal (`events.read_page`, §21.6 "Polling"). A loaded session's through its own connection under its
    `Database`'s lock (never the session's lock); any other's from its file through `db.reading_file`, opened and
    closed for the read, never through `load`; from the file also when an unload closed the connection meanwhile
    (`sqlite3.ProgrammingError`). The connection is the one `reading(sid)` gives: the loaded Swarm's, or, while
    `_unload` stops it, the Swarm it took out of `swarms` until its database is closed (`_unloading`, filled before
    the Swarm leaves `swarms`, emptied after the close). So no reader in a thread opens the file next to an open
    writer: one that did, at the moment of the close, would keep SQLite from folding the `-wal` file back into
    `swarm.db`, and the stopped session would be left with `-wal` and `-shm` files holding its run. The close waits
    for a reader that holds the `Database`'s lock. The rows' `data` is decoded after the `Database`'s lock is released
    (`read_page(..., decode=False)`, then `events.event_data`), since the event loop takes that lock too. A session
    without a database has no events (head 0). A file that cannot be read now is `SessionError` 503
    (`sessions.JOURNAL_TEXT`, the cause logged), never an empty page: that would tell a client which has read `final`
    that nothing more will come, and it would stop early. Blocking: v1 calls it in a thread.
  - `starting`: the sessions with a start on its way. Each such start has a mark of its own: `mark_starting(sid,
    mark=None)` adds one (a new object unless the caller gives one), puts the session in `starting`, pokes its
    waiters and returns the mark; `unmark_starting(sid, mark)` takes that mark away (the session leaves `starting`
    with its last mark). `start(sid, marked=mark)` starts the session only while its mark is there, checked again
    under the session's lock (None otherwise: a delete, or a stop asked after the mark was placed, that held the lock
    while it waited is never undone),
    and takes its own mark away when it ends, whatever its outcome, never another start's (a second caller's, or a
    new session's that got the folder name of a deleted one). `delete()` takes every mark of the session away, and
    `stop()` (without `remember`) the marks placed before it was called (read before its first await), as they take
    it out of `resume_pending`: a start announced after the stop (a v1 `continue` sent after it) keeps its mark and
    starts the session again once the stop is over, whether the stop held the lock already or not, so requests
    keep their order. `create(..., start=True)` marks the new
    session before its first write of session.json (which lists it: `ids()`, v1's listing) and starts it with that
    mark; `create(..., start=False, mark=m)` puts the caller's mark `m` on it at the same point and the caller starts
    it later with `start(sid, marked=m)` (a v1 create or `continue` that starts a session in the background, which
    answers in between); a create that fails after marking takes its mark away. The create holds the session's lock
    from that first write until the session is made (its skills committed, its folder set: `_set_workspace_locked`),
    so a listing shows it `starting`, never final, and a stop, a start, a `continue`, a folder change or a delete
    asked meanwhile waits for it: a run never starts without the skills asked for, a delete never leaves a half-made
    folder behind, and a stop or a delete then takes the create's mark away (its start starts nothing).
  - `start(sid, ..., then=fn)` calls `fn(swarm)` with the running Swarm once the start succeeded (also when the
    session ran already), still under the session's lock, so nothing that waits for the lock (a stop sent meanwhile,
    a `stop_when_done` stop) comes between the start and it: v1's `continue` gives its text there (§21.2). It is
    synchronous; an error it raises is logged and the start stands. Nothing is called when nothing started.
  - `resume_pending`: the sessions resume() will try. `plan_resume()` chooses them by their autostart mark alone
    (session.json reads, no log line: the launcher calls it before its port opens) and fills the set;
    `cancel_resume()` drops the plan when resume() does not run. resume() uses the plan (else chooses now) and
    empties the set one session at a time. At each one's turn it skips, with its log line, a finished session and
    one of an earlier version (both keep their mark), and a session stopped (out of the set, its mark cleared) or
    deleted meanwhile; it checks that last condition again under the session's lock and starts it there
    (`_start_locked`), so a stop that held the lock while resume() waited is never undone.
- `SessionError(message, status=400, *, code=None, holder=None, **extra)` (a ValueError) carries an HTTP status and
  `extra` (put into the JSON answer: `exists` for a skills clash, `pending_skills` for a refused delete): 400 bad
  input or invalid settings, 404 unknown session, 409 conflict (deleting `main`, files in use, a dirty repository to
  adopt or to start in, a folder of another session, a folder that changed since the user was asked, a missing
  workspace folder at start, a `workspace` with files for a copy, a session made by an earlier version), 413 a copy
  over its limits, 500 damaged or cannot be opened (404 is also an unknown or used upload of `copy_from_upload`).
  `code` is the HTTP API v1's code where the status alone does not say it (§21.1), never in `extra`, so the internal
  answers do not show it: `folder_busy` (`FOLDER_BUSY`: `_plan`'s folder of another session, `_check_reserved`'s
  create in progress), `folder_not_ready` (`FOLDER_NOT_READY`: every `_repo_refusal`, so also `_check_adopted_repo`;
  `_check_workspace_ready`'s missing folder and `_check_journal`'s unfinished move; a server folder's repository that
  would make DreamTeam's git write outside it, `_plan` with `within` and `_check_server_git`; a missing root at a
  start), `forbidden_folder` (`FORBIDDEN_FOLDER`, 403: a server folder that no longer lies inside its root, `_plan`
  with `within`, or whose root no longer allows it, `_check_server_folder`, §21.10), `conflict` (`control`'s wrap-up
  before the first start), a CopyError's own code (`bad_name`, `file_conflict`, and a server folder's
  `forbidden_folder`, `not_found`) when `create` turns it into a SessionError; `_move_error` keeps the code of the
  SessionError that failed a workspace change, unless files could not be put back (500), and its `holder`.
  `holder`: the session whose folder it is (`_plan`'s `folder_busy`; none for a create in progress), never in
  `extra` either: v1 names it by its uid, to a caller who sees it, in a text of its own (§21.10). v1 answers a code
  with that code's own status (§21.1), which may differ from `status`: `folder_not_ready` is 409 there, also for the
  two refusals of a create that are 400 on the internal routes (a folder inside a repository, a repository's own
  database).
- **Sessions of the HTTP API v1** (§21.4). `create(..., api={answers, stop_when_done, client_ref, request_digest,
  folder})` (those keys only, `API_GIVEN` defaults for the missing ones; another key or a value of the wrong kind is
  400) writes `"via": "api"` and the `api` block, with `base_commit`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `start_error` and
  `error` null (`API_LATER`), in the first session.json write; `api_meta(meta)` reads that block (None for any other
  session; `{}` for a v1 session whose block is not an object). `create(..., sources=[copyfrom.Source])`: v1's
  claimed uploads and a copy-mode server folder (a Source with `root` and `parts`, read below its root by
  `nofollow`, §21.10) copied by `copy_sources` instead of `copy_into`, not with `copy_from` or `copy_from_upload`
  (400 before any claim); the caller claims and settles the uploads. `create(..., folder_threads=)`: where that copy
  runs instead of the loop's default executor (`_in_thread(threads=)`, which still waits for it after a cancel):
  v1 passes its folder threads (`ApiV1.threads.start`) when a server folder is among the sources (§21.1 "Threads").
  `create(..., workspace=, within=root)`: an in-place server folder, which every `_plan` on the create's way
  (`create`'s own, `_set_workspace`'s and `_change_folder`'s last one, under the workspace claims just before
  `_carry_out` makes the missing folders), and `_carry_out` itself around each folder it makes and around `git init`
  (`_Plan.within`, `_check_inside`), finds inside `within` again, by text and by file identity, else 403
  `forbidden_folder` (these run in the loop's default executor, as for any workspace); with git on, a folder with files
  there must also pass `apifolders.git_dir_refusal` (409 `folder_not_ready`), before git reads it. A workspace move
  by the owner (`_change_folder` without `creating`) sets an in-place `api.folder` to null. Every later write of
  the block is a read-modify-write of session.json under the session's lock (`_api_write`, which logs and never
  raises):
  - `_start_locked`, on every start path: with `answers: "auto"` it calls `swarm.hold_auto_reply()` right after
    loading, before `swarm.start()`; at the first start (`started_at` null) it sets `swarm.workspace.record_head`,
    and once the start succeeded it writes `started_at` and `base_commit` (`Workspace.head_at_init`) with the rest of
    session.json; every start that succeeds clears `start_error` and `finished_at`. That write comes once the swarm
    runs, so its failure is logged, never raised (the start is no failed one: its callers would record a start error
    for a running session). A start that fails, because the
    session cannot be loaded (not a 404, never a session of an earlier version, which is not written to), because
    `_check_workspace_ready` or `_check_adopted_repo` refuse it, or because `swarm.start()` raises, writes
    `start_error` {code, text} and `finished_at` before it raises (and before `session.stopped` is journaled): `code`
    the error's own code, else by the SessionError's status (400 `bad_request`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `conflict`, 413
    `too_large`, an earlier version `earlier_version`), else `internal`; `text` through `_public_text(sid, text)`,
    as is the `session.stopped` error of a failed `swarm.start()`. An error names a folder unquoted, spaces included,
    and `without_abs_paths` alone would cut it at its first space, so `_public_text` names this computer's folders
    first (`eventtext.without_abs_paths(value, named=(), exact=(), hidden=())`: (path, name) pairs, longest first,
    with either separator, single or doubled, in any case, whole components only): `named`, also at the start of a
    path below them, the user's home as `~` (the path below it is then named by its last component) and, by their
    last component, the workspace, an unfinished move's two folders, the session's folder and the home (what lies
    below them stays, relative); `exact`, only where the text names that very folder, every folder above those (a path
    below one may be anyone's: `C:\Users\alice\x` must not become `Users\alice\x`) and the home's `sessions`;
    `hidden`, only a path below it, replaced whole: the home's `sessions` as `SessionManager.OTHER_SESSION`
    (`(a folder of another session)`), since another session's folder name is its title (the session's own folder is
    longer, so named first); each also resolved. The external API's error texts go through it too
    (`_public_text(sid | None, text, *, named=())`: `sid` None, an error of no session, names only the user's home and
    the home; `named` takes the caller's pairs first, unresolved: the roots of `[api] folders` by their names, §21.1
    "Paths in answers"; then a session that works in a server folder in place has that folder named `<root>` and
    its path below the root with the hub's separator, `apifolders.shown(root, path, os.sep)`, §21.10).
    `_public_text_in_home(sid | None)` says whether it looks at no folder outside the home (the user's home aside): no
    session, one whose session.json cannot be read, or one in its own folder or another folder of the home, with no
    move journal; v1 then redacts in the loop's default executor rather than its folder threads (§21.1 "Paths in
    answers"). A start cancelled inside `swarm.start()` (the hub stops) writes `finished_at` and no `start_error`.
  - `_unload` of a running v1 session writes `finished_at` after `Swarm.stop`, whatever the reason.
  - What runs beside a v1 session's run (`_RunWatch`, tied to its Swarm, kept in `_run_watch[sid]`):
    `_start_locked(sid, auto_reply=False, *, resumed=False)` starts it once the swarm runs and its pending goal is
    set (`_start_run_watch`), on every start path: `autoreply.SessionAutoReply` with `answers: "auto"` (§21.5), and
    the stop_when_done watcher (`_watch_end`) with `stop_when_done` true, which follows the journal from its head
    read just before `session.started` (§21.4). `resume()` passes `resumed=True`. `_unload` cancels both and waits
    for them before `Swarm.stop`. The watcher never awaits a stop: `_stop_soon` schedules
    `_stop(sid, reason=..., still=...)` as a task kept in `_stopping`; `_stop` is `stop()` with a check made under the
    session's lock (`still`: the session still runs that Swarm and the reason still holds), else it does nothing; with
    `still` it leaves the marks of starts announced meanwhile (`mark_starting`, `resume_pending`) alone.
    `shutdown()` sets `_closing` (`_stop_soon` then schedules nothing: the resume check covers those), waits for the
    scheduled stops, then unloads.
  - `api_answers(api)`: the block's `answers`, `API_GIVEN`'s "auto" when it has none; the auto-reply hold,
    `_start_run_watch` and `summary` read it.
  - `summary(sid)` adds `via` and `answers` for such a session only.
  - `control(sid, *, max_cost_usd=None, max_agents=None, wrap_up=None, complete_goal=None, goal_summary=None)`
    (v1's PATCH, §21.2; `complete_goal`: `swarm.complete_goal_by_user(goal_summary)` after the limits and before
    wrap-up, the order of `swarm_control`, thread sessions only, §22.9. Its own rules replace the general ones below.
    The session must run: v1 checks this before calling `control` (409 `not_running`). Under the lock, a session that
    no longer runs (it stopped while the call waited for the lock) is 409 `not_running` too; it is never loaded for
    it. Its goal is checked first under the lock, before the limits. No goal, or a goal already done, is 409
    `conflict` with the swarm's text, and nothing is written. These are not the 400 below.) does what
    `swarm_control` does with the limits and wrap-up mode, as the user, under the session's lock: `set_limits` (a
    budget pause the new limit covers is lifted), then `wrap_up` / `end_wrap_up`. For the limits and wrap-up mode, a
    stopped session is loaded
    (one that never started gets its database) and unloaded again unless it was loaded before (the board views
    it). 400 for a value of the wrong kind (a bool, NaN, a `max_agents` that is no whole number) or one the swarm
    refuses (ToolError), with nothing written; 409 `conflict` for `wrap_up: true` while the session has a pending
    goal its first start has not set yet (that `set_goal` ends wrap-up mode), decided before a database is made;
    409 for an earlier version. Nothing given: the summary, nothing loaded. It announces an `updated` change and
    returns the summary.
  - `sid_of_uid(uid)` (32 lowercase hex, else None), `api_sids()` and `sid_of_client_ref(ref)` read an index of every
    session.json (uid → folder name, the v1 sessions, and their `client_ref` → folder name, the first by name when two
    share one), built once and read again when a session comes or goes (`_changed` `created` / `deleted`, an
    import's rewrite or settings) or the sessions folder's mtime changes (another process). A uid the index does not
    know, and every `api_sids()` and `sid_of_client_ref()`, also compare the session folders (`ids()`, no
    session.json read) with those the index was read from: another process makes a session's folder before it writes
    its session.json, which changes no mtime of the sessions folder. A uid two sessions share (a folder copied by
    hand) names neither; the legacy `main` has no uid; a hit is checked against the session.json it names, so a
    deleted session's uid never reaches the session that got its folder number. So a v1 create with a `client_ref`
    reads no session.json per session (§21.4).
  - `read_lists(db_path, conn=None)` → (tasks, agents) of a session database, read-only like `read_stats`, in the
    shape and order of the snapshot (`Task.to_dict()` by priority then id, closed ones too, without the board's
    computed fields; every `agents` row in hiring order): a stopped session's result without loading it (§21.7).
  - An import keeps `via` and the block but sets `client_ref`, `request_digest`, `start_error`, `error` and `folder`
    to null (`API_IMPORT_DROPS`, `_import_meta`, §21.9).
- Session ids are `NNN-slug` from the title (Cyrillic and Ukrainian transliterated, accents dropped; e.g.
