  `001-snake-game`) and match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}\Z`. `main` is the legacy session: a home that was a
  single-swarm project (`<home>/.dreamteam/swarm.db`) lives in the home itself, uses the global settings
  directly (including a `swarm.goal`; always a board session, §22.1), cannot get overrides and cannot be deleted
  from the UI;
  `sessions/main/` is ignored. Titles are one line, at most 200 chars (default: the goal's first line,
  shortened to 60 characters at a word by `goal_text.shorten_title`, else "Session"; an empty `title` lets the
  server derive it).
- **Identity.** The sequence id is not an identity across homes (two homes both make `017-session`). `create`
  writes `"uid": new_uid()` (uuid4, 32 lowercase hex) into session.json; `_write_meta` keeps unknown keys, so
  `update`, `set_workspace` and `start` keep it. (`_write_meta` writes a temporary file and puts it in place with
  `os.replace`; a replace refused with PermissionError, as on Windows while a reader holds session.json open for a
  moment, such as a thread of the HTTP API v1, is tried again, `META_REPLACE_TRIES` = 10 × `META_REPLACE_PAUSE`
  0.02 s, before the error is raised.) `session_uid(meta)` is the stored uid when it is 32 hex characters
  (lowercased), else `uuid5(UID_NAMESPACE, "created_at:" + repr(float(created_at))).hex`, derived on read and never
  written (so a session made before uids existed, or a folder copied by hand, has the same identity in every home
  it is in); None without a finite numeric `created_at` and for the legacy `main` session (never matched).
  `summary(sid)` carries `uid` (None for a damaged session). `UID_NAMESPACE` is fixed forever.
- Effective config of a session = the global settings without `swarm.goal` / `goal_description` and `swarm.mode` (a
  session without a `swarm.mode` override is board whatever the home's default; the mode itself is its database's,
  §22.1), deep-merged
  with its `overrides`. Overrides may only touch the sections swarm, agents, shell, workspace, mcp and tracing
  (`OVERRIDE_SECTIONS`; not models, server, roles or teams: the role catalog and the saved teams are global, and a
  session chooses its starting team with `swarm.starting_roles` / `start_agents`); they are validated at create and
  update time (`update` applies them to a loaded swarm at once via `reconfigure`). `config_view(sid)` is the public
  view of the effective settings (the global ones when the overrides are invalid now).
- Partial update (`update(sid, settings=...)`, the settings dialog of the board, §18.4): `settings` is
  `{section: {key: value | None}}`; each key is set in the stored overrides, None (or "") removes it so the session
  inherits the global value again, and a section left empty disappears. The other overrides (those given at
  creation: language, team, model...) stay. Same sections, cleaning (`clean_overrides`, no goal keys) and
  validation as `overrides`; nothing is written when it fails (also not a `title` passed along). Passing both
  `overrides` and `settings`, a non-object, or `main` is a 400. A loaded swarm is reconfigured as for `overrides`.
- The work mode (§22): `create` writes `swarm.mode` = "thread" and the effective `swarm.goal_rule` into the overrides of
  a thread session only (a board session stores neither key: missing = board), and makes a thread session's database at
  once (kv `swarm_mode`, the authority). `update` refuses to change or clear the mode (400 `the mode is chosen when the
  session is created`) and to clear a thread session's rule, puts both back into a thread session's full `overrides`
  replacement, and refuses `swarm.goal_rule` in a board session (§22.8 "The mode of a session", "Updating a session").
- `create` splits the goal as `set_goal` does (`goal_text.split_goal(goal, description)`) and stores it already
  split as `pending_goal` {title, description, actor} (only with a non-empty title); the first `start` sets it
  once the members exist (a failure keeps it). Module function `pending_goal(meta)` → {title, description} | None
  splits again on read (a `session.json` written before the split may hold a multi-line title); the summary and
  the snapshot's `session.pending_goal` use it. `auto_reply=True` (the request carried the auto-reply header, §14;
  passed on by `create` to its `start`): `_start_locked(sid, auto_reply)` calls `swarm.auto_reply_seen()` right after
  loading (also when the session runs already), so before `swarm.start()`, and again right before the pending
  `set_goal`, so a `dreamteam -p` session gets the classic planning card even when its start outlasts the grace
  (§3.1). `start` marks `autostart`; an explicit `stop` clears it
  (`remember=True`, used at shutdown, keeps it), and `resume()` starts the marked sessions except finished ones
  (`finished(sid)`: the goal is done and no task is open, read from the summary without loading it; False when it
  cannot be read), which stay stopped until started by hand, and sessions made by an earlier version (below).
  `stop` unloads the swarm (stop + close its database).
  Every unload (`stop`, `delete`, a workspace move, `shutdown`) goes through `Swarm.stop`, which ends the session's
  background jobs and closes their logs and handles before it returns (§7.1), so the folder can be moved or deleted
  on Windows too.
- `load(sid)` constructs the swarm without starting it (a stopped session is viewable) and closes the traces a
  crashed process left running (`tracer.recover()`). Load, start, stop, delete and set_workspace run under a
  per-session lock and re-check that the session still exists (404). `shutdown()` also waits for sessions in the
  middle of such an operation (e.g. a workspace move that starts the session again) and then stops them.
- **Sessions of an earlier version.** This version does not open a session made by an earlier DreamTeam; there
  is no conversion, no read-only view and no compatibility mode. `db.made_by_earlier_version(source) -> bool`
  (beside `db.max_tools_revision`, read-only through `_reading`, never creating the file) is true when the
  session database has a kv `tools:<name>` record whose `rev` is an integer below `frozen.OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION`
  (5, §6.1; one numbering for both modes, so a thread record, 6, is never below it, §22.5; retired members count;
  valid or not), or `history` rows of an agent with no usable record (missing, not
  JSON, or not `frozen.valid`, §6.1, the same test `frozen.read` makes: an agent that ran before tool sets were
  frozen). False without a database file (a session
  never started) and for a database with neither (no LLM member ever ran: only the user, external members, or
  members hired and never started): nothing in it is frozen, it is opened as usual, and its LLM members get the
  current revision at their first start. The check is the first step of `Swarm.__init__` once its `config` is
  resolved, before its `logs`
  mkdir and `Database(...)` (whose `SCHEMA` and `ADDED_COLUMNS` would write into the old file), and raises
  `EarlierVersionError` (a ValueError), so it
  covers a session and a single-swarm project (§15) alike: `_load_locked` turns it into `SessionError(…, 409)`
  before its 500 wrap, with `EARLIER_VERSION_TEXT` (en; the hub's errors are English): `Session {sid} was made by
  an earlier version of DreamTeam and cannot be opened by this one ({version}). Open it with the version that made
  it (export it here, then import it into a home of that version: once this one saved its settings, that version
  may not read this home), or delete it.` (`version` = `dreamteam.__version__`; 0.1.x checks the keys of `[swarm]`
  strictly, and this version writes `crew_review` into the home's dreamteam.toml at its first settings save, so
  the old version reopening the home itself usually fails, while export and import work); a project gets `The swarm in {dir} was made by an
  earlier version of DreamTeam and cannot be opened by this one ({version}). Open it with the version that made
  it.`, and the legacy `main` (`MAIN_EARLIER_VERSION_TEXT`), which has no delete, `Session main (the swarm in
  {home}) was made by an earlier version of DreamTeam and cannot be opened by this one ({version}). Open it with the
  version that made it, or remove {home}/.dreamteam/swarm.db (with its -wal and -shm files) by hand.` (`the home`
  in place of {home} when a caller has none; `sessions.earlier_version_text(sid, home, version=None)` renders
  both, and a CLI attached to a hub passes the hub's home and version from `/api/hub`). The web page
  and the TUI show the twin from the summary flag (the home page's card takes `{version}` and `{home}` as §18.4 says
  for that card; home.js `earlierText`, whose en twins are these texts word for word): «Сессия {sid} создана более ранней версией DreamTeam, и эта
  версия ({version}) не может её открыть. Откройте её в той версии, которой она создана (экспортируйте её здесь и
  импортируйте в домашнюю папку той версии: после того как эта версия сохранила настройки, та может не прочитать
  эту папку), или удалите.», for `main`
  «Сессия main (рой в {home}) создана более ранней версией DreamTeam, и эта версия ({version}) не может её открыть.
  Откройте её в той версии, которой она создана, или удалите вручную {home}/.dreamteam/swarm.db (вместе с файлами
  -wal и -shm).» In the TUI, `{version}` is the hub's, else this one's, and the legacy `main`'s `{home}` is the
  summary's `dir`, else the hub's home, else its project; the TUI's own home only for a launcher it runs itself,
  else a neutral word («<домашняя папка>» / "the home"). A TUI attached to a session that becomes one of an earlier
  version (an import replaced it: the close 1011 with the reason `made by an earlier version`, or a start answered
  409 with `earlier_version`, e.g. for a message typed into it while stopped) prints the message in the user's
  language, leaves the session and stops reconnecting (the typed message is not sent); print mode exits 1 with
  the English text. The CLI's texts (the project message, `traces`, `console`, `-r`, `-p`) and the import reason
  (§20.4) are English, like the hub's errors, except where the TUI shows the twin; `-c` and `-p -c` whose most
  recent session is such a one say a shorter message of their own in the user's language (§18.3). Such a session is listed and
  marked (summary `earlier_version`), and only listing (its summary),
  `delete` and export (§20.2: it reads a copy of the database and never opens the session) act on it; every other
  operation is refused with that message and writes nothing: `load` (viewing, the board, the session REST and
  WebSocket, its `/mcp`, so `join_swarm` too), `start`, `stop` (a 409 like the others: the session is never
  running, and an unloaded `stop` would write `autostart=False`, so the mark stays), `resume()` (skipped with one
  warning in the log; the `autostart` mark stays), `update` (PATCH), `set_workspace`, `session_skills` and
  `decide_skill` (each refused right after the session's existence check, `SessionError(text, 409,
  earlier_version=True)`); a profile rename
  of `update_settings` leaves its database alone. `default_session()` (also its fallback to the only session),
  the TUI's `-c` and the CLI's pick of a session for `console` and `traces` skip it. The legacy
  `main` is no exception, except that it still cannot be deleted (`delete` and `sessions rm main` stay a 409): the
  web card, the TUI and the `-r` picker show its own message, which names the file to remove by hand. Docs:
  README.md / README.ru.md (updating), docs/TUI.md and docs/en|ru/transfer.md, and the release note of the
  version, say to finish or export the sessions before updating, that this version lists them but does not open
  them, and that there is no conversion; 0.1.0 has no `dreamteam export` either, so they name the route of updating
  and then exporting with this version (which exports them with a warning, §20.2). The README's short "Updating to 0.2.0" / «Обновление до 0.2.0» (under
  Install) links to the full section of that name in docs/en|ru/getting-started.md (also linked from the docs
  index, features.md's "Sessions" row, terminal.md and transfer.md); they say "sessions in which agents already
  worked (almost every session of 0.1.x)", never every session of 0.1.x, since one in which no LLM member ran opens
  as usual. To open one again the docs name DreamTeam 0.1.1, not "that version" as the hub's message does: 0.1.0 has
  neither `dreamteam export` nor `dreamteam import`, and 0.1.1 (tool set revision 4 like 0.1.0) opens the sessions of both; the export takes
  only the sessions (`--include sessions`) and goes into a separate home of 0.1.1, for example through
  `uvx --from "git+…@v0.1.1" dreamteam import FOLDER --home NEW_HOME` (a new, empty folder, never the home this version uses). The legacy `main` is never said to be
  exported: finish it before updating, or remove its database by hand afterwards.
  Tests: a session with a revision-4 record, one with a history and no record, and one with a history and a record
  that is not `frozen.valid` are each listed with `earlier_version`, refused with the message and writing nothing
  through `load`, `start`, `stop`, `resume()`, PATCH, `set_workspace`, the skills routes, `/mcp`, `-c`, `-r`,
  `traces` and
  a single-swarm project's `run` / `status` (no `logs` folder either); each can be deleted (`main`: the 409 and its
  own message) and exported, and `dreamteam import` refuses it before writing anything. A session with no database
  file, and one whose database holds neither history nor records, open as usual. The fixtures that write a
  `history` row, tests/test_transfer.py (`_fill_db` and the WAL test's 'bob') and tests/test_cli_transfer.py
  (`_exported`), and tests/test_runtime.py `test_restart_continues_an_activation_cut_short_without_tasks`, also
  write the agent's record (`frozen.write(db, name, frozen.current_record("en"))`), so their sessions open.
  tests/test_frozen_tools.py `test_view_only_access_writes_no_tool_record` asserts that the reopen and
  `dreamteam status` are refused (`EarlierVersionError`, exit 1). The tests of an agent on an older revision than
  the code's write a record of `OLDEST_OPEN_REVISION` into an opened swarm while the code builds a simulated later
  revision (the `later_revision` fixture of tests/test_frozen_tools.py, or the same monkeypatch of
  `frozen.TOOLSET_REVISIONS["board"]` and `frozen.current`); `AgentRuntime` does not check the revision (§6.1 "Oldest
  revision opened").
- `delete(sid)` renames the directory to `sessions/.deleted-<sid>-<ns>` first (a session whose files are open
  stays intact: 409), then removes it in a thread; leftovers are purged at the next delete. A workspace folder
  outside the session directory is never deleted (it is the user's folder): `delete` returns it (read under the
  session's lock, so a `set_workspace` that ran just before counts), else None.
- `update_settings(update)`: `apply_update` + validation; every session must still produce a valid config,
  except damaged sessions and sessions whose overrides were already invalid (skipped); a session override that
  pins a renamed profile follows the rename (also in a swap), one whose profile was deleted falls back to the
  default (an `updated` event); then the file is written. A profile rename (`profile_renames(update)`) then reaches
  the members hired on it, before the reconfigure: a loaded session through `Swarm.rename_profiles`, every other one
  (`main` too) by `rename_member_profiles(db_path, renames)` on its `.dreamteam/swarm.db`, in a thread under the
  session's lock (opened by its plain path after an exists() check, so a home on a UNC path or a mapped drive works;
  a 2-s busy timeout, one statement; a missing file or one without an `agents` table is left alone; an error is
  logged and never fails the save, and such a member falls back to the default profile, `make_llm`). A deleted
  profile keeps `agents.model` as it is; a rename by a hand edit of the file has no `renamed_from` and is not
  followed. Then
  every loaded swarm is reconfigured (a failure is logged per session). Returns `{"settings": public view,
  "applied_to": [sids]}`. Edits of the settings file made by hand
  while the server runs are picked up (mtime/size) before reads and updates; an invalid hand edit is ignored
  with a warning.
- `default_session()`: the running session (the most recently active one when several run), else the only
  session, else None; a session made by an earlier version is never it ("Sessions of an earlier version"), nor one
  created through the HTTP API v1 (`instruct.without_api_sessions`, and `api_sids()` for the fallback: an API
  client's job never takes the launcher MCP's calls without `session` or `serve`'s console, §21.4).
- Summary (`list()` sorts running first, then by last activity or creation, newest first; a session that
  cannot be summarized appears as `{"id", "title", "status": "stopped", "error"}`):
  ```json
  {"id","title","legacy","dir","created_at","status":"running|stopped","loaded","autostart","language",
   "model_profile","model","max_cost_usd","max_agents","overrides","config_error","url":"/s/{sid}/",
   "goal":{"title","description","status":"active|done|pending","summary"}|null,
   "tasks":{"total","done","open","by_status"},"agents":{"total","working","llm","external"},
   "spent_usd","paused","pause_reason","wrap_up","last_activity","jobs":{"running"},
   "question":{"asker","message_id"}|null,"requests"?:n,"clarify":bool,
   "workspace":{"path","default","adopted","exists"},"skills":[names],"skills_pending":[names],
   "copied_from":{"source","files","bytes","at"}|null,"earlier_version":bool,"via"?,"answers"?,
   "mode":"board|thread","goal_rule":"democracy|veto"|null,"goal_vote":{...}|null,"posts":n}
  ```
  `earlier_version` (`read_stats`, `db.made_by_earlier_version` on the same read-only connection, in a try of its
  own after the other figures, so a database missing a table they read still reports it; false without a
  database): the session was made by an earlier version and is not opened ("Sessions of an earlier version").
  `read_stats` opens its own connection through `db.reading_file`, so listing leaves no `-wal` or `-shm` behind.
  `question` (`read_stats`, from kv `paused`, default None): the member's question that holds the pause, set only
  for a paused slot with reason `question`, a non-empty asker and an integer message_id (the test of
  `Swarm.pending_question`, §3.1); `requests` (`read_stats(..., requests=True)`, default 0, in a try of its own),
  present only with `summary(sid, requests=True)`, which only the HTTP API v1's summary passes (§21.7): how
  many requests to the user wait (`autoreply.requests_from` on the same connection, with the session's `clarify`:
  the kinds the HTTP API v1 lists, §21.5), and for a session that does not run only those that block its work
  (`read_stats(..., running=False)`, `autoreply.listed_requests`). The board's summaries (`list()`, which the
  sessions page polls, `default_session()`, the routes of §18.1) leave it out: its queries take longer as the
  journal grows (§21.5 "Cost"), and nothing there shows it. `clarify`: the session's `[swarm] clarify`
  setting (its own override, else the global one: `cfg.swarm.clarify`; the auto-reply lease is not counted here).
  `mode`, `goal_rule`, `goal_vote` and `posts`: the thread mode (§22.8; a summary without `mode`, e.g. an older
  hub's, is a board session's).
  `workspace` (= `workspace_of(sid)`): the folder the session works in; `default` = its own `workspace/` (created
  on demand, so it never counts as missing at start), `adopted` = a folder that held files before (the user's),
  `exists` = it is a folder now. `jobs.running`: the session's running background jobs (`read_stats` counts the
  rows, in a `try` of its own: a database older than background jobs gives 0). `skills`: the attached skills' names,
  `skills_pending`: those members proposed that wait for the user's library decision (from memory when loaded,
  else `read_session_skills` of the session's data dir). `copied_from`: the files copied in at create ("Copying
  files into a new session" below), None for a session made without a copy.
  `via` and `answers` are there only for a session created through `/api/v1` (§21.4): session.json's `via`
  (`models.API_VIA`, `"api"`) and its `api.answers` (`"auto"` or `"manual"`), so the sessions page marks it "API"
  (§18.4), `session_line` marks it ` | HTTP API` (§18.2), and `dreamteam -p` sends no
  automatic replies or approvals of its own to an `auto` one (`autoreply.hub_answers(summary)`, §21.5).
  `last_activity` (the time of the newest journal event) leaves out `session.started` and `session.stopped` (§21.6),
  and `dreamteam -c` and `-p -c` never pick a session whose `via` is `"api"`, nor do the other picks the user did
  not name (`console` and `traces` without `--session`, the hub's `default_session()`):
  `instruct.without_api_sessions(sessions)` drops them first. When nothing is picked only because of that, the
  message says how to reach one (`-p -c`: printmode `no_sessions_api`; the TUI: `no_sessions_continue_api`;
  `console` / `traces`: cli `API_NOT_PICKED`). `-r <id>` and `--session` open such a session as any other.

#### Workspace folder
A session works in `<session dir>/workspace` (`default_workspace(sid)`) unless its `session.json` has
`"workspace": {"path": "<absolute path>", "adopted": bool, "in_home"?: "<relative path>"}` (absent = the default
folder; any other shape makes the session damaged, 500). `in_home` (posix, no `..`) is stored for a folder inside
the home, e.g. `projects/x`: the folder is then found relative to the home wherever the home is mounted (the
Docker sandbox's `/swarm`) or moved, and `path` is only informative. `config_for(sid)` sets
`Config.workspace_path` / `workspace_adopted` from it (`data_dir` stays in the session directory); a stored path
that is not absolute on this system (a Windows path read inside a Linux container) maps to a folder that does not
exist. `Swarm.reconfigure` keeps the workspace of a loaded swarm (it changes only through `set_workspace`, which
restarts the swarm) and, for a started swarm in an adopted folder, its `workspace.git` (a change applies at the
next start, which checks the folder).

`async set_workspace(sid, path, *, expect=None)` (`path` absolute, None = the default folder) returns
`{"mode": "moved"|"adopted"|"unchanged", "from", "to", "git": "moved"|"existing"|"initialized"|"disabled"|"none",
"mcp_moved": [names], "old_kept": path|null, "old_missing": bool, "old_changed": null|{"paths", "commit",
"error"}, "restarted": bool, "start_error": str|null}`:
- **Checks first** (nothing changes before they pass; symlinks and junctions are resolved). 400: not a string,
  empty, a relative path (clients resolve relative paths themselves), a drive or file system root, the user's
  home itself or a folder containing it, the DreamTeam home or a folder containing it, anything in
  `<home>/.dreamteam/`, anything in `<home>/sessions/` except this session's own default folder, the session's
  data folder, a repository database (a path with a `.git` component, a bare repository, a folder with `HEAD`,
  `objects/` and `refs/`; whether git is on or not), the shared MCP library (`mcp.library_dir`, the global one and
  the session's) or a folder inside or containing it, the shared skills library (`Config.skills_library_dir`, §19)
  or a folder inside or containing it, the skills' environments folder (`Config.skill_envs_dir`: "... is
  DreamTeam's skill environments folder ..., or inside it or contains it (every session runs its skills' packages
  from there)") or a folder inside or containing it, a folder inside the current workspace or containing it (or
  containing the session directory), an existing file, a folder that cannot be created or written (a temporary
  probe file `.dreamteam-probe-*`, created and removed at once, in the folder or its nearest existing parent:
  `_check_writable`; the web check of a folder never writes it, "Choosing a folder from the web UI" below),
  another DreamTeam home (a folder with `sessions/` and `dreamteam.toml`; never the session's own
  folder, whatever its agents built there, so `--default` always leads back) or a folder inside one, the
  hub tokens' folder (`hubauth.tokens_dir()`) or a folder inside or containing it, on POSIX a folder under
  /proc, /sys or /dev (as `copyfrom.resolve_source` refuses them to a copy), and, when the hub runs in the Docker
  sandbox's container (`copyfrom.hub_in_container`), a folder outside what is mounted there (`_container_refusal`,
  right after `_target_refusal`, also by the create; a path of Windows shape, `PureWindowsPath(text).is_absolute()`,
  is decided earlier, at the absolute-path check before `resolve()`, with this text in place of "not absolute"):
  "The hub runs in the Docker sandbox and sees only its home (<home>) and the [api] folders roots that work in
  place: <path> is not there, and a folder made there would be lost with the container. Choose a folder inside
  <home>, e.g. <home>/projects/<name>. To work in a folder of your computer, mount it inside the home (docker
  compose), or add it to [api] folders with in_place = true (which lets every HTTP API client work in it too) and
  start the sandbox again (docker compose: also mount it as docker-compose.yml's comment shows)." Mounted means
  inside the DreamTeam home (its refused parts are refused above) or inside a root of `apifolders.roots(config)`
  whose `in_place` is true and whose folder in the container is a mount point (`os.path.ismount`: the sandbox
  mounts it writable at `/dreamteam/api-folders/<name>`, §21.10 "Sandbox", but `docker.api_folder_mounts` skips a
  root that is missing or refused on the host or that `-v` cannot name, and a target under such a root's path would
  again be made in the container), compared by `treecopy.is_within`; the session's own default folder is in the
  home. Before this rule a missing POSIX path was created in the container's own file system, which nothing outside
  the container sees and which `docker run --rm` throws away. Other mounts of a compose setup are not guessed from
  `/proc/self/mountinfo` (a tmpfs `/tmp` or a named volume would pass and still be lost or out of the user's
  sight): a folder mounted inside the home is in the home, and one mounted elsewhere is named as an `in_place` root,
  which is a grant to the HTTP API's clients as well (§21.10); the comment above docker-compose.yml's volumes says
  both (§18.4 "Working folder" says what the user sees). 409: a folder another session works
  in, or inside / containing one (the legacy `main` works in `<home>/workspace`), compared by text and by file
  identity (`treecopy.is_within`: on a file system that ignores letter case or Unicode form where `normcase` does
  not, APFS or a casefold mount, `jobs/Acme` is `jobs/acme`). The current folder itself: `"unchanged"`, nothing
  happens. 404 unknown session; 409 for `main` (see below).
- `expect` (`"moved"` | `"adopted"`, anything else 400): the mode the user agreed to; the TUI and the console send
  the one their question announced. 409 when the folder turns out otherwise (e.g. files appeared in a folder that
  was empty when the user was asked); nothing changes.
- **Empty or missing target → move** (`"moved"`): every entry of the current folder (files, `.git` last,
  `mcp/`) is moved into it (a rename per entry; a copy and a delete across volumes); parents are created; the
  session's own default folder is removed afterwards (recreated on demand), another old folder is left empty.
  `git`: `"moved"` when the folder had a repository, else a repository is initialized there (`"initialized"`;
  `"disabled"` when `workspace.git` is off, `"none"` without git). After an *adopted* folder (the user's), an empty
  target starts a fresh workspace instead: the user's files stay where they are (`old_kept`), only the
  session's MCP servers move, and a repository is initialized.
- **Target with files → adopt** (`"adopted"`, stored `adopted: true`): the agents work with its files and their
  commits go to the current branch of its repository. With `workspace.git` on and git installed: refused (409)
  when the repository has uncommitted changes or untracked, not ignored files (`repo_state`, §7: `git status
  --porcelain --untracked-files=normal`, whatever the user's status settings; the agents commit with
  `git add -A`; the `mcp/<name>` folders of the session's own servers, absent there, are left out as at every
  start: a folder the session worked in before may track them, and their move brings them back; so are the files of
  a required filter DreamTeam's git does not run, which no commit of DreamTeam takes, §7), is in a
  detached HEAD, has a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect stopped halfway (the
  agents' next commit would conclude it), or git cannot read it; refused (400) when the folder is inside a
  repository but not its root; a folder that is not in a repository gets one (`init_repo`: git init, `.gitignore`
  if missing, an initial commit of the files there; `"initialized"`). The repository's configuration is never
  modified (no `_configure_repo`, §7), and the agents' commits there follow the user's line-ending settings. The
  one setting DreamTeam writes goes into a repository it creates on a Linux file system without POSIX bits
  (`treecopy.without_posix_bits`: WSL's drvfs, Docker Desktop's 9p, such as a Windows folder in the sandbox):
  `core.filemode=false`, right after git init. There every file Windows wrote reports 0o777, while git init's own
  probe passes on the file it makes; with `core.filemode=true` the first commit would record each of those files as
  100755, and git on Windows (which keeps no such bit) would see every one of them as changed.
  The refusal for changes says which of them line endings alone make (`repo_state(line_endings=True)`: the lines a
  second status with `-c core.autocrlf=true` no longer lists; it runs with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, since a status
  that found those files unchanged would store their stamps in the index, and the next check without the setting
  would take them for unchanged too) and names `git config core.autocrlf true` in the repository itself: a checkout
  of Git for Windows, whose system config sets `core.autocrlf=true` (CRLF in the files, LF in the repository), is
  changed for a git that does not read that config, the Docker sandbox's (§21.10 "Sandbox"). The start check of an
  adopted folder says the same. The old folder stays as it was (`old_kept`). The session's forged and imported MCP
  servers (`mcp_servers` rows with another origin than `config`, folders `<old>/mcp/<name>/`) move to
  `<target>/mcp/<name>/` (409 before anything changes when one of those exists there). Adopting the session's own
  default folder (which still holds its old files) is a plain switch back (stored without "workspace", not adopted, no
  git checks).
- **Leaving an adopted folder** (for an empty folder or the default one): the user's files stay, only the
  session's MCP servers move along. Those of them that the user's repository tracks (`tracked`: the agents'
  `git add -A` committed them there) would leave deletions behind, so with git on DreamTeam commits just their
  removal there (`commit_paths`, author DreamTeam, "Remove mcp/<name>: ..."), and the repository stays clean.
  `old_changed` = `{"paths": ["mcp/<name>", ...], "commit": hash|null, "error": why not|null}` (no commit on a
  detached HEAD, during a merge or rebase, or with git off for the session: the result says to commit the removal
  or restore the folders); null when nothing of the user's folder changed.
- **One change at a time per home**: under the session's lock the target is checked and a loaded session is
  unloaded; then, under a home-wide lock (also taken by `create(workspace=)`), the target is checked again with
  nothing running (an agent may have forged a server meanwhile, the folder may have changed, another session may
  have taken it: its `session.json` names it by then; another mode than the first check found is a 409, as with
  `expect`), the change is carried out and `session.json` is written. Two sessions never take one folder.
- **A loaded session** is unloaded first (stop + close, as `stop`, autostart kept; events `stopped`, then
  `updated`, then `started` after the restart of a session that was running). A restart that fails after a
  successful change leaves the session stopped and is reported in `start_error`.
- **Failures**: `.dreamteam/workspace-move.json` (`{"from","to","mode","started_at"}`) is written before the first
  change. Any failure undoes everything done so far in reverse, removes the journal, starts a session that was
  running again and raises SessionError: 409 when a file is in use or a name appeared in the target meanwhile,
  else 500, naming the folder the session still uses. The undo touches only what the change made: a move is
  recorded once its destination holds the entry; a destination that exists is never replaced or merged into
  (FileExistsError, also across volumes); an entry is put back only where nothing new appeared meanwhile (else it
  is reported); created folders are removed only when empty; `.git` / `.gitignore` only when the change created
  them (a `.git` that appears in the target meanwhile is a 409, never initialized over); in a server folder of the
  HTTP API only from the folder git init ran in, found again inside its root (§21.10 "Resolution"). When the undo
  cannot finish, the error (500) lists the files left in the target and the journal stays: `start` and `set_workspace`
  then refuse (409) naming both folders and the journal to delete once the files are together.
- The members hear of it at the next start: `n_workspace_moved` {path, old}, or `n_workspace_changed` {path, old}
  after an adopt or a fresh start (session.json `workspace_notice` until then); quietly for LLM members (their
  next wake-up), with a wake-up for external members (an MCP client's `wait_for_events` returns it).
- **Start** (and `resume()`, which logs the error and goes on): a session whose (non-default) folder does not
  exist or is not a folder does not start: SessionError 409 naming the path and how to fix it: "The workspace folder
  of session <id> does not exist: <path>. Bring it back (e.g. reconnect the drive), or move the session to another
  folder: Change folder… on its card on the sessions page, /cd <folder> (/cd --default for its own folder) in
  `dreamteam` or `dreamteam console --session <id>`, session_cd in MCP." ("is not a folder" alike; an HTTP API
  client reads it through `_public_text`, whose surfaces are the owner's); `Workspace.init`
  never creates it. Viewing it (`load`) still works. An adopted folder with git on is checked again before every
  start (the user may have worked there while the session was stopped, or git was off at the adopt): 409 for
  uncommitted changes or untracked files (the session's own `mcp/<name>` folders and `.scratch/` are left out), a
  detached HEAD, an operation in progress, an unreadable repository, or a folder inside another repository (a folder in no
  repository gets one at the start, as at an adopt). A session that works in a server folder of the HTTP API v1 in
  place (`api.folder`) is checked again too, from every surface (§21.10 "Starts": `_check_server_folder` in
  `_check_workspace_ready`, then `_check_server_git`, before the adopted-folder check). `_start_locked` runs
  `_check_workspace_ready` in a thread (a folder on a share that does not answer never stalls the hub).
- **Legacy `main`**: refused (409, `LEGACY_WORKSPACE_TEXT`): `dreamteam run` can still open the home as a
  single-swarm project, which reads only `dreamteam.toml` and would work in `<home>/workspace` again.
- `create(..., workspace=path)`: the same checks before anything is created (with the overrides' `workspace.git`),
  then the session is created in its own folder and `set_workspace` runs before the first start. A failure removes
  the new session; its error names only the folder (and what could not be removed there), never the removed
  session. The returned summary then has `"workspace_result"`: the result with mode `"created"` for an
  empty/missing folder or `"adopted"` (`old_kept` null: the unused default folder is removed). With a copy
  (`copy_from` / `copy_from_upload`) the folder must be empty or missing, and the copied files move there ("Copying
  files into a new session" below). `create(..., expect=)` (`"created"` | `"adopted"`, only with `workspace`, else
  400 "\"expect\" needs \"workspace\"."; anything else 400 "\"expect\" must be \"created\" or \"adopted\"." in the
  style of the move's route; "adopted" with a copy 400 "\"expect\": \"adopted\" cannot go with a copy: a copy goes
  into a new or empty folder.", which `_plan(copying=True)` would refuse with a 409 anyway): the mode the
  user agreed to, from the web check (POST `/api/sessions` `expect`, §18.1); "created" is the plan's `"moved"`. It
  is checked against the create's first `_plan` and passed on to `_set_workspace_locked(creating=True, expect=)`
  (`"moved"` for "created"; a copy keeps its own `"moved"`), so the second check under the home-wide lock holds it
  too: 409 "The folder <target> now holds files: the new session would work with them instead of starting afresh
  there. Nothing was created; check the folder and try again." or "The folder <target> is now empty or missing: the
  new session would start afresh there instead of working with its files. Nothing was created; check the folder and
  try again." (the new session removed as for any failure). Without `expect` nothing changes (the CLI, the TUI, the
  MCP: their folder is the one the user typed, and they report what happened).
- `external_workspaces(home)` → `[(sid, stored path)]` of the sessions whose folder is outside the home (no
  `in_home`; read from the `session.json` files, nothing opened): `dreamteam sandbox` warns about them (only the
  home is mounted).

#### Choosing a folder from the web UI
The launcher's two folder routes (§18.1 `POST /api/folders/check`, `POST /api/folders/list`) let the web UI choose a
folder of the hub's computer and say beforehand what will happen there (its fields and dialogs: §18.4 "Working
folder", "Folder browser", "Change folder"). They are the server's: the paths are the hub's, a browser's own
directory picker (`webkitdirectory`, `showDirectoryPicker`) gives files or a handle but never a path of the hub's
computer, and a remote browser cannot look at that disk. The check is `_plan` itself (and `resolve_source` for a
copy), so its rules have one source; no JS copy of them exists. The plain helpers (the text rules of a path, drive
letters, the scan, the sort, the marks' budget) are in `folderlist.py` (stdlib, `treecopy` and `workspace.is_link`;
imported by sessions.py alone); the manager's methods below hold the rules.
- **POSTs, never GETs**: both routes take a JSON body. A page of another site can make a browser send a GET to a
  loopback hub without a token with no Origin header at all (`<img src="http://127.0.0.1:8765/...">`; the guard
  checks Origin only when one is sent, §14), and a listing of `\\host\share` would make the hub's Windows open an SMB
  connection to that host with the hub user's credentials, or wake a drive, or tell by its timing whether a path
  exists. A JSON POST needs a CORS preflight that the hub never answers, so only the hub's own pages and local
  programs (which can do all of this anyway) send one.
- **Network paths by their text** (`folderlist.network_path(text)`: on Windows a path whose
  `PureWindowsPath(text).drive` starts with `\\` or `//`: `\\server\share\x`, `//server/share`, `\\?\...`, `\\.\...`;
  never on POSIX): the listing refuses one before any file system call (403 "<path> is a network or device path: the
  folder browser does not open those. Type the folder's path in the field instead."), leaves out a root of that shape (a
  `recent` parent or an api root on a share) and never follows a link there: on Windows (`folderlist.network_target`)
  each link on the way of the listed path, of a root before it is resolved and of a link entry is read with
  `os.readlink` (the link itself, never its target; a junction's `\\?\` spelling of a local path is local), at most
  `LINK_HOPS_MAX` (32) links per path, and a way that reaches a network or device path (or a longer chain) is shut
  before any `stat`, `resolve` or `scandir` follows it (the listed path 403 "<path> leads to <target>, outside the
  places this hub shows.", an entry below). The check runs them: a project on a share is a valid folder, and the check's
  POST comes from the hub's own page. The existing `GET /api/skills?workspace=` (launcher `_workspace_query`, a GET that
  reads `<folder>/.claude/skills`) had the same hole and refuses such a path by its text too: 400 "'workspace' must be a
  folder of this computer, not a network path." (so the new-session dialog offers no `claude-project` rows for a project
  on a share). A drive letter mapped to a share (`Z:`) is the user's own mapping and is opened like any drive.
- **`async check_folder(path=None, *, use="workspace", sid=None, default=False)`** → a dict. It never raises for a
  refusal of the folder (that is its answer); it raises SessionError for the call itself.
  - `use` `"workspace"`: `sid` None checks a new session's `workspace` (`default` then 400 "'default' needs
    'session'."); with `sid` it checks a move of that session (`_check`, `_refuse_earlier`, the legacy `main` 409
    `LEGACY_WORKSPACE_TEXT`, as `set_workspace`), `default` true for its own folder (`path` then absent: 400 "Give
    'path' or 'default', not both."; neither: 400 "Give 'path' or 'default'."). The path is trimmed, one pair of
    quotes is dropped (`copyfrom.unquote`) and a leading `~` is the hub user's home (`os.path.expanduser`, as
    `resolve_source` does: the field names a folder of the hub's computer, so its `~` is the hub's); a path still not
    absolute is the refusal "<path> is not a full path. Give the full path of a folder on the hub's computer, e.g.
    C:\work\project." (`/home/me/project` on a POSIX hub), in place of `_plan`'s text about the clients' current
    folders, which means nothing on a web page. With `sid`, then `_check_journal(sid, meta)` (an unfinished earlier
    move: its 409 text is the answer, since the move would refuse it) and `config_for(sid)` (a ValueError of invalid
    settings is 400, as in `_set_workspace_locked`). Then `_plan(sid, target, git_on=, mcp=, network_off=,
    dry=True)` with the session's config and `mcp=self._forged_servers(sid)`, or for a new session the home's
    settings (`workspace.git`, `swarm.network`: the dialog has no git field, and the network only makes git offline)
    and `mcp=None`, as `create` passes; then `_container_refusal` and `_check_reserved(plan.target)`. Nothing is
    reserved and no lock is taken: the answer is a forecast; the create or the move checks again, and the `expect`
    the UI sends from this answer catches a folder that changed meanwhile (409, nothing changes).
  - Its answer: `{"use": "workspace", "path": <the value as sent>, "target": <the folder the create or the move
    gets: the path unquoted, `~` expanded, not resolved; the session's own folder for `default`>, "state":
    plan.state, "mode": "created" | "moved" | "adopted" | "unchanged" ("created" is a new session's "moved"),
    "expect": the value to send (`"created"` / `"adopted"` for a new session, `"moved"` / `"adopted"` for a move,
    null for "unchanged"), "fresh": the move leaves an adopted folder for an empty one (the user's files stay, the
    session starts afresh; `cd_preview`'s `text_fresh`), "back": the target is the session's own folder, which still
    holds its earlier files (`text_back`), "lost": the current folder does not exist (nothing moves, `text_lost`),
    "git": plan.git, "branch": plan.branch, "mcp": plan.mcp (the session's servers that move along), "running": the
    session runs (its agents stop for the move), "api_folder": {"root", "path"} of a session that works in place in
    a server folder of the HTTP API v1 (`apifolders.in_place_folder((meta.get("api") or {}).get("folder"))`: the
    move drops it, §21.10 "Starts"), else null}`. `_Plan` gains `state` (`"missing"` | `"empty"` | `"files"`: what
    `_plan` found at the target; None for "unchanged", where `_plan` returns before it looks) and `branch`
    (`repo_state`'s branch of a folder with files in a repository, with git on; else None); `set_workspace`'s result
    is unchanged.
  - A refusal of the folder (a SessionError of `_plan`, `_check_journal`, `_container_refusal` or
    `_check_reserved`) is the answer `{"use", "path", "error": <its text>, "status": <its status>}` with HTTP 200:
    the check worked, the folder cannot be used. Never its `code` or `holder`: those stay out of the internal
    answers (SessionError above), and the UI needs neither (the text names the other session; the browser's `busy`
    mark is its own). The UI shows `error` verbatim (the texts already say what to do, e.g. "Commit or stash them
    first").
  - `use` `"source"` (a copy into the session's own folder): `copyfrom.resolve_source(path, home=, config=,
    sandbox=hub_in_container(config))` (it unquotes and expands `~` itself); `sid` or `default` there is 400 "'session'
    and 'default' are for use \"workspace\".", no `path` (or an empty one) 400 "Give 'path'.". Answer `{"use": "source",
    "path", "target": str(source.path), "state": "folder" | "zip"}`; a CopyError is the refusal above (in the sandbox a
    missing or Windows-shaped path gets its text: "The hub runs in the Docker sandbox and sees only its home (<home>): X
    is not there. Upload the folder as a .zip in the New session dialog of the sessions page instead."). No pre-scan:
    counting a large folder takes as long as the create's own pre-scan, which refuses it (413) before a byte is copied.
  - `use` anything else: 400 "'use' must be \"workspace\" or \"source\".".
  - **No side effects** (`dry=True`): `_check_writable` (the probe file) becomes `_can_write(folder, shown)`,
    `os.access(folder, os.W_OK | os.X_OK)` with the same text ("Cannot write to <shown>: permission denied. Choose
    a folder you can write to."). On Windows `os.access` ignores the read-only attribute of a folder (CPython looks
    at it for files only) and sees no ACL, so `_can_write` is true for every folder there: the create's or the
    move's real probe refuses one that cannot be written, as that request's error. git reads with
    `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (`repo_state(..., optional_locks=False)`, every git call of it): a plain `git status`
    would refresh the stat data of the user's `.git/index`, a write; `hubgit.run_git` already disarms fsmonitor,
    hooks and filters, so a check runs no code of the user's repository. Nothing else in `_plan` writes;
    `resolve_source` only reads. The create and the move keep the real probe: a folder that cannot be written must
    be refused before anything moves.
  - **Off the loop**: the work runs in a daemon thread (`procs.daemon_call`: a folder on a share that does not answer
    never holds the hub's exit), awaited at most `FOLDER_TIMEOUT` (20 s); past it the answer is the refusal "<path>
    did not answer within 20 s (a network folder, or a drive that sleeps?). Try again, or choose another folder."
    with status 504, and the thread is left to finish. **Slots**: at most `FOLDER_OPS_MAX` (4) folder threads per
    hub, checks and listings together; a slot is taken without waiting before the thread starts and given back when
    the thread itself ends, not at its 504, so folders that never answer hold at most 4 threads. While a thread
    that passed its timeout still runs, its path is kept (`_folders_hung`, by `_fold_key` of the path as given): a
    request for that path or one inside it gets the 504 refusal at once, with no thread. No free slot: 429 "Too many
    folder checks at once; try again in a moment.", or, when every slot is held by a thread past its timeout, 429
    "Folders that did not answer still hold the hub's folder checks (<paths>): try again when they answer, or
    restart the hub.". The UI counts a 429 as a check that could not run (`fo_check_failed`, which blocks nothing,
    §18.4) and asks one check at a time per field.
- **`async list_folders(path=None, *, use="workspace", sid=None)`** → one folder's subfolders for the browser.
  Folder names only: never a file's name, never a content.
  - **Roots** (`folder_roots(use, sid)`, computed per call from text alone, so a disconnected share among them never
    slows a listing; each `{"path", "kind", "name", "selectable"}`, `selectable` by kind; whether a root exists and its
    own marks are learnt when it is opened; `name`: the last part of the path for `home` and `recent`, the home folder's
    name for `dreamteam`, the letter for a `drive` ("C:", path "C:\"), "/" for `system`, the root's name for `api`):
    - on the host: `home` (`Path.home()`; not selectable: the home itself is refused, the folders in it are not); the
      navigation roots, never selectable (a drive or file system root): on Windows one `drive` per letter of
      `GetLogicalDrives()` (ctypes: a bitmask, so no drive is touched and an empty card reader or a sleeping network
      drive costs nothing until it is opened; `name` "C:"), elsewhere `system` "/"; `recent`: the parents of the
      folders the sessions work in outside their own default folder (adopted or moved, the session `sid` too;
      `_workspace_entry`, read from the `session.json` files), deduplicated by `_fold_key`, without a parent that is
      the home, a navigation root or a network path, newest session first (ids sort by creation), at most
      `FOLDER_RECENT_MAX` (8), selectable (the listing says when one is refused); `api`: the roots of
      `apifolders.roots(config)` (`name` the root's; for `use` "workspace" only those with `in_place`; network paths
      left out), selectable.
    - in the container (`hub_in_container`) only what is mounted: for "workspace" `dreamteam` (the DreamTeam home,
      not selectable: refused, its `.dreamteam` and `sessions` closed) and the `in_place` api roots that are mounted
      (`os.path.ismount`, as `_container_refusal` counts them: the one file system call of the roots, a local one);
      for "source" every mounted api root (a `copy` root is mounted read-only, which a copy needs) and no `dreamteam`
      root (the home is never a copy source, `resolve_source`). No drive, `/`, `home` or `recent` root there.
    - `use` "source" on the host: the roots of "workspace", with every api root.
    - The roots are built in a daemon thread (`procs.daemon_call`, never the default executor git uses).
  - **The folder**, in this order: `path` absent answers the roots alone (`"path": null`, `"entries": []`). Else, by
    text: not a string, empty or not absolute (after `copyfrom.unquote`; no `~` here) 400 "'path' must be an absolute
    folder path."; a network path 403 (above); `os.path.abspath` (`..` folded by text) must lie inside a root by text
    (`folderlist.inside_text`: `os.path.normcase` and `commonpath`, no file system call), else 403 "<path> is outside
    the places this hub lets you browse.". Then, in the thread: the path and that root are resolved, and the resolved
    path must lie inside the resolved root or inside another root resolved alike (`treecopy.is_within`; the roots that
    hold it by text first, the others only when none of those does), else 403 "<path> leads to <real>, outside the
    places this hub shows."; a mapped drive (`Z:\` resolves to `\\server\share\`, and so does every path on it) still
    compares, since its root is resolved the same way. A closed folder is 403 with its refusal; a path that is missing
    or a file lists its nearest existing ancestor inside the same root, with `"fallback": true` (a typed new folder
    opens at its parent). The resolved folder is the one scanned, its entries' paths joined to the listed text. A folder
    that cannot be read (`os.scandir` raises: no permission, an empty card reader "device not ready", an I/O error), the
    root itself missing included, is 200 with `"entries": []` and `"error"` "Cannot read the folder <path>: <strerror>."
    (the status line shows it; the breadcrumb and Up still work).
  - **Entries**: `os.scandir` of the folder, at most `FOLDER_SCAN_MAX` (10 000) entries read, files included (a
    folder of a million files never stalls a listing); kept: folders and links to folders (`is_dir()` follows the
    link; a link to a file and a broken one are left out); sorted with names starting with `.` and, on Windows,
    folders with the hidden or system attribute (`st_file_attributes`: `$Recycle.Bin`, `System Volume Information`)
    after the others, each group by `name.casefold()`, then the name; at most `FOLDER_LIST_MAX` (500) after the
    sort; `truncated` true when either cap cut. Each entry `{"name", "path", "link", "open", "refused", "busy",
    "current", "repo", "files", "noaccess"}`:
    - `link`: `workspace.is_link` (a symlink or a junction; a cloud placeholder is an ordinary folder); followed only
      when its resolved target lies inside a root of this listing, else `open` false and `refused` "<name> leads to
      <target>, outside the places this hub shows." (in the sandbox a link in the home to /etc stays shut); a link whose
      way reaches a network path (above) is that shut entry with no file system call through it (kept when the link
      itself is a directory link or a junction, its own attributes; never resolved, peeked or tested); `path` is the
      entry's own path, never its target, and so is the answer's `path` once it is opened (the breadcrumb never jumps to
      where a link leads);
    - `refused`: the static reason the folder cannot be chosen, by `use`: for "workspace" `_target_refusal(entry, sid)`
      and `_container_refusal`; for "source" `copyfrom.source_refusal(entry, home=, config=)` (the location rules of
      `resolve_source` without its existence and kind checks, extracted from it: a drive or file system root, the user's
      home or a folder containing it, inside or containing the DreamTeam home or one of DreamTeam's own folders, another
      DreamTeam home, /proc, /sys, /dev; no `_container_refusal`: a read-only `copy` root is a valid source). One
      context per listing: the homes, libraries, environments and tokens folders (and in the container the mounted
      places of `_container_refusal`) resolved once, `_other_home` asked of the entry alone (the listed folder's
      ancestors were checked with it). Else null; the full check of the chosen folder still decides (git state,
      writability, a file in place);
    - `open`: false for a closed folder, one whose every descendant is refused too by the same `use`'s rules (for
      "workspace" `_target_refusal` refuses `<entry>/x`: a `.git`, `<home>/.dreamteam`, `<home>/sessions`, the
      tokens folder, the libraries, the skill environments, another DreamTeam home, /proc, /sys, /dev; for "source"
      the DreamTeam home and its own folders, another DreamTeam home, /proc, /sys, /dev), and for a link out of the
      roots; a refused folder that is not closed (a drive root, the user's home, a folder that contains the DreamTeam
      home) opens, to reach the folders inside it;
    - `busy`: `{"sid", "title"}` of another session whose folder it is, lies inside or contains
      (`_other_workspaces(sid)` once per listing, `is_within` both ways; the title from its `session.json`),
      `{"sid": null, "title": null}` for a create in progress there (`_creating_in`), else null; for "workspace" a
      busy folder cannot be chosen, for "source" it is shown only (copying another session's folder is allowed);
      `current`: the session `sid` works in it;
    - `repo`: `os.path.lexists(<entry>/.git)`; `files`: it holds any entry (one `scandir` peek), null when not
      looked at; `noaccess`: the peek raised PermissionError.
    - **Budget**: the marks cost a few file system calls per entry (a stat through a link, `lexists`, the peek,
      `_other_home`'s stats), which on a slow share can outlast `FOLDER_TIMEOUT` for 500 entries; so they stop after
      `FOLDER_MARKS_BUDGET` (5 s) of the listing, and the remaining entries get `refused`, `repo` and `files` null,
      `open` true and the answer `"partial": true` (the full check of a chosen folder still decides). On macOS the
      entries `Desktop`, `Documents`, `Downloads`, `Pictures`, `Movies`, `Music` and `Library` of the user's home get no
      look inside at all (no peek, no `.git` test, no refusal checks, which stat names inside them): the marks past the
      budget (`refused`, `repo`, `files` null, `open` true; `busy` and `current` by text): each look would pop a privacy
      (TCC) prompt for the hub's terminal app at every listing of the home; opening one is the user's own act, and macOS
      may then ask once.
  - Answer: `{"path" (the folder listed, in its text form: the given path normalized, or the `fallback` ancestor),
    "parent" (null at a root), "root" (the path of the innermost root it lies in, by text), "roots", "entries",
    "truncated", "partial", "fallback", "error" (null, or the text of a folder that cannot be read), "refused",
    "selectable" (not refused, not the home or a navigation root, for "workspace" not busy), "busy", "current", "sep"
    (`os.sep`: the browser joins a new folder's name with it)}`, the listed folder's own marks computed as an entry's.
    The same daemon thread, `FOLDER_TIMEOUT` (504 "<path> did not answer within 20 s ...") and slots as the check.
- **Who reaches them**: the launcher's hub-token holders only, who can already point a session at any folder these
  rules allow and whose agents run commands with the hub user's rights; the listing shows them folder names under
  the same refusals. Never on a session app (`/s/{sid}/api/folders/list` is that app's 404), never under `/api/v1`
  (the API token opens no internal route, §21.1 "What the API token reaches"), no MCP tool. A loopback hub without a
  hub token serves them to every local program, as it serves every internal route (§21.1 "The rest of the hub"),
  and docs/en|ru/security.md says so; pages of other sites never reach them (POSTs, above).
- **Tests**: tests/test_session_workspace.py — `check_folder` (each `state` / `mode` / `expect`, `state` None for
  "unchanged", `fresh`, `back`, `lost`, `branch`, `mcp`, `running`, `api_folder` with and without `meta["api"]`; a
  refusal as the answer with its status and without `code` or `holder`; an unfinished move's journal refused as an
  answer; invalid session settings 400; a new session checked with `mcp=None`; `~` expanded and a relative path
  given the web text; `target` unresolved; no `.dreamteam-probe-*` ever created and `.git/index` unchanged (bytes
  and mtime) after a check of a repository with a touched file; a read-only folder refused by `_can_write`, skipped
  on Windows and as root; the 504 with a `_plan` that blocks, its slot held until the thread ends, a second
  request for that path 504 at once, the 429 texts; `use` "source" and the sandbox text), `create(expect=)` (400
  without `workspace`, 400 "adopted" with a copy, 409 both ways, the session removed; the second check under the
  lock), `_container_refusal` (`hub_in_container` patched: outside the home and the `in_place` roots refused, a
  Windows path given its text at the absolute-path check, inside the home, a mounted `in_place` root, the default
  folder and v1's `within` pass, a `copy` root and an `in_place` root that is not a mount point refused) and
  `list_folders` (roots per place and `use`, no file system call while the roots are built, `recent` without
  duplicates of the home and the drives, Windows drives with `GetLogicalDrives` patched, a mapped drive with
  `resolve` patched to a UNC path, a network path refused with no file system call (`os.scandir`, `os.stat` and
  `Path.resolve` patched to fail), a path outside the roots refused by text alone, the sort, both caps and
  `truncated`, files never listed, a link out of the roots shut and one inside followed with the link's own path in
  the answer, `fallback`, an unreadable folder's `error`, each mark per `use` (a `copy` root's folder selectable as a
  source in the container, a busy folder selectable as a source, a folder in the DreamTeam home refused as a
  source), closed folders, the marks' budget with a slow `scandir` giving `partial`, the macOS entries not peeked);
  tests/test_launcher.py — the two routes over HTTP (bodies, statuses, 429 with held slots, the guard's token, a GET
  of either route 405, 404 for `/s/{sid}/api/folders/list` and v1's `not_found` for `/api/v1/folders/list`),
  `POST /api/sessions` with `expect`, `GET /api/skills?workspace=\\host\share` 400 with nothing read.

#### Copying files into a new session
`copyfrom.py` (it imports treecopy, skills, workspace and hubauth, never sessions.py) copies a folder or a zip into
the folder a new session works in, before its first start: `create(..., copy_from=<absolute folder or .zip path on
this computer>)` or `create(..., copy_from_upload=<token of POST /api/uploads>)`, not both (400 "Give copy_from or
copy_from_upload, not both."); the HTTP API v1 passes `sources` instead ("Sessions of the HTTP API v1" above), the
same order with `copy_sources` in place of `copy_into` and no claim of its own. The surfaces: REST `copy_from` /
`copy_from_upload` (§18.1), the launcher MCP's
`session_create(copy_from=)` (§18.2), the CLI's `--copy-from` (§18.3), the TUI's `/copy-from` (docs/TUI.md) and the
home page's «Рабочая папка» → «Копия папки или zip» (§18.4). The source is only read and nothing is copied back.
The members are never told where the files came from: no source path goes into `pending_goal` or any prompt.
- **Order** (the cheap checks first, the copy last):
  1. an upload is claimed first (`uploads.claim`, its claimed name computed first by `claim_path`; an unknown or
     used token is the 404 here): from now on a create that names an upload uses it up, whatever refuses it later
     (the sessions page uploads again for each try, so failed tries never pile up);
  2. "not both", then the overrides are validated (as without a copy);
  3. `copy_from` is refused early, in a thread, by `resolve_source(text, home=, config=, sandbox=)`;
  4. with `workspace`: `_plan(..., copying=True)`, where a folder with files is a 409 before any repository check
     ("<target> already has files (it holds .git, .DS_Store; hidden files count): a copy goes into a new or empty
     folder. Choose an empty folder, or leave out the copy to work with the files in <target> itself.": at most 5
     entries named, `.git` and dot names first, since the user may see no files there), then
     `check_target(source, plan.target)` for `copy_from`; then the target is reserved for this create
     (`_creating_in`, the resolved target, checked and added with no await between; removed in `finally`): a
     second create meanwhile (a double click, a client's retry) into the same folder, a folder inside it or one
     containing it (compared as NFC text ignoring case, since a folder not created yet has no file identity) is 409
     "Another session is being created in <target> right now[ (<other> is inside it or contains it)]; when it is
     done, that folder is taken." before it copies anything; `set_workspace` of another session into such a folder
     gets the same 409 after its first `_plan`;
  5. the skills are prepared (unchanged, "Skills" below);
  6. the leftovers of earlier copies are removed (`clean_copy_leftovers`: `uploads.clean()` and `_clean_copies`),
     and `copy_into(source, staging, limits, check)` builds the copy in `sessions/.copying-<pid>-<run>-<hex8>/`
     (`copyfrom.staging_name()`; never a session: `ids()` needs `SESSION_ID` and a session.json);
  7. `_create` makes `sessions/<sid>/`, renames the staging to `sessions/<sid>/workspace` (one volume; a failure
     removes `sessions/<sid>/`, 500 "Could not move the copied files into ..."), writes session.json with
     `copied_from` and commits the skills as before; with `workspace`, `_set_workspace(creating=True,
     expect="moved")` moves the copy into the target and `init_repo` commits it (files that appeared there
     meanwhile: 409, and everything is removed);
  8. `finally` (around all of the above): the staged skills are discarded, a claimed upload is released
     (`uploads.release`, synchronous: two
     unlinks, so no await follows a success and a cancellation cannot turn a created session into an error), and
     a staging that was not renamed in is removed.
- **Refusals of the source** (`resolve_source`, CopyError 400, before anything is done; one pair of matching
  quotes around the text is dropped first, `console.unquote`, as Explorer's "Copy as path" adds them): not a
  string or blank ("'copy_from' must be an absolute path of a folder or a .zip file."); not absolute after `~` is
  expanded; missing ("Nothing to copy at ..."); a file whose suffix is not `.zip` (any case); neither a file nor a
  folder; for a folder also a drive or file system root (on POSIX also a mount point directly in `/mnt` or
  `/Volumes`, or in `/media` or `/run/media` one or two levels down: a whole disk, `_disk_mount`; a folder mounted
  elsewhere, such as a devcontainer's `/workspaces/x`, is fine, and so on Linux is a bind mount of one folder there,
  such as docker's `-v ./app:/mnt/app`: `_mount_root` reads its root field in `/proc/self/mountinfo`, and only "/",
  a whole file system, is a disk; where mountinfo cannot be read the place alone decides), the user's home itself,
  or a folder containing
  it; for both kinds
  a path inside or containing the DreamTeam home, or DreamTeam's own folders outside it (`config.library_dir`,
  `skills_library_dir`, `skill_envs_dir`, `hubauth.tokens_dir()`: a `copy_from=~/.dreamteam` would put hub tokens
  and library code where the members read them); another DreamTeam home, or a path inside one (a folder with
  `sessions/` and `dreamteam.toml`, as `cli.is_home`: its dreamteam.toml can hold API keys; "... is a DreamTeam
  home (<folder>) or inside one ..."); on POSIX a path inside `/proc`, `/sys` or `/dev`
  (`/proc/self/environ` holds the hub's API keys, which the members' shell leaves out). The comparisons are
  `treecopy.is_within` (text and file identity). `check_target`: a target inside a folder source ("... the copy
  would copy itself"), or a source inside the target, is 400; through `create` a source inside a target with files
  gets the 409 of step 4 first.
- **A folder** (`copy_into`; `staging` must not exist yet, else CopyError 500 and that folder is left alone, so the
  cleanup never removes what the call did not make): a stat-only pre-scan (`scan_tree(hash=False)`) with the
  limits refuses a huge folder before a byte is written; then `copy_tree(src, staging,
  exclude_names=COPY_EXCLUDE_NAMES, exclude_paths=EXPORT_EXCLUDE_PATHS, skip_files=COPY_SKIP_FILES,
  fold_names=True, modes="writable", max_files=, max_bytes=, check=)` (§20.5). Left out: `.git`, `node_modules`,
  `.venv`, `venv` and `__pycache__` at any depth in any letter case, a DreamTeam workspace's `.scratch/_skills` and
  `.unavailable-workspace`, links (never followed) and special files; `.DS_Store` and `Thumbs.db` files
  (`COPY_SKIP_FILES`, as in a zip) are skipped without a word and counted in `skipped_count`. A folder swapped for a
  link (or another folder) while the walk runs is never walked (§20.5): an error, so the copy is refused.
  `modes="writable"`: the owner can always read and write (a read-only file is editable in the copy; the root hub
  of the sandbox reads a 000 file), the group and others never write, a file reported as 0o777, or any file of a
  source on a Linux file system without POSIX bits (WSL's `/mnt/c`, Docker Desktop's 9p, FAT, exFAT, NTFS, SMB:
  `treecopy.fs_type`, §20.5), becomes 0o644, or 0o755 when it starts with `#!`, `\x7fELF` or a Mach-O magic
  (otherwise every file would be committed as 100755), and the setuid, setgid and sticky bits are dropped (the sandbox hub runs as
  root: a kept setuid file would be a setuid-root program for the `dreamteam-agent` commands of an offline
  session, §7.2).
  `TreeLimit` is 413 "<src> holds more than N files to copy ([workspace] copy_max_files; .git, node_modules, .venv,
  venv and __pycache__ do not count). Nothing was copied." (or "N MB ... copy_max_mb"); unreadable files (the
  result's `errors`, without the `vanished` ones) are 400 "Cannot read N file(s) in <src>: <rel> (<reason>); ...
  Nothing was copied: check the permissions, or close the program that holds them." (at most 5 named); a file
  deleted while the copy runs (an editor's temporary file, build output: `vanished`, FileNotFoundError) is not
  refused but listed in the result's `vanished`; a file replaced meanwhile (a new inode) is still refused. A folder
  gone meanwhile (`treecopy.GONE_DIR` in `errors`, never `vanished`), or a source root that is gone, no folder or
  another folder after the copy than the lstat taken before the count (another `(st_dev, st_ino)`: moved, renamed
  or swapped), is 400 "<src> was moved, renamed or deleted while it was copied (<rel>, ...). Nothing was copied:
  copy again once it stays in place." (otherwise a session would hold a part of the source). A
  `FileExistsError` while writing in the new staging means the target's file system folded two names of the
  source (a case-sensitive source written onto a case-insensitive home) and is 400 `skills.folded_names_text`:
  "<src> holds names that the folder they are written to cannot tell apart (they differ only in letter case or
  Unicode form): '<rel>'." (the path relative to the source, not the staging path); another write error is 500.
- **A zip** (a `.zip` path or a claimed upload): a file over `copy_max_mb` is 413 "The zip is larger than N MB
  ([workspace] copy_max_mb)."; then `skills.unpack_zip(path, staging, copyfrom.zip_rules(limits), check=)` (a
  claimed upload: the file `_open_upload` opened in place of the path),
  streamed from the file (§19): the directory pre-check; at most `max(5000, 2 × copy_max_files)` entries (folders
  and left-out ones count); the declared sizes of the planned files after planning (left-out members do not
  count) and the streamed bytes against `copy_max_mb`; at most `copy_max_files` files; no compression ratio bound
  (sparse, zero-filled and database files compress far better, and the streamed cap bounds a bomb);
  `COPY_EXCLUDE_NAMES` casefolded against every path part; `__MACOSX`, `.DS_Store` and `Thumbs.db` skipped
  (`.dreamteam.json` is copied); links left out and listed; folder entries created (empty folders kept).
  **Unwrap**: when every planned entry lies under one top folder (one-part folder entries such as `mywork/`, which
  `zip -r`, Finder and `shutil.make_archive` write, aside) and no excluded or link member sits beside it (`node_modules/x.js` next to
  `app/` shows that the zip's root is the project's root: `app/` stays, as in a folder copy; `mywork/.git/HEAD`
  does not block), that folder's contents are unpacked and the result's `top` names it; left-out paths are
  reported as written in the zip. `EXPORT_EXCLUDE_PATHS` (`.scratch/_skills`, `.unavailable-workspace`) are left
  out as in a folder copy, matched after the unwrap. Names stored without the UTF-8 flag (which zipfile reads as
  cp437) are read again from their bytes (`redecode_names`), all in one encoding decided for the archive (a short
  cp866 name such as `раб` or `тип` is valid UTF-8): the first of UTF-8 and the OEM code page of Windows
  (`GetOEMCP`, cp866 on a Russian one) that decodes every such name, the OEM code page first when every such
  member was made on MS-DOS / Windows (`create_system` 0, 6, 10 or 14: its old "Compressed folder", 7-Zip and
  WinRAR without the flag), UTF-8 first otherwise (macOS Finder and Linux tools write UTF-8 without the flag); a
  hub on another OS (the Docker sandbox included) knows no OEM code page and keeps zipfile's cp437 when the names
  are not UTF-8. A name read again tells a folder by its own last character (`/` or `\`), not by zipfile's cp437
  reading, which on Windows ends in `/` for a double-byte character whose second byte is 0x5C (cp932 `ソ`). The
  Windows name rules (`_portable`, "file names in the zip
  cannot ...") apply on Windows only; names that differ only in letter case or Unicode form collide on Windows and
  macOS (their default file systems ignore case) and are two files on Linux, as in a folder copy. Where the file
  system written to folds them anyway (a Linux hub whose home is a case-insensitive Docker Desktop bind mount),
  `unpack_zip` creates the folders one by one and a name that meets one written before is 400
  `folded_names_text("The zip", name)`: two folders are never merged. A `SkillError` becomes a CopyError with its
  status.
- **Result** (`copy_result` of the create's summary, transient: every caller pops it, REST answers it as `copy`):
  `{"source", "kind": "folder" | "zip" | "upload", "files", "bytes", "links" (at most 20), "links_count",
  "excluded" (at most 20), "excluded_count", "special_count" (folder), "skipped_count" (OS litter), "vanished" (at
  most 20; folder: files deleted while the copy ran), "vanished_count", "top"}`.
  `copy_text(result)` words it for the CLI and the MCP: "Copied N files (size) from <source>[ (the contents of
  <top>/ in the zip)] into the session's folder." and, when something was left out, "Left out: N link(s) (a, b, c,
  ...); N folder(s) by name (...); N special file(s); N file(s) deleted while they were copied (...)."; the TUI,
  `-p` and the web toasts show the links, folders and special files only. `size_text(n)` is "N bytes", "N.N KB" or
  "N.N MB". Names from the source (links, excluded, vanished, top) and the names in the zip refusals pass
  `skills.printable_name` (what is
  not printable becomes `?`): a member name with an escape sequence (OSC 52 sets the clipboard) cannot drive the
  terminal of `dreamteam serve --copy-from` or of an MCP client.
- **session.json** `"copied_from": {"source": str(path) | "upload: <file name>", "files", "bytes", "at"}`, written
  with the rest of the new meta. The summary's `copied_from` is cleaned (`_copied_from`), because session.json may
  come from an import or a hand edit: exactly those four keys, the source one line of printable characters cut to
  300 (`SOURCE_SHOWN_MAX`, `copyfrom.printable_line`), the numbers finite and at least 0; None for anything else.
- **The first commit**: the default workspace gets its repository at the first start (`Workspace.init` →
  `init_repo`, "Initialize workspace"), a `workspace` at the create (§7); either way the copied files are in the
  first commit. One copy of the source's `.gitignore` comes along (`.git` never does), so `init_repo` writes no
  `DEFAULT_GITIGNORE`, and the files that `.gitignore` ignores are in the folder but not committed.
- **Cancel and cleanup**: the claim, the copy and the rename run through `_in_thread(fn, ..., on_cancel=)`, which
  waits for the thread before a CancelledError goes on; the first cancel sets an event that `check` turns into
  `CopyCancelled` in the worker, and `copy_into` removes the staging on any exception. A cancelled or failed create
  leaves no session, no staging and no claimed upload. A process killed outright leaves `.copying-<pid>-<run>-*`
  (and a claim), which `clean_copy_leftovers` removes at the next create with a copy and the launcher's sweep at
  its start and every `UPLOAD_TTL` (in a daemon thread, `procs.daemon_call`: the hub's exit does not wait for a long
  removal, which the next sweep finishes) (`copyfrom.left_over(pid, run, name)`: of this pid, an earlier run, or this
  run's when no longer in use; else not another live pid). `staging_name()` and `Uploads.claim_path()` add the name
  to an in-process set until `done_with(path)` (create's finally, `release`), so a staging or claim whose removal
  failed (a file still open on Windows) is removed by the next clean, while the hub runs. `RUN`
  (`secrets.token_hex(4)` at import) is in the names because a pid alone is not enough: the hub of the
  Docker sandbox has the same pid at every container start, so a killed container's leftovers would look live.
  `_in_thread(..., threads=)` runs the work in threads of the caller's instead of the loop's default executor
  (v1's folder threads for the copy of a server folder, §21.1), and waits for them the same way.
- **Docker sandbox** (`copyfrom.hub_in_container(config)`: `config.skills_host_library_dir is not None` for
  `dreamteam sandbox`, or `DREAMTEAM_IMAGE=1` for docker compose and a plain docker run of the image; not any
  container, since DreamTeam run directly in a devcontainer sees its folders; the `container` of `/api/hub` and
  `/api/skills`): a missing path or a Windows-shaped one is 400 "The hub runs in the Docker sandbox and sees only
  its home (<home>): X is not there. Upload the folder as a .zip in the New session dialog of the sessions page
  instead."; the refusal of a path in the home adds " In the Docker sandbox, upload the folder as a .zip
  instead.". Other paths of the container are not refused here (a copy only reads them: the mounted roots of `[api]
  folders` are where such a source is found); a `workspace` outside the mounts is ("Workspace folder" above,
  `_container_refusal`); uploads land in `/swarm/.dreamteam/uploads`. The web UI's check of a source gives these
  texts before the create (`check_folder(use="source")`, "Choosing a folder from the web UI" above).
- **Uploads** (`copyfrom.Uploads(root)`, the manager's `uploads`): `receive(chunks, *, filename, length, limits)`
  (`POST /api/uploads`, §18.1): the file name cut to its last part (`\` read as `/`) and to one printable line of
  at most 200 characters ("upload.zip" when empty); a Content-Length of ASCII digits above `copy_max_mb` is 413
  "The file is larger than N MB ([workspace] copy_max_mb)." before reading; `clean()`; at most 8 uploads waiting
  or arriving (`UPLOAD_MAX_PENDING`, else 429 "N uploads already wait for a session; each is removed when a session
  uses it or an hour after its upload. Try again later."; the count and the create of the upload's `<token>.part`
  are made one upload at a time per store, under an `asyncio.Lock`, so uploads that arrive together each count the
  ones before them; the count is the tokens of the store's `.zip`, `.bin` and `.part` files joined with the uploads
  this store let in that have not ended yet, kept in memory and read before the folder, because a listing of a
  folder may miss a file renamed while it is read, an upload's `.part` becoming its `.zip` or `.bin`; one whose
  `.part` `clean()` removed, past its hour, no longer counts, as it can no longer be stored);
  `<token>.part` (O_EXCL, 0o600) streamed against the same 413; an empty body is
  400 "The upload is empty.", a file that is not a zip 400 "The file is not a zip archive."; then `<token>.json`
  `{"filename",
  "bytes", "at"}` and the rename to `<token>.zip`. Any failure (an exception from `chunks`, a disconnect included,
