  goes on to the caller) removes the `.part`. The token is `secrets.token_urlsafe(18)`; a value that is not 24
  characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` is 400 "'copy_from_upload' must be a token from POST /api/uploads." before any path
  is built. `peek` is 404 for an upload that is missing, used, or older than `UPLOAD_TTL` (3600 s, by the json's
  `at`, else the file's mtime). `claim` renames it to `<token>.claimed-<pid>-<run>-<hex8>.zip` under a lock (a
  rename on Windows is not exclusive: two can both succeed, the second moving the first one's file), so the loser
  gets FileNotFoundError: 404, another create took it (a claimed file that vanishes before `copy_into` reads it is
  the same 404). The create claims first (Order above), so from the claim on it is deleted whatever happens. `clean`
  (best effort) removes waiting names over the TTL and the claims `left_over` names (never by age, never one a
  create of this run uses); names of neither pattern stay. The HTTP API v1 (§21.3) uses the same class on its own
  root: `receive(..., kind="file", unpack=, max_pending=, caller=)` keeps any file as `<token>.bin` under a name
  `check_upload_name` passes (refused, not cleaned up), a 429 carries the code `too_many_uploads`; `peek_many`,
  `claim_many` (all or none, under the same lock), `unclaim` (renamed back, its hour unchanged) and `settle` (every
  claim of a create, released or given back, in its `finally`); `copy_sources` copies several into one staging
  folder, each in a `staging_name()` folder of its own beside it, then merged (`ZipRules.exclude_top`: the names
  the session keeps for itself, `SESSION_NAMES`, left out at the top of an unpacked zip). Both stores are read
  never through a link (§21.3 "Never through a link"): their folders are 0o700 on POSIX and a json 0o600; `peek`
  is 404 for a `<token>.zip` that is not a regular file with one name (`lstat`); a claim is opened with
  `O_NOFOLLOW` and checked again by `fstat` (`copyfrom._open_upload`), and its zip unpacked from that open file.
- **Clients that give up waiting**: a large copy may take longer than a client waits. The TUI and `-p` wait 900 s
  (`MOVE_TIMEOUT`) on a plain REST request, which a client going away does not cancel: the hub finishes the copy
  and creates the session anyway, so they check `dreamteam sessions` or the sessions page before trying again. An
  MCP client has its own tool timeout, and on it sends `notifications/cancelled` (the MCP SDK's dispatcher
  interrupts the handler; the streamable HTTP transport also cancels it on a disconnect): `session_create` awaits
  `manager.create` unshielded, so the copy stops and nothing is kept ("Cancel and cleanup" below). The user docs
  say to raise the client's tool timeout (Claude Code: `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`) or use the CLI or the web dialog for a
  large copy.
- **Accepted costs**: a target on another drive is copied twice (the staging under `sessions/`, then the move
  across volumes). The pre-check takes the largest of the plain end record's counts and those of a ZIP64 record
  whose locator precedes it (zipfile uses the ZIP64 ones whatever the plain record says), so a lying plain record
  cannot hide a ZIP64 directory. A forged central directory (a record that understates its entries, with a
  directory size within the `max_entries * 512` bound) can still make `zipfile` build one `ZipInfo` per 46-byte
  minimal entry: at the
  default `copy_max_files` up to about 100 MB of directory, on the order of 1 GB of memory for a moment. The upload
  is behind the hub's auth, a lower `copy_max_files` lowers the bound, and the pre-check keeps an honest huge zip
  from getting that far.

#### Skills
The manager's side of §19, for the home page, the CLI and the launcher MCP (`via` home / cli / launcher-mcp):
- `global_config()`: the home's settings (`Config`) as the library routes use them (re-read when the file changed).
- `skills` of `create` and `start`: a list of references (`x`, `library:x`, `claude-user:x`, `claude-project:x`
  against the session's folder, `host-library:x`) or sources (an absolute folder or .zip path on this machine, a Git
  URL; `source_spec`). Everything is made ready first, in a thread (`_prepare_skills`): references resolved and
  checked, sources staged (`stage_source`, not yet in the library). SessionError 400 (not a list of non-blank
  strings, a bad source, a source holding several skills: "... holds several skills (a, b): add them in the Skills
  tab and name them."), 404 (an unknown name), 409 (a source whose skill the library has with other content,
  `exists`; two different skills of one name); nothing staged is left behind. Then the staged sources are committed
  to the library (`by` user, `via`) and every skill is copied into the session (`swarm_skills.attach_files`,
  `attached_via` "create").
- `create(..., skills=)`: prepared before the session exists; committed right after `session.json` is written and
  before `set_workspace`, so a failure (the new session is removed) leaves nothing in the user's folder. The first
  start mirrors them; the members find them in their first wake-up.
- `start(sid, skills=)`, also for a running session (the start itself is then a no-op): a name already attached
  with other content is 409 (`exists`: "replace it in the session's Skills tab"); past `[skills] max_attached` 409.
  A stopped session gets the copies before its Swarm starts (`SessionSkills.attached_again(names)` takes the names
  out of kv `skills_detached`, as a live attach does); a running one attaches them live with
  `swarm.skills.attach(USER, ref, via=via)` (the members are told).
- `async session_skills(sid, show=None)` → `{"attached": [...], "running"}`, stopped or running, always the snapshot
  items of §14.1: a loaded swarm's `SessionSkills.public()` (on the loop: `deps` read live state), else the same keys
  from the session's files (`swarm_skills.stopped_public`, in a thread: `path` the mirror's, `roles` from its
  catalog, `deps` []); `show` adds that session copy's `files_list`, `skill_md`, `deps` and `install` (the global
  `[skills]` switches its preview line is worded by: the home page's proposal dialog may open before anything else
  loaded them; 404 when not attached).
- Messages about a source show it as `Staged.shown` (a Git URL without its user info), never as typed.
- `decide_skill(...)`: a running session's `SessionSkills.decide`; a stopped one's `decide_files` (`via`
  "stopped-session", `project` = the session's swarm name, `session` = sid; a loaded swarm's cache is reloaded); an
  `updated` event, and after a save (also the saves of `delete(sid, skills="save")`) a `skills` one (session None:
  an open home Skills tab reloads the library). SessionError 404 / 409 as §19.
- `delete(sid, skills=None)`: proposals waiting for the user's decision are never lost silently: 409 "Session X has
  skills waiting for your library decision: a, b. Save them to the library first, or delete them with the
  session." (`pending_skills`) unless `skills` is `"save"` (every one saved first; a name the library has with other
  content refuses the delete before anything is saved, 409 `exists`; a stopped session's are saved on its files with
  `via` "stopped-session", as `decide_skill` does) or `"discard"`; anything else 400.
- **The mirror in the user's folder**: an adopted folder never keeps `.scratch/_skills` once the session leaves it:
  `Swarm.stop` removes it, and so do `delete` (a crashed or never-stopped session) and `set_workspace` when it
  leaves an adopted folder (`_drop_mirror`, never following a link; a failure is logged).

### 17.3 Role catalog (roles.py)
A leaf module (no package imports; config.py uses it to check `[[roles]]`). The catalog is global: the settings
of a home or a project, never a session override (§17.2).
- **Built-in roles** `ROLE_PRESETS: {language: {id: (name, description)}}`, in catalog order (`PRESET_IDS`):
  generalist «Универсал»/Generalist, developer «Разработчик»/Developer, tester «Тестировщик»/Tester, reviewer
  «Ревьюер»/Reviewer, analyst «Аналитик»/Analyst, architect «Архитектор»/Architect, writer «Технический
  писатель»/Technical writer, researcher «Исследователь»/Researcher. `DEFAULT_ROLE_ID = "generalist"`
  (`prompts.DEFAULT_ROLE` is its name). The descriptions are addressed to the agent ("You ...", the same in both
  languages): they go into a new member's system prompt right after "Your role: <name>.". The architect and the
  developer name the contracts file `CONTRACTS.md`, the one the planning task asks for.
  In a thread session the presets' names and descriptions come from `ROLE_PRESETS_THREAD` (§22.6): `reviewer` is
  «Критик» / Critic there unless a `[[roles]]` entry has that name (§22.6).
- **`[[roles]]` entries** (`RoleSettings`): `name` (required: a built-in role's id or its name in either language
  customizes that role, only with the fields given; any other name is a role of the user's own), `description`
  (a non-empty one replaces a built-in description in both languages; required for an own role unless it is
  hidden), `instructions` (added for every member of the role), `model` (a profile of `[models]`; `""` = none),
  `hidden` (not offered: not in the team composer, not listed to agents; it still resolves), `skills` (skill names
  its agents get attached to their session at hire, marked as their own, §19; built-in presets list none). Deleting
  the entry
  of a built-in role resets it. `parse_roles` checks: a list of tables, at most 100 (`MAX_ROLES`); names 1–60
  characters (`NAME_LIMIT`) without `,` or `*` (they separate the items of a team), unique by `role_key`; texts at
  most 4000 characters (`TEXT_LIMIT`); errors `[[roles]] must be a list of role tables (write each role as a
  [[roles]] table)`, `At most 100 roles`, `[roles.N] name is empty`, `... the role 'X' is listed twice (also as
  role J)`, `... 'X': a role of your own needs a description`, `... 'X' uses the model profile 'M', which is not
  defined in [models]`, `[roles.N] skills: 'Bad Name' is not a skill name (lowercase letters, digits and
  hyphens)` (`skills.NAME_RE`, at most 64 characters), `[roles.N] skills: at most 20 skills per role`
  (`MAX_ROLE_SKILLS`) (and unknown keys or types as for the other sections); whether the library has a role's
  skills is not checked (a missing one is reported at hire). Stored normalized: a built-in role by its id, texts
  stripped, `model = ""` as None, skill names stripped and deduplicated in order.
- **Merge and resolution**: `catalog(entries, language, *, include_hidden=False) -> list[Role]` = the built-in
  roles in `PRESET_IDS` order with their entries applied, then the own roles in entry order; `Role(key, name,
  description, instructions="", model=None, builtin=False, customized=False, hidden=False, skills=())`, `key` = preset id or
  the casefolded name. `normalize(name)` collapses whitespace; `preset_id(name)` matches an id or a built-in name
  in either language, any case; `role_key(name)` = preset id or casefolded name; `find_role(entries, name,
  language)` (hidden roles too; None = a new role); `close_roles(entries, name, language, n=3)` (difflib, cutoff
  0.6, over the visible names, the preset ids and the other language's names; names in `language`);
  `summary(text, limit=200)` (the first sentence, else a cut at a word with "…").
- **Into an agent** (§3 `hire`): the canonical name in the member's language ("Tester" hired in a ru swarm becomes
  «Тестировщик»), the description into the frozen system prompt, the role's instructions before the hirer's, its
  model profile unless the hirer names one. A catalog edit reaches only members hired afterwards (also in running
  sessions, through `reconfigure`); existing members keep their prompts. Agents see the catalog in the `agents`
  output (§12), a new member's system prompt names it, and the kickoff lists the team (`Team: Name — Role; ...`).
- **Modes** (§22.6): `catalog(..., mode="board")` and `find_role(..., mode="board")` take the session's mode; in a
  thread session `find_role`, `close_roles` and `missing_roles` also match the thread names («Критик» / Critic →
  `reviewer`) unless a `[[roles]]` entry has that name (the reviewer then keeps its board name in the thread
  catalog, §22.6); `preset_id` and `role_key` do not change. A `[[roles]]` description (a built-in one's replacement
  or an own role's) and the instructions go into prompts verbatim in both modes, so word them for the mode the role
  is used in: a thread session has no tasks, reviews or planning task.
- **Starting team** (no field of its own): `swarm.starting_roles` (ordered; a name repeated per agent; preset ids,
  built-in names in either language or own role names) and `swarm.start_agents`.
  `starting_team(starting_roles, start_agents)`: member i gets `starting_roles[i]`; members beyond the list and
  blank entries are generalists; roles beyond `start_agents` are ignored (`[]` + 3 = three generalists). A name
  not in the catalog is an own role without a description. UIs show the team as rows:
  - `team_rows(starting_roles, start_agents) -> [(role, count)]`: consecutive equal roles grouped, order kept (the
    same role may appear in two rows); a row's role is a preset id or an own role's name as written (its
    `role_key` is the catalog key);
  - `team_value(rows) -> (starting_roles, start_agents)`: expanded, built-in names stored as ids, trailing
    generalists dropped (`[("generalist", 3)]` → `([], 3)`), so an untouched default never changes the settings;
  - `parse_team(text) -> list[str]` (`--team`, `/team`): `"architect, developer*2, tester"` → `["architect",
    "developer", "developer", "tester"]` (names kept as typed, normalized); ValueError `'developer*0': the count
    must be a whole number from 1 to 50`, `'*2': the role name is empty`, `'<item>': a role name cannot be longer
    than 60 characters`, `The team is empty`, `A team has at most 200 agents`.
- **Saved teams** (`[[teams]]`, `Config.teams`): `name` and `roles`, an ordered list with a name repeated per agent;
  the size is its length, and trailing generalists stay. No model: an agent's profile comes from its role. No limit
  on hiring: a team sets only who starts. `config.parse_teams(raw, entries)` checks shape only (messages
  `[teams.N] ...`, a 400 on `PUT /api/settings`) and normalizes as `[[roles]]` does at each load (`PUT` itself stores
  what was sent, §17.1); a name holding a control or invisible character (Unicode Cc, Cf) is refused, since it cannot
  be typed and is printed, except the format characters of ordinary text: U+200C, U+200D (Persian and Indic words,
  emoji sequences) and the tags U+E0020-E007F (subdivision flags). A name of those alone counts as empty. Names match
  by `team_key`: casefolded, whitespace collapsed. Whether the
  catalog has the roles is checked where a team is chosen, and the settings form
  refuses a save that leaves a team on a role it just lost. A team may share a role's name. `team_choice(text, teams,
  entries)` is the rule of `--team` and `/team`: a list or `*N` is roles (a saved team's name there that is no catalog
  role is refused); a bare word is the saved team, else a catalog role; with teams saved any other bare word is
  refused (`word*1` makes a new role), and with none it is a new role (`--team` says so on stderr, §18.3). A team's name
  is looked up in the home in use: `--home`, else a `dreamteam.toml` in the current folder, else `$DREAMTEAM_HOME`,
  else `~/DreamTeam`. A team is copied where it is chosen, into
  `swarm.starting_roles` and `start_agents`: by `--team`, `/team` and `session_create(team_name=...)`, and by the
  new-session dialog into its rows, which it sends as `starting_roles` even when the default equals them. POST
  `/api/sessions`, `SessionManager` and `session.json` take no team name (`overrides.swarm.team_name` and
  `overrides.teams` are refused), and nothing looks a team up after the copy.
- **Views**: `presets_view()` → `[{id, name: {ru, en}, description: {ru, en}}]`; `catalog_view(entries)` →
  `[{key, builtin, customized, hidden, name: {ru, en}, description: {ru, en}, instructions, model, skills}]` (hidden roles
  included; an own role has the same text under both languages). Served by `GET /api/settings` (§18.1); the
  visible roles of one swarm by `GET /api/roles` (§14).
- **Compatibility**: no `[[roles]]` → the 8 built-in roles; existing `starting_roles` keep working (built-in names
  now bring their description); no database change. An older version refuses a file with `[[teams]]` (`Unknown config
  sections: teams`), but only once a team exists: with none the file has no such key. Session folders are untouched.

## 18. Launcher: web, MCP, CLI, UI

### 18.1 Web (launcher.py)
`create_launcher_app(manager, host="127.0.0.1")` returns the app wrapped in the same `GuardMiddleware`
(host/origin, JSON POSTs), with `api=True` (the external API's branch, §14, §21.1) and
`raw_posts={"/api/uploads": "application/zip", "/api/v1/uploads": ("application/octet-stream", "application/zip")}`:
the guard's 415 rule lets a POST to `/api/...` pass when its content type starts with `application/json`, or when
`raw_posts` maps that exact path (no prefix: `/api/uploads/` is not it) to its type, or to a set holding it, without
parameters, ignoring case; on the v1 branch a path `raw_posts` lists takes its own types alone (`/api/v1/uploads`:
415 for JSON too, §21.3), while `/api/uploads` keeps the rule above. Host, Origin, token and cookie
checks run before that rule and are unchanged; `application/zip` is not a CORS-safelisted type, so a cross-site
page cannot send it without a preflight, which the hub never answers. Session apps pass no `raw_posts`. Inside the
guard `_ApiFirst` sends a path `web.is_api_path` takes to `ApiV1.app` (§21.1 "Dispatch"; `app.api` is the `ApiV1`)
and every other path, and the lifespan, on. A
`SessionRouter` in front sends `/s/{sid}/...` to that session's app
(`web.create_app(swarm, on_library_change=...)`, §14, served with `root_path = /s/{sid}`; a library change there
emits `sessions.changed` with change `skills`, also a `skill_attach` or `skill_approve` of `/api/act` that
succeeded: either may have changed the library) and everything else to the launcher routes.

| method path | response |
|---|---|
| GET `/` | `static/home.html` (launcher page, `no-store`) |
| GET `/static/{file}` | static files (`UIStaticFiles`, `no-cache`) |
| GET `/api/hub` | `{"pid","project": str(home),"home","name":"DreamTeam","version","mode":"launcher","sandbox","container","api"}` (`container`: `copyfrom.hub_in_container`, §17.2 "Copying files into a new session"; `api`: the hub has an API token of its own, `hubauth.api_digest() is not None`, §21.1: `dreamteam status` then prints the API's address; never the token or its digest) |
| GET `/api/sessions` | `{"sessions": [summary...]}` |
| POST `/api/sessions` | body `{title?, goal?, description?, overrides?, start?=true, workspace?, skills?: [ref or source], via?}` → `{"session": summary}` (201); the header `X-DreamTeam-Auto-Reply: 1` (§14) is passed as `create(..., auto_reply=True)`; `overrides.swarm.clarify` (bool) is clarify mode (§3.1); `skills` attached before the first start (§17.2 "Skills"; `via` the surface recorded for them: `home` when absent, `cli` from the terminal's client, anything else 400); `goal` may be multi-line and `title` "" (the server splits the goal and derives the title, §17.2); with `workspace` (an absolute folder, §17.2 "Workspace folder") also `"result"` (mode `created` or `adopted`), and `expect?: "created"\|"adopted"` the mode the user agreed to (the web check's `expect`; 409 when the folder turned out otherwise, nothing created; 400 without `workspace`, or `adopted` with a copy); `copy_from` (an absolute folder or .zip path on the hub's computer) or `copy_from_upload` (a token of POST `/api/uploads`), strings, not both: copied into the new session's folder before its first start (§17.2 "Copying files into a new session"), the answer then also has `"copy"` (`copy_result`); 404 for an unknown or used upload, 409 for a `workspace` with files, 413 over `[workspace] copy_max_mb` / `copy_max_files` |
| POST `/api/uploads?filename=<name>` | the raw zip as the body (`Content-Type: application/zip`, not base64 JSON; the guard's `raw_posts`) → 201 `{"upload": token, "filename", "bytes", "expires_in": 3600}` (`manager.uploads.receive` with the limits of `manager.global_config()`); 415 JSON when not `application/zip` (the handler checks too), 413 over `copy_max_mb` (Content-Length or streamed), 429 when 8 uploads wait, 400 empty, not a zip, or interrupted (starlette's `ClientDisconnect`: "The upload was interrupted."), 500 for other failures (`_failure`); the token is used once by `POST /api/sessions` within an hour |
| GET `/api/sessions/{sid}` | `{"session": summary, "config": manager.config_view(sid)}` |
| PATCH `/api/sessions/{sid}` | body `{title?, overrides?, settings?}` → `{"session": summary, "config": config_view(sid)}`; `overrides` replaces all of them, `settings` `{section: {key: value \| null}}` changes only those keys (null: the global value again; §17.2 "Partial update"; `{"swarm": {"clarify": true \| false \| null}}` is the ⚙ field and the TUI's `/clarify`, §3.1); both at once, a bad value or `main` → 400 and nothing changes |
| DELETE `/api/sessions/{sid}?confirm={sid}&skills=save\|discard&via=` | `{"ok": true}` (+ `"workspace_kept": path` when the session worked in a folder outside it, which is never deleted); 400 without a matching confirm; 409 `{"error", "pending_skills"}` when members' proposals wait for the user's decision and `skills` is not given (§17.2) |
| POST `/api/sessions/{sid}/workspace` | body `{"path": "<absolute>"}` or `{"default": true}`, optionally `"expect": "moved"\|"adopted"` (the mode the user agreed to, §17.2) → `{"session": summary, "result": set_workspace result}`; 400 bad body or target, 404 unknown session, 409 dirty repository, MCP name conflict, a folder of another session, a folder that is not what `expect` says, a file in use, `main` |
| POST `/api/folders/check` | body `{"path"?: str, "use"?: "workspace"\|"source" (default "workspace"), "session"?: sid, "default"?: true}` → 200 `check_folder` answer (§17.2 "Choosing a folder from the web UI"): `{use, path, target, state, mode, expect, fresh, back, lost, git, branch, mcp, running, api_folder}` for a folder that can be used, `{use, path, target, state}` for a copy source, or `{use, path, error, status}` for a refused one (also status 504 when the folder did not answer within 20 s, at once while an earlier thread for it still runs); 400 a bad body or invalid session settings, 404 an unknown session, 409 `main` or a session made by an earlier version, 429 when the 4 folder threads are busy (its own text when folders that did not answer hold them); a GET 405 |
| POST `/api/folders/list` | body `{"path"?: str, "use"?: "workspace"\|"source" (default "workspace"), "session"?: sid}` → `list_folders` (§17.2): `{path, parent, root, roots: [{path, kind: home\|drive\|system\|recent\|api\|dreamteam, name, selectable}], entries: [{name, path, link, open, refused, busy: null\|{sid, title}, current, repo, files, noaccess}], truncated, partial, fallback, error, refused, selectable, busy, current, sep}`, subfolders only (never a file), at most 500 of the first 10 000 entries; without `path` the roots alone; a folder that cannot be read 200 with `error`; 400 a bad body, a relative path or a bad `use`, 403 a network path, a path outside the roots (by its text, then resolved) or a closed folder, 404 an unknown session, 429, 504; a GET 405 (a POST, so that no page of another site can make the hub touch a path, §17.2) |
| POST `/api/sessions/{sid}/start` / `/stop` | `{"session"}`; another action → 404; start takes an optional body `{"skills": [...], "via"?}` (attached first; live when it is running; `via` as for create; the delete's `?via=` too); start with the auto-reply header → `start(..., auto_reply=True)`, also for a running session |
| GET `/api/sessions/{sid}/skills?show=` | `manager.session_skills(sid, show)`: the attached skills (snapshot items, §14.1), also of a stopped session |
| POST `/api/sessions/{sid}/skills/{name}/decide` | body `{"approve": bool, "comment"?, "replace"?}` → `{"text", "session"}` (`decide_skill`, via home) |
| GET / POST `/api/skills`, GET / DELETE `/api/skills/{name}` | the library routes of §14 (`skill_routes` with `manager.global_config`, via `home`, no swarm: no `attached`, no `attach`, no `from=session`, no `deps-log`); `?workspace=<absolute>` names the folder whose `.claude/skills` is offered (a relative one 400; on Windows a network path 400 by its text, nothing read, §17.2 "Choosing a folder from the web UI"); a change emits `sessions.changed` (session None, change `skills`) |
| POST `/api/skill-envs/cleanup` | `EnvManager.cleanup(env_retention_days, every_unused=True)` now (a daemon thread: every env no session uses, whatever its age) → `{"removed", "kept"}`; emits change `skill-envs` |
| GET `/api/settings` | `{"settings": public view, "providers": PROVIDER_CHOICES, "role_presets": roles.presets_view(), "role_catalog": roles.catalog_view(config.roles), "path": str(settings file), "home", "network_isolation": netoff.shown(netoff.isolation()) (§7.2)}` (a hand edit of the file is picked up first); `settings.teams` holds the saved teams, `[{name, roles}]` (§17.3): a REST client starts one by posting its roles as `overrides.swarm.starting_roles` and `start_agents` |
| PUT `/api/settings` | body `{"settings": {...sections}}` (`settings.roles`: the complete list of `[[roles]]` entries, `[]` removes every customization; `settings.teams`: the complete list of `[[teams]]` entries, `[]` removes the key, shape checked only: a team may name a role the catalog lacks) → `{"settings","applied_to","role_presets","role_catalog"}`; 400 with the `[roles.N] ...` or `[teams.N] ...` text for a bad role or team (nothing saved) |
| POST `/api/settings/check` | body `{"profile": {...}, "name"?: stored profile name for the key fallback, "live"?: bool}` → `check_profile` result; 400 when the fallback would send the stored key to another provider or base_url than the saved one, or a key from the hub's environment to an endpoint that neither the provider's default, a preset nor a saved profile uses with that variable |
| WS `/ws` | pushes `sessions.changed` events (manager.listen) |
| `/mcp` | launcher MCP (§18.2) |
| `/api/v1/...` | the external HTTP API v1 (§21; dispatched in front of `SessionRouter` to `ApiV1.app`) |
| GET `/s/{sid}` | 307 redirect to `/s/{sid}/` (query kept) |
| GET `/s/{sid}/` | the session's `index.html` (board UI) |
| `/s/{sid}/api/*`, `/s/{sid}/ws`, `/s/{sid}/mcp` | the session app; `manager.load(sid)` loads a stopped session for viewing |

- Errors are `{"error": text}` with SessionError.status; a body that is not JSON, not an object or has fields of
  the wrong type is 400; unexpected failures (e.g. the swarm failed to start, a locked file) are JSON 500s.
- `POST /s/{sid}/api/*` without `Content-Type: application/json` is 415 (the guard only knows `/api/...`).
- The folder routes (`POST /api/folders/list`, `POST /api/folders/check`) are routes of the launcher app alone,
  behind the guard with the hub token like the other internal routes, JSON POSTs only (the guard's JSON type rule
  then keeps other sites' pages out, §17.2): a session app has none (its `/api/files` stays confined to the
  session's folder), the v1 branch none (the API token never opens them), the launcher MCP none; neither clashes
  with `/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`.
- The app's lifespan runs `_clean_envs_daily(manager)`: unused skill environments are removed
  `ENV_CLEANUP_DELAY` (60 s) after the start and then every `ENV_CLEANUP_EVERY` (24 h), with the settings read
  each time (`env_retention_days = 0`: none); a failure is logged; the task is cancelled at exit.
- An unknown sid: 404 JSON for `/api` and `/mcp` paths, an HTML error page otherwise, WebSocket close 1008. A
  session that cannot be opened: its status as JSON for `/api` and `/mcp`, an HTML page for the board, close
  1011; so a session made by an earlier version (§17.2) gets 409 with its message for `/api` and `/mcp` (JSON
  `{"error": <message>, "earlier_version": true}`; checked before the stopped answer, the database read in a
  thread; the answer to a `SessionError` of a load carries the error's extra fields too), the HTML
  page with it for the board, a WebSocket accepted and then closed 1011 with the reason `made by an earlier
  version` (a close reason holds at most 123 bytes; the page shows the full message; an open board keeps that
  message and stops reconnecting, §18.4 "Topbar"), and the same 409 from
  `POST .../start`, `POST .../stop`, `PATCH`, `.../workspace` and the `.../skills` routes, while `GET
  /api/sessions`, `GET` and
  `DELETE /api/sessions/{sid}` work (the summary carries `earlier_version`). After shutdown began, no new session
  app is built (503).
- Session apps are cached per sid and rebuilt when the manager's swarm object changes. Each one's lifespan (its
  MCP `StreamableHTTPSessionManager.run()`) runs in a task of its own, entered when the app is built and exited
  when the session unloads or the server stops (a request cancelled meanwhile stops it too). On stop and on
  start the session's WebSockets are closed with code 1012, so the browsers reconnect and reload the state.
- A **stopped** session (loaded but not running) is read-only:
  - GET routes work;
  - `POST /s/{sid}/api/act/*` and any session `/mcp` request return 409 `{"ok": false, "result": STOPPED_TEXT,
    "error": STOPPED_TEXT}` with `STOPPED_TEXT = "The session is stopped. Start it on the sessions page."`;
  - the session's `/api/state` snapshot has `swarm.session.status = "stopped"`.
- `serve_launcher(manager, host, port, log_level="warning", *, on_started=None, resume=None, on_listening=None)`
  sets `manager.hub_url` (and the loaded swarms' `hub_url`), starts uvicorn, calls `on_listening` as soon as
  the port is open (write hub.json there), then resumes the autostart sessions when `server.resume_sessions` is
  on (or `resume=True`) — only once the port is ours, so a second launcher losing the race never runs them —
  then calls `on_started`. Which sessions it will try is chosen before uvicorn starts (`manager.plan_resume()`: by
  their mark alone, no log line), so the first request already finds them in `resume_pending`; a launcher that does
  not get the port drops the plan (`cancel_resume()`). On exit (cancelled, or a callback failed) it stops the web
  server and `manager.shutdown()` (sessions keep their autostart mark).

### 18.2 Launcher MCP (launcher_mcp.py)
`build_launcher_server(manager)`, `LauncherMCPEndpoint(manager, host, extra_hosts=())` (served at `/mcp`) and
`serve_stdio_launcher(manager)` (stdio, with hub_mcp's `_StdinLines`):
- Session tools (`LAUNCHER_TOOLS`): `sessions_list`, `session_create(goal, title?, description?, language?,
  start_agents?, max_agents?, team?, team_name?, max_cost_usd?, model?, network?, clarify?, mode?, goal_rule?,
  start?=true, workspace?,
  copy_from?, skills?)` (unset values come from the global settings; the board URL is shown only when a web server runs;
  `goal`: one line, or several, split as in §17.2; `team`: role names in order, a name repeated per agent (§17.3) →
  `swarm.starting_roles` (normalized) and `start_agents = len(team)` unless `start_agents` is given, `[]` = no team;
  not a list of non-blank strings →
  "team must be a list of role names, e.g. [...]", more than 200 → "A team has at most 200 agents.", a name over
  60 characters → "'<name>': a role name cannot be longer than 60 characters.", a name with `,` or `*` (the
  `--team` syntax) → "'<name>': a role name cannot contain ',' or '*'; give one item per agent and repeat a name
  for several agents, e.g. [...]."; `team_name`: a team saved in the settings (§17.3 "Saved teams"), looked up in
  `manager.global_config()` and copied now: its roles become `swarm.starting_roles` and its size `start_agents`, and
  `max_agents` is not raised, as with `team`; absent or `""` = none given; with `team` or `start_agents` → "team_name
  sets the roles and their number: give it without team and start_agents.", not a string → "team_name must be the name
  of a saved team.", an unknown name → "No saved team 'x'. Saved teams: a, b.", or with none saved "No saved team 'x'.
  None are saved yet: Settings > Teams.", a team that cannot start → "The team 'X' uses roles that are not in the role
  catalog: y, z. Fix it in Settings > Teams.", and a `team` item that names a saved team and no role
  (`roles.saved_team_in`) → "'coding' is a saved team, not a role: pass it as team_name."; nothing is created on any of
  these; `clarify`: a boolean, `swarm.clarify` (§3.1;
  `false` overrides a global
  `true`), any other value → "clarify must be true or false." and nothing is created; `mode`, `goal_rule`: the
  thread mode, §22.9 "Launcher MCP"; `workspace`: an absolute
  folder, §17.2; `copy_from`: an absolute folder or .zip path on the hub's computer copied into the new session's
  folder first (§17.2 "Copying files into a new session"; not a string → "copy_from must be an absolute path of a
  folder or a .zip file.", blank = no copy; the reply adds `copy_text(copy_result)`; `copy_from_upload` is not
  offered: an MCP client has the hub's file system or the REST route); `skills`: names or sources attached before
  the first start, §17.2 "Skills"),
  `session_start(session, skills?)` (the skills attached first, live when it runs), `session_stop(session)` and `session_cd(session, path)` (`set_workspace`; `path`
  absolute or `"default"`; the result in words by `workspace_text(result)`, worded as the TUI and the console
  word it: "Moved the session's files to X" only when they moved, "The session now works in X" after a folder of
  the user or a missing one, and what changed in the user's folder it left (`old_changed`)). `sessions_list`
  shows the folder of a session that does not work in its own one (`folder: <path> (adopted, MISSING)`), the source
  of a session made with a copy (`copied from: <source>`, one printable line of at most 300 characters again: the
  summary may be a remote hub's JSON), and for a
  running session with background jobs ` | jobs N running` (`session_line`, from `read_stats` "jobs"); a running one
  in the user's wrap-up mode is `[running, wrapping up]`; one paused for a member's question (summary `question`,
  §3.1) is `[paused (waiting for your answer to Anna Smith, question #12)]`; a session created through the HTTP API
  v1 (summary `via` "api", §21.4) has ` | HTTP API` right after the cost, before the marks that follow; a session
  without network ends its first
  line with ` | no network` (summary `network`, §7.2), one in clarify mode with ` | clarify` (summary `clarify`,
  after ` | no network`); a thread session shows ` | thread (<rule>) | posts N` (summary `goal_rule`, democracy or
  veto) in place of ` | tasks d/t done`, then, while #1 exists, ` | goal vote F/C for (needs K)` (`, A against`
  before the parenthesis when a counted member dislikes #1; §22.9); a session made by an earlier version
  (summary `earlier_version`, §17.2) is `[stopped]`
  ending its first line with ` | made by an earlier version: cannot be opened` (`session_start`, `session_cd` and
  every hub tool with it as `session` answer with the message of §17.2); a
  session with skills gets `skills: a, b (waiting for your
  library decision: b)`. The last session tool is `skill_library(action: list | show | import | delete, name?,
  source?, pick?, replace?)`, the home page's Skills tab in words (via `launcher-mcp`): `list` the library, the
  host library and Claude Code's skills; `show` an entry (`name` may be `claude-user:x` / `host-library:x`) with
  its source, files, the dependency preview and SKILL.md; `import` either `source` (a folder or .zip path, a Git
  URL) or `name` (`claude-user:x`, `host-library:x`); several skills without `pick` list them; `delete` a library
  entry (the sessions keep their copies). Library changes emit `sessions.changed` (change `skills`). There is no
  `session_delete` tool.
- Every hub tool (§13) with an extra optional `session` property. Without it the call goes to
  `manager.default_session()` (never a session created through the HTTP API v1, §17.1); when there is none, the
  error lists the sessions, and adds `A session created through the HTTP API is never the default.` when one is
  listed. An unknown or stopped session is an error result (`session_start` is suggested; for a session made by an earlier version, its message).
- Calls run `hub_mcp.hub_call` on the session's swarm (same actor rules: `as_agent`). A call still running when
  its session stops or is deleted ends with `Error: session X was stopped while <tool> was running.` Each call is
  dispatched inside `hub_mcp.serving_client(client_key(ctx, local))` (`local` = `local:<uuid>` per launcher server),
  so the session's `hub_call` knows the MCP client (§13: its own messages never come back to it as news).
- `dispatch_launcher_call(manager, name, args)` answers a tool name nobody knows (close matches + the list);
  `call_launcher_tool` turns SessionError / ToolError / unexpected failures into error results.
- `INSTRUCTIONS` explain sessions (with `skill_library` and the `skills` of `session_create` / `session_start`,
  with "`session_create(..., team_name=<name>)` starts with a team saved in the settings; an unknown name is answered
  with the saved names.",
  and: "A session created with clarify=true first asks you about its goal; `sessions_list` shows a session that waits
  for your answer as "paused (waiting for your answer to X, question #N)".", and after the `workspace=<folder>`
  line: "`session_create(..., copy_from=<folder or .zip>)` copies those files into the new session's folder first:
  the agents work on the copy, the originals stay untouched."), then the hub instructions (they hold
  the answer rule, §13).
- Thread sessions (§22.9): `session_create`'s `mode` (board | thread → `swarm.mode`) and `goal_rule` (democracy |
  veto → `swarm.goal_rule`, thread only; with an effective board mode it is refused); `sessions_list` shows
  ` | thread (<rule>) | posts N` in place of ` | tasks d/t done`, then, while #1 exists,
  ` | goal vote F/C for (needs K)` (with `, A against` when a counted member dislikes #1); the hub tools are
  the union of both modes' (`hub_specs(None)`), a tool of one mode marked
  " [Board sessions only.]" / " [Thread sessions only.]"
  and refused by a session of the other mode; `INSTRUCTIONS` are mode-neutral, with one paragraph on the modes, and
  the `clarify` description covers both modes.
- `/s/{sid}/mcp` keeps the per-session hub MCP (§13).

### 18.3 CLI (cli.py)
```
dreamteam [tui|chat] ["PROMPT"] [-c | -r [SID]] [-p [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--timeout S]
          [--no-auto-reply]] [--verbose] [--home H] [--lang ru|en] [--model PROFILE] [--agents N]
          [--team "ROLE[*N],..." | NAME] [--max-agents N] [--budget USD] [--title T] [--workspace DIR]
          [--copy-from DIR|ZIP] [--skill REF|PATH|URL ...] [--host H] [--port P] [--network on|off]
          [--clarify | --no-clarify] [--mode board|thread] [--goal-rule democracy|veto]
dreamteam serve [DIR | --home H] [--host H] [--port P] [--goal G [--title T] [--workspace DIR] [--copy-from DIR|ZIP]
          [--skill REF|PATH|URL ...] [--network on|off] [--clarify | --no-clarify] [--mode board|thread]
          [--goal-rule democracy|veto]] [--no-console] [--no-browser]
dreamteam sessions [DIR | --home H]
dreamteam sessions rm SID [SID ...] [--yes] [--skills save|discard] [--home H]
dreamteam traces [AGENT] [--home H] [--session SID] [--id N] [--span N [--context]] [--status S] [--limit N] [--json]
dreamteam console [DIR | --home H | --url URL] [--session SID] [--lang ru|en]
dreamteam mcp [DIR | --home H] [--no-web]
dreamteam status [DIR | --home H]
dreamteam sandbox [DIR | --home H] [--build] [--port P] [--goal G] [--network on|off]
dreamteam export FOLDER [--include CATEGORIES]... [--session ID]... [--dry-run] [--home H] [--quiet]
dreamteam import FOLDER [--include CATEGORIES]... [--session ID|UID]... [--dry-run] [--yes] [--home H] [--quiet]
```
- Default command (`_default_command`): `dreamteam` alone runs `tui` when stdin and stdout are terminals,
  else `serve`. Options only: `tui` when one of them is a TUI option (`-p -c -r --output-format --model
  --budget --agents --team --max-agents --verbose --timeout --no-auto-reply --lang`), `serve` when one is
  serve-only (`--no-console --no-browser --goal`) or there is no terminal, else `tui`. A first word that is not a command
  is the TUI prompt (`dreamteam "Сделай змейку"`), except a mistyped command name, which argparse reports
  (`_mistyped`: one word of at least 3 letters one edit from a command — a letter inserted, deleted or replaced, or
  two neighbours swapped; a word of 3 letters only with two swapped, `rnu`).
- Event loop start (`run_loop`, issue #62): the commands, `tui.main_tui` and `tui.main_print` start their loop with
  `cli.run_loop(main)`. On Windows (`LOOPBACK_SOCKETPAIR`) each asyncio loop first opens a `socket.socketpair()`,
  which Python makes by connecting to itself over 127.0.0.1 and accepting with no timeout: a program that holds local
  connections (network filtering of an antivirus or firewall, its unseen "allow?" window, a VPN or proxy client)
  holds `asyncio.run` there, silently and deaf to Ctrl+C. `run_loop` first opens and closes one pair in a daemon
  thread, waiting in 0.1 s steps: Ctrl+C works between them (KeyboardInterrupt as from `asyncio.run`, `main` closed
  unstarted). After `LOOPBACK_WAIT` (5 s) `loopback_text()` goes once to stderr (never stdout) and to the log when one
  is set up (INFO): the program file of the process (`_python_image`, not a venv launcher or a Store alias), likely
  causes, fixes (and to start again if it does not go on after them) and docs/en/getting-started.md; once the pair
  opens, "... DreamTeam goes on." A failed pair (a proxy's "Unexpected peer connection") gets the failure form, then
  `asyncio.run` runs. Should the loop's own pair be held after the check passed (a program that asks for each
  connection), a daemon thread writes the same text after `LOOPBACK_WAIT` unless the loop's first step ran by then,
  saying Ctrl+C cannot stop that wait. `run_loop` closes `main` only when the loop never ran it: a task that a Ctrl+C
  during `asyncio.run`'s cleanup left pending stays as `asyncio.run` leaves it. Elsewhere `run_loop` is `asyncio.run`.
- `tui` (docs/TUI.md): `tui.main_tui` (interactive; refuses without a terminal, exit 2) or with `-p`
  `tui.main_print` (text piped into stdin — a pipe or a file, never a terminal or NUL — is appended to the
  prompt; no prompt → exit 2). `-r` without an id opens the session picker (`/sessions`). The flags `--model`,
  `--agents`, `--max-agents`, `--budget`, `--title` become the overrides of a session the TUI creates. The
  prompt is the goal: its first line becomes the title, the rest the description (split by the hub, §17.2).
  `--team "architect, developer*2, tester"` or `--team NAME` (also with `-p`) is checked before anything starts
  (`dreamteam: --team: <error>` on stderr, exit 2): `roles.parse_team`, then `roles.team_choice` (§17.3 "Saved teams")
  over the home's settings (`_team_choice`). Exit 2 also for a bare word that is neither a saved team nor a role while
  teams are saved (`no saved team or role 'codng' (there are: coding, Тексты). For a new role with no description write
  'codng*1'`; the list is `roles.close_roles` plus all the saved names), a saved team's name that is no catalog role,
  in a list or with `*N` (`'Тексты' is a saved team: choose it whole, with no other roles and no *N`), a team that
  cannot start (`the team 'Тексты' uses roles that are not in the role catalog: y, z. Fix it in Settings > Teams`), a
  team with `--agents` (`the team 'Тексты' sets the number of agents: --agents cannot go with it`), and a bare word
  that is no built-in role when the settings cannot be read (`cannot read the settings to look up 'Тексты': <reason>`;
  a list passes). The refusal of `--agents` adds `. For the role write 'tester*1' and keep --agents` when the word is
  also a catalog role: `tester*1 --agents 2` is one tester and a generalist, what the word means with no such team. `-p`
  with `-c` or `-r ID` continues a session and never reads the team, so it checks only the syntax. A note on stderr,
  with no change in the exit code or stdout, for a bare word with no role or saved team in a home with no saved team
  (`no role or saved team 'coding' in <home>: starting a new role with no description (write 'coding*1' to mean that)`:
  the teams may be in another home). A saved
  team reaches the TUI as its list of roles, copied now, anything else as the raw text (`overrides["team"]`, only when
  given); the TUI turns it into `swarm.starting_roles` of the sessions it creates (`start_agents` = the team's size
  unless `--agents` is given; `--max-agents` passes through, also below the size). With auto-replies on, `-p` also
  approves the tasks that wait for the user's review (print mode `AUTO_REVIEW`, docs/TUI.md); with `--no-auto-reply`
  they wait.
- `--network on|off` (`tui`, `-p`, `serve` with `--goal`, exit 2 without it; `run`; `sandbox`): `[swarm] network`
  (§7.2) of the session that run creates (`overrides["network"]` → `swarm.network`, tui.commands.FLAT_OVERRIDES; serve:
  `create(..., overrides={"swarm": {"network": ...}})`), of `run`'s swarm for this run only (the settings file keeps
  its value), and for `sandbox` the firewall of the container (`docker.wants_firewall`) plus `--network` of the
  command inside (a project's `run`, or `serve --goal`). Neither a TUI-only nor a serve-only flag (`_default_command`).
- `--clarify` / `--no-clarify` (`argparse.BooleanOptionalAction`, default None: the settings decide; help
  `cli.CLARIFY_HELP`; `tui`, `-p`, `serve` with `--goal`, `run`): `[swarm] clarify` (§3.1). `tui`:
  `overrides["clarify"]` (only when given; tui.commands.FLAT_OVERRIDES → `swarm.clarify`) of the sessions this window
  creates, also with `-c` / `-r` (there it is the window's setting for new sessions, as `/clarify` without a
  session, docs/TUI.md §4.5); `serve`: `create(..., overrides={"swarm": {"clarify": ...}})`, exit 2 without `--goal`
  (`--clarify needs --goal: it is a setting of the session that --goal creates (an existing session changes it in
  its ⚙ settings or with /clarify).`); `run`: its swarm for this run only (the settings file keeps its value, as
  with `run --network`). The help of `serve` and `run` is built from the same phrase as `CLARIFY_HELP`, without its
  `-p` clause. `-p` refuses with exit 2, before anything
  starts: first `--clarify` or `--no-clarify` with `-c` / `-r` (`dreamteam -p: --clarify is a setting of a new
  session; change an existing one with /clarify in dreamteam tui or in its ⚙ settings on the board.`), then
  `--clarify` without `--no-auto-reply` (`dreamteam -p: --clarify needs --no-auto-reply: with automatic replies
  nobody answers the questions, and the session plans as usual.`). Neither a TUI-only nor a serve-only flag;
  `sandbox` does not forward it (the dialog or the ⚙ settings set it).
- `--mode board|thread` and `--goal-rule democracy|veto` (argparse choices, default None; `tui`, `-p`, `serve` with
  `--goal`, `run`): the work mode and the goal rule of the session that run creates (FLAT_OVERRIDES `mode`,
  `goal_rule`); refused with `-p -c` / `-p -r` and for `serve` without `--goal` (exit 2), and for `run` a `--mode`
  that differs from its swarm.db's mode; `sandbox` forwards neither (§22.8 "CLI").
- `--workspace DIR` (`tui`, `-p`, and `serve` with `--goal`): the folder the session created by that run works in
  (`create(..., workspace=)`, §17.2: an empty or missing folder becomes its workspace; a folder with files is
  adopted, its repository must be clean). `~` and a relative DIR are resolved against the current directory
  (`os.path.abspath`); the hub checks the rest. Exit 2 for a file, with `-c` / `-r` (an existing session moves
  with `/cd`), and for `serve` without `--goal`. The TUI applies it to the first session it creates (and says so
  under the welcome box); `-p` names the folder on stderr with `--verbose`; `serve` prints the result
  (`launcher_mcp.workspace_text`) on stderr.
- `--copy-from DIR|ZIP` (`tui`, `-p`, and `serve` with `--goal`): a folder or .zip copied into the folder of the
  session that run creates before its first start (`create(..., copy_from=)`, §17.2 "Copying files into a new
  session"; with `--workspace` into that folder, which must be empty or missing). `_copy_from_arg`: `~` and a
  relative path are resolved against the current directory; an existing file that is not a .zip is refused here
  (`dreamteam: --copy-from <path> is a file but not a .zip archive.`, exit 2); the hub checks the rest. Exit 2 with
  `-c` / `-r` (`dreamteam: --copy-from copies files into a new session; it cannot be used with -c / -r.`) and for
  `serve` without `--goal` (`--copy-from needs --goal: it fills the folder of the session that --goal creates.`).
  The TUI applies it to the first session it creates (`TUI.copy_from_override`, as `/copy-from`; shown under the
  welcome box); `-p` prints the copy on stderr (with or without `--verbose`, not with `stream-json`), plus the
  left-out counts when something was left out; `serve` prints `Session <id>: <copy_text>` on
  stderr before the workspace result. Like `--workspace`, it is neither a TUI-only nor a serve-only flag. The CLI
  does not upload a zip to a sandboxed or remote hub itself: a host path the hub cannot see gets the hub's "upload
  the folder as a .zip" refusal.
- `--skill X` (repeatable; `tui`, `-p`, and `serve` with `--goal`, exit 2 without it): a skill attached to the
  session (§17.2 "Skills"). A URL (`scheme://` or `user@host:path`) is passed as given, a path (it has a separator,
  starts with `.` or `~`, ends in `.zip`, or is a folder or .zip here) is made absolute against the current
  directory, anything else is a reference checked before anything starts against the home's settings
  (`resolve_ref`; `claude-project:x` against the `--workspace` folder; not checked when resuming, the hub resolves it
  against the session's folder): `dreamteam: --skill X: <error>` on stderr, exit 2. The TUI attaches them to the session it creates, or
  with `-c` / `-r` to the resumed one (`POST .../start {"skills", "via": "cli"}`, live when it runs; `-r` without an
  id: the session picked; one attempt, so a failed one never attaches them to another session later; a session
  refused as one of an earlier version — `-r ID`, the picker, `-c`, or a start the hub answers 409 with
  `earlier_version` — ends the resume attempt: no later resumed session gets them; a session the TUI then creates
  does, as after `-c` with no sessions); `-p` the
  same; `serve` passes them to `create(..., skills=, via="cli")`. `--skill` is not a TUI-only flag (`serve` takes it too).
- The directory: `--home`, else DIR, else the current directory when it has `dreamteam.toml`, else the default
  home (`serve` never takes the current directory: `--home`, DIR or the default home). It is a launcher **home**
  when `--home` is given, when it has `sessions/` next to `dreamteam.toml`, or when it is the default home;
  otherwise it is a single-swarm project (§15). `serve`, `mcp` and `sandbox` create a home on demand; the
  listing commands (`sessions`, `status`, `traces`) never create one.
- `sessions rm SID...` (also `delete`, `del`, `remove`) deletes sessions as the sessions page does: through the
  running hub (`DELETE /api/sessions/{sid}?confirm={sid}`, which stops a running session first), else with a
  `SessionManager` of the home — unless another live DreamTeam process may run the home's sessions without a
  hub that answers: a `hub.json` of a live process (or of a Docker sandbox), or a launcher marker
  `<home>/.dreamteam/launcher-<pid>.pid` that `serve`, `mcp` and the TUI's in-process launcher keep while they
  run (markers of dead processes are removed). Then nothing is deleted (exit 1). All ids are checked first (an
  unknown one or the project's own `main` session: nothing is deleted, exit 1). It shows the sessions and asks
  `[y/N]` in a terminal (Ctrl+C: exit 130); without one it needs `--yes` (exit 1). Before deleting without a hub
  it looks for a hub again. A workspace folder outside the session is kept and named in the output. A session
  whose members' proposals wait for the user's library decision is refused (409, the error plus " Pass --skills
  save (to the skills library first) or --skills discard.", exit 1) unless `--skills save|discard` is given
  (`&skills=` on the hub's DELETE, `delete(sid, skills=, via="cli")` without one). The words
  of `sessions` are `[DIR]` or `rm SID...`, in any order with the options.
- `hub.json` lives in `<home>/.dreamteam/hub.json`, written once the port listens (before the resume) and
  removed at exit (only by the process that wrote it, and never a file of another computer whose hub has the same
  pid). `running_hub(dir)` trusts it only when `GET /api/hub` confirms the pid and the directory. It records
  `"machine": cli.this_machine()` (`platform.node()`; None inside a container, `netoff.in_container()` or
  `DREAMTEAM_IMAGE=1`, whose name is the container's). Before a hub (`serve`, `run`, `mcp` with its web UI) or the
  TUI's launcher writes its own file,
  `_warn_other_machine` reads the one it replaces; when it names another computer (compared without the domain
  part and case: `mbp.lan` = `MBP.local`) it prints once per home and process to stderr (and the log):
  `warning: <home> was last served by the computer <name>. Do not run one DreamTeam folder on two computers at the
  same time; move sessions with dreamteam export / dreamteam import.` It never refuses and never changes
  `running_hub`'s answer. `_session_holders` names a `hub.json` of another computer as `the hub of the computer
  <name> (<path>): stop DreamTeam there, or delete that file if it no longer runs`.
- `export FOLDER` / `import FOLDER` (§20): the positional is `folder`, never the home (`_home_arg` with `dir`
  None: `--home`, else the current directory when it has `dreamteam.toml`, else the default home). Both are commands for
  `_default_command`, so `dreamteam export E:/dt` never becomes a TUI prompt (on 0.1.0 it was `['tui', 'export',
  'E:/dt']`, which exits 2 with `unrecognized arguments`). `--include` values go through `transfer.parse_include`
  before anything else (an unknown word: its message on stderr, exit 2).
  - `export`: refuses a folder that is not a home (`cli.is_home`: SessionManager would create one; exit 1). The
    sessions a hub runs come from its `GET /api/sessions` (status `running`) through `running_hub`; without an
    answering hub, `_session_holders(home, clean=False)` only notes other processes (an export never removes
    launcher markers). Either way the sessions are exported as they are on disk (a snapshot, warned). Then
    `transfer.export_home(...)` and `render_export_report`. Exit 0 when `report.ok`, 1 when something asked for
    was left out or the export failed (`TransferError`, `SecretFound`), 2 for a `TransferError` with `usage`
    (an unknown `--session`), 130 for Ctrl+C (the partial export is removed).
  - `import`: the target is a home, or a missing or empty folder (`_import_target`: it becomes a home only after
    the user says yes; until then it is planned against an empty home in a temporary folder); anything else is
    refused (exit 1). A mistyped `--session` is a usage error (exit 2, `check_session_names`) whatever runs the
    home. `_import_blockers`: a hub that answers (`running_hub`; one that asks for a token no client here sends
    counts too), else `_session_holders(home, clean=not dry_run)`. With a blocker everything but `--dry-run` is
    refused (`Nothing imported: another DreamTeam process may be running the sessions of <home> (...). Stop it,
    then import again (--dry-run shows the plan meanwhile).`, exit 1); a dry run warns and prints the plan. The
    plan (`render_import_plan`) is printed; `--dry-run`, or a plan without changes, exits with
    `plan.exit_code`. Otherwise `[y/N]` (`Import? [y/N] `; `y`, `yes`, `д`, `да`) when `_stdin_is_terminal()`,
    else `--yes` is required (`Nothing imported: pass --yes to import without a confirmation.`, exit 1); another
    answer prints `Nothing imported.` (exit 0); Ctrl+C there exits 130. The blockers are checked again after the
    answer. The import runs in this process (`SessionManager(home)`, `run_loop`) with its own launcher marker
    (`write_launcher_marker`, removed at the end) and a `before_swap` hook that checks the blockers again right
    before each session is renamed in (a process that started meanwhile fails that session). It prints
    `render_import_result` and exits with `result.exit_code` (130 when Ctrl+C stopped it; a second Ctrl+C breaks
    off and says that what was imported stays).
  - Progress (both): `export_home`, `plan_import` and `apply_import` take `progress=`, called with a frozen
    `transfer.Progress` (op export | plan | import; stage sizing, settings, skills, mcp, session, database, files,
    swap, secrets, git, cleaning, replacing, done; item, index/count; done/total bytes and files, totals from a
    stat-only pre-pass for an export and from the manifest for an import, unknown when that pre-pass fails;
    `done_*` never above a total). An export's done comes once it is in place (after a replaced export is removed):
    a KeyboardInterrupt from that event changes nothing; one from any earlier event removes the export. Bytes come
    from
    `treecopy.copy_tree(progress=)` per chunk and file, the sqlite backup in steps (immutable reads only: a live
    database is copied in one step), the import's checked database copy and the secret scan. A KeyboardInterrupt
    the callback raises is a Ctrl+C (in the import's staging thread it is carried out as `_Interrupted`). Each stage
    start is also logged to `dreamteam.transfer` at INFO. The CLI renderer `_ProgressLine` writes to stderr: in a
    terminal one line, `'\r'` plus text padded to the width less one (no ANSI escapes), byte updates at most 8 a
    second, cut and padded in terminal cells, cleared before the plan, the question, warnings (the stderr log
    handler's filter clears it) and the result, and closed for good at the end (a staging thread still running
    after a Ctrl+C draws nothing); else one plain line per stage of each item (`export: session 003-snake (2/5):
    files`). Characters that are not printable show as `?`; stdout is flushed before each write (one log of both
    streams keeps the plan first); a failing or missing stderr only hides it. `--quiet` (`-q`) turns it off.
- `serve`: refuses when a hub already runs for the home (opening that one in the browser unless
  `--no-browser`, whether this process has a hub token or not; a hub that asks for a token no client here may send
  ends it with `TokenRequired`'s text) or when the port is busy, and, right after the check
  for a running hub and before anything is created or started, an address other than loopback without a hub token
  (`run` too; §14.2);
  `--goal` creates and starts a session (its first line becomes the title unless `--title`) and opens its board.
  Only the create races a stop signal (Ctrl+C): `_serve_home` runs `manager.create(..., start=False)` through
  `_until_stopped(coro, stop)` and then `await manager.start(id)` outside the race, as `create(start=True)` would
  (a failed start is still "Could not start the session: ..." and exit 1), so a Ctrl+C never cancels a half-done
  swarm start. A stop during the create (a long copy) cancels it, and `create` undoes it (§17.2); the exit code is
  130 with "Stopped before the session was created: nothing was kept." or, when the cancel came too late (a new id
  appeared), "Stopped: session <id> was created but not started (dreamteam sessions lists it).".
  `_until_stopped` returns `(False, result)` (the coroutine's exception goes on) or `(True, the result it still
  returned despite the cancel, else None)`; when the race itself is cancelled, the coroutine is cancelled and
  awaited too. Then the server starts;
  the terminal console attaches to the running session when stdin is a real terminal (on Windows the NUL device
  is not one). Settings errors and unusable homes are messages, not tracebacks. Right after the `DreamTeam is
  running.` banner (and after `run`'s, §15) stderr gets `settings.unpriced_line(config)` (§17.1) when a model
  profile has no prices.
- `console`: with a launcher hub it works against `{base}/s/{sid}` (`--session`, else the running one); `--url` is
  an address the user typed, so `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN` goes there whatever its host (§14.2); it
  refuses a URL where no hub answers and a stopped session, except a stopped session whose folder outside it
  does not exist (it cannot start, and `/cd` is what fixes it: the console attaches and says so). Commands include `/trace [Name|#id]`,
  `/span N [ctx]` and `/session` (the current session; another one is `dreamteam console --session ID`),
  `/approve N [comment]` and `/reject N what to fix` (a task in review; the comment is free text taken as typed,
  without one pair of quotes around all of it, as in the TUI; a name instead of N approves or rejects
  an MCP server), `/hire Role [| instructions]` (instructions `""` when omitted: a catalog role needs none) and
  `/wrapup [off]` (`swarm_control` wrap_up true / false, §3; the TUI's words: `on`/`вкл` or nothing, `off`/`выкл`).
  `/skills` (the user's `skills` tool) with `lib` (the library, the host library and Claude Code's skills, marked when
  attached; `GET /api/skills`), `add X [--pick a,b] [--replace]` (a reference → `skill_attach name`; a URL or a path,
  resolved as for `/cd`, → `skill_attach source`), `update X` (`skill_attach <from>:X` with replace; a member's
  proposal has no source), `rm X` (`skill_detach`), `show X` (the entry and the first 40 lines of SKILL.md;
  `from=session` when attached), `approve X [replace]` / `reject X [reason]` (`skill_approve`), `reinstall X
  [python|node]` (`skill_reinstall`), `log X [python|node]` (`GET /api/skills/X/deps-log`: the path and the log) and
  `clean-envs` (the launcher's `POST /api/skill-envs/cleanup`; a single-swarm hub has none).
  `/cd` prints the session folder (`GET {hub}/api/sessions/{sid}` → `workspace`); `/cd PATH` or `/cd --default`
  prints the question worded as in the TUI (`console.cd_preview`, docs/TUI.md §4.5) ending in `[y/N]`: the next
  line `y`/`yes`/`д`/`да` moves the session (`POST {hub}/api/sessions/{sid}/workspace`) and prints the result
  (`console.cd_result_lines`), `n`/`нет`/an empty line cancels, any other line cancels and is handled as usual.
  `--yes` (`-y`) at either end skips the question. `~` and relative paths (and a Windows path rooted without a
  drive, `\projects\app`, which gets the current drive as with `--workspace`) are resolved against the console's
  current directory only when the hub runs on this computer (`Console(..., local=)`): the console inside `serve`
  and a hub found through the home's `hub.json` are local whatever their address, a `--url` one when its address
  is a loopback one; otherwise only absolute paths. A single-swarm hub (no `/s/{sid}` in the base URL) has no
  `/cd`.
- `mcp`: a running hub (for a home: the launcher) → a stdio proxy to its `/mcp` that hands on its
  instructions; otherwise a home gets the in-process launcher (SessionManager, the web UI when its port is free,
  resumed sessions) with the stdio launcher MCP, and a project the in-process swarm (§13).
- `traces`: with a hub, the session's REST (§16.3; `--session`, else the running one, else the only session this
  version opens; a picked session made by an earlier version prints its message, exit 1); without one, the
  session database is read directly (default: the most recently active session this version opens, printed on
  stderr; a session that never started prints "No traces." without creating its database; a session or a
  single-swarm project made by an earlier version, §17.2, prints its message (the project one for a project) on
  stderr, exit 1, and its database is not opened: `db.made_by_earlier_version` runs right after `_session_db`
  returns an existing path, before `Database(...)`, so one check covers the home and the project).
- Sessions made by an earlier version (§17.2 "Sessions of an earlier version"): `sessions` and `status` list them
  marked (`session_line`, as in §18.2); `-c` and `-p -c` continue the most recent session (never one created
  through the HTTP API v1, which they pass over as if it were not listed: `instruct.without_api_sessions`, §17.2;
  with only such sessions they say there is no session to continue and that `-r <id>` / `/resume id` opens one),
  and when that one was
  made by an earlier version they never pass over it for an older session the user did not ask for: they say so
  and that a new session is needed, and create nothing (`-p` exits 1 with the print mode's `continue_earlier` on
  stderr, en `The most recent session, {sid}, was made by an earlier version of DreamTeam and cannot be opened by
  this one ({version}). Start a new session: run without -c.`, ru «Последняя сессия, {sid}, создана более ранней
  версией DreamTeam, и эта версия ({version}) не может её открыть. Начните новую сессию: запустите без -c.»; the
  TUI says its `continue_earlier` under the welcome box, en `The most recent session, {id}, was made by an earlier
  version of DreamTeam and cannot be opened by this one ({version}): start a new session`, ru «Последняя сессия,
  {id}, создана более ранней версией DreamTeam, и эта версия ({version}) не может её открыть: начните новую
  сессию», and attaches nothing; a prompt given with `-c`, or with `-r ID` of a session that did not open, is
  never sent (nor when the hub or its session list failed): it is left in the input line, to send on purpose; `{version}` is the hub's); a default picked without the user asking for the last
  session (`console` and `traces` without `--session`) still skips sessions made by an earlier version, and those
  created through the HTTP API v1 too (which the `-r` picker and `/sessions` mark `HTTP API` after the status,
  uitext `sess_api`, as `session_line`'s ` | HTTP API`); `-r ID` of
  one prints its message (the TUI says it under the welcome box and creates nothing; `-p` exits 1); the `-r`
  picker and `/sessions` show them with the status «прежняя версия» / "earlier version", Enter shows the message
  instead of attaching (the picker closes and the message is printed; `/resume ID` the same; the legacy `main`'s Del
  and `/delete` show its message too), Del deletes as usual; `console --session ID` refuses one with the message (exit 1, before
  its stopped check; without `--session` it picks, like `traces`, only among the sessions this version opens);
  `sessions rm` deletes them as any session (the legacy `main` stays undeletable there too, and its message names
  the file to remove by hand).
- `status` of a home lists the sessions (from the hub, or read from the home), then `Home:` and `Hub:`, and `API:
  <hub>/api/v1` when the running hub's `/api/hub` says `api` (it has an API token, §21.1; the line `serve` prints,
  never the token); of a project, `swarm_status`. `sessions` prints the same list without the `API:` line.
- `console` prints the session it opens as `Session <id>: <title>`, the title as one printable line
  (`copyfrom.printable_line`: one made on the board or over MCP, or a remote hub's, may hold control characters).
- `sandbox` refuses when a hub runs for the directory; the container runs `serve /swarm` for a home and
  `run /swarm` for a project, on `--host 0.0.0.0` with a hub token of its own (§14.2: printed with the board URL and
  the MCP command, kept on the host outside the mounted folders for the host's `dreamteam` commands; the container gets only its SHA-256). `docker.sandbox_command` starts it with `docker run --rm --init ...`: a tiny init
  (tini) is PID 1, reaps the orphans of agents' commands (dreamteam never does, and a zombie would keep a job's
  process group alive) and forwards `docker stop`'s SIGTERM to dreamteam, whose `Swarm.stop` ends the jobs within
  Docker's 10 s grace (a launcher home unloads its sessions one after another, so with jobs in several sessions the
  last final commits may be cut off; the processes die with the container anyway). Ports that agents' dev servers
  open inside the container are not published. `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`: no program in the
  container gains privileges through a set-user-ID bit or file capabilities (the firewall's `NET_ADMIN` is given at
  the start, `setpriv` only drops). Only the directory is mounted (and for a home the roots of its `[api] folders`,
  §21.10 "Sandbox"): for a home, `docker.outside_home_warning(home, mounts)` prints a warning listing the sessions
  whose workspace folder is outside it (`external_workspaces`), but for those under a writable mounted root's mount
  point:
  they cannot start in the container (their start reports the missing folder). A folder
  inside the home is found in the container (session.json `in_home`, §17.2). The hub there refuses a new folder for a
  session outside what is mounted (`_container_refusal`, §17.2 "Workspace folder"), and the web UI's folder browser
  offers only the mounted folders (§17.2 "Choosing a folder from the web UI"). The host's skills library is mounted
  read-only at `/dreamteam/host-skills` with `DREAMTEAM_HOST_SKILLS_DIR` pointing there and `DREAMTEAM_SKILLS_DIR=
  /swarm/.dreamteam/skills-library` (the sandbox's own library inside the mounted home; not `.dreamteam/skills`,
  the default library's name: a home that is the user's home folder would make the host's library writable);
  `env_passthrough` never passes the two skills variables by name; `run_sandbox` creates the host folder first and
  warns when the library is inside the mounted directory (`library_inside_warning`: writable through `/swarm`
  then), `sandbox_command` stays a pure argv builder; `~/.claude/skills` is not mounted (§19). The skills'
  environments are a named volume per home, `dreamteam-skill-envs-<sha256 of the home's path, 10 hex>` mounted at
  `/dreamteam/skill-envs` (`docker.envs_volume`; `DREAMTEAM_SKILL_ENVS_DIR` and `UV_CACHE_DIR=/dreamteam/skill-envs/
  .cache/uv` set; never the host's envs: another platform); `docker volume rm` resets it. Node is not in the image,
  so Node skills show as unavailable there. The image also has `iptables` and the user `dreamteam-agent` for the
  sessions without network and git's identity as `--system` settings, and `build_image` labels it
  `dreamteam.dockerfile=<dockerfile_hash()>`; the firewall (`--cap-add NET_ADMIN`, dropped again at once,
  `netoff.sandbox_entry`) and the rebuild of an image with another label: §7.2. The image has no `safe.directory`:
  git's ownership check stays on there, and a manual `docker exec ... git` in a folder of the host's uid (a Linux
  bind mount) needs `-c safe.directory=<path>`. The processes DreamTeam starts for a session (`JobManager.run`: the
  members' commands and their jobs; `MCPForge._new_connection`: the stdio MCP servers and their smoke test) get
  `netoff.trust_workspace(env, root)`: in the image only (`netoff.in_container()`, or `DREAMTEAM_IMAGE=1`, which
  the image sets for a runtime that leaves no marker file; the host's git stays as the user has it),
  `safe.directory=<root>` and `<root>/*` (the repositories nested in it; git 2.46+, hence the image's base
  `python:3.13-slim-trixie`: git 2.47), and for a workspace without a `.git` of its own (git off, adopted inside a
  repository) the work tree git finds from it, its first ancestor with a `.git`, exactly (no `/*`), appended as
  `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` pairs after those already there (`netoff.git_config`, which
  `netoff.environment` uses too: the two compose in either order under one `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`). DreamTeam's own
  git keeps its per-command `-c safe.directory` (§7). git refuses only a repository of another uid: with network
  on the commands run as root, who owns every session folder DreamTeam creates, so the check does not separate the
  sessions. The image installs the versions of `uv.lock`
  (`uv export --locked --no-dev`, hashes required, into the system Python; uv itself at a fixed version):
  `build_context` copies it next to the repository's pyproject.toml, the generated one goes without it (the
  Dockerfile copies `uv.lock*`, an installed package's image gets the ranges), and `.dockerignore` lets it into the
  compose context.
- `run [DIR]` stays the single-swarm server of a project (§15); it does not serve the launcher.

### 18.4 UI
- **Look** (the tokens of style.css, shared by both pages): one quiet surface per theme (light and dark; the system
  preference unless the theme button chose), hairline borders, one accent — the TUI's orange `#d97757` (filled
  controls carry dark text on it). Monospace (`--mono`) is for what is read as data: ids, numbers, times, costs,
  badges, column and section labels; the rest is the sans font. Status colours: in progress blue, waiting amber,
  review violet, done green, failed red; «working» (an agent, a running session) is the accent. Icons are line
  icons of `icons.css` (`<i class="ic ic-NAME">`, a CSS mask in the colour of the text), not emoji. A member's
  colour is the one of the TUI (tui/theme.py `agent_color`: the palette, crc32 of the case-folded name; app.js
  `agentColor`), so an agent looks the same in the terminal and in the browser; its avatar is a rounded square
  tinted with it. The agent's activity in the chat drawer follows the TUI too: a coloured bullet per step, a tool
  result hangs under its call (⎿).
- **Skills on both pages** (§19): `skills.js` (loaded before home.js and app.js; `Skills`, also a Node module for
  the tests) holds what they share: the add form (sources «Папка» — a folder or .zip path on the server's computer —,
  «Zip» — a file read in the browser and sent as base64, refused over `max_archive_mb` before the upload — and
  «Git» — a URL, `#ref:subdir` or a GitHub / GitLab tree link) with its flow (`runImport`: a source holding several
  skills lists them as checkboxes and posts again with `pick`; a clash with the library, 409 `exists`, asks «Заменить?»
  and posts again with `replace`; Enter in a field imports and never submits an enclosing form, such as the
  new-session dialog's), the report line of an import (imported, attached, failed, skipped files) and the
  packages preview (`previewLine`: «Установится автоматически: pypdf, … (requirements.txt).» plus the trust line
  «Установка запускает собственный код пакетов с вашими правами (вне песочницы Docker).», an unsupported manifest's
  reason, or «Установка пакетов выключена в настройках.»; `install.proposals` decides for a member's proposal
  and a `claude-project` skill). A skill's SKILL.md is shown as Markdown on the session page (`md()`, its YAML front
  matter left out: `bodyOf`; the card shows the name and description) and escaped as preformatted text on the home
  page (it has no Markdown renderer); every other skill text is escaped. The icon is `ic-skill` (a book).
- **Folders on both pages** (§17.2 "Choosing a folder from the web UI"): `folders.js` (loaded before home.js and
  app.js, after skills.js; `Folders`, also a Node module for the tests) holds the folder field's check line, the
  folder browser and the «Сменить папку…» dialog. Each page passes its `t`, `esc`, request function (the board its
  `launcherApi`: the routes are the launcher's, at the root, never `/s/{sid}/...`; a failure carries its HTTP
  `status`), `toast` and modal functions (`Folders.setup`, at the page script's load); the texts (`fo_*`, `fp_*`,
  `cf_*`, `cd_*`) live in both pages' dictionaries, ru and en.
  - **Check line** (`Folders.checker(input, line, {use, session, isDefault, old, onChange})` → `{run(now), ready(),
    result}`; `old()` the session's current folder, the `{old}` of the `cd_text_*` texts; `onChange(result)` after
    every change of what the line shows or of `ready()`, as the change dialog's button and the new-session dialog's
    project skills follow it): every
    `input` or `change` of the field restarts a 400 ms timer (`CHECK_DELAY`; a paste is an `input`; a `change` of a
    value whose answer is shown, as when the field is left for the dialog's button, keeps it, but not a check that
    could not run: that one is tried again); a choice in the browser and `run(true)` check at once. A field no
    longer in the page (its dialog closed) sends nothing more, and a late answer for it changes nothing. The value
    sent is `Folders.unquote(field.value)`: trimmed, with one pair
    of matching quotes dropped (the twin of `console.unquote`: Explorer's "Copy as path" adds them); an empty value
    sends nothing and empties the line. Each request carries a number (`seq`): an answer whose number is not the
    latest, or whose `path` (the value sent) is no longer `Folders.unquote(field.value)`, is dropped, so a slow
    answer for an earlier value never shows over a newer one (the request itself is not aborted: the hub's slots
    bound them). «Проверяю папку…» / "Checking the folder…" (`fo_checking`) shows only after 300 ms (no flicker for
    a quick answer). `ready()` is true only while the shown result is the answer for the current
    `Folders.unquote(field.value)`: false while the 400 ms timer runs and while a request is out, so a path typed and
    submitted at once never goes with the `expect` of an earlier value. The line is `role="status"` with
    `aria-live="polite"`; the field gets `aria-describedby` to it and `aria-invalid="true"` while it shows an error.
  - **Words of the line** (class `ok`; `warn` for an adopt, for a move of a running session and for `api_folder`;
    `err` for an error): an `error` verbatim (English, as every hub error), status 504 included, and so the text of
    another 4xx of the call itself (a bad body, an unknown session: an error, it blocks as one); a request that failed
    (no connection, 429, 5xx) `fo_check_failed` «Не удалось проверить папку: {error}. Хаб проверит ее при создании
    или переносе.» / "Could not check the folder: {error}. The hub checks it when the session is created or
    moved." ({error} without its own final full stop). `use` "source": `fo_src_folder` «Папка найдена: ее файлы
    скопируются в папку новой сессии.» / "Folder found: its files are copied into the new session's folder." or
    `fo_src_zip` «Архив .zip найден: его содержимое скопируется в папку новой сессии.» / "A .zip found: its contents
    are copied into the new session's folder.". `use`
    "workspace" for a new session: `fo_new_missing` «Папки нет: она будет создана, и сессия начнет в ней с чистого
    листа.» / "The folder does not exist: it will be created, and the session starts there afresh."; `fo_new_empty`
    «Папка пустая: сессия начнет в ней с чистого листа.» / "The folder is empty: the session starts there afresh.";
    with files `fo_new_files` «Папка с файлами: агенты будут работать с ними и коммитить в текущую ветку
