  `too_many_files`, `skip_files`, `exclude_names` (casefolded path parts left out and listed), `links` ("refuse" |
  "skip"), `exclude_paths` (exact '/' paths after the unwrap, left out and listed), `exclude_top` (casefolded names
  left out at the top level after the unwrap, listed like `exclude_paths`), `portable` (the Windows name
  rules), `fold_collisions` (False: exact names), `names_in` (the `_portable` message), `folders` (create folder
  entries), `unwrap` (one top folder with no excluded or link member beside it: its contents), `redecode_names`
  (names without the UTF-8 flag read again, once per archive, as UTF-8 or in the Windows OEM code page, the OEM
  one first when every such member was made on MS-DOS / Windows by `create_system`; a folder then by the name's own
  last character),
  `max_ratio`
  (None: no ratio bound) and `declared_first` (True: the declared sizes of all members are checked before planning,
  as for skills; False: of the planned files after it); the skills' defaults keep the order and texts above. A
  path is opened once and streamed (a 1 GB zip is not read into memory). Before `zipfile` parses the central
  directory, a pre-check (`_zip_directory`) reads the entry count and the directory size from the
  end-of-central-directory records, searched for in zipfile's window (the last 64 KiB + 22 bytes, whatever the
  comment length says): the largest of the plain record's values, a marker left out, and those of a ZIP64 record
  whose locator precedes it, at the locator's offset or just before it (zipfile uses those whatever the plain record
  says); with no ZIP64 record the plain values count as stated, a 0xFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF marker included (zipfile
  never uses the count and reads the plain directory size). More than `max_entries` is the 413 of
  `too_many_entries`; a directory over `max_entries * 512` bytes (zipfile reads and parses all of it, whatever
  count the record states) is a 413 of its own, "The zip's directory (its list of entries) is larger than N MB: its
  names, comments or extra fields are too long." (for skills 2.4 MB: a zip with long per-entry comments or extra
  fields can be refused here). A file without a plain end record leaves it to `zipfile`, which
  refuses it. `check()` runs before each member is written and after each chunk.
- Git (`parse_git_source(text) -> GitSource(url, ref, subdir, shown, scheme)`, pure): `https://`, `ssh://`,
  scp-like `user@host:path` and `file://`; plain `http://`, `transport::` remote helpers, a leading `-`, spaces, a
  user or host starting with `-` and invalid hosts are refused. `URL#ref:subdir`, `URL#ref`, `URL#:subdir`; GitHub
  `/tree/<ref>/<sub>` and `/blob/<ref>/<sub>/SKILL.md` and GitLab `/-/tree/` / `/-/blob/` become the repository URL,
  the ref and the folder (a ref with `/` in a tree URL cannot be told from the path: `URL#ref:path`). Refs match
  `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*`, ≤ 200 characters, without `..`, `@{`, `//` or a trailing `/`, `.` or `.lock`;
  folders are plain relative POSIX paths (no `\`, `:`, `..`, `.` or empty parts) and are checked again after the
  checkout (inside the clone, no link on the way). **Credentials**: `shown` has no user info (except the bare user of
  ssh / scp URLs), no query and no fragment; it is the only form stored (`source.url`), shown, logged or put into an
  error; `redact(text, src)` removes the full URL, the user info (git prints it without the scheme too) and any
  `//user:secret@` from git's output. A credential helper is recommended over a token in the URL.
- `clone(src, dest, limits, git=None, timeout=120)` (a dedicated helper, not `run_git`): no git → 400 "git is not
  installed: …"; `-c` options before the subcommand: `credential.interactive=never`, `core.symlinks=false`,
  `core.longpaths=true`, `protocol.allow=never` with `https` and `ssh` allowed (`file` only for a `file://` URL: a
  user `url.<base>.insteadOf` can never reach a remote helper), `core.hooksPath=<staging>/nohooks` (an empty folder:
  no global or system hook runs), `core.fsmonitor=` (no daemon for the staging folder), `submodule.recurse=false`,
  `fetch.recurseSubmodules=false`. With git ≥ 2.35:
  `clone --depth 1 --single-branch --no-tags --filter=blob:none --no-checkout [--branch=<ref>] -- URL DEST`, then
  `sparse-checkout set --no-cone -- /<subdir>/` (or `/*`) and `checkout` (only the folder's blobs are fetched; a
  server without filter support falls back to a full shallow clone); older git: a plain shallow clone. The
  environment (`clone_env`): `git_env()`, `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1`, the user's
  `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` / `GIT_SSH` / `GIT_SSH_VARIANT` put back, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` when the
  user has neither those nor a `core.sshCommand` (a host-key question or a passphrase fails at once). stdin is
  closed, and on POSIX git runs in a new session (no controlling tty for ssh to read). A watchdog sums the staging
  folder every half second and kills git (`shell.kill_tree`) past `max_archive_mb` (413 "point the URL at the
  skill's folder") or the timeout. The user's git configuration is only read, nothing is ever written. Errors give
  the first `fatal:` line, redacted: "Could not clone <shown>: …". `rev-parse HEAD` gives `commit`. Origin `git`,
  `source = {url: shown, ref, subdir, commit}`.
- Claude Code (`claude_skills(config, workspace=None) -> [item]`, `[]` when `[skills] claude` is false): one level
  of folders in each Claude Code skills folder (links skipped); an item is `{name, description, origin, path, files,
  size, digest, manual, renamed_from?, library: "absent"|"same"|"different", agent_writable? (claude-project),
  error?}`; names and descriptions are normalised with `strict=False`, so existing Claude Code skills are attachable.
  "Add to library" is `{"claude": name, "origin": …}` (origin `claude-user` / `claude-project`, `source = {path}`).
  SKILL.md files written for Claude Code may name its tools or `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`: they are copied unchanged.
- Requests (`import_request(config, body, workspace=None, *, by, via)`): exactly one of `path`, `zip`, `git`,
  `claude` (or `host`), else 400 "Give exactly one of path, zip, git, claude."; `pick` a list of strings, `replace`
  a bool; a `workspace` for `claude-project` must be absolute. `read_import_body(request, config)` reads a JSON
  body capped by `body_limit(config)` (the base64 of `max_archive_mb` plus 64 KB; 413 from Content-Length or while
  streaming, 415 when not JSON). `SkillError(message, status, **extra)` maps to the HTTP status; `to_json()` is
  `{"error", **extra}`.
- Previews (what the user sees before attaching): `show_folder(folder, limits) -> {files_list, skill_md, deps}`
  (`deps: {}` and `error` when it cannot be read); `deps_preview(folder) -> {"python"?: {files, packages,
  unsupported?}, "node"?: {files, packages, lock, unsupported?, ignored?}}` (`skill_deps.detect`: files read, no tool
  probed, nothing started; `{}` without manifests or when they cannot be read); `install_info(config) -> {enabled,
  proposals, scripts}` (`[skills] install`, `install_proposals`, `install_scripts`), which the skills routes add as
  `install` so a preview can say whether the packages would be installed.

**The session's skills** (swarm_skills.py; `Swarm.skills: SessionSkills`). A skill attached to a session is
visible to all its members. No database table: the authoritative copies are `<data_dir>/attached-skills/<name>/`
(`skills_dir`; not `skills/`, since for a project in the home folder the data dir is `~/.dreamteam`, whose `skills/`
is the default library; outside every workspace, so never committed; they survive `/cd` moves and are deleted with
the session), each with the session's `.dreamteam.json` = `{name, description, digest, files, size, from: library | claude-user | claude-project
| host-library | agent, source (the library entry's source plus its "origin", or {path}), attached_by,
attached_at, updated_at, owner (from = agent), attached_via: user | role:<Role> | create | proposal, manual,
library: none | pending | saved | rejected, comment, decided_while_stopped}`. `read_session_skills(data_dir, library_dir=None)`
lists them without a Swarm (a stopped session); a folder without valid metadata is left out. `library_clash(data_dir,
library_dir)`: the session's folder is the library, or inside it or contains it (a `library_dir` set to it); then
nothing is read from it, `load()` cleans nothing there, and attach and detach are 409.
- `SessionSkills`: `load()` (in `Swarm.__init__` and `start()`; `.t-*` / `.o-*` leftovers cleaned), `list()`,
  `get(name)`, `names()`, `pending()`, `public()` (the snapshot's `skills`, §14.1, from memory), `shown_path(name) ->
  (text, inside)`, `agent_dir()` (`DREAMTEAM_SKILLS` of the agents' shells), `role_skills(member)` (the names its
  catalog role lists, resolved live), `source_digest(skill)` (its own source's digest now: the library entry for
  `library`, the folder at `source.path` for Claude Code, the host library; None when gone or for `agent`),
  `detached()`, `proposed()`, `hire_report(name)`.
- `async attach(actor, ref, *, replace=False, announce=True, attached_via="user", via="act", exclude=()) -> (SessionSkill,
  "attached" | "updated" | "unchanged")`: only USER (ToolError "Only the user can attach skills to the swarm.");
  the reference is resolved with `resolve_ref` against the session's workspace (`claude-project` only when named);
  under the lock: the same name with the same digest is "unchanged", other content is ToolError 409 unless
  `replace`, a new name past `[skills] max_attached` is 409; `copy_skill` into `<data_dir>/attached-skills/` with the
  metadata, then its script dependencies planned in a daemon thread and held in use ("Script dependencies" below),
  the mirror sync, `skill.attached`, the name leaves kv `skills_detached`, (`announce`) `n_skill_added` /
  `n_skill_updated` to the members but `exclude`, and last `ensure_deps([name])`, which only starts the builds.
- `async attach_source(actor, source, *, pick=None, replace=False, via="act") -> ImportReport + {"attached": [{name,
  status, files}], "failed": [{name, error, status}]}`: a folder or .zip path on the hub's machine, or a Git URL
  (`source_spec`: `scheme://` or `user@host:path` is Git), imported into the library (`import_source`, `by` user),
  then each imported skill attached as `library:<name>`; one attach refused (the cap, a clash) leaves the others
  attached and is listed in `failed` (it stays in the library); `skill_attach` reports both and is an error only
  when nothing was attached. With `need_pick` nothing changes.
- `async detach(actor, name, *, via="act") -> SessionSkill`: only USER; 404 when not attached; the session copy is
  renamed away and removed, its environments leave the session's in-use set (they stay for other sessions and
  cleanup), the mirror synced, `skill.detached`, the name added to kv `skills_detached` (a role never attaches it
  again until the user does), `n_skill_removed` to the members.
- Errors are ToolErrors carrying `status` (and `extra`, e.g. `exists`) for REST callers (`skill_error`).
- `attach_files(data_dir, folder, name, frm, source, limits, *, info=None, attached_via="create", library_dir=None)
  -> (SessionSkill, "attached" | "unchanged")` (module function, no Swarm): a checked folder copied into a session
  being created or a stopped one about to start (`SessionManager`, §17.2); the same digest is "unchanged", other
  content 409 (`exists`), a `library_clash` 409; the caller checks `max_attached`. `attached_again(names)` takes such
  names out of kv `skills_detached` once the Swarm runs.

**The mirror** `<workspace>/.scratch/_skills/<name>/` (`workspace.SKILLS_MIRROR`) is what agents read: `read_file`
cannot leave the workspace, and a link would be refused, so it is a real copy (`copy_skill(..., readonly=True)`:
files 0o444 / 0o555, the read-only attribute on Windows; no `.dreamteam.json`). Its expected state lives only in
memory (`_mirror`: name -> (session copy digest, the mirror copy's listing as it was written, from copy_skill's
manifest)); nothing in the mirror is trusted. A sync (in a thread, under the skills lock and a files lock that the
removal at stop shares) runs `ensure_scratch()`; when `scratch_is_local(root)` it rebuilds a copy when asked for a
full sync, when it is missing or a link, when the session copy's digest changed, or when `_listing` of it differs
(every entry with its kind, size and mtime: unlike the skill walk, the skip-list's names such as `node_modules/` or
`.git` and links count too, and the walk stops past the expected number of entries) (each rebuild is copy_skill's
build-and-swap, so a reader never sees half a skill), and removes everything else there (detached skills, folders a
command put there). A removal Windows refuses (a process holding a file there or using
it as its working directory) does not fail the caller: the name goes into `_pending_removal`, is left out of the
index and retried by every later sync. Syncs: full at every `Swarm.start`, on every attach and detach, and from the
scheduler at most every `SKILLS_CHECK_SECONDS` (60 s), so a tampered mirror is repaired within a minute and at every
start. `write_file` / `edit_file` refuse the mirror (§7). The listing leaves out the places of DreamTeam's own
`node_modules` links, which are checked by themselves ("Script dependencies"). Without a local `.scratch` there is
no mirror and agents are shown the session copy's absolute path with `skills_path_outside` ("read it with `shell`");
the Node link then goes into the session copy. In an adopted folder
`Swarm.stop` removes `.scratch/_skills` after the agents stopped; a session's own folder keeps it (it is rebuilt at
start anyway).

**Delivery to agents.** The system prompt is frozen at hire and the tool array until a compaction, so running agents
learn through texts: new members' system prompts have a generic **Skills** bullet (no concrete names) and item 1 of
"How you work" says the wake-up shows the skills. The **Skills index** (§6.3): `skills_index` (with
`skills_index_own` when the member's role lists an attached skill) followed by one `skills_item` line per skill
(`- name{own}: description → path{deps}`): the member's role skills first, then the rest, by name; `own` is `skills_own`
(" (your role's)") for its role's skills plus `skills_manual` for a `disable-model-invocation` skill; the description
is cut to 300 characters and `<` / `>` become ‹ ›; the path is `shown_path`; `deps` is the dependency fragment
(`deps_fragment`, "Script dependencies"), "" for a skill without manifests. The header tells how to use a skill
written for Claude Code (its tool names mapped to `shell`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`;
`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` = the folder shown) and what a line's packages part means (a named Python runs that skill's
scripts, install nothing into it; linked Node packages are found, run no npm install or npm ci in the skill's
folder; a line without one lists none: install what SKILL.md asks for with `shell`, best in the scratch folder). It
is shown in full once per agent memory (`Swarm._skills_shown`), then
as `skills_names` (`names_line`); `AgentRuntime._replace_with_summary` puts the full index into the compaction text
(after the notes) and sets `skills_shown(name, True)`, or None when there is none. Notifications
(`SessionSkills._announce(key, exclude, *, name, description=None, owner=None)`: every non-retired member but
`exclude`, AI agents with `wake=False`, external members with a wake so `wait_for_events` returns; `path` and
`deps` per recipient): `n_skill_added` {name, description, path, deps} on an attach, `n_skill_updated` on a replace,
`n_skill_removed` {name} on a detach, `n_skill_deps_ready` / `n_skill_deps_failed` {name, deps} when a build this
session waited for ends. External members have no wake-up index: `join_swarm` lists the attached skills
(also on a rejoin, "Welcome back"; it adds that `skill_propose` proposes one) and `swarm_status` gives "Skills: N attached (a, b)" (with the item lines for a
member, not with `brief`; "; packages being installed for 1 (pdf)" / "; packages failed for 1 (pdf)" when that
applies); `agents` ends with
"Skills attached to the swarm: a, b (the wake-up lists them; read their SKILL.md with read_file)." The user's tools:
`skills` (the attached list with source, who, description, path and "source changed" / "source gone" against
`source_digest`, and a `packages: python ready; node manual (...)` line; `available=true` adds the library's, the
host library's and Claude Code's skills not attached), `skill_attach` (name or source; its result ends with " Its
packages (requirements.txt) are being installed; members are told when they are ready." or " Its packages are
installed already."), `skill_detach`, `skill_reinstall` (§12).

**Proposals** (`skill_propose(path)`, audience llm and external, so every AI agent and external member has it; the
system prompt's Skills bullet ends with the proposing sentence (a member hired by a build from before `skill_propose`
and never started keeps the system prompt it was hired with, which lacks that sentence, §6.1)).
`SessionSkills.propose(actor, path)`: not the user ("Members propose skills; the user attaches them with
skill_attach."); `[skills] max_proposals = 0` → "Proposing skills is turned off in this swarm's settings."; the path
goes through `Workspace.resolve` (inside the workspace, never `.git`), a `SKILL.md` file means its folder, and a
folder under `.scratch/_skills/` is refused ("That is the swarm's copy of an attached skill. Copy the folder
(without node_modules) into your scratch folder, edit it there, and propose that copy."); `check_skill_dir(strict=True)`
(the name as written,
no tag-like description), its error followed by " Fix SKILL.md and call skill_propose again.". Names (ToolError 409,
with a suggested free name: `<name>-<the proposer's first name, slugged>`, then `<name>-2`, ...): a name attached by
the user, a role or another member → "A skill named 'x' is already attached; choose another name, e.g. 'x-ann'.";
a name the library or the host library has, or a catalog role lists, unless it is the proposer's own attached
proposal → "The skills library already has a skill named 'x' (or a role lists it); choose another name, e.g.
'x-ann'." (a later role attach would take the draft for the role's skill, and the approval would clash). Count: kv
`skills_proposed` holds every name members proposed in the session (detached ones too); a new name past
`max_proposals` is 409; proposing one's own name again replaces it and counts once; a new name past `max_attached`
is 409. The same content as the attached copy changes nothing ("Your skill "x" is unchanged ...") while the
session copy still holds it (else it is copied again, as a replacement). Otherwise, under
the lock, `copy_skill(strict=True)` into the session folder with `from = agent`, `owner = attached_by = actor`,
`attached_via = proposal`, `library = pending`, `source = {path: workspace-relative}`; then its dependencies planned
(trust class `agent`), the mirror sync, and after
it, also when that await is cancelled (as `mcp_create`, no silent proposal): `skill.proposed`, `n_skill_shared`
{owner, name, description, path} to every other member (`n_skill_updated` for a replacement), `u_skill_proposed`
{owner, name, description without its final period, files, installs: `u_skill_installs` when its packages are
installed automatically, else ""} to the user; then `ensure_deps([name])`. The result: `Skill "x" is attached to the swarm (4 files, 12 KB) and every member sees it at
.scratch/_skills/x/SKILL.md. The user was asked whether to save it to the skills library; you are told the answer.
Edit it by proposing the same name again.` (a replacement: `Your skill "x" was replaced by the new version ...; ...
The user was asked again ...`), plus the links left out, plus " Its packages (requirements.txt) are being
installed; you are told when they are ready." (an AI member, whom the quiet news does not wake: "...; a later
wake-up of yours says when they are ready (the install does not wake you).") or " Its requirements.txt is not
installed automatically: <reason>.".

**The user's decision** (`skill_approve {name, approve, comment?, replace?}`, user only; `SessionSkills.decide(actor,
name, approve, *, comment="", replace=False, via="act") -> str`): only USER; `check_name`; the skill must be
attached (404) and `library == "pending"` (409 "Skill 'x' is not waiting for a library decision (status:
saved)."). The file part is `decide_files(data_dir, library, name, approve, *, comment="", replace=False,
via="stopped-session", project="", session=None, stopped=True) -> (SessionSkill, text)`, a plain function over a data
dir, so a stopped session's proposal can be decided without a Swarm.
approve: the session copy is checked again and must still have the digest recorded at the proposal (an agent's
shell can write into the session folder): else 409 "Skill 'x' changed since it was proposed, so it is not saved.
Detach it, or ask its owner to propose it again." and nothing changes; then `Library.add(<session copy>, "agent",
source={owner, project, session, swarm}, replace, by="user", via, info=<that check>)` (copy_skill refuses bytes that
differ from it);
another skill of that name in the library is 409 "The library already has a different skill 'x'. Approve with
replace to overwrite it, or reject." (`exists`); the result `Skill "x" saved to the skills library.`. A "no" keeps
it attached to this session only: `Skill "x" will not be saved to the library; it stays attached to this swarm
(detach it to remove it).`. The session metadata gets `library` saved / rejected, `comment` (whitespace collapsed,
at most 2000 characters) and `decided_while_stopped` (`stopped`). A running swarm then emits `skill.library` and
tells the owner (`n_skill_saved` {name} / `n_skill_not_saved` {name, comment: " <comment>" or ""}, a wake) unless it is the user or
has left; a decision on a stopped session's files is told quietly by the next `SessionSkills.start`, once (the
flag is cleared). There is no switch to skip the decision: saving to the library always takes the user's yes. A
proposal the user detaches is discarded.

**Role skills.** A `[[roles]]` entry may list `skills` (§17.3). `SessionSkills.ensure_role_skills(names=None, *,
announce=True) -> {"attached": [names], "missing": {role: [names]}, "detached": {role: [names]}, "over_cap": {role:
[names]}}` takes the given members (default: all), each role once: names already attached are skipped, names in kv
`skills_detached` go to `detached` (the user's detach stands), a name past `max_attached` to `over_cap`, the rest
are attached as bare names (the library, `claude-user`, the host library; never the workspace's
`.claude/skills`) with actor USER, `attached_via = "role:<canonical role name>"`, `via = "role"`, the given members
not told; a name nothing has goes to `missing`. The user is told once per (role, names) in memory:
`u_role_skills_missing` {role, names}, `u_role_skills_over_cap` {role, names, max}. It never raises (a hire or a
start goes on; failures are logged). Callers: `Swarm.hire` (the new member), `Swarm.start` (everybody,
`announce=False`) and `Swarm.reconfigure` (the background task, §3). `hire_agent` appends ` They also got the skills
of their role: a, b.` (the role's skills attached now), ` Not found in the skills library (the user was told): c.`,
` Detached by the user, so not attached: d.` and ` Not attached, the swarm has the maximum of 40 skills: e.`;
`agents` shows a role's skills in its catalog line (`- Tester (model x; skills: a, b): …`). Marks are resolved live
(`role_skills`): skills a role brought stay attached when the role stops listing them, without the "your role's"
mark, until the user detaches them; the snapshot's `roles` lists the catalog roles that list a skill.

**Docker sandbox** (§18.3): the hub runs in the agents' container and agents have `shell`, so the host library is
mounted read-only at `/dreamteam/host-skills` (`DREAMTEAM_HOST_SKILLS_DIR`; `host_skills(config)` lists it as the
read-only source `host-library`, attachable, never written), and the sandbox's own writable library is
`/swarm/.dreamteam/skills-library` (`DREAMTEAM_SKILLS_DIR`), i.e. `<home>/.dreamteam/skills-library` on the host,
which the host never reads by itself (import that folder on the host to keep a sandbox skill). It is not
`.dreamteam/skills`, the default library's name: for a home that is the user's home folder that would be the host's
own library, writable from the container. A host library inside the mounted directory would be writable through `/swarm`, so
`run_sandbox` warns about it. `~/.claude/skills` is not mounted (it
would expose all of the user's personal skills); add a Claude Code skill to the host library first. In the sandbox,
folder paths are container paths: the zip upload is the portable source. The pages say both when the listing's
`sandbox` is true: the add form's folder field gets a hint (`sk_folder_sandbox`; skills.js `setSandbox` shows it in
a form mounted before the listing came) and the home Skills tab's Claude Code section says to add such a skill to
the library of a DreamTeam run on the host (`sk_claude_sandbox`). (The MCP library is not mounted into the
sandbox at all; it stays container-local.) The sandbox's skill environments are a named volume per home (§18.3).

**Script dependencies** (skill_deps.py). A skill's `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` (Python) or `package.json`
(Node) is installed automatically into an environment of its own, one per skill and dependency set, shared by every
session that attaches the same skill with the same manifests; without one, agents install what SKILL.md asks for
themselves (the index header says so). SKILL.md prose is never parsed.
- **Detection** (`detect(folder) -> Detected(python: PyManifest | None, node: NodeManifest | None)`, pure). Fixed
  places: `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `scripts/requirements.txt`, `scripts/pyproject.toml` (every one found
  goes into one venv, in that order: `-r` each, a pyproject as a generated `pyproject-deps-<n>.txt` of its
  `[project].dependencies`), `package.json` then `scripts/package.json` (the first one; the other and a lone
  `yarn.lock` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` are `ignored`) with `npm-shrinkwrap.json` or `package-lock.json` beside it. A
  manifest is a regular file (never a link), at most 256 KiB (a lock 8 MiB), UTF-8; an empty dependency list means
  none. A skill's own `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv` never reach the session copy (skip list). Requirement lines
  (`parse_requirements`: continuations joined, comments dropped; `-r` / `-c` includes inside the skill, at most 5
  deep, their bytes in the key): requirements with extras, specifiers and markers, `name @ https://…` and
  `git+https://`, `--hash`, `--pre`, `--prefer-binary`, `--only-binary`, `--require-hashes` are kept; refused, so
  the agent installs by hand (`unsupported`, a text naming the file, the line and the rule, without parentheses):
  `-e`, local paths, `file:`, every index option (`-i`, `--extra-index-url`, `-f`, `--trusted-host`, `--no-index`: a
  skill never chooses the index), any other option, `${…}`, `http://`, credentials in a URL, more than 1000 lines.
  Hashes are all or nothing: when one line or file uses them, every requirement must be pinned with `==` and hashed,
  and no pyproject may take part. `parse_pyproject` reads only `[project].dependencies` and `requires-python`
  (`dynamic` dependencies and Poetry / PDM tables are unsupported; optional dependencies ignored); the key covers the
  canonical JSON of those two, not the file. `python_satisfies(spec, version)` checks `requires-python` against the
  environments' Python (`>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<`, `==`, `!=`, `~=`, `==X.*`; an unknown specifier is ignored).
  `parse_package_json`: `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `overrides` (with a lock also `devDependencies` and
  `peerDependencies`, which `npm ci` compares); a spec is kept only when it is a semver range or tag, an `npm:` alias
  (its own spec checked too), an `https://` tarball, a `git+https://` or `github:` spec, or a hosted `user/repo`
  shorthand; refused: `workspaces`, `file:`, `link:`, `workspace:`, `portal:`, local paths, `http://`, credentials and
  every other scheme (`git:`, `ssh:`, `git+ssh:`, ...). The env always gets a generated `package.json` (no `scripts`,
  `bin` or the like: the skill's own lifecycle scripts never run); `check_lock` wants lockfileVersion 2 or 3, no
  `link: true`, every `resolved` https.
- **Environments** under `Config.skill_envs_dir` (`~/.dreamteam/skill-envs`): `<skill[:24]>-py-<key12>` /
  `…-js-<key12>` (`env_dirname`, `DIRNAME_RE`). `env_key` hashes the skill name, the ecosystem, the trust class, the
  manifests' material and the tool: Python's implementation, minor version, platform, cache tag, ABI flags, base
  interpreter path, C library and Linux distribution (`os_marker`), or Node's major version, ABI, platform and arch.
  Not the installer, the index configuration or the skill's other files (editing a script reinstalls nothing).
  Trust class (`trust_class(from)`): `user` for `library`, `claude-user`, `host-library`; `agent` for `agent` and
  `claude-project` (agent-writable origins): the two never share an environment, both are shared across sessions.
  Layout: `env.json`, `src/` (the manifests, the generated files), `venv/` or `package.json` + lock +
  `node_modules/`, `views/<owner12>/node_modules` (Node), `install.log` (redacted, at most 2 MiB), `failed.json`,
  `ok` (written last: "ready"), `used` (mtime = last use); `.locks/`, `.cache/`, `.trash-*` are reserved.
- **Tools** (`INSTALLERS`, a `RealInstallers`; tests replace it): Python is `[skills] python` (default the base
  interpreter DreamTeam runs on), probed once per process (`probe_python`, `-I -c`; a probe that failed is run again
  after 5 minutes, or at once by `skill_reinstall`, which also plans an `unavailable` skill again); the installer is
  uv when there is one (`uv venv --python <interp> venv`, then `uv pip install --python <venv python>
  [--require-hashes] -r …`),
  else the interpreter's pip ≥ 22.3 (`-m venv --without-pip`, then `-m pip --python <venv python> install`), else a
  venv's ensurepip; none: unavailable. Node: the real `node` binary behind any shim (`process.execPath`; on Windows
  only `node.exe`), npm run as `node npm-cli.js` (never `npm.cmd`), `npm ci` with a lock else `npm install`, both
  with `--omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund` and `--ignore-scripts` unless `install_scripts`. Commands run with cwd =
  the env folder, as contained process trees (`ProcessTree`), the venv step 120 s and the install `install_timeout`
  (then killed: "timed out after 900 s"), in `installer_env(config, trust)`: `scrubbed_env` (`keep_url_credentials`
  for the `user` class: a private index's password in `PIP_INDEX_URL` stays; the `agent` class gets the same index
  without it, so its install fails there), plus `install_env` for the `user` class only, without `VIRTUAL_ENV`,
  `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONPATH`, `PIP_USER`, `UV_PYTHON` and the like, with `PIP_NO_INPUT`, `PYTHONNOUSERSITE`,
  `UV_NO_PROGRESS`; the user's own pip / uv / npm configuration applies.
  On Windows with long paths off, a venv holding a path of 260 characters or more fails with a text saying so.
- **The manager** (`EnvManager.for_config(config)`, one per process and root): `plan(folder, skill, trust,
  settings, *, config, proposal) -> [EnvSpec | state]` (blocking, a daemon thread; a state for off, unsupported,
  unavailable), `peek(spec, owner) -> state` (never blocks: memory, then stats; a ready env is verified at most
  once a minute: the venv's python and every installed dist-info, or npm's hidden lockfile and every dependency's
  folder; one that fails is broken, shown as installing and rebuilt), `ensure(spec, *, owner, force) ->
  Future[state]` (one build per env in the process, joined by later callers), `use(owner, dirnames)`,
  `exclusive(dirname, requester)`, `check_reinstall`, `view(spec, owner)` / `view_ok`, `touch`, `cleanup(days)`,
  `log_tail`, `subscribe(fn) -> unsubscribe` (published on the subscriber's loop with a phase: queued, waiting,
  started, done). A build takes the OS build lock `.locks/<dirname>.lock` first (another process's build is waited
  for, as `installing, other_process`, holding no slot, at most `install_timeout + 120` s, then a failure kept in
  memory), then decides: ready (reused), failed less than an hour ago (not retried; a reinstall is), failed or half
  built (removed and rebuilt), broken (rebuilt for everyone), ready with `force` (the reinstall: refused 409 while
  another session uses it); then one of `INSTALL_PARALLEL = 2` slots (`installing, queued` meanwhile), the manifests
  copied (the bytes must be the key's), the commands, the checks, and `ok` last. A failure writes `failed.json`
  (`error` = the first `ERROR` / `error:` / `npm ERR!` line or the last one, redacted, prefixed by the installer);
  an exception outside the commands (env.json or the log cannot be written: a full disk, a lock, a long path) is a
  failure too (`OSError: …`), and one whose `failed.json` cannot be written is kept in memory (the half-built folder
  alone would read as installing). A build that raises before that (a reinstall's exclusive lock refused) publishes
  the env's real state as its end (still ready, an older failure, else a failure in memory) before the caller gets
  the error, so no subscriber keeps waiting. While this process takes or holds an env's use lock exclusively, its own
  shared takes (a peek, `use`) wait: taking one back would make that exclusive lock fail.
  **In use**: every process holds a shared OS lock (`LockFileEx` / `flock`) on `.locks/<dirname>.use` while one of
  its sessions has the env attached (taken before the first peek); a reinstall of a ready env, a removal and cleanup
  take it exclusively: "The environment of skill "x" is used by N other running session(s); stop them, or
  reinstall from there." / "... is used by another DreamTeam process; ...". A rename is no in-use test (Windows
  renames a venv whose python runs).
- **Per session** (`SessionSkills`): the plan of each attached skill is cached by (digest, `settings_hash`) and made
  in a daemon thread at `start()` (every skill; then `use`, and the views of ready Node envs), on every attach and
  proposal; `ensure_deps(names=None, *, force, ecosystem)` starts the builds in the background (at every start and
  after each attach); `deps(name)` (the snapshot's `deps`) and `deps_fragment(name, lang, shell=None)`: `skills_deps_python`
  {python: the venv's python written for the swarm's shell (`shell_ready`: bare or `& '…'` in PowerShell, always
  quoted for cmd, `shlex.quote` elsewhere; never in backticks), files, extra: `skills_deps_bin` {names, bin} for the
  commands its packages installed, `skills_deps_own` when a pyproject is among the files}, `skills_deps_node`
  (linked) or `skills_deps_node_path` (the link could not be made), `skills_deps_installing` (an external member,
  whom the end wakes: "you are told when they are ready") or, with `quiet` (the default; an AI member, `item_lines`
  and `_announce` pick it by kind), `skills_deps_installing_quiet` (a later wake-up says so: the install does not
  wake it), `skills_deps_failed`
  {files, error, log} and `skills_deps_manual` {files, reason: `deps_reason_off` / `_proposals` / `_unavailable`
  {detail} / `_python` {need, have} / `_unsupported` {detail}}. The subscription emits `skill.deps` and, when a build
  ends that this session saw as installing (or an env it saw as failed turns out ready: another process built it, a
  retry succeeded), `n_skill_deps_ready` / `n_skill_deps_failed` to the members (quiet for AI
  agents, a wake for external ones) and `u_skill_deps_failed` {name, files, error, log} to the user. Node: when its
  env is ready the session's view is made (a hardlink farm of the env's `node_modules`, a copy where the file system
  has no hardlinks; reused while it matches the env's `ok`) and the mirror copy gets a `node_modules` link to it at
  its package.json's folder (made after the copy's swap; checked by every sync: a missing, dangling or re-pointed
  link is made again, a view an agent's command emptied rebuilt, a real folder in its place — an agent's own npm
  install — left alone until the next full rebuild); an agent's `npm ci` or `rm -rf node_modules/` through the link
  reaches only that view. A view that cannot be made shows as failed ("this session's view of its node_modules could
  not be made: …"; the members are told) and is tried again by the minute check: an agent is never pointed at the
  shared env itself. `reinstall(actor, name, ecosystem=None)` (`skill_reinstall`, user only): "Reinstalling the
  packages of skill "x" (requirements.txt); members are told when they are ready.", "... are being installed
  already; ...", "No skill "x" is attached to this swarm." (404), "Skill "x" has no requirements.txt,
  pyproject.toml or package.json.", "Skill "x" has no Python packages (requirements.txt or pyproject.toml)." / "...
  no Node packages (package.json).", "Skill "x": its packages are not installed automatically (<reason>).", the 409
  texts above. `touch_envs()` (hourly from the scheduler) refreshes the `used` stamps, rebuilds broken envs,
  retries failures older than an hour and builds an env that reads as installing while nothing in this process
  builds it (`ensure`: another process's build is waited for); `stop_deps()` at `Swarm.stop`.
- **Cleanup** (`EnvManager.cleanup(retention_days) -> {"removed": [dirname], "kept": [{dirname, why: in use | being
  built}]}`): envs whose `used` is older than `env_retention_days` (0: none by age), failed or half-built ones older
  than a day, views unused for a day, trash older than an hour; never an env whose use lock any process holds or
  whose build lock is held; `ok` goes first, then the folder is renamed away (a refused rename puts `ok` back).
  A standalone `dreamteam run` runs it once, 60 s after the start, in a daemon thread; the launcher 60 s after its
  start and then daily (`ENV_CLEANUP_DELAY`, `ENV_CLEANUP_EVERY`, §18.1), and at once on `POST
  /api/skill-envs/cleanup` (the home page's button, the console's and the TUI's `/skills clean-envs`). The user's run
  is `cleanup(…, every_unused=True)`: every env no session uses now goes, whatever its age and also with
  `env_retention_days = 0` (which only turns the automatic runs off); the in-use and being-built ones are kept and
  reported.
- **Trust model**: Installing a skill's dependencies runs code from the packages it lists (Python build backends of
  source packages; npm install scripts of its dependencies only when `install_scripts` is on) with DreamTeam's
  rights, which outside the Docker sandbox are the user's. It happens only for skills attached to a session — by the
  user, by a role in the user's catalog, or by a member's proposal. Packages come from the indexes the user
  configured, or from https and git URLs the skill names directly (including the resolved URLs of its npm
  lockfile); a skill cannot add or replace an index, or name a local path or an environment variable. Skills a
  member proposed, or taken from the workspace's agent-writable `.claude/skills`, install into environments kept
  apart from the user's own skills and never get `install_env` or the credentials of the URLs in their environment
  (§7 `scrubbed_env`); `install_proposals = false` and a session without network (§7.2) install nothing for them.
  A non-sandboxed agent can still write
  `~/.dreamteam/skill-envs` directly, as it can write the skills library: environments are a convenience, not a
  security boundary. Logs, errors and the recorded commands are redacted (URL credentials, the values of
  `install_env` and of the index variables).
- **Not in v1**: Poetry, PDM, `[dependency-groups]` and optional dependencies; PEP 723 inline metadata; conda,
  Pipfile, pnpm and yarn; installing the skill itself (`pip install .`); local paths, `-e` and indexes a skill names;
  one environment for several skills; a skill's venv or `.bin` on agents' `PATH` (the index names the folders);
  settings for the installer, `node` and `npm`; a per-environment list, removing one environment, launcher MCP
  actions for them, a size cap; Node in the Docker image.

**Security.** "Only the user attaches, imports, deletes and saves to the library" is a user-interface convention,
not a security boundary, as `mcp_approve` is: a hub without a token (the default `dreamteam serve` on
127.0.0.1) has no authentication (GuardMiddleware stops browsers on other sites, not local processes), and without the sandbox agents run as the user and can write
`~/.dreamteam/skills` directly. What DreamTeam does: the sandbox mounts the host library read-only; library entries
changed outside DreamTeam are flagged (`changed_outside`); a hub MCP client cannot save to the library a proposal of
a member it acts as, nor one of any external member when nothing names the client (§13); the library gets only
the content that was proposed (the digest is checked again); every library change records `by` and `via`, and every
attach the surface it came through (`skill.attached` `via`); agents' shells never get `DREAMTEAM_SKILLS_DIR`,
`DREAMTEAM_HOST_SKILLS_DIR` or `DREAMTEAM_SKILL_ENVS_DIR` (§7);
`<workspace>/.claude/skills` is never used implicitly; Git URLs are hardened and redacted; zips and folders are
checked as above; sizes are capped per skill (`max_mb`, `max_files`), per archive or checkout (`max_archive_mb`) and
for SKILL.md (100 KB). A hub with a token (§14.2: the Docker sandbox, docker compose, `DREAMTEAM_HUB_TOKEN`) asks its
own loopback for it too, so the agents' commands in the sandbox's container, whose environment holds only the token's
digest, cannot call its API; a token for every hub is out of scope.

**Not in v1**: Claude Code plugin skills; automatic updates of library skills from their Git source (the recorded
`commit` makes a later check possible); per-role visibility; mounting the MCP library or `~/.claude/skills` into the
sandbox; rendered Markdown on the home page; refs given as commit SHAs (`--branch` takes branches and tags only).

## 20. Export and import (transfer.py, treecopy.py, mcp_library.py)

A home moves to another computer (or into a backup) as one folder: `transfer.export_home` writes it, and
`plan_import` / `apply_import` bring it into another home, adding what is new and rewriting what changed; nothing
the export does not carry is ever deleted. Stage 1 is the CLI only (§18.3: `dreamteam export`, `dreamteam
import`): no launcher route, no MCP tool, no UI. User docs: docs/en/transfer.md.

```python
# transfer.py
CATEGORIES = ("settings", "skills", "mcp", "sessions")
FORMAT, FORMAT_VERSION, MANIFEST = "dreamteam-export", 1, "dreamteam-export.json"
def parse_include(values) -> tuple[str, ...]          # comma lists, repeatable; every category for None / empty;
                                                      # an unknown word: TransferError(usage=True)
def export_home(home, dest, *, include=None, sessions=None, running=None, dry_run=False, git=None) -> ExportReport
def read_manifest(folder) -> dict
def check_session_names(folder, sessions) -> None   # --session values the export holds (id or uid), else usage
def plan_import(manager, folder, *, include=None, sessions=None) -> ImportPlan          # changes nothing
async def apply_import(manager, plan, *, before_swap=None) -> ImportResult
def render_export_report(report) -> str; def render_import_plan(plan) -> str; def render_import_result(r) -> str
class TransferError(ValueError)      # (message, *, usage=False): usage → the CLI exits 2, else 1
class SecretFound(TransferError)     # .places: where a secret was found, never the value
```

### 20.1 Categories

- `settings`: every section of `dreamteam.toml` (`read_raw`), `[models.*]` and `[[roles]]` included, without
  `[mcp.external]` and without keys (`scrub_settings`, §20.3).
- `skills`: the skills library (`Config.skills_library_dir`).
- `mcp`: the MCP library (`Config.library_dir`, approvals included) and `[mcp.external]` without env values.
- `sessions`: whole sessions (database, `.dreamteam/{mcp,attached-skills,jobs}`, workspace files; a thread
  session's forum tables are in its database, §22.9).

`include` defaults to every category; `sessions` (ids or uids) picks sessions and adds the `sessions` category, the
others still follow `include`. On import, `include` is intersected with the manifest's `include`; a category named
in `include` that the export does not hold goes to `plan.missing` with a warning (the plan is not ok: exit 1).

### 20.2 The export folder

```
dreamteam-export.json                 the manifest, written last (<name>.tmp + os.replace): a folder without it is an
                                      incomplete export, which import refuses
settings/dreamteam.toml               dump_toml(scrub_settings(raw)) after a two-line comment
skills/<name>/                        skills.copy_skill of each valid library skill, plus .dreamteam.json {name,
                                      description, origin, source (URL credentials stripped), by, via, added_at,
                                      updated_at, digest}; never the stat manifest (mtimes of this computer)
mcp/library/<name>/                   server.py + meta.json (mcp_library.write_entry_folder); an entry whose
                                      `project` is the folder of a session of this home has `project_session: <uid>`
                                      instead
mcp/external.json                     {name: {command, cwd, description, env_keys}} (scrub_external)
sessions/<id>/session.json            session.json without "id"/"legacy", with "uid" written, overrides through
                                      scrub_overrides
sessions/<id>/.dreamteam/swarm.db     the sqlite backup of the database (_copy_db), finished by _finish_db
sessions/<id>/.dreamteam/{mcp,attached-skills,jobs}/   treecopy.copy_tree, no excludes
sessions/<id>/workspace/              copy_tree of the session's own folder or its in_home folder with the export
                                      excludes (§20.5); a folder outside the home is not copied (its path is in
                                      session.json and the manifest)
```

- **Destination** (`_check_dest`): missing, empty (OS metadata such as `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`
  ignored), or a previous export (only `LAYOUT` names, with the manifest): then the new export is built in the
  sibling `.<name>.export-<hex8>` and swapped in through `.<name>.old-<hex8>` (`_put_in_place`; when the swap can be
  neither done nor undone both folders are kept and named, `_Kept`); stale siblings of an interrupted export older
  than `STALE_SECONDS` (1 h) are removed first. Refused: a drive or file-system root, a mount point, a link, a file,
  any other non-empty folder, a folder inside the home's `sessions/` or `.dreamteam/`, the skills or MCP library
  (when exported), the workspace of any session of the home (exported or not), and a folder that contains the home
  or any of these. A new folder is created with mode 0700 on POSIX (`_mkdir_private`; on Windows it inherits its
  access rules); an empty one is chmod 0700 and must belong to the current user on POSIX.
- **Sessions** (`_pick_sessions`): every session but the legacy `main` (left out; refused only when named), by id
  or uid (an unknown or ambiguous one: usage error). Left out (refused) per session: a damaged session.json, no
  uid (`session_uid` None), `.dreamteam/workspace-move.json`. Two picked sessions with one uid are warned. The
  workspace kind is `own`, `in_home` (`_home_relative(meta["workspace"])`) or `outside`. A session the caller lists
  in `running` (the CLI asks the hub) is exported as a snapshot with a warning (`running_at_export`). A failure of
  one session (`_Refused`: its database changed twice while read, is damaged or cannot be read; or an error of the
  destination's file system: names differing only in case, a file of 4 GiB or more on FAT32, a name or path it
  cannot hold, `_write_refusal`) removes that session from the export and the others go on; a full disk stops the
  export.
- **Database copy** (`_copy_db`, `_read_db`): never writes next to the source. A database with both `-wal` and
  `-shm` is read through them (`?mode=ro`: WAL content included); one with a `-wal` only is read from a private
  copy of both; one without either as `immutable=1`, read again once when its file changed meanwhile, then
  refused. `_finish_db` on the copy: `journal_mode=DELETE`; command credentials stripped (§20.3); `VACUUM` (no free
  page keeps deleted text); `PRAGMA quick_check` must be "ok"; then its figures (events, last event of the work as
  §20.4, MCP servers, `max_tools_revision`). The session is never opened, so one made by an earlier version (§17.2)
  is exported like any other (an import by this version refuses it, §20.4), with a warning in the report (`session
  {sid} was made by an earlier version of DreamTeam: this version and the same one on the other computer refuse it;
  only the version that made it imports and opens it (keep this folder)`; `db.made_by_earlier_version` of the copy,
  of the database itself in a dry run), since the report's closing advice is to use the same version there.
- **Order** (`_export_parts`): settings, skills, mcp, sessions; then `scan_for_secrets` over the whole folder; then
  the manifest; then the swap. Any exception (TransferError, OSError, KeyboardInterrupt) discards what was written
  (`_discard`: the temp folder, or the contents of the user's empty folder; retried `DISCARD_TRIES` times), naming
  what could not be removed. `dry_run` measures the same parts without writing (no secret check).
- **Manifest**: `{format, format_version, dreamteam_version, created_at, source: {machine: platform.node(), os:
  sys.platform, home, python}, schema: {db_columns: sorted(db.known_columns()), toolset_revision,
  toolset_revisions}, include,
  settings: {sections, models, roles, omitted} | null, skills: [{name, digest, origin, files, size,
  changed_outside}] | null, mcp: {library: [{name, digest, approved, changed_outside, project_session}], external:
  [{name, env_keys, credentials_removed}]} | null, sessions: [{id, uid, title, created_at, last_event: {id, ts,
  type}, events, max_tools_rev, db_sha256, db_bytes, attached_skills, mcp_servers, running_at_export, workspace:
  {kind, in_home, path, adopted, files, bytes, tree_digest, compare_digest, carried?}, modes, swarm_mode}] | null,
  left_out: [{what, reason, refused}], warnings, not_copied: [{session, path}]}`. `modes` holds the permission bits
  worth restoring (`treecopy.mode_record`) by path inside the session; `carried: false` marks a workspace folder
  that was missing at export (the import keeps the files the target has). `toolset_revision` is
  `frozen.NEWEST_REVISION`, `toolset_revisions` the current revision of each mode (`TOOLSET_REVISIONS`), and
  `swarm_mode` the session's mode (`db.session_mode` of the copied database, §22.9).
- `ExportReport.ok`: nothing asked for was refused (the legacy `main` session left out by rule does not count).

### 20.3 What never travels, and the secret check

Never exported: `models.*.api_key`; a key typed into `api_key_env` (`_pasted_key`: not a variable name, or a name
no variable has that looks like a key); secret-looking entries of `models.*.extra` at any depth (`_scrub_extra`:
names matching shell's `_SECRET_RE` or `SECRET_NAMES` such as `authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`; values like
`Bearer <8+ chars>`), each with a warning; every `[mcp.external.*].env` value, global and in session overrides
(`env_keys`: the sorted names only); credentials in MCP commands (below); `dreamteam.toml.bak`, `hub.json`,
launcher markers, logs, `tui_history` and everything else of `<home>/.dreamteam/`; a session's `.dreamteam/`
except `swarm.db` and `SESSION_DATA_PARTS`; `sessions/.deleted-*`, `.importing-*`, `.replaced-*`; skill
environments; hub tokens; the files of workspace folders outside the home; the legacy `main` session and `dreamteam
run` projects.

`strip_command_credentials(command) -> (command, removed)`: URL user information (`shell.strip_url_credentials`),
credential query parameters (`?api_key=`, `?token=`, `?sig=`, ...), the value of a credential flag (`--token X`,
`--api-key=X`, `-token=X`, `--password X`, `--client-secret X`, `--auth X`; not `--no-...`), credential headers
(`Authorization: Bearer X`, also as `--header`/`-H` with two arguments or as a JSON object), `NAME=value`
assignments whose name the shell treats as secret, and lone `Bearer X` / `Basic X` / `Token X` arguments become
empty; a command written as one string is split as mcp_forge splits it. It applies to `mcp/external.json`, to
session overrides and, in each exported database, to `mcp_servers.command` of origin `config` (start() registers
them again from the target's settings). Every removed value, and the command credentials of every `mcp.created`
event of the journal, is also removed from every text value of the copied database (`_strip_db_credentials`:
journal, histories); each affected server is warned (`re-enter the credentials of ... on the other computer`).

`known_secrets(raw, overrides, environ) -> Secrets` (value → label; values shorter than `MIN_SECRET` = 8 and the
`PLACEHOLDER_KEYS` of `settings.PROVIDER_CHOICES`, e.g. `lm-studio`, are not kept): the stored key of every profile
(also one typed into `api_key_env`); the value of every variable a profile names; every environment variable
`shell._is_secret` accepts with `_KNOWN_SECRETS`, `key_env_names()` and the profiles' variables; the header values
of `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` / `OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS`; the values of the `[shell] pass_env` and `[skills]
install_env` variables; the env values and command credentials of the `[mcp.external]` servers of the global
settings and of every session's overrides (also sessions not exported); `hubauth.env_token()`,
`hubauth.api_env_token()` (the API token, §21.1: main() took it out of os.environ, so the scan of the variables misses
it) and the tokens in `hubauth.tokens_dir()`; plus everything the export itself removed.

`scan_for_secrets(root, secrets, *, git=None) -> [place]`: each value is searched for as it is, JSON-escaped (with
and without ASCII escapes) and escaped twice, each as UTF-8 and UTF-16LE (`_Matcher`, chunked with an overlap).
Every file below `root` is searched as bytes (links skipped, `long_path`); a SQLite file is also read row by row
(`_scan_db`: every value of every table and the schema text; a long value lies on overflow pages), a hit named
`<file> (table.column:rowid, ...)` (at most three rows per value and column). Every git repository database below
it (`looks_like_git_dir`) is read whole with `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch --unordered` (blobs, trees,
commits, tags; packed or loose, reachable or not), run with `hubgit.fixed_args()`, `-c safe.directory=*`,
`core.longpaths` on Windows, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` set to the null device; a hit is named
`<repo> (git object <id12>)`. No git on PATH or a git that cannot start or exits non-zero is a TransferError
(the history could not be checked); on Windows a repository path longer than `GIT_PATH_MAX` (250) only picks the
"its path in the export is too long" text of that error (git that succeeds on it is fine). Places are
`<path>: <label>`, sorted. Any place found raises `SecretFound` (exit 1, nothing left at the destination):
"Nothing exported: the export would contain a secret of this computer ... in: - <place> ... Remove it there, or
leave that part out (--include, --session), then export again."

### 20.4 Import

**Manifest** (`read_manifest`): refused (`Nothing imported: ...`) when the folder is missing, has no manifest, has a
link among the `LAYOUT` names or `mcp/library`, the manifest cannot be read (files an import reads whole are capped
at `SMALL_FILE_MAX` = 64 MiB) or is not `format: dreamteam-export`, or `format_version` is not a positive int; a
`format_version` above `FORMAT_VERSION` says `Update DreamTeam here first.`

**Plan** (`plan_import`): pure. The export folder must not lie inside the target's `sessions/`, `.dreamteam/` or
the workspace of an own or in_home session (`_check_source`). Items are `ImportItem(category, name, action, reason,
target, warnings, status, error, backup)` with `action` add | rewrite | unchanged | skip | refuse; `ImportPlan`
has `changes` (something is added or rewritten), `blocked` (something is skipped or refused), `ok` (not blocked
and nothing missing), `exit_code` (0 when ok, else 1), `id_map` (exported id → id here) and `warnings` (the
export's `left_out`; an earlier import's interrupted swap; another source OS: agents keep its shell in their
frozen instructions and its paths in their histories).

**Settings** (`merge_settings(target, exported, *, home, environ) -> SettingsMerge`): sections are deep-merged,
exported values winning; keys this version does not know, sections not in `_SECTION_FIELDS` and invalid profile
names are dropped and listed; `swarm.goal` / `goal_description` are not taken; the machine-local keys
`LOCAL_KEYS` = `server.host`, `server.port`, `shell.program`, `skills.library_dir`, `skills.envs_dir`,
`skills.python`, `mcp.library_dir`, `api.folders` (§21.10) keep the target's value (listed as
`kept as they are here` when they differ). `[api]` counts as changed only when it differs as stored
(`settings.api_values`, without its default values), so an exported default value changes nothing, while it still
replaces a value set here.
Profiles: missing ones are added, the others rewritten from the export (an exported `api_key` is never taken);
profiles only here stay. When the profile's endpoint (`settings._endpoint`: provider, base_url) is the same, the
stored key stays (no `api_key` in the update), and so do its secret `extra` entries and its `api_key_env` when the
export names none; otherwise `api_key = ""` removes the stored key (`enter the key for profile <name> again`), and
secret extras or a key variable configured here are dropped with a warning. A local-endpoint preset without key
gets its placeholder key back. Roles (by `roles.role_key`): added or rewritten, the others stay; a role model that
is not a profile after the merge is dropped with a warning. Teams (by `roles.team_key`): added or rewritten, the
others stay; a team naming a role the catalog lacks after the merge stays, with a warning (`team 'X' uses the role
'Y', ...`): the load check is shape only, so nothing blocks the import, and the team is refused when chosen (§17.3
"Saved teams"). An `agents.default_model` that is not a profile here
keeps the target's value. Warnings: a profile without a key here, a base_url on localhost. The merged settings are
validated (`validate`; an error refuses the item) and saved by one `SessionManager.update_settings(update)`, with
`models`, `roles` and `teams` as complete lists, so `apply_update` deletes nothing.

**Skills**: identity is the folder name; the exported folder must pass `check_skill_dir` with the target's limits
and its SKILL.md must name it; a link of that name in the target library is refused. Same digest: unchanged;
otherwise rewrite, or add. Applied by `Library.add(src, origin, source, replace=True, by=<exported by>,
via="import")`.

**MCP library**: identity is the name; `mcp_library.read_folder` and `check_requirements` must pass. `project`:
when the entry's `project_session` uid maps to a session here (`uid_targets`, after the sessions are applied),
`str((sessions_dir / sid).resolve())`; otherwise the target entry's own `project` stays, else none
(`_project_updates`; `project_session` is never written). `approved_digest` travels as exported (an approval the
target records for the same digest is kept). Unchanged iff the code and the resulting meta.json are the same; a
link in the library is replaced (the link only). Warnings: requirements without `uv` on PATH; an approved entry
while `[mcp] require_approval` is on here. Applied by `mcp_library.add_entry(root, src, name=, replace=True,
meta_updates=, meta_drop=)`.

**`[mcp.external]`** (`merge_external(target, exported, *, keep_others=True, where="Settings")`): identity is the
table name; command, cwd, description and the other keys come from the export. The target's env values for a
server (also keys only here), and its command with the credentials stored here, stay when `_same_program` holds:
the same command credentials aside (a string command is split, so `"npx -y X"` equals `["npx", "-y", "X"]`) and the
same cwd; otherwise they are dropped (`... the env values stored here for it were dropped: enter ... again`).
Exported names without a value here: `enter <KEY> for <server> in <where>`; a command the export emptied of
credentials: `re-enter the credentials of <server> ...`. Servers only here stay. Warnings: `command[0]` not on PATH,
an absolute cwd that does not exist, a session override with env values only whose global server's command
changes. All servers are saved by one `update_settings({"mcp": ...})`.

**Sessions** (`_plan_sessions`, `_plan_session`). Identity is `session_uid` (§17.2), never the id.
- A uid held by more than one exported session (a folder copied by hand there) is refused unless named by id with
  `sessions`; a named copy is matched by its id only (the target session of that id when its uid or `origin_uid` is
  that uid), else added: with a fresh uid and `origin_uid` = the shared one when a target session holds that uid or
  this import already adds or keeps it, otherwise with the shared uid (no `origin_uid`). A uid held by more than one
  target session is refused unless named by an id among them (when the exported id is not one of them, it is
  refused whatever is named: delete or move the unwanted copy here). An exported session whose `origin_uid` is the
  uid of the target session with its id comes back to that copy. Two exported sessions that would rewrite one target are
  refused.
- Refused per session (the others go on): an invalid id, an unreadable session.json or one whose uid does not
  match the manifest, a link among its folders, `workspace-move.json` in the export or here, a database that
  `_check_export_db` rejects (no `db_sha256` in the manifest, a different sha256, `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` files
  next to it, `db.unknown_columns`, `db.foreign_objects`, `db.max_tools_revision` > `NEWEST_REVISION`, a `tools:*`
  record of a mode this version does not know (§22.9), and
  `db.made_by_earlier_version` (§17.2), checked last, with the reason `it was made by an earlier version of
  DreamTeam and cannot be opened by this one ({version}); import it with the version that made it`), overrides
  that `import_overrides` or `validate` refuse, a placement that fails (below). A session running here is
  `skip`.
- A target of the same uid whose mode (`db.session_mode`, §22.1) differs from the export's is refused before the
  unchanged / settings-only / rewrite decision: `its mode differs here (board/thread): the mode is chosen when a
  session is created; delete one copy or import it as a new session` (§22.9). `swarm.mode` is no `LOCAL_KEYS` entry:
  it travels in the overrides; when the exported overrides name another mode than the exported database, the
  database's mode is kept, with the warning `its settings named another mode than its database; the database's
  ({mode}) is kept` (§22.9).
- No target: **add** under the exported id when it is free and not reserved by this import, else `_free_id(title)`
  (`as <id>: <id> is taken here`).
- A target: **unchanged** when the last events of the work `(id, ts, type)` are equal (a run's `session.started` and
  `session.stopped` are left out, as for `last_activity`, §21.6: a hub restart alone is no newer work), the files
  match (`compare_digest` of the exported workspace equals that of the target's folder; always true when the target
  works outside the home or the export carries no files) and `_settings_differ` finds nothing (title, overrides as
  the import writes them, `pending_goal`); when only those differ: **rewrite** of session.json alone (`settings_only`,
  `import_settings`, no backup). When the export carries no workspace files and the target's folder has some:
  refused. Otherwise **rewrite**, whatever the history says, with the reason: `its files differ`, `the export has
  newer work in it` (the export holds the target's last event), `this computer has newer work in it` (the target
  holds the export's last event) or `both computers worked on it since they last had the same copy`.
- Overrides (`_session_overrides`, then `SessionManager.import_overrides`): sections outside `OVERRIDE_SECTIONS`
  and unknown keys dropped; `LOCAL_KEYS` removed from the export and the replaced copy's values put back; its
  `[mcp.external]` merged with the replaced copy's by `merge_external(keep_others=False)`; a server overridden with
  another command or folder than the target's global server of that name gets the inherited env values blanked;
  an `agents.default_model` that is not a profile here is dropped (warned).
- Placement (`_placement` → `ImportedWorkspace(kind, folder, path, adopted)`): a rewrite of a target that works
  outside the home keeps that path (the export's workspace files go to the session's own folder, warned); `own`
  stays own; `in_home` goes to `<home>/<in_home>`, the target's own in_home folder on a rewrite, else the first
  free of `<in_home>-<id>`, `<in_home>-<id>-2` ... (warned), refused when it would leave the home, lie in
  `sessions/` or `.dreamteam/`, overlap the export folder or another session's folder, or fail
  `SessionManager._target_refusal`; `outside` keeps the path: a relative or missing folder is warned (`put the
  project at that path, or run /cd`), a file or a folder overlapping another session or the export folder is
  refused, an existing non-empty folder is adopted (the user's project), an empty one is used as is.
- Warnings: names the target's file system cannot hold (`_portability_warnings`: Windows-invalid names on win32,
  case-only clashes on win32 and darwin; copying them fails the session), agents whose model profile is missing
  here (they use the default profile).

**Apply** (`apply_import`): first `recover_swaps()` (finish or undo the swaps of an import that died halfway) and
`clean_staging()` (stale `.importing-*` of processes that are gone); when a swap was put back, the planned sessions
are `not done` (`import again`). Then the items in `APPLY_ORDER` = settings, skills, sessions, mcp (library entries
before `[mcp.external]`, so a library entry's `project` can name an imported session). refuse → `refused`, skip →
`skipped`, unchanged → `unchanged`; one item that fails is `failed` with its error and the others go on. A
cancellation or KeyboardInterrupt lets the item in progress finish or undo (`_to_end`), marks the rest `not done`
and sets `interrupted` (exit 130). When the settings or `[mcp.external]` were saved, `dreamteam.toml.bak` is
rewritten with the settings from before the import. `ImportResult.exit_code`: 130 interrupted, 0 when every item
is added, rewritten or unchanged and nothing is missing, else 1.

A session is staged in `staging_path(id)` = `sessions/.importing-<id>-<pid>-<hex8>` (`_stage_session`: the
database copied with its sha256 checked against the manifest, the data parts and `workspace/` by `copy_tree(...,
modes="import")` with the recorded `modes`; a link or an unreadable file fails it). `_import_meta` writes the uid
(it must be 32 hex), `autostart: false` (imported sessions never start by themselves), the overrides checked
against this home, and the workspace entry rebuilt for this home (`_workspace_meta` for in_home, `{path, adopted}`
for outside); a session of the HTTP API v1 keeps `via` and its `api` block with `client_ref`, `request_digest`,
`start_error`, `error` and `folder` set to null (§21.9). `_finish_staged` opens the database once with
`db.Database` (`ADDED_COLUMNS`, WAL again), points
absolute job-log paths at the copy's own `.dreamteam/jobs/` (or clears them), and writes session.json last.
`before_swap(id)` (the CLI's holder check) runs right before the rename; an exception fails that session with
nothing changed.
- `import_add`: under the id's lock; when the id is taken meanwhile, `_new_id(title)`; `_swap_added` places the
  in_home folder and renames the staged copy in, undoing both on failure. Emits `created`.
- `import_rewrite(sid, ...)`: under `_lock(sid)`; refused (409) when session.json changed since the plan
  (`expect`), when a workspace move is unfinished, or when the session runs; a loaded swarm is unloaded.
  `_swap_replaced` creates `sessions/.replaced-<id>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-N]/` with the journal `swap.json` {sid, pid,
  planned, done, created}, rewritten after every step, and renames: the session folder → `session/`, its in_home
  folder → `workspace/`, the staged `workspace/` → its in_home folder, the staged copy → the session folder. Renames
  are retried (`RENAME_TRIES` = 10 × `RENAME_PAUSE` 0.2 s) and never replace anything; a failure undoes every done
  rename (`Could not replace session ... its files are in use ... Nothing was changed.`, 409) and removes the
  journal. Then `_carry_environments` moves `KEEP_ON_IMPORT` = `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules` (at any depth, not
  inside `.git`) from the backup's workspace to the same free place of the new one, and `_drop_old_backups` removes
  the older backups of the same session (same uid, no journal): only the last one is kept. Returns {id, backup,
  kept, removed_backups, warnings, dropped_model}; emits `updated`.
- `import_settings(sid, meta, *, expect)`: the same checks, session.json rewritten in place (its workspace entry
  kept), no backup.
- `recover_swaps()`: for each backup with a journal whose process is gone: all renames done (also the one just
  before the process died, seen on disk) → the journal goes; otherwise the done renames are undone newest first
  (a place taken meanwhile is reported, the journal stays). `interrupted_swaps()` lists such backups for the plan.

### 20.5 Tree copy (treecopy.py)

`copy_tree(src, dst, *, exclude_names=EXPORT_EXCLUDE_NAMES, exclude_paths=EXPORT_EXCLUDE_PATHS, modes="keep",
apply_modes=None, progress=None, fold_names=False, max_files=None, max_bytes=None, check=None, skip_files=())
-> TreeResult` and `scan_tree(src, *, exclude_names, exclude_paths, hash=True, fold_names=False, max_files=None,
max_bytes=None, check=None, skip_files=()) -> TreeResult` (the walk without copying). Links (symlinks, junctions)
are never followed and are listed; FIFOs, sockets and devices are listed as special; unreadable files are listed in
`errors`, and the files that were gone (FileNotFoundError: deleted while the walk ran) in `vanished` too (a folder
that was gone is only in `errors`, with the reason `GONE_DIR` "the folder was moved or deleted while it was copied");
`skip_files` names regular files left out without a word (counted in `skipped`; `COPY_SKIP_FILES` = `.DS_Store`,
`Thumbs.db`); Windows paths use `workspace.long_path`. On POSIX (`os.scandir` takes a descriptor) each folder is
opened with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`, its `fstat` compared with the stat its parent's listing gave, and listed
through that descriptor (kept open while its entries are read); elsewhere a folder that is now a link is refused.
A folder swapped for a link or another folder while the walk runs is therefore never walked: the error "the
folder was replaced while it was copied" (`TreeResult.errors`), as a file replaced meanwhile is. `dst` must be
missing or an empty folder and not inside `src`. `EXPORT_EXCLUDE_NAMES` = `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`,
`__pycache__` (at any depth); `EXPORT_EXCLUDE_PATHS` = `.scratch/_skills`,
`.unavailable-workspace` (relative paths); `.git` and `.scratch/<member>` are kept. `TreeResult`: files, bytes,
digest, links, excluded, special, errors, entries `(path, size, sha256)`, modes. `tree_digest(entries)`: sha256
over the sorted lines `<NFC path with '/'>\0<size>\0<sha256>\n`, the same on every OS (empty folders do not
count). `compare_digest` leaves out `volatile` files (below a `.git`: index, `*.lock`, logs, FETCH_HEAD,
ORIG_HEAD, COMMIT_EDITMSG and the like, never objects or refs; anywhere the `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` file next to
its database). `modes`: "keep"; "export" copies the bits where the destination can hold them and records
`mode_record` bits (POSIX: executable, read-only or owner-restricted files; Windows: read-only); "import" ignores
the medium's bits and sets the recorded ones (`valid_mode`), never writable by group or others; "writable" (a
copy into a new session) keeps the bits as "keep" does, but the owner can always read and write (`S_IRUSR |
S_IWUSR`; on Windows it clears read-only), the group and others never write (`& ~0o022`), a file reported as
0o777 on POSIX, or any file when `fs_type(src)` (the longest mount point of `/proc/self/mountinfo` holding the
source; None elsewhere) is one without POSIX bits (`9p`, `drvfs`, `vfat`, `msdos`, `exfat`, `cifs`, `smb3`,
`smbfs`, `ntfs`, `ntfs3`, `fuseblk`: they report 0o777, 0o755 for a CIFS share, 0o555 for a read-only Windows
file), becomes 0o644, or 0o755 when its first bytes are `#!`, `\x7fELF` or a Mach-O magic, and the setuid, setgid
and sticky bits are dropped (folders are created with the default mode).
`is_within(path, parent)` compares as text and by file identity. `progress(bytes, files)` is called after each
chunk written `(bytes, 0)` and each file copied `(0, 1)`. The limits, for a copy into a new session: `fold_names`
matches `exclude_names` ignoring case; `max_files` / `max_bytes` raise `TreeLimit(what="files" | "bytes", limit)`
before the file that would pass them (by the size the file system reports, and again while the bytes are read: a
file that grows; only regular files that are walked count, and reaching a limit exactly is allowed); `check()` is
called before every file and after every chunk read, and what it raises (a cancellation) stops the walk. After a
`TreeLimit`, or what `check` or `progress` raised, the partial copy stays for the caller to remove, as after a write
error; an unreadable file is still only listed in `errors`. `COPY_EXCLUDE_NAMES` = `EXPORT_EXCLUDE_NAMES` plus
`.git` (DreamTeam makes the new session's own repository and first commit). `copyfrom.py` (§17.2 "Copying files
into a new session") uses it with `fold_names=True`, `skip_files=COPY_SKIP_FILES`, the limits, `check` and
`modes="writable"`, after a `scan_tree(hash=False)` with the same limits.

### 20.6 MCP library on disk (mcp_library.py)

The library is `Config.library_dir` (§17.1), one folder per server in mcp_forge's format (`server.py` of at most
`mcp_forge.MAX_CODE_BYTES`, `meta.json` of at most `MAX_META_BYTES`). `read_folder(folder, name=None)`,
`read_entry(root, name) -> LibraryEntry | None`, `scan(root) -> Scan(entries, skipped)`, `list_entries(root)`,
`check_requirements(requirements)`, `write_entry_folder(folder, code, meta)`, `add_entry(root, src, *, name=None,
replace=False, meta_updates=None, meta_drop=()) -> "added" | "rewritten" | "unchanged"` (staged in a temp folder
of the root and renamed in, the old entry renamed away first; another entry without `replace`: `LibraryError` 409
`exists=[name]`; an approval recorded for the same digest is kept), `remove_entry(root, name)` (renamed away, then
deleted; a link is removed itself). `LibraryEntry`: name, path, meta, code, requirements, `digest`
(`snapshot_digest` of the files), `stored_digest`, `approved_digest`, tools; `approved` = approved_digest ==
digest; `changed_outside` = stored_digest != digest (content-based: it holds on another computer). Links are
never followed. mcp_forge keeps its own library code in stage 1.

### 20.7 Not in stage 1

Export and import through a running hub (launcher routes), in the TUI, console or web UI; an MCP tool for either;
`--update` of an existing export; a path map for folders outside the home; the legacy `main` session and
`dreamteam run` projects; a command that lists or restores `.replaced-*` backups.

## 21. External HTTP API v1 (api_v1.py, autoreply.py, eventtext.py)

A stable HTTP interface for programs that use the swarm as a service: a site uploads a document (or names a folder the
owner listed, 21.10), starts a session with a goal, shows its timeline, answers the agents if asked and gets the
result as JSON and files. It is the HTTP form of `dreamteam -p` (docs/TUI.md §2), not a mirror of the board:
everything is said in terms of a session, its goal, events, requests to the user, the result and files, so that a
session in another mode (a feed instead of a task board) can answer the same routes. The internal routes (§14, §18.1)
stay as they are and may change; `/api/v1` changes only as 21.1 says. What a thread session adds (create, options,
PATCH, summary, result, timeline, `continue`) is in §22.9.

### 21.1 Where, who, format

- **Where.** Every launcher serves v1 under `/api/v1/`, next to the routes of §18.1: `dreamteam serve`,
  `dreamteam mcp` in a home (its web part), the TUI's in-process launcher, and `dreamteam sandbox` of a home (which
  runs `serve` in the container and passes the API token's digest). All of them go through `launcher.serve_launcher` →
  `create_launcher_app`. `dreamteam run` and `dreamteam sandbox` of a single-swarm project have none: `web.create_app`
  never takes the API token. With an API token `serve` prints `API: <base>/api/v1` among its addresses, and
  `dreamteam sandbox` of a home prints the same line with the header it needs (`docker.access_lines(..., api=True)`),
  naming `DREAMTEAM_API_TOKEN`, never the token or its digest.
- **Dispatch.** `create_launcher_app` makes `ApiV1(manager, host)` (21.9) and puts a dispatcher in front of
  `SessionRouter`: a path that `web.is_api_path` takes (`/api/v1` itself, or a path that starts with `/api/v1/`) goes
  to `ApiV1.app`, every other path to `SessionRouter` as before. The guard (§14) chooses its v1 branch by the same
  predicate. v1 is a Starlette app of its own because the routes of `inner` sit behind `SessionRouter` and get
  Starlette's plain-text 404 and 405 and its slash redirects. `ApiV1.app` has `redirect_slashes` off (a bare `/api/v1`
  is a JSON 404, never a 307) and an `HTTPException` handler that answers 404 `not_found` and 405 `method_not_allowed`
  (with its `Allow` header) as JSON. It has no catch-all route: Starlette takes the first full match before any
  partial one, so a catch-all for every method would turn a wrong method into a 404. A path is one route with its
  handlers by method (`ApiV1._route(path, {method: handler})`), never one route per method: Starlette answers a wrong
  method with the first partial match alone, so its 405 would name one route's methods. The 405's `Allow` names every
  method of the path, sorted. A route takes only the methods it names: HEAD and OPTIONS are 405 like any other
  (Starlette would add HEAD to a GET route). Every route goes through one wrapper, which answers 401 `token_required`
  when the request did not come through the guard's v1 branch (no `scope["dreamteam.api_caller"]`), the manager's
  errors (`api_v1.CODED_ERRORS`: `SessionError`, `CopyError`, `SkillError`, and `sessionopts.OptionError` of a
